title: Data Analytics Manager
description:
## **About this Role**

👋 Hi, I’m [_Kevin_](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adamantine/). I manage the Data team and our analytics products at Ashby. I’m hiring our first **Data Analytics Manager** at an important point in Ashby’s growth, and I hope you have the patience to read a job posting that may be a little unconventional.

You will manage Ashby’s three Data Analysts: two core analysts and one analyst focused on Revenue Operations. Our Data Engineer will initially continue to report directly to me, so this role is deliberately more focused on the analytical side of the team while remaining a close partner in the broader data ecosystem.

The primary result of your successful management will be a team of analysts with excellent judgment, strong technical methods, clear communication, and a deep sense of ownership. I am looking for someone who can help that team do better work, choose better work, and grow into the next stage of Ashby alongside the company.

Rather than begin with a long list of tools or years of experience, I want to share four questions that sit at the center of this role. If you apply, your answer should be “yes” to each. Should we get a chance to talk, what I will really want to understand is the nuance: your unique how, why, and what behind your answers.

1. **Can you identify and hire talented people?**

We will continue to grow the analyst team, and you will play a meaningful role in finding and assessing future teammates. Great analysts combine technical judgment, curiosity, communication, business context, and a willingness to own work end to end. Can you recognize that combination in others?
2. **Can you develop and amplify the data practices that let a small team do excellent work?**

Ashby’s Data team is lean, and our practices will need to evolve as the company becomes more complex. I see this role as an opportunity to improve the ways we prioritize work, review it, share knowledge, maintain quality, and collaborate.
3. **Can you lead the team through the transition from broad shared context to meaningful specialization?**

Today, each analyst can know a great deal about the company and data stack. That will become more challenging as Ashby grows across products, regions, systems, and business functions. We will need to develop stronger domain context and clearer ways of working without turning the team into a set of narrow, disconnected specialists.
4. **Can you help the Data team navigate the rapidly evolving implications of AI?**

AI will affect how our analysts work, how the company self-serves analytical questions, and how other teams use internal business data. Much of that work depends on trusted, well-modeled, appropriately accessible warehouse-derived data. You will help the Data team explore and evaluate the relevant tools, workflows, and partnerships—bringing ambition, practicality, and a high bar for accuracy.

These questions add up to a simple reality: Ashby is growing quickly, and the surrounding data needs are becoming more complex. We are becoming a multi-product, global company with more business systems and larger team dynamics. This is a great opportunity at a great company, but it will be hard and consequential work. I am looking for a manager who is excited to help shape the Data function and build an excellent team for its current and future members.

##   
**Your responsibilities as a Data Analytics Manager**

To understand the role, it helps to understand how our team works today.

Data Analysts at Ashby are full-stack members of the Data team. We do not have a traditional split where Analytics Engineers build models and Data Analysts perform analysis only on prepared datasets. Our analysts work across raw and modeled data, contribute to dbt models and metric definitions, conduct deep analysis, build dashboards and other internal data products, and collaborate directly with partners throughout the company.

As a rough sketch, the team receives work through a standardized request process. Anyone can make a request; we triage it, assess the actual need, and decide whether it can be addressed quickly or should become a more deliberate project with a kickoff and plan. We do not currently organize ourselves around universal SLAs, sprints, or points. Instead, we aim to be good partners: communicate clearly, assess capacity honestly, prioritize thoughtfully, and make deliberate choices about what not to do. You will have a lot of leverage in aiding this process well.

Ashby’s [_Operating Principles_](https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles) place principled thinking ahead of reflexively leaning on prior experience or convention. In practice, that means work at Ashby does not always start with “let’s get all the data and metrics.” Data is one useful tool for resolving uncertainty; it is not automatically the first or only tool. That said, as the company matures and more teams optimize their work, demand for data will likely continue to grow. You will help us meet that demand with good judgment.

## **Why You Should or Shouldn’t Apply**

At Ashby’s current size, this is a player-coach role. You should expect to get hands-on with analytical work as you learn the business and the team, and to remain close enough to the work to guide its quality well.

You could be a strong fit if you:

- Have exceptional analytical judgment. You can calibrate the depth and rigor of an analysis to the decision at hand: knowing when precision matters, when uncertainty is material, and when additional work would not change the outcome.
- Can produce and evaluate transparent, rigorous analysis. You bring readers along through the problem context, data considered, assumptions, meaningful cleaning or reduction steps, caveats, statistical pitfalls, and practical conclusion.
- Are a strong visual and written communicator. You care about clear tables and charts, meaningful labels and definitions, coherent narratives, and making complex work understandable without overstating certainty.
- Have deep hands-on SQL experience, plus working fluency with dbt-style data modeling, cloud data warehouses, and BI tools. You do not need to have owned a warehouse as a Data Engineer, but you should be comfortable working across the analytical data stack.
- Have led, managed, or functionally acted as a manager for data practitioners in a high-growth company. Formal people-management experience is valuable, but not required if you have demonstrated equivalent judgment, coaching, hiring, and team-leadership abilities.
- Bring a product-manager-like instinct for finding the core need behind a request, understanding users and business context, and turning ambiguous questions into useful work.
- Are pragmatic and intellectually flexible. You see data as one important input to good judgment alongside qualitative research, collaboration, user understanding, and clear thinking.
- Are intimately familiar with the B2B SaaS industry, workflows and organizational structures.
- Have an eye and instinct for simplicity over complexity in all matters.
- Have experience in a growth-stage, product-oriented technology company and are energized by helping a lean team scale.
- You can appreciate the whole distribution as much as a point estimator.

## **Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if:**

- You are looking for a pure-management role removed from the details of analytical work. You will need to be comfortable getting hands-on as you learn the team and helping analysts work through difficult problems.
- You have only worked in an environment where analysis begins after another team has fully prepared the data. Ashby analysts are expected to work across the stack, from modeling through final analysis and dashboards.
- Spreadsheet-only analytical work is your preferred mode. Fluency with SQL in a modern data warehouse is essential.
- You would rather use a metric, dashboard, experiment, or process by default than first ask what degree of evidence is actually needed to make a good decision.
- You are looking for consumer-scale data infrastructure projects. We have a large and interesting dataset (see our [_Talent Trends_](https://www.ashbyhq.com/talent-trends-report) reports!), but we are a B2B SaaS company. Relative to many B2C services, we are small but mighty.
- You are seeking an in-person work experience. Ashby is remote, although there are employee hotspots around the world and we meet in person at various events throughout the year.
- You have never formally managed a data team.

Naturally, this role is important and represents a combination of different skills. You may not meet every dimension perfectly, and that’s OK. If the dot product of your skill vector with this requirements vector is close to 1, please consider applying, but please note it does not have to be 1.0.

## **Data Culture at Ashby**

At Ashby, we draw a clear distinction between when to look to data for "the answer" and when to use data to aid principled thinking for decision making. In general, a primary consideration is whether or not data is needed to help clarify points of uncertainty. When data is considered necessary, a secondary consideration is to what depth data will be required. Data questions lend themselves to ongoing "what about..." or "what if..." explorations, which can be important in some situations but are not always necessary.  
  
With these dynamics in mind, we do not foster an environment where every decision we make should be backed by data, but we do foster an environment where teammates ask whether or not data will fit the task at hand well. This, in turn, allows us to operate a lean team focused on projects where data provides true leverage to our overall business and product goals.  
  
As a related but distinct point, Ashby’s data culture, as far as transparency and access goes, is very open. We share company-wide access to our financial standings, progress, goals, and generally make any data and reporting results broadly available. Outside of constraints related to whether a teammate has access to a particular tool, there are close to no constraints on access the state of the company as told by data or reporting. In general, we would like to continue and extend open access to data throughout the company (with your help!), but with consideration and not as a substitute for principled thinking :)

## **Interview Process**

Our interview process is thorough, but we aim to be respectful of the total candidate time invested. We aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to determine if Ashby is the right fit for you. The expected process for this role is as follows:

- Hiring Manager Screen (30 mins)
- Technical Screen (45 min)
- Assessment: Mini Analysis and Write-up (45min)
- Final Round - Virtual Onsite (~2.5, can be split into multiple days)

  - (45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Productivity
  - (45 mins) Data Team: Analysis and Collaboration
  - (30 mins) Business Partnership
  - (30 mins) Chat with a Founder
  - (15 mins) Follow-Up Conversation + Debrief with the Hiring Manager

**Note:** please do not reach out to the broader Ashby team requesting more information or time to connect. We will diligently review all applications in detail after the public posting period is over.

## **Benefits**

- Competitive salary and equity.
- 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby - do it when you feel financially comfortable.
- Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.
- A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.
- Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!
- $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.
- If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

If you've made it this far and are excited about Ashby, please apply and[ _follow us on LinkedIn_](https://www.linkedin.com/company/ashbyhq) to stay up to date!

*Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.*

*Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.*

title: Backend & Data Engineer(Junior - Mid Level)
description:

title: Software Engineer - AI Expert
description:
Apply directly through: https://alpheva.ai/experts/

Get paid to help build better AI.

Alpheva AI is looking for experienced software engineers to participate in paid, project-based work that helps train and evaluate the next generation of AI coding systems.

This is not a full-time job. You work remotely and asynchronously on projects that fit around your existing schedule.

Your engineering experience becomes the signal that helps AI systems learn what good software engineering actually looks like.

What you'll do

Depending on the project, you may:

Build: Solve realistic software engineering problems and produce high-quality implementations.
Evaluate: Review AI-generated code, pull requests, architectures, tests, and debugging approaches.
Debug: Diagnose failures in real or realistic software repositories and explain what went wrong.
Review: Assess whether an AI agent's implementation is correct, maintainable, secure, and production-ready.
Demonstrate: Complete software engineering workflows in real development environments so AI systems can learn how experienced engineers actually work.
Create evaluations: Develop challenging engineering tasks and criteria for measuring AI coding agents.
Compare solutions: Assess multiple AI-generated solutions and identify meaningful differences in correctness, quality, and engineering judgment.

Projects may involve repository navigation, implementation, testing, debugging, code review, system design, and other software engineering workflows.

Who we're looking for

We're looking for experienced working software engineers, not necessarily AI researchers.

You should have:

3+ years of professional software engineering experience
Strong programming and debugging skills
Experience working in production codebases
Ability to understand unfamiliar repositories and systems
Strong code review and technical judgment
Experience writing and reviewing tests
Ability to clearly explain why a solution is correct or incorrect

Experience with any of the following is valuable:

Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Java, C++, Rust, or similar
Backend or distributed systems
APIs and microservices
Databases and data systems
Cloud infrastructure
DevOps / CI/CD
Security
Frontend engineering
Mobile development
Machine learning infrastructure
Agentic AI or coding agents

You do not need prior experience working in AI.

What matters most is that you know how to do software engineering well.

What the work looks like

You might be asked to:

Fix a bug in an unfamiliar repository.

Review an AI-generated pull request and identify the issues.

Implement a feature and write the appropriate tests.

Compare two AI-generated implementations and determine which actually works.

Debug a failing application and explain the root cause.

Evaluate whether an AI coding agent successfully completed an engineering task.

Work through a multi-step software engineering task in a real development environment.

The goal is not simply to determine whether code looks good.

The goal is to capture the judgment an experienced engineer uses to determine whether software actually works.

Compensation

Paid project-based work.

Rates vary based on your experience, specialization, and project requirements. Your applicable rate and project scope will be shown before you commit to a project.

Some projects are short assignments. Others may involve recurring work over a longer period.

There is no fixed schedule and no minimum commitment.

Work arrangement
Remote
Asynchronous
Project-based
Flexible hours
Work around your existing job or commitments
Paid for qualifying project work
Why Alpheva

AI coding systems are becoming remarkably capable at generating code.

But writing a plausible-looking patch is not the same as being a good software engineer.

AI needs to learn how experienced engineers:

Understand unfamiliar systems
Make architectural tradeoffs
Debug failures
Write reliable tests
Review code
Handle edge cases
Reason about security and performance
Decide when an implementation is actually production-ready

That's where you come in.

Your engineering judgment helps shape how AI learns to build software.

How it works

1. Apply

Tell us about your engineering background, experience, and areas of expertise.

2. Get qualified

Complete a short, paid software engineering assessment designed around the type of work you'll perform.

3. Get matched

When your experience matches an active project, we'll share the scope, requirements, and compensation.

4. Do the work

Complete projects remotely and asynchronously.

5. Get paid

Receive the agreed rate for your completed work.

Important

You are not required to share confidential information, proprietary source code, trade secrets, or materials belonging to your employer.

Projects are designed so that your professional expertise can be applied without exposing confidential employer information.

Help teach AI how great engineers actually work.

Apply to become an Alpheva Software Engineering Expert.

description:

title: Rust Backend Engineer

title: Head of Growth, cofounder track
location: Atlanta; Austin; Boston; Chicago; New York City; Philadelphia; New York; Richmond; Newark; San Francisco Bay Area; Los Angeles County
description:
Commission and equity. No salary. That's the whole deal and it's at the top for a reason.

Gabb builds neuroadaptive language learning for K-12 English learners. 3,973 students across 102 school deployments. 25 paying schools. Live on web, Android and VR, with iOS and AR this quarter. Seven years in, revenue in the bank, a government pilot running in Jordan.

Here's the number that should interest you: our customer acquisition cost is $35 and we have never spent a dollar on paid acquisition. Every customer we have came from the product working and somebody telling somebody else. We also have 77 school deployments that aren't paying and nobody working on them.

That is an enormous amount of free money sitting on the table because there is no growth function. There is me, and I'm doing eleven other things.

What you'd own

Demand. All of it. Content, channels, the funnel from a stranger seeing us to a school booking a demo, and the 77 deployments we've never tried to convert.

You decide the strategy. There's no marketing plan for you to execute because there isn't one.

Cofounder track, honestly

It means this: you start on commission and a small equity grant. At 90 days we sit down and look at what happened. If you've moved the number, we restructure to real cofounder equity and the title that goes with it. If you haven't, we part as friends and you keep what vested.

I'm not going to hand cofounder equity to someone I've known for three weeks and neither would you. But the path is real and it's short.

What you get

10% of first-year contract value on every school or district you source that closes.
An initial equity grant on a four year vest with a one year cliff, revisited at 90 days.
Direct work with me every day and a seat in product.
A category where almost nobody markets well, which means the bar you have to clear is lower than you think.

What you don't get

A salary. A budget. Anyone to tell you what to do.

Who this is for

Someone who has actually grown something, even something small, and can tell me the number. Early career is fine; I care about whether you've done it, not how long you've been doing it.

How to apply

Send me one thing you grew and the number it went from and to. One paragraph. That's the whole application.

Malcolm Lee, Founder and CEO
malcolm@gabbglobal.com

acceptedRemoteLocations: San Francisco, California; San Francisco Bay Area, United States; Atlanta, Georgia; Chicago, Illinois; New York City, New York; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; Providence, Rhode Island; Richmond, Virginia
description:
Founding Designer, Gabb Global

Equity now, salary when our round closes. That's the whole deal and it's at the top for a reason.

The problem

A 12 year old in Amman says a French sentence out loud. In the four seconds that follow, our engine reads five things: how accurate the sounds were, how long she waited before she started, how fast she spoke, how loud, and whether she got it right. All of it measured against her own voice in her own first language, not against how a native speaker sounds. Then it decides whether the next thing gets harder or easier.

That decision is the entire company. It is based on real psycholinguistics, it works, and right now the student sees almost none of it. She just gets a different question and no idea why.

Designing that moment is the job. Making an invisible adaptive system legible to a child, in a way that builds trust instead of anxiety, without turning the screen into a dashboard. Nobody in this category has solved it. Duolingo doesn't try. Immerse doesn't try.

title: Associate Member of Technical Staff, AI Engineering
description:
**About Himaya**

Himaya is an AI-native security platform for small and midsize companies. We protect email against phishing, BEC, vendor fraud and malware. We stop sensitive data from leaving through outbound DLP, monitor SaaS apps, cloud accounts and data stores, and keep customers audit ready. Our engine combines large language models with deterministic detection, sandboxing and threat intelligence. Most threats are investigated and handled automatically, so lean IT teams get enterprise grade protection.

We're a small team, so you will ship to production in your first weeks and own real parts of the system.

**The role**

You will join the team that keeps Himaya's detection accurate and dependable. Your time will be split across three areas:

* detection quality
* the open source models behind our reasoning and data classification;
* the platform those models run on.

**What you'll do**

Detection hygiene and improvement:

* Review false positives and false negatives from live email traffic, find the root cause and fix it. That might be a pattern rule, a scoring threshold, a prompt or a model.
* Maintain and extend our detection rules for phishing, BEC, impersonation, malicious links, attachments and QR codes.
* Build and maintain evaluation sets and regression tests, so every change to the engine is measured before it ships.
* Monitor model cost, latency and accuracy, and propose improvements backed by data.

Models:

* Help stand up and maintain open source models for security reasoning, used in threat triage and investigation.
* Build and improve data classification models for Workspace Security and DLP. These detect credentials, personal data, financial data and regulated data across email, SaaS apps and data stores.
* Run experiments: prompt design, fine tuning, distillation and model comparisons. Turn the results into production changes.
* Keep model serving reliable, with fallbacks, timeouts and observability.

Platform engineering:

* Contribute to our Python and FastAPI backend, our workers and our integrations with Google Workspace and Microsoft 365.
* Work with Postgres, Redis and containerized services on Azure and AWS.
* Improve CI, tests and deployment tooling, and help keep production healthy.

What we're looking for:

* A recent graduate in Computer Science, AI or a related field, or up to 1 year of work experience.
* Hands-on experience with machine learning or LLMs: building with model APIs, running open source models such as Llama, Qwen or Mistral, fine tuning, or building evaluation pipelines. University projects, research, internships and open source work all count.
* Strong Python. You write clean code, and you write tests for it.
* Comfortable with SQL, Git and the Linux command line.
* Curious about security, and careful by nature. In this job, a wrong verdict can either put an employee at risk or hold back a legitimate email.
* Clear written communication. You can explain why a change is right using evidence.
* Nice to have
* Experience with inference servers such as vLLM, TGI or Ollama, or with cloud model platforms such as AWS Bedrock and Azure AI Foundary.
* Experience with text classification, named entity recognition or PII detection.
* An understanding of email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) or phishing techniques.
* Docker, any cloud platform, or a background in CTFs and security research.

title: Video Editor & Content Designer
description:
**About iris & Affinity Answers**

Affinity Answers is a self-funded, profitable global company that helps 400+ advertisers, agencies and publishers across the US, EU and APAC understand and target human behaviour.

iris by AdChoreo, incubated by Affinity Answers, is a fully managed patient-growth service for independent clinics in India: aesthetics and skin, dental, eye care, wellness and Ayurveda, and fertility and metabolic health. iris gets a clinic found (website, weekly Google posts, monthly blogs, ads), chosen (Google Business Profile, genuine reviews, social media) and booked (Iris Concierge, which engages and books leads inside the clinic's existing WhatsApp Business app).

We have audited 1,000+ independent clinics across India; the average online visibility score is 47 out of 100. One Mumbai skin clinic went from no website to being cited in Google AI Overviews within 3 days of going live, with zero ad spend.
We need someone who can make iris look and sound as good on Instagram as the results it delivers.

**What you'll own**

• Edit our shoots into Instagram-ready content. The team shoots founder talks, clinic visits, client testimonials, explainers and behind-the-scenes. You turn raw footage into Reels, Stories and carousels with tight cuts, captions, sound design, colour correction and hooks that hold attention in the first 2 seconds.

• Design static posts with real people in them. Carousels, announcement posts, case-study cards and quote cards featuring team members, clients and real product screenshots. Static work must be designed by you; AI can assist, but it cannot be the whole post.

• Use AI video tools where they genuinely help. Higgsfield, Runway and similar tools for B-roll, motion, transitions, background clean-up or concept visuals, blended with real footage so the output never looks AI-generated.

• Run a weekly content pipeline. Turn the content calendar into a steady output: target 4–5 Reels and 3–4 static posts a week, delivered in Instagram-native formats (9:16, 4:5, 1:1) with cover frames.

• Keep the brand consistent. Build and maintain templates, type styles, caption styles, lower thirds and intro/outro elements so every post is recognisably iris.

• Learn from what performs. Review reach, saves, watch time and shares with the Growth Marketing Lead every week, and change the edit style based on what the numbers say.

• Support clinic content where needed. iris offers a social media add-on to clinics (posts, reels and shoots). You may edit and design for client clinics as that grows, following each clinic's brand and medical-content guidelines.

**Tools & skills**

• Video editing - Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve, at a professional level

• Motion & effects - Basic After Effects: titles, text animation, simple motion graphics

• AI video - Hands-on with Higgsfield and/or Runway

• Static design - Photoshop and Figma (or Illustrator) for posts and carousels

• Audio - Clean-up, levels, music and SFX placement

• Instagram craft - Reels formats, safe zones, trending audio, captions, cover frames

**Who we're looking for**

• A portfolio, not a promise. You can show 10+ Reels or short-form edits you made, ideally with the raw footage or a before/after.

• Taste. You know why one Reel feels premium and another feels cheap, and you can explain it.

• Speed with quality. You can turn a 20-minute raw shoot into 3 usable Reels within 48 hours.

• Real over synthetic. You use AI to save time, not to replace real people. Healthcare audiences trust faces, clinics and results they can verify.

• Ownership. You track your own deliverables, ask for footage when it's missing and flag when a brief isn't working.

• Healthcare sensitivity. You're careful with before/after content, patient privacy and claims, and you follow the guidelines we give you.

• Communication. Comfortable in English; Hindi is a plus for regional content.

**Role details**

• Engagement - Full-time consultant, 3-month contract, renewable on performance

• Compensation - ₹25,000/month fixed

• Location - Remote · India; occasional in-person shoots may be requested with notice

• Hours - Full-time, with overlap during Indian business hours for reviews

• Equipment - Your own laptop capable of 4K editing and licensed or legitimate software access

• Ownership of work - All edited and designed content belongs to iris / Affinity Answers

• Reports to - Growth Marketing Lead, iris by AdChoreo

**What We’re Looking For**

- Experience in community management, growth, partnerships, or a closely related role
- Comfortable doing outreach and relationship-building at volume, this is a hands-on, high-touch role early on
- Strategic thinker who can also execute; you’ll be building the playbook, not just following one
- Genuinely interested in community-building and/or the African startup ecosystem

**Why Join Now**

You’d be one of the first core team members shaping how BLOCspace grows from 30 listed communities toward the scale where monetization kicks in. Equity now means real ownership in that growth story.

title: AI-Powered Growth Marketing Leader (Industrial + SaaS + Growth)
description:
**Remote | Full-Time | B2B Industrial AI | Growth Stage**

Industrility is looking for an **AI-powered marketing guru** who can think strategically, execute hands-on, and orchestrate multiple marketing channels into **one powerful, consistent growth engine**.

This is not a role for someone who manages one channel.

We need someone who can simultaneously think about an upcoming trade show, a LinkedIn campaign, an email nurture sequence, a new website page, a customer story, a webinar, SEO, paid campaigns, CRM conversion, and sales follow-up — and make all of it feel like **one cohesive Industrility story**.

You should be exceptionally comfortable using AI to research, ideate, write, design, analyze, repurpose, personalize, automate, and accelerate your work.

Think **CMO mindset + growth marketer + content strategist + AI power user + hands-on executor.**

## About Industrility

Industrility is an **Industrial AI company building enterprise software for industrial and commercial machinery manufacturers**.

We help manufacturers transform their aftermarket and service businesses using **Agentic AI, Generative AI, Digital Twins, IoT, knowledge graphs, and connected field intelligence**.

Industrility was featured by Google Cloud among the startups **“building the agentic future,”** and was the only Industrial AI company highlighted in the article.

We are growing quickly, solving complex real-world problems, and building at the intersection of AI, industrial equipment, field service, aftermarket, and customer experience.

## Your Mission

Your mission is simple:

**Turn Industrility's technology, customer outcomes, ideas, events, and expertise into a nonstop demand-generation and brand-building machine.**

You will own the connective tissue across marketing.

A webinar should become a LinkedIn campaign.

A customer insight should become a blog, an email campaign, a sales asset, an infographic, and a short video.

A trade show should generate content before the event, engagement during the event, and pipeline afterward.

A product launch should appear consistently across our website, email, LinkedIn, paid campaigns, presentations, and sales outreach.

Nothing should exist in isolation.

## What You Will Own

- **AI-Powered Marketing Orchestration** — Use AI aggressively to research markets, develop messaging, create campaigns, personalize content, generate creative concepts, analyze results, and dramatically increase marketing velocity.

- **LinkedIn Marketing** — Own Industrility's organic LinkedIn presence and coordinate with agencies to build executive thought leadership, company content, campaigns, and audience engagement.

- **Email Marketing** — Build and manage targeted campaigns, nurture programs, newsletters, event follow-ups, and account-based outreach using platforms such as Zoho Campaigns.

- **Website & Digital Content** — Own and continuously improve Industrility's WordPress presence, landing pages, messaging, SEO, conversion paths, and campaign experiences.

- **Content Engine** — Develop and repurpose compelling blogs, ebooks, white papers, customer stories, webinars, videos, product content, thought leadership, SEO pages, and social content.

- **Event Marketing** — Create campaigns around trade shows, webinars, customer events, launches, and industry conferences — before, during, and after the event.

- **Performance Marketing** — Manage and optimize campaigns across LinkedIn Ads, Google Ads, YouTube, retargeting, and other relevant channels.

- **Creative & Visual Storytelling** — Create or direct compelling graphics, diagrams, presentation slides, campaign creative, website imagery, video concepts, and social assets.

- **CRM & Funnel Hygiene** — Ensure leads don't disappear into a black hole. Track prospects, MQLs, campaign attribution, follow-ups, lifecycle stages, and movement from marketing into sales.

- **Marketing Analytics** — Build visibility into what is actually working. Track traffic, engagement, MQLs, pipeline influence, campaign performance, CAC, conversion rates, event ROI, and channel effectiveness.

- **Agency Leadership** — Manage external agencies and specialists while maintaining ownership of the strategy, message, quality, and business outcome.

- **Founder Partnership** — Work closely with the founders to turn raw ideas, customer conversations, product innovations, industry observations, and strategic vision into powerful market-facing narratives.

## The Person We Are Looking For

We hire **rock stars**.

We value people who love solving real-world problems, move fast, learn constantly, and care deeply about the quality of what they put into the world.

The ideal person is both **strategic and extremely hands-on**.

You should be able to spend one hour shaping our positioning with the founders and the next hour building a landing page, improving an email campaign, creating a graphic with AI, reviewing campaign analytics, or turning a customer conversation into a great LinkedIn post.

You don't wait for a team of ten people to execute an idea.

You figure out how to make it happen.

## Your Superpowers

We would love to meet you if:

- You are an **exceptional AI power user** and use tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, image-generation tools, AI video tools, research agents, and automation platforms as extensions of yourself.
- You understand how to create a **single narrative across website, social, email, events, content, paid media, and sales enablement**.
- You have strong experience in **B2B technology marketing**, ideally enterprise software, industrial technology, manufacturing, field service, IoT, AI, or SaaS.
- You can communicate sophisticated technical ideas in a way that executives, engineers, salespeople, and customers can immediately understand.
- You can develop a marketing strategy — and then personally execute it.
- You are an excellent writer with strong instincts around messaging, storytelling, positioning, and brand.
- You understand demand generation, ABM, lead nurturing, funnels, MQLs, CRM discipline, and sales alignment.
- You have hands-on experience with email marketing, CRM, marketing automation, WordPress, analytics, and social platforms.
- You have strong creative instincts and can create or direct graphics, presentations, videos, diagrams, and campaign assets.
- You are comfortable managing agencies without outsourcing your thinking to them.
- You obsess over results rather than activity.
- You thrive in the ambiguity, speed, and ownership that come with an ambitious startup.

## Bonus Points

Experience with any of the following is especially valuable:

Industrial OEMs, machinery manufacturers, aftermarket/service businesses, field service, manufacturing technology, Industry 4.0, IoT, Digital Twins, AI/ML, enterprise SaaS, Zoho CRM/Campaigns, WordPress, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Ads, SEO, webinars, video production, or startup marketing.

## What Success Looks Like

You help Industrility become impossible to ignore within the industrial manufacturing ecosystem.

Our message becomes sharper.

Our content becomes dramatically better.

Our campaigns become more coordinated.

Our events generate pipeline.

Our website converts.

Our founders become stronger thought leaders.

Our sales team receives better-qualified opportunities.

And every customer interaction reinforces the same clear story about why Industrility represents the future of industrial aftermarket and service.

**Be ready to work hard, think big, move fast, experiment constantly — and have fun building something remarkable.**

Please share your CV, write a brief statement of your superpower and alignment with our company and some examples of content that you feel is relevant for this application.

title: Certified Nutrition Specialist
description:
**Certified Nutrition Specialist (CNS)**  
Capitated Model | Contract / Remote (US-Only)

**About The Role**

Mochi Medical, originally founded as an obesity management practice, is expanding its virtual care model beyond weight management. We're looking for Certified Nutrition Specialists who are committed to delivering high-quality, accessible, and affordable medical nutrition therapy alongside our Registered Dietitian Nutritionists. While obesity and metabolic health remain core areas of focus, our providers also support patients in areas such as dermatology, hormone replacement therapy, depression and anxiety, longevity, and hair loss. You will guide patients through their health journey with personalized, evidence-based nutrition care as part of a physician-led team.

**What You'll Do**

- Conduct one-on-one virtual medical nutrition therapy and nutrition counseling visits, including personalized meal planning.
- Provide nutrition counseling that supports patients across multiple specialty areas and recognizes the link between nutrition and whole-body health.
- Build rapport, credibility, and engagement with patients through exceptional communication.
- Use motivational interviewing to guide patients toward sustainable lifestyle change.
- Document visits in our EMR using our nutrition note templates.
- Stay current with research on obesity medicine, GLP-1 therapy and nutrition, binge eating disorder, and emerging specialty areas.
- Practice only in states where you are legally permitted to provide MNT and only with patients located in those states.
- Adapt to a fast-paced startup environment and contribute to team-wide improvements.

**Who You Are**

**Required Qualifications**

- Active Certified Nutrition Specialist (CNS) credential in good standing with the Board for Certification of Nutrition Specialists (BCNS).
- At least 1 year of experience providing individualized nutrition counseling or MNT to patients with obesity, diabetes, or other cardiometabolic conditions.
- Legally permitted to provide medical nutrition therapy in at least one state where Mochi sees patients. A state nutritionist license or certification is required for insurance-covered visits (see "A note on states" below) and is strongly preferred.
- Individual professional liability (malpractice) insurance, or willingness to obtain it before your start date.
- Proficient in online scheduling tools, EMR systems, and video-visit coordination.
- Skilled in motivational interviewing and patient education.
- Comfortable working in a dynamic, evolving startup environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Current state license or certification as a nutritionist in one or more of: Florida, New York, Washington, North Carolina, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Minnesota, Massachusetts, Kentucky, Connecticut, New Mexico, Montana, Delaware, North Dakota, District of Columbia, or Alaska. CNS candidates practicing in other states are also encouraged to apply.
- Experience with GLP-1 or other anti-obesity medications and the nutrition considerations that accompany them.
- Experience or interest in nutrition as it relates to dermatology, hormone replacement therapy, mental health, longevity, or hair loss.
- Bilingual (English/Spanish) (a plus).

title: Project Manager
description:
**About** [**Kontakt.io**](http://Kontakt.io)

Inside health systems, where every second can matter, operations are still spread across dozens of disconnected tools and platforms.[ ](https://kontakt.io/why-kontakt-io/)[_Kontakt.io_](http://Kontakt.io) is changing that.

We combine proprietary hardware, AI-powered intelligence, and deep integrations with the technology health systems already have in place to build real-time understanding of what's happening across their operations. Backed by Goldman Sachs and trusted by leading health systems including HCA Healthcare, Sutter Health, AdventHealth, Trinity Health, Northwell Health, Cleveland Clinic, and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, we’ve more than doubled our revenue and are rapidly scaling with a clear path toward $100M in annual recurring revenue.

If you're excited to solve hard problems and help health systems deliver better care, we'd love to meet you!

You’ll be the boots-on-the-ground owner for hospital deployments of [Kontakt.io](http://Kontakt.io) solutions—coordinating site readiness, installation crews, hospital IT, and vendors to turn SOWs into live, stable systems that deliver measurable outcomes.

- **Vendors & budgets**: coordinate third-party installers and OEMs to SLAs; track actuals vs. plan to protect PS margin.
 

**You’ll thrive here if you**

- Like being on site, solving real-world blockers quickly and safely.
- Keep work highly organized (lists, logs, labels) and communicate crisply.
- Are hands-on and high-agency—comfortable coordinating crews and moving hardware.
- Treat time, cost, scope, and safety as non-negotiables.
 

**Must-haves**

- Healthcare delivery environment experience (facilities, biomed, infection control, EHS).
- Strong contractor/vendor coordination and multi-site scheduling experience.

- Excellent written/verbal communication; clean checklists, acceptance docs, and status notes.
- **Ability to travel frequently to hospital sites.**

- Reading floor plans and creating as-builts (Visio/CAD/Bluebeam).
- Certifications: PMP/PRINCE2, OSHA-10/30, BICSI, Prosci (or similar).
 

**How we work**

- **IC ownership:** outcomes over activities; clear scope, gates, and acceptance.
- **Decision speed**: explicit owners, decision logs, and 24h escalation when blocked.
- **Enterprise-grade delivery**: change control, QA, and rollback plans on every cutover.
- **Vendor accountability**: SLAs, scorecards, and documented acceptance at each gate.
- **Two clocks, one plan**: we align project schedules with clinical realities; patient care comes first.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
description:
Worthy is an AI native debt resolution company that negotiates settlements on behalf of consumers. Our mission is to give every consumer struggling with debt a fair and affordable path back to financial stability.

We operate a consumer app (web and mobile), an API for consumer fintech applications to embed debt resolution, and an AI-powered negotiation engine that automates work that used to take rooms of human negotiators.

This industry has a long history of scams and predatory practices. We built Worthy to be the opposite: compliant, transparent, and accountable in every state we operate in.

This technology stack lets us offer debt settlement services at a 2.5–3x lower price than legacy providers, while negotiating faster and more consistently than manual, phone-based processes. Our AI has already negotiated $2.6M in debt, and we’re just getting started against a $65B market of debt in collections.

We’re hiring a Senior Full Stack Engineer to be the person who takes a problem from “the CEO described it in two sentences” to “it’s in production and we can see it working.” There is no backend team to hand things to — you’ll pick up whichever layer the problem lives in, across the API, the web apps, mobile, and the infrastructure underneath.

You’ll also build the systems that make a four-person team move like a bigger one. 100% of our code is now written with AI, and we’re pushing further: agents that triage errors, open fix PRs, run our QA suite, audit our dependencies, and handle the recurring engineering work that would otherwise consume a headcount. Extending that toolchain isn’t a side project here, it’s a core part of the job.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer (AI)
description:
A client's rental properties are often 30 to 50% of their net worth. The tool their financial advisor uses to think about them is a spreadsheet.

Leveridge takes a client's tax return and turns it into every property they own in one view, then models what happens if they hold, sell, or exchange. The advisor makes the call. We do the math.

We launched in mid-May. 13 advisory firms pay for Leveridge, up from 7 in early August.

We're four people, two founders, our founding engineer, and a front-end engineer. You'd be the fifth, and the third engineer, which means you'd touch nearly all of it and your name would be on a lot of it. We're in the middle of raising a pre-seed.

**What you'd own**

An advisor sits down with a client and has to say what to do with the largest asset that client owns. Hold it, sell it, or exchange it. The numbers on the screen when they make that call came from our code, and they're going to defend those numbers out loud with their license behind them. That's the job.

Today, when an advisor hits a hard case, they email us, or ask for fifteen minutes before the client meeting, or want to walk back through it afterward. What they're pulling on is what we know about real estate, and too much of that still lives in our heads instead of in the product. Getting it into the software is the work. The advisor should walk in alone and be the expert in the room.

The math has to be exactly right, and the data it runs on doesn't exist anywhere yet. Purchase price is in a closing file. Basis and depreciation are on a tax return, often a different one each year. The loan is on a lender's statement, the value is somebody's estimate, and part of it is in no system at all and has to be asked of the owner, because the owner is the only one who knows. A household arrives across several documents and several years, the same property reads differently in each, and the system has to reconcile that instead of quietly averaging it. If the data is wrong, the recommendation is wrong, so nothing downstream runs on a number nobody has stood behind.

Underneath that the engine is deterministic. Depreciation, basis, recapture, federal and state brackets, to the dollar. AI reads the documents and writes the narrative. It doesn't touch the math.

Portfolios have had a system of record for decades. Real estate never has.

You'd start on the document pipeline, which turns tax returns into the data everything else runs on. It works today, it isn't good enough, and nobody has owned it end to end. After that the roadmap is mostly open and you'd have a real say in it. A conversational layer over a client's whole portfolio. Monitoring that tells an advisor something changed before the client calls them. None of it is built.

None of that is every week, though. It's four people, so some weeks it's clearing a stack of bugs because the product needs that more than the roadmap does. That's the job too.

**Who we're looking for**

You've shipped production software on a real team for four or more years, and you can take an idea from nothing to running in production on your own. That matters more here than anything else on this list.

You've done applied AI work, not prompt wrapping and not research. You've built something where a model sat inside a pipeline that had to be right, and you had to measure whether it was.

A background in fintech, wealthtech, or financial planning helps. It isn't required, and neither is real estate. We'll teach you the domain.

The people who do well here bring us a problem while they're still inside it, instead of only showing finished work. They find the edge cases themselves. Interest-only loans, ARMs, HELOCs, a property carrying four paid-off liens. We need you hunting for what breaks. They say when something will be done, and then it's done, or you hear why before you have to ask. At four people, we're each counting on that.

**How we work**

Standup every morning, and that's most of the process. A decision gets made in a huddle the same day instead of in a planning cycle. You'd work directly with both founders and with Davis, our founding engineer, who spent years building financial planning simulation software before this. You'd also meet the people using what you build. We're on calls with advisors every week, and what they tell us lands in the product in days, not quarters.

It's also a lot of work. Four people are building something advisors use with real clients, and every one of us has something on the line. Everyone here works hard, founders included, and we hold each other to a high bar. If that's the team you want to be on, we should talk.

**Comp**

You pick where you sit on the range, more cash and less equity or the other way around. It's below market. What you get instead is a real piece of the company, a surface you own outright, and a say in what gets built. Neither founder has taken a salary yet, so it's the same bet we're making.

**How we hire**

We read every application. If it looks like a fit, you'll have a short call with me or my co-founder about how we work. Then a working session with Davis on a real problem, no whiteboard algorithms. If that goes well, we make an offer.

**To apply**

Skip the cover letter. Start your message with one sentence on the last thing you shipped that you're proud of, and why it was hard. Then tell us what you'd want to own here.

**Skip the line**

Want to jump in front of all the other applications? Send a GitHub link to something you built that shows your skills and the quality of what you ship. If you don't have any public projects, send a GitHub link to this one: create a simulation engine where you simulate buying and selling real estate over a period of time, and include some form of visualization. It's intentionally vague, so show us some creativity.

title: Tech Lead, Machine Learning: Element Classification
description:
**About Teleskope**

Teleskope is redefining data security for the AI era with the only dedicated platform that combines precise visibility with automated remediation. Teleskope continuously scans, catalogs and classifies data in-motion and at-rest while automating policy-based actions, helping organizations proactively manage data sprawl while securely enabling AI adoption.

Following our $25 million Series A round, Teleskope is entering a high-growth phase backed by top-tier investors and exceptional product-market fit.

**About the role**

We're hiring a **Tech Lead** to own the technical direction of our element classification system, the engine that powers every customer workflow on the platform. You'll lead the engineers and data scientists building entity classification across text, documents, relational data, and OCR. You'll set the roadmap, decide where the pipeline needs to improve, and make sure our methods stay at the state of the art.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll split your time between setting direction for the team and doing the hardest technical work yourself. You'll report to the Director of Data Science and ML and work closely with annotation, QC, engineering, and product.

This is a hybrid **role requiring 3+ days in-office in New York City**.

**What You'll Do**:

- Own the element classification roadmap: set priorities, sequence the work, and align the team and stakeholders on tradeoffs.
- Lead the team's technical work: break large problems into scoped projects, assign and unblock work, review designs and code, and hold a high bar for quality.
- Own evaluation strategy: build benchmarks, regression suites, and production monitoring that show where the pipeline is failing and why, so the team focuses on the gaps that matter.
- Track new work in NLP, LLMs, and information extraction, and decide what to adopt. Run focused experiments and take the winners to production.
- Set the standard for data quality: refine labeling guidelines, work with annotators and qc teams on label quality, and build training and eval sets that reflect real world problems.
- Run delivery with checkpointed milestones, and keep leadership and cross-functional partners updated on progress, risks, and decisions.
- Set engineering practices for model deployment, versioning, CI/CD, and operational monitoring.
- Mentor and grow the team, and help with hiring as the team scales.

**About you:**

- 6+ years building and deploying ML systems in production, including 1+ year as a tech lead or in a similar role guiding the technical work of others.
- Deep experience with NLP, especially NER, entity classification, or information extraction.
- Strong instincts for evaluation: you can build test sets that predict real-world performance and diagnose failures from metrics.
- Hands-on experience curating datasets, including annotation guidelines, label quality control, and synthetic or weakly supervised data.
- Up to date on current methods (LLMs, distillation, efficient inference) and able to judge them critically.
- Still writes production code: comfortable taking work from research prototype to CI/CD and production pipelines in Python with modern ML tooling.
- Turns ambiguity into a plan the team can execute, and communicates progress honestly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Leads through influence and makes the people around you better.

**What you'll get:**

- Technical ownership of the system behind the core of our product.
- A team to lead and a direct hand in shaping how ML is built at Teleskope.
- A beautiful, well-stocked office in NYC’s Financial District.
- Flexible vacation and work from home days.
- Competitive salary and meaningful equity.
- Health, vision, dental, 401k and more benefits, heavily subsidized by Teleskope.

**What We Value:**

At Teleskope, we value strong engineers who build real systems. We look for people who combine ML depth with pragmatic execution, take ownership of critical infrastructure, and ship reliable solutions that deliver real security and privacy outcomes.
