title: Sales Enablement Manager
description:
**About AirGarage**

AirGarage is on a mission to bring real estate online, starting with parking.

We replace broken parking machines, fragmented software, and manual, labor-intensive operations with a unified, data-rich operating system for parking real estate. We handle everything it takes to run and optimize a parking asset: payments, dynamic pricing, enforcement, license plate recognition, analytics, and more.

By building all of our technology in-house, we are able to deliver a magical experience for drivers while providing real-time visibility and revenue increases of 20-50% or more for real estate owners. That’s why national real‑estate leaders like Hines and Greystar, as well as technology companies like Meta, partner with AirGarage to optimize their parking facilities.

AirGarage uses datapoints like real-time occupancy, local events, weather, driver behavior, competitor pricing, and more to bring true intelligence to real estate owners’ assets for the first time.

We’re investing aggressively to make the physical world legible to a digital system: cameras, sensors, and software that generate a firehose of real-time data about the world around us. That data fuels models and algorithms that allow us to optimize performance at each property while giving owners the clarity and control they’ve never had before.

Before you can optimize an asset, you need to observe it. Before you can observe it, you need to bring it online.

We are starting with the $131 billion US parking real estate market because it is one of the most offline and mismanaged commercial real estate asset types. 26% of the land area in the median American urban core is dedicated to parking.

We are backed by top tier investors including Headline Growth, Andreessen Horowitz, Floodgate, Founders Fund, Abstract Ventures, and angel investors who have founded or worked at companies like Uber, Opendoor, Flexport, and more.  
  
Want to learn more about AirGarage and the problem we're tackling?   
  
Check out these podcasts:   
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AU0NkDK51E4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AU0NkDK51E4)  
[https://youtu.be/_8aM6NQHYiE?si=p5WIujBWUA1sG-b7](https://youtu.be/_8aM6NQHYiE?si=p5WIujBWUA1sG-b7)

## **THE ROLE 💼**

AirGarage's growth depends on how well our sales team executes - and this role is on the front lines of making that happen.

We are looking for a hands-on Sales Enablement Manager to build and run the day-to-day enablement programs that help our AEs and SDRs ramp faster, sell more effectively, and operate as a cohesive team. You will work directly with our VP of Sales to deliver onboarding, training, content, certification and tooling programs that compound rep productivity over time.

This is not a content librarian or training coordinator role. While you will own the systems and assets, the broader expectation is to own measurable improvements in ramp time, rep productivity, and sales execution.

You will partner closely with Sales Leadership, Revenue Operations, Head of Sales Development, Marketing, and Product to translate sales strategy into the programs, tools, and content that make every rep better.

If you want to build enablement programs from the ground up at a scaling sales org - and grow into a senior enablement leader as we scale - this role offers the chance to do exactly that.

You will:

- Build and run onboarding and ramp programs for new AEs and SDRs
- Operationalize sales methodology (MEDDPICC) into the day-to-day workflows of the sales team
- Create and maintain sales content: battlecards, talk tracks, objection handling, discovery libraries, ROI tools, and call libraries
- Run ongoing training programs tied to specific funnel gaps and business priorities
- Partner with Revenue Operations on Gong, sales tools, and AI capabilities that improve seller productivity
- Support frontline managers with coaching enablement, training, and program delivery
- Build readiness programs for new product launches

Over time, this role will be the foundation of AirGarage's sales execution engine - with real opportunity to grow into a senior enablement leader as the function scales.

## **What You'll Own 📊**

**1) New Hire Onboarding & Ramp**

Run the onboarding and ramp programs that get every new rep productive faster.

- Build and continuously improve AE and SDR onboarding programs with milestone-based certifications
- Deliver new hire training across product, pitch, prospecting, discovery, demo, and methodology
- Track ramp metrics by cohort and surface what's working and what isn't

Success measured by faster ramp time and stronger early productivity vs. prior cohorts.

**2) Sales Content & Playbooks**

Build and maintain the content stack that compounds rep productivity.

- Work with Product Marketing to create and own battlecards, talk tracks, objection handling, discovery question libraries, messaging, ROI tools, and call libraries
- Build playbooks for discovery, multi-threading, competitive selling, and late-stage execution
- Maintain a single source of truth for sales content that reps actually use
- Surface top-performer behavior from Gong and turn it into team-wide best practice

**3) Ongoing Training & Skill Development**

Run a calendar of training programs tied to actual business needs.

- Identify funnel gaps with RevOps and design targeted training to close them
- Run quarterly training calendars covering methodology reinforcement, skill development, and product, pricing, and packaging launches
- Deliver training in formats that stick - workshops, role plays, certifications, async modules
- Tighten the SDR → AE handoff in partnership with Sales Development leadership
- Reinforce training in the field by coaching managers on what to look for in 1:1s and pipeline reviews

Success measured by improvements in the specific funnel metrics each training is designed to move.

**4) Sales Tools, Gong & AI**

Make the sales tech stack a force multiplier, not a tax.

- Partner with RevOps on Gong, CRM workflows, LMS, and sequencing tools
- Build call libraries, scorecards, and Gong workflows that reinforce methodology and best practices
- Identify and pilot AI tools - call analysis, deal-risk scoring, automated coaching, generative content - that make every rep meaningfully better
- Help administer and roll out new tools with training, certification, and adoption tracking
- Track AE utilization of tools

**5) Cross-Functional Partnership**

Act as a connective layer across GTM.

Partner closely with:

- VP of Sales on priorities, methodology rollout, and program design
- Head of Sales Development on SDR ramp, outbound playbooks, and handoff quality
- Revenue Operations on tooling, data, and instrumentation
- Marketing on messaging, references, and competitive intelligence
- Product on launches, ensuring sellers are certified before go-live
- Operations on customer handoffs, post-sale best practices, and using insights from launching and supporting customers to sharpen the sales motion

This role helps ensure GTM work turns into revenue.

## **WHO YOU ARE: 🦚**

Our ideal candidate has:

- 3-5+ years in sales enablement, sales operations, or sales productivity roles
- Hands-on experience building or running an onboarding program at a scaling sales org
- Prior selling experience as an AE or SDR
- Comfortable creating content from scratch - battlecards, playbooks, training decks, certifications
- Familiarity with MEDDPICC or a comparable sales methodology
- Working knowledge of Gong, Salesforce, LMS, sequencing tools, and emerging AI capabilities
- A self-starter who thrives in ambiguous, fast-moving environments
- Strong cross-functional instincts and a desire to grow into a senior enablement leader

## **🚨 WHY THIS ROLE MAY NOT BE FOR YOU 🚨**

- You want a head-of-function role with a team and budget on day one
- You prefer to set strategy rather than execute on programs hands-on
- You expect a fully built playbook, content library, and ramp program to operate from
- You are not comfortable with content creation, training delivery, or tool administration
- You want to focus exclusively on either AE or SDR enablement, not both
- You prefer pure project management over building durable systems
- You want to inherit a mature function rather than build the foundation

**IMPORTANT NOTE 🚨**

AirGarage is a remote-first company, but we also value in-person collaboration to strengthen trust and teamwork. Team members should expect ~6 weeks of travel per year for:

  - 2–3 full company offsites, “Remote Weeks”
  - Lending a hand to support one new location launch
  - In-person onboarding as well as supporting other onboarding sessions for new team members

The rest of the year, team members can work remotely from wherever (US time zones) they’re most comfortable as long as they are performing well in their role. Attendance at in-person events throughout the year is expected—if you’re not open to traveling ~6 weeks per year for work, our team won't be a good fit for you.

**THE UPSIDE 📈**

  - 📈 Equity: Have a stake in the business that you’re helping to build and grow.
  - 🌴 Work remotely: Live and work wherever you like! We believe in folks working where they are happiest and most productive. We currently hire teammates that are located anywhere within North America.
  - 🏥 Health insurance: We offer health insurance and currently cover 85% of the cost of medical, dental, and vision plans for the primary employee and 50% of the cost of plans for dependents.
  - 🍼 Parental Leave: We offer 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave to all parents to bond with a newly born, adopted, or fostered child. The 12 weeks can be taken as a continuous leave or intermittently over the first 18 months of the child's life.
  - 💻 Home office setup: Get a laptop + additional equipment needed to set you up for success.
  - ⛺ Time to recharge: We have an unlimited PTO policy with a minimum requirement of 10 days per year.
  - 🤑 401k: Make financial planning right for you with a 401k retirement savings program.
  - ✈️ Team Off-sites: ~2 times per year our team comes together for a full week in places like Tahoe, Charleston, San Diego, Park City, and Austin.
  - 📚 BookGarage: Our team loves to learn and grow together, so join us for our optional recurring book club.
  - 🪴Room to grow: Our team will be orders of magnitude larger within a few years; as a part of our foundational team, you'll have opportunities to grow with us.
  - 🏙️ Transform our cities: The opportunity to change the way that the world thinks about real estate use in our cities.
  - 👐 Work with a diverse team: At AirGarage, we've always been committed to building a thriving team that represents the communities we serve. Our team is currently 40% female and 30%+ from underrepresented communities.

**Note**: Employment with AirGarage is contingent upon successful completion of a background check and employment verification conducted in compliance with applicable laws. Background checks are completed only after a conditional offer of employment has been made.

*We understand that there's no such thing as a 'perfect' candidate. We're looking for someone passionate, with grit and determination, who is excited to face the challenges of a rapidly growing startup. AirGarage is the type of company where you can grow exponentially, and we encourage you to apply to us even if you don't 100% match the candidate description.*

AirGarage is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.  Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance.  We will never discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

title: Global Head of Solutions
description:
**Who we are:**

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

**Our culture:**

- We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.
- We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.
- We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible *within* your country, not borderless.

**Global Head of Solutions**

**Location: San Francisco**

**About the role:**

As Head of Solutions at Sardine, you'll own every technical team that stands between a signed contract and a customer who's actually live and successful. Just before a contract is signed, Integration Engineering works with our customers to scope the integration and then over the next several months, gets them live onto our platform. Support engineering helps keep our clients satisfied whenever any issues arise. You'll bring these teams together under one set of standards and one bar for quality, scaling an organization that's growing fast.

This is a 20-person org spanning both technical ICs and managers. You'll work alongside strong technical leads who are ready to grow into the next level of people leadership, and you'll need to be technical enough to help guide strategic decisions, team planning, and training as you coach them there. This role is as much about developing leaders as it is about the technology itself.

**What you'll be doing:**

- Own Integration and Support engineering, roughly 20 people across three functions
- Build out the playbooks, onboarding, best practices, and SLAs that will let this organization scale smoothly as it grows
- Coach and develop technical leads, helping them grow their teams and their own leadership range
- Get hands-on with scoping and contract structuring where deals need real technical judgment, not just a demo
- Partner with Sales and Account Management leadership so solutions work actively drives cross-sell, upsell, and net revenue retention
- Partner with our POC team that includes Data Scientists to help drive POCs to a success
- Bring deep product fluency so you can guide the team through scoping, delivery, and people challenges alike

**What you'll need:**

- Experience leading large technical teams (20+) in B2B SaaS, including building out the management layer beneath you
- Domain experience in financial services, fraud, risk, compliance, or banking
- Deep technical and product expertise — enough to guide strategic decisions, contribute to team planning and training, and be credible on integration complexity and scoping
- A track record of building operational rigor — playbooks, SLAs, structured processes — as organizations scale
- Experience scaling a team through a period of rapid growth
- Strong coaching instincts — you can take a talented, fast-rising leader and help them grow
- Comfort leading through growth and change, joining a team that's evolving quickly

**Bonus Points:**

- Experience spanning both pre-sales (sales engineering/solutions consulting) and post-sales (implementation/professional services) motions
- Familiarity with fintech more broadly, even outside fraud/compliance specifically

**Benefits we offer:**

- Generous compensation in cash and equity
- Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested
- Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture
- Flexible paid time off and Year-end break
- Health insurance, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents - *US and Canada specific*
- 4% matching in 401k / RRSP - *US and Canada specific*
- MacBook Pro delivered to your door
- One-time stipend to set up a home office — desk, chair, screen, etc.
- Monthly meal stipend
- Monthly social meet-up stipend
- Annual health and wellness stipend
- Annual Learning stipend

Join a fast-growing company with world-class professionals from around the world. If you are seeking a meaningful career, you found the right place, and we would love to hear from you.

*To learn more about how we process your personal information and your rights in regards to your personal information as an applicant and Sardine employee, please visit our* [*Applicant and Worker Privacy Notice*](https://www.sardine.ai/applicant-and-worker-privacy-notice)*.*

title: Sr. Sales Engineer (Forward Deployed Engineer - Pre Sales)
description:
**_About Monte Carlo_**

Monte Carlo is the agent trust platform that unifies data and agent observability to monitor, troubleshoot, and improve production AI systems. As enterprises prepare to deploy thousands of agents across business-critical use cases, Monte Carlo provides the reliability infrastructure to support them along this AI transformation, from human-guided agents to fully autonomous operations. Founded in 2019 and backed by leading investors, Monte Carlo empowers data and AI teams to ship trusted AI at scale. Learn more at [_montecarlo.ai_](https://montecarlo.ai)

## The Opportunity

The largest US enterprises are deploying agents into production right now — and discovering that trust, reliability, and observability are the difference between a pilot and a platform.

We're looking for a sales engineer who has lived that reality and can help our strategic customers navigate it. You'll own the technical win inside strategic US accounts, partnered directly with Account Executives, and working fully remote.

## What You'll Do

- **Run technical sales cycles end to end.** Own discovery, solution design, demos, POV execution, and technical close for opportunities within strategic US enterprises. Partner with Account Executives on commercial strategy; drive the technical win independently.
- **Sell into the agentic stack.** Our customers are deploying agents on Databricks, Snowflake, and their own platforms. You'll help them understand how to observe, trust, and improve those systems — from the data pipelines feeding agents, to the context they retrieve, the decisions they make, and the outputs they produce.
- **Drive POVs that convert.** Design proofs of value with agreed success criteria, manage the evaluation, and deliver results that remove technical objections and accelerate the commercial close.
- **Build technical champions.** Identify and develop the advocates inside each account who will carry Monte Carlo into the next budget cycle, platform decision, or executive review. Run briefings, workshops, and architecture reviews that position our platform as infrastructure.
- **Bring a technical point of view.** Understand each customer's data and AI architecture deeply — where agents run, how they're instrumented, and where reliability breaks down. Bring that perspective to every account plan and QBR.

## What We're Looking For

- **Hands-on experience with enterprise AI and agent deployments.** You've deployed agents in enterprise organizations — or worked closely enough with teams that do to understand the architecture, the failure modes, and the operational reality. You know what it takes to get an agent from demo to production.
- **Fluency in AI observability concepts.** Traces, spans, evaluations, instrumentation — these are working vocabulary, not buzzwords. Experience with OpenTelemetry is highly prized, as is exposure to Databricks Genie, Snowflake Cortex, or similar enterprise AI platforms.
- **3+ years in pre-sales, solutions engineering, or strategic technical account management** within B2B AI-first companies and SaaS organizations, with meaningful experience in enterprise accounts. You've navigated procurement, infosec reviews, and multi-stakeholder buying committees.
- **Domain background in data, observability, agent trust, or agent-first products.** You've worked in one of these, not next to one.
- **Equal parts technical and business focused.** You can whiteboard an agent architecture and hold a conversation with a VP of Data & AI about ROI and competitive positioning. Credible with engineers, effective with executives.
- **Self-directed and accountable.** A lean team with high-value accounts. You prioritize your own time, know when to escalate, and know when to push back.
- **Strong communicator across seniority levels.** Equally comfortable in a technical deep-dive with a platform engineer and presenting a business case to a C-minus-1.

## Preferred, Not Required

- Modern data stack experience: Snowflake, Databricks, dbt, Airflow, BigQuery, or similar. Data observability or data quality experience is a plus.
- Experience growing existing enterprise accounts — expansion, upsell, or land-and-expand motions.
- Familiarity with MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, or similar sales qualification and value frameworks.
- Experience selling into enterprises across multiple countries and regulatory environments.
- Hands-on prototyping during a sales cycle.

## How We'll Measure Success

- **Technical win rate on POVs.** The POVs you run should convert. You set agreed success criteria upfront and deliver against them.
- **Technical execution against pipeline.** Every opportunity properly scoped, proven, and technically closed.
- **Revenue growth.** Closed commitments should translate into growing consumption over time, and your technical work sets that trajectory.

## This Is Not For You If

- Your background is post-sales or implementation only, without having carried a technical win inside a live deal
- You get handed qualified opportunities and run the demo, rather than owning discovery yourself
- You can't describe a real agent deployment — its architecture, how it was instrumented, or how it failed
- Your enterprise experience stops at mid-market, without procurement, infosec review, or multi-stakeholder buying committees

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
**About Payle**
Payle is building the financial infrastructure layer for the AI agent economy. Our platform enables AI agents to transact under human-defined rules: programmable spending policies, deterministic authorization, and a hash-chained append-only ledger that makes every transaction verifiable.
We are a YC applicant backed by an independently audited, production-grade authorization engine. Our engineering culture is built on three non-negotiable principles: deterministic code decides where money moves, every decision is traceable to its source, and nothing ships without tests that prove it.
We operate as a remote-first, async-first distributed team across four countries. We hire by artifact: every engineer and researcher ships a working challenge before we discuss terms.


**The Role**
We are seeking a **Senior Machine Learning Engineer** to design, build, and own the risk and trust scoring systems that underpin autonomous payment authorization. This is a foundational role: you will define how Payle evaluates risk for machine-initiated financial transactions, establish the ML infrastructure from first principles, and set the standards for model governance, explainability, and fairness that the company operates by going forward.
You will report directly to the CTO and work closely with the CEO on product strategy, regulatory alignment, and the technical roadmap for the risk and credit domains. 

**What You Will Build**
Risk Scoring Systems

1. Design and deploy real-time transaction risk scoring for AI-agent-initiated payments, with a hard latency budget of 20ms at p99
2. Build fraud detection models covering velocity anomalies, amount outliers, new-merchant risk, structuring patterns, and behavioral deviations from agent baselines
3. Develop agent trust scoring: longitudinal models that evaluate an agent's historical transaction behavior, outcome verification rate, policy adherence, and dispute history

**Feature Engineering Infrastructure**

1. Design and implement an offline/online feature store with point-in-time correctness guarantees, backed by our append-only transaction ledger
2. Build feature pipelines from raw event streams (authorization, outcomes, chargebacks, policy violations, merchant interactions) with automated freshness and consistency validation
3. Establish feature lineage, documentation standards, and automated leakage detection integrated into CI

**Model Development and Governance**

1. Train, evaluate, and deploy models starting with gradient-boosted trees (LightGBM/XGBoost) on tabular transaction data, evolving toward more complex architectures as labeled data volume supports
2. Implement SHAP-based explainability for every production decision: per-transaction factor attribution with stable, auditable output
3. Establish model versioning, registry, and staged deployment (shadow mode → canary → full production) with documented rollback procedures
4. Build drift monitoring: population stability index (PSI) tracking per feature, automated alerting on distribution shift, and scheduled retraining pipelines triggered by drift thresholds

**Credit and Underwriting Models (Future)**

1. Design behavioral underwriting models for agent-initiated credit (FundingFlex): probability of default, exposure at default, and loss given default models trained on agent transaction history
2. Build adverse action reason code generation: every credit decision must produce machine-generated, human-readable justification codes compliant with regulatory requirements
3. Implement disparate impact testing and fairness metrics (demographic parity, equalized odds) on all underwriting-adjacent models, with documented thresholds and review cadence 


**What We Look For**
**Required:**

1. 5+ years building and deploying ML systems in production, with at least 2 years on fraud detection, risk scoring, credit underwriting, or a related financial services domain
2. Strong Python with production ML frameworks: scikit-learn, LightGBM/XGBoost, pandas, NumPy
3. Deep understanding of point-in-time feature correctness, target leakage, and the failure modes of offline-online feature skew
4. Experience with model explainability (SHAP, LIME, or equivalent) and the ability to translate model outputs into business-actionable insights
5. SQL proficiency for feature extraction from transactional databases at scale
6. Experience with model versioning, A/B testing infrastructure, and staged rollout strategies
7. Master's or PhD in a quantitative field (Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Economics) or equivalent demonstrated experience

**Preferred:**

1. Experience with on-device or edge ML deployment
2. Familiarity with GDPR Article 22 (automated decision-making), ECOA/Reg B adverse action requirements, or EU AI Act risk classification
3. Experience building ML systems for payment networks, digital wallets, or BNPL platforms
4. Publications or open-source contributions in fraud detection, anomaly detection, or credit risk modeling

**What We Offer**
* **Compensation: $60,000-90,000/year** equivalent, structured as monthly payments (part-time to start, full-time at YC acceptance)
* Equity: 0.5-1.0% (4-year vesting, 1-year cliff), granted upon full-time conversion
* Ownership: You define the ML infrastructure, the model governance framework, and the evaluation standards. You are the first and senior ML voice at Payle.
* Data: A proprietary behavioral dataset every AI agent transaction with full context, outcome, and policy trace that no credit bureau, payment network, or fraud consortium has ever collected
* Impact: Your models directly gate financial transactions. Your explainability framework sets the standard for regulatory compliance. Your fairness testing establishes the company's ML ethics baseline.
* Team: A distributed, artifact-driven engineering culture. Direct access to the CEO and CTO. No layers, no bureaucracy, no meetings that could have been a Slack message.

title: YouTube Host & Content Creator
description:
# YouTube Host & Content Creator — AI, Fintech & Technology

### About Payle

Payle is building the financial infrastructure layer for the AI agent economy. Our platform enables AI agents to transact under human-defined rules through programmable spending policies, deterministic authorization, and a verifiable transaction ledger.

As AI transforms how people interact with technology, commerce, and financial services, Payle is building the infrastructure that will make autonomous transactions possible.

We are a remote-first, async-first startup operating across four countries. We are looking for creative people who want to help explain the future of AI and fintech to a global audience.

### The Role

We are looking for a **native English-speaking YouTube Host & Content Creator** to become an on-camera voice of Payle and help build our YouTube presence from the ground up.

This is an opportunity for a confident, charismatic, and creative communicator who enjoys presenting, interviewing interesting people, exploring emerging technologies, and turning complex ideas into engaging video content.

You will be responsible for developing and hosting YouTube episodes, conducting interviews and podcasts, creating educational and entertaining content, and helping viewers discover Payle and understand our product.

You will work directly with the founder and collaborate with the marketing team on content strategy, production, distribution, and channel growth.

We are looking for someone who can do more than read a script. You should be comfortable on camera, capable of leading a conversation, asking thoughtful questions, researching topics independently, and developing a recognizable presentation style.

You will help shape the channel's identity, build an audience interested in AI and technology, and turn that audience into awareness and interest in Payle.

### What You Will Own

**1. YouTube Hosting & Original Episodes**

1. Host regular YouTube episodes covering AI agents, fintech, payments, e-commerce, startups, and emerging technology.
2. Research topics and develop compelling episode concepts, narratives, and scripts.
3. Explain complex technical and financial concepts in an accessible and engaging way.
4. Develop recurring video series that give viewers a reason to return to the channel.
5. Present product explainers, demonstrations, commentary, and educational videos that introduce audiences to Payle.
6. Develop a distinctive on-camera presence and help establish the channel's personality.
7. Collaborate with the founder and marketing team on editorial priorities and upcoming episodes.

**2. Podcasts & Interviews**

1. Host podcast-style conversations with founders, AI researchers, developers, fintech executives, investors, and other relevant guests.
2. Research guests and prepare interview questions that generate insightful conversations.
3. Conduct remote interviews and, where practical, participate in in-person recordings.
4. Guide conversations naturally, ask follow-up questions, and make technical subjects accessible to a broader audience.
5. Identify interesting people and emerging companies that could become guests or content collaborators.
6. Turn longer interviews into multiple pieces of content for YouTube Shorts and other social platforms.

**3. Video Production & Content Development**

1. Participate in the complete content creation process, from topic research and preparation to recording and publication.
2. Develop video hooks, titles, episode structures, and concepts designed to attract and retain viewers.
3. Work with editors and other team members to produce polished, engaging videos.
4. Where needed, independently handle basic filming, recording, editing, and post-production.
5. Review edits and provide feedback on pacing, storytelling, visual presentation, and overall quality.
6. Repurpose long-form episodes into short-form videos, clips, highlights, and promotional content.
7. Maintain a consistent publishing schedule and contribute ideas for improving the channel.

**4. Product Discovery & Brand Awareness**

1. Create content that helps potential users understand what Payle does, who it serves, and why its technology matters.
2. Develop product demonstrations, use-case videos, explainers, and educational content.
3. Integrate Payle naturally into relevant episodes without making every video feel like a traditional advertisement.
4. Help viewers move from discovering the channel to visiting the website, exploring the SDK, or learning more about the product.
5. Work with the marketing team to align content with product launches, company milestones, and growth initiatives.
6. Identify video topics that attract relevant developers, founders, e-commerce businesses, and potential customers.

**5. YouTube Growth & Audience Development**

1. Help develop the channel's content and publishing strategy.
2. Experiment with titles, thumbnails, video formats, opening hooks, and episode lengths.
3. Monitor views, watch time, audience retention, returning viewers, and subscriber growth.
4. Identify which topics and formats generate meaningful engagement and repeat viewership.
5. Collaborate with the marketing team on distribution across LinkedIn, X, TikTok, and Instagram Reels.
6. Use performance data to improve future episodes and develop repeatable content formats.
7. Contribute to a sustainable channel that grows its audience and creates long-term value for Payle.

### What We Look For

**Required:**

1. Native English proficiency, with excellent pronunciation, fluency, and the ability to communicate naturally on camera.
2. Strong presentation skills and the confidence to host episodes, interviews, and podcast-style conversations.
3. A genuine interest in AI, technology, fintech, startups, or digital commerce.
4. Excellent communication, storytelling, research, and interviewing skills.
5. The ability to explain complex subjects in clear, engaging language.
6. Creativity, initiative, and the ability to develop original content ideas.
7. Comfort working independently in a remote-first environment.
8. Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage recording schedules and content deadlines.
9. A willingness to experiment, receive feedback, and continuously improve presentation and content quality.

**Preferred:**

1. Previous experience as a YouTube host, presenter, podcast host, journalist, interviewer, or video creator.
2. A portfolio of published videos, interviews, podcasts, or other on-camera work.
3. Familiarity with YouTube Studio, video analytics, content strategy, and audience retention.
4. Experience with video editing tools such as Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or CapCut.
5. Experience interviewing founders, technical professionals, or industry experts.
6. Familiarity with AI agents, APIs, fintech infrastructure, payments, or e-commerce.
7. Experience growing a YouTube channel or building a personal brand through video.

### The Practical Challenge — Required to Join the Team

We believe candidates should demonstrate their ability to create compelling content rather than rely exclusively on a CV.

As part of the recruitment process, candidates will be asked to complete a practical video challenge.

The challenge will include:

1. **On-camera introduction:** Record a short video introducing yourself and explaining an interesting development in AI or fintech.
2. **Product storytelling:** Prepare a short video explaining Payle's product to someone without a technical background.
3. **Interview simulation:** Demonstrate how you would interview a founder, developer, or technology executive.
4. **Content planning:** Propose three YouTube episode ideas, including titles, target audiences, and the reasoning behind each concept.
5. **Creative judgment:** Explain how you would turn a long-form episode into multiple short-form videos and promote the content across social media.

We will evaluate communication, camera presence, storytelling, research quality, creativity, and the ability to make complex topics interesting.

### What We Offer

* **Fixed compensation:** A base salary agreed according to experience, location, and working arrangements.
* **100% of eligible YouTube channel revenue:** The creator receives the agreed share of eligible revenue generated directly through YouTube monetization, subject to the terms of the compensation agreement.
* **Direct collaboration with the founder:** Participate in conversations about the product, company vision, and emerging developments in AI.
* **Creative ownership:** Help develop the channel's editorial identity, recurring series, and presentation style.
* **Remote-first flexibility:** Work remotely with an international team.
* **Long-term opportunity:** Build a channel and content library with the potential to generate recurring revenue as the audience grows.

### Working Arrangements

* **Location:** Remote
* **Hiring region:** Worldwide, subject to employment and contracting arrangements
* **Preferred time zone:** Central European Time (CET), with flexibility for interviews and guests in other time zones
* **Job type:** To be agreed based on availability and scope
* **Reporting to:** Founder & CEO, in collaboration with the marketing team
* **Primary platform:** YouTube
* **Additional distribution:** YouTube Shorts, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, and Instagram Reels

### How to Apply

Please include:

* Your CV or professional profile.
* Links to videos, interviews, podcasts, or other content in which you appear on camera.
* A short introduction video in English.
* Examples of content you have hosted, researched, or produced.
* A brief proposal for three YouTube episodes you would create for Payle.

**We are looking for an individual creator and host, not a content agency.**

title: Lead Security Engineer
description:
### About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services — operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform, with customers and pros on both sides and real money moving every day.

### About Security at LawnStarter

Security is already part of how we build — today it's owned by our Cloud & DevOps team, who've kept it solid as we've scaled. As we grow a $150M+ marketplace that processes payments, holds customer and pro data, and runs on AWS — and as AI agents let us ship faster than ever — we're ready to take security to the next level with a dedicated leader.

You'd be that person: the lead who takes security from a distributed, informal practice to a deliberate, instrumented one, and who sets the multi-year direction the org — and eventually a team — follows. You'll partner closely with the delivery teams and with Cloud & DevOps, and you'll start by doing most of the heavy lifting yourself, with the autonomy of a founding hire and the backing of an engineering org that already cares about getting this right. Part of the job is building security so it can outgrow one person: the standards, playbooks, and hiring bar you lay down now are the foundation for the team you'll grow into leading.

### The Role

You lead security at LawnStarter end-to-end: the PHP/Laravel and TypeScript/React codebase, the AWS infrastructure, the payments and customer-data flows, and the compliance posture. You set the multi-year direction, build the controls, and are the person the org looks to on every security question.

You start hands-on — security-of-one for now — with an explicit path to leading a small team within roughly 12-18 months, once the foundation is solid and the first hire makes sense. This isn't a hands-off management role: you lead by doing first. You'll collaborate heavily with the delivery teams and lean on Cloud & DevOps where it helps, but most of the heavy lifting is yours today. So you'll prioritize ruthlessly, automate hard, and pick the few things that actually reduce risk over the long list that merely looks thorough.

**What makes this role different:**

- **You lead the function.** You'll take security from a distributed, informal practice to a deliberate, instrumented one — threat models, automated scanning, incident runbooks — all bearing your design, and all built to scale past you.
- **You span every layer.** AppSec one day, AWS IAM the next, PCI scoping the day after. Breadth is the job, not a stretch.
- **You secure an AI-agent codebase.** Most new code here is authored by AI agents. Keeping that safe — at speed — is a problem most security engineers haven't faced yet.
- **You build for the team you'll grow.** You're not just solving today's problem; you're laying the standards, playbooks, and hiring bar for the security team you'll lead next.
- **You set the bar.** You're the lead security voice, and the standard for the org — and its future team — is the one you define and champion.

**Requirements**

### What You'll Own

- **Application security** — threat modeling the critical path, secure-SDLC practices, code and design review, SAST/secret-scanning/dependency-scanning in CI, and a vulnerability-management loop that actually closes findings.
- **Cloud & infrastructure security** — AWS posture (IAM, network, encryption), secrets management, EKS/Kubernetes hardening, partnering with Cloud & DevOps on the guardrails that keep misconfigurations out of production.
- **Compliance & data protection** — mapping PCI scope for payments, driving SOC 2 and LGPD readiness, vendor risk, and being the person who can confidently answer a customer or auditor security questionnaire.
- **Detection & response** — strengthening detection coverage on the critical path (Datadog, Sentry, AWS signal), an incident runbook, and the muscle to lead a response when something fires.
- **The security bar for AI-agent code** — the scans, review gates, and conventions that let agent-authored code ship fast and safely.
- **The foundation for the team you'll lead** — the standards, playbooks, and hiring bar that let security scale beyond one person.

### Problems to Solve

### Leading security across a $150M marketplace

The surface is broad — payments, customer and pro PII, three brands, a shared codebase, live AWS infra — and for now it's just you. The hard part isn't knowing what to do; it's sequencing it well when you can't do everything at once, and automating enough that one person can hold a high bar while planning for the team that comes next. How do you find the risks that matter most, burn them down first, and build in a way that a second and third engineer can pick up cleanly?

### Keeping pace with AI-agent-authored code

Most of our code is now written by AI agents, which means more code shipping faster than any human reviewer can read. Manual security review alone doesn't scale to that. How do you build automated gates, secure-coding conventions, and evals that catch real vulnerabilities at agent speed — without becoming the bottleneck the engineering org routes around?

### Maturing our compliance posture

We take payments and protect customer data with care; the next step is formalizing that into structured, audit-ready compliance (PCI scope, SOC 2, LGPD). You'll map what's in scope, decide what's worth doing now versus later, and get us audit-ready without turning the company into a checkbox factory. What's the right program that protects customers and unblocks deals?

### Becoming the trusted security voice — and building the team behind it

You'll partner with engineers across the org rather than command them. If security is seen as the thing that slows everyone down, it loses. How do you make secure the easy path, build controls people actually adopt, mentor the engineers around you, and set yourself up to hire and lead a team that carries that same standard forward?

### What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

- **Risk is mapped and the top of it is gone.** A threat model and risk register exist for the critical path, and the highest-severity risks you found are closed — with evidence, not assertions.
- **Security is in the pipeline.** SAST, secret scanning, and dependency scanning run in CI, with a review loop tuned for AI-agent code. Findings get triaged and fixed.
- **Compliance has a real baseline.** PCI scope is mapped, SOC 2 / LGPD readiness has a credible plan or a first milestone passed, and you can answer a security questionnaire with confidence.
- **We can detect and respond.** Detection coverage spans the critical path, an incident runbook is written and rehearsed, and you've established baseline MTTD/MTTR.
- **The team has a plan.** A credible multi-year security roadmap exists, along with a concrete plan and business case for the first security hire(s) — scope, level, and timing — so the org can decide when to grow the function.
- **No P1 from a known gap.** No customer- or pro-facing security incident traceable to a risk you'd identified and deprioritized without flagging it.

### Who You Are

**AI-native.** You use AI tools daily in security work — triaging findings, threat modeling, reviewing agent-authored code, drafting detections and policy. You have opinions about where AI sharpens security and where it creates new risk. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI tools or prefer to do everything by hand.

**Deep across most of the stack.** You have real, hands-on expertise in at least three of appsec, cloud, compliance, and response — not surface familiarity, but the kind of depth where you've built and owned controls in each — and the range to pick up the fourth fast. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you only want to work one narrow lane and hand off the rest.

**A builder and a leader-in-training.** You're energized by shaping a practice and leveling it up — taking it from informal to instrumented — and by setting standards that make the engineers around you better, even before you have a title that says "manager." This is unlikely to be a good fit if you only want to be heads-down with no interest in growing a function or the people on it.

**A pragmatic risk-prioritizer.** You ship the control that reduces the most risk for the least friction, and you're comfortable saying "not now" to a real-but-low risk. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you treat every finding as equally urgent or chase a perfect posture over a shippable one.

**A hands-on engineer.** You write the script, build the pipeline, configure the AWS guardrail, ship the detection. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your security experience is policy, audits, and slide decks without building the controls yourself.

**A strong collaborator.** You work shoulder-to-shoulder with delivery teams and Cloud & DevOps, bringing them along rather than throwing findings over the wall. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your instinct is to gatekeep, block, and police rather than enable.

**Payments- and marketplace-minded.** You care that real customers and pros and real money flow through this platform, and you reason about risk in those terms. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you think about security in the abstract, detached from the business it protects.

### This Role Is NOT

- **Not a specialist lane.** If you want to do only appsec, or only cloud, or only GRC, this isn't it. You'll touch all of it.
- **Not a gatekeeper seat.** Your job isn't to block releases and say no — it's to make shipping safely the easy path.
- **Not a paper-and-policy role.** Compliance is part of the job, but if you can't build the technical controls behind the policy, you'll struggle here.
- **Not a hands-off management role.** You lead by doing first: you start as an individual contributor, security-of-one, and you're explicitly hired to build and lead a small team within roughly 12-18 months — hiring, mentoring, and setting the standard they'll work to. If you want to skip straight to managing without doing the work yourself, this isn't it.
- **Not a caretaker role.** You're not inheriting a finished program to keep ticking — you're shaping and leveling up the practice, and that's the point.

**Benefits**

- **Base salary:** $80,000–$100,000 USD annually.
- **Lead security and take it to the next level.** This is the rare chance to define a company's security function, build the case for its first team, and take it forward with your fingerprints on every decision. The scope and autonomy are the draw.
- **Top-of-market cash compensation.** Paid above senior-level security engineering rates, reflecting the lead scope and the technical leadership this role expects.
- **Fully remote.** You work with a US-distributed engineering team. Deep focus and asynchronous work are how security gets done here; we trust you to run your own environment.
- **AI tooling provided.** Claude Code and the agent stack the rest of engineering uses — security included.

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Code for America believes government can work for the people, by the people, in the new digital age, and that government at all levels can and should work well for all people. For more than a decade, we’ve worked to show that with the mindful use of technology, we can break down barriers, meet community needs, and find real solutions.

Our employees build and transform government and community tools and services, making them so good they inspire change. We merge the best parts of technology, nonprofit, and government to help support the people who need it most.

With a focus on transparency and fairness, and deep empathy for partners in government and community organizations and the people that our partners serve, we’re building a movement of motivated change agents driven by meaningful results and lasting impact.

At Code for America, you contribute to exciting work while learning and developing in a supportive and flexible environment. Our compensation and benefits are holistic and thoughtfully curated to represent our employees and our mission. Help us drive real generational change that lasts.

 

Code for America is looking for a talented **Staff Software Engineer** who will help shape the technical direction of an engineering team that is contributing to high-impact government services. In this role you will drive reliable, high-quality software delivery — improving how the team builds, tests, and ships the systems that make public services more accessible and effective for the people who need them most.

The pace of change in the policy and government landscape is accelerating at the same time that technology possibilities are shifting rapidly. Together, these shifts create new windows of opportunity to develop technical solutions that make critical public services more effective for the people who need them. Staff software engineers keep delivery moving through those moments, supporting staff and holding high delivery standards so that what we ship stays reliable and effective.

#   
**About the role:** 

All Code for America software engineers are involved in every stage of our products' lifecycle, from prototyping and design to developing features in response to user feedback, to operating technical systems at scale. **Staff Software Engineers** pair hands-on engineering with leadership — guiding their team’s technical direction, demonstrating sound judgment, and enabling their fellow engineers through collaboration and mentorship. Staff Software Engineers strengthen their team's delivery practices and help other engineers on their team grow, setting a standard for technical judgment and collaboration within their project.

This role will report to the **Engineering Manager** and is expected to travel no more than **10%** of the time. 

Code for America is based in California and can employ those who reside full-time within the United States. This is a remote position.

# **In this position you will:**

- **Technical Delivery**
  - Craft new features that help users more easily navigate government services and receive a dignified experience.
  - Write automated tests and develop monitoring strategies to ensure a high level of service quality.
  - Work iteratively to ship minimal features, learn, and harden them to scale once proven
  - Contribute to design, implementation, and code review, and make technical trade-offs alongside your team, responsibly using AI-assisted development.
  - Own architecture and data-modeling decisions for significant parts of a production system, weighing tradeoffs across competing priorities — speed vs. maintainability, the familiar tool vs. the right one, ideal vs. feasible.
  - Support Engineering's culture of writing by producing quality documentation and learning materials for internal and external audiences.
- **Technical Leadership & Enablement**
  - Establish direction for technical work within your team or project, anticipating challenges, documenting decisions, and helping the team understand the *why* behind approaches, not just the *what*.
  - Collaborate with Product Managers and other cross-functional peers and adapt your approach as priorities, technology, and team needs shift — and actively help others do the same when facing major changes in direction or tooling.
  - Biasing to action when the team is stuck, committing to a path forward and revising as new information emerges.
  - Mentor engineers on sound technical judgment and engineering practice, and create conditions for them to grow into unfamiliar problem spaces through pairing, documentation, structured learning, or direct coaching.
  - Act as connective tissue within your team—guide team norms, surface dependencies early, align on shared patterns, and bring in practices that have worked well elsewhere to strengthen how your team delivers
- **Other duties as assigned**

 

# **About you:**

- 7+ years of software engineering experience, with strong expertise in system architecture, data modeling, web technologies, and API design.
- Experience working across multiple languages, frameworks, and tech stacks — or a demonstrated ability to ramp quickly into unfamiliar ones.
- Demonstrated ability to use AI coding tools judiciously, validating and refining generated code for quality, and modeling that discipline for teammates is needed for this specific role; organizationally, a curiosity about emerging AI tools and a commitment to using them responsibly and effectively
- Experience with Agile Software Development models like Scrum, XP, TDD, or BDD
- Demonstrated technical leadership in a team environment: setting direction and guiding sound decision-making in constrained or ambiguous contexts
- Experience with cloud infrastructure and IaC tooling
- Eager collaboration with peers, and in providing technical and professional mentorship
- Truly excellent written and verbal communication skills in English
- Expert understanding and experience communicating with cross-functional peers, and in translating those conversations into actionable tasks
- A deep commitment to Code for America's mission of making government services work well for the people who need them most

 

# **It’s a bonus if you have:**

- Deep expertise in one or more specific technology or domain areas relevant to Code for America's product portfolio.
- Experience with making government services better for people who need them most
- Personal or professional experience with the justice system, social safety net, or other mission relevant experience
- Experience building and integrating AI-powered features in production systems, with evaluation and monitoring.

#   
**What you’ll get -**

## **Salary:** 

Code for America’s salary bands are transparent as a part of our commitment to transparency and fairness. As part of our hiring practices, we aim to target the midpoint of the 2nd quartile of the range for all new hires.

Offer targets vary based on market / geographic location. The offer targets for this role range from **$128,945 to $157,850**, annually. Your Recruiter will discuss compensation in more detail & answer any related questions, during the initial Recruiter phone screen.

##   
**Benefits and perks:** 

This role includes a comprehensive benefits package including the following:

- **Values:**
  - Leadership and teammates who share a strong work ethic and values, and who respect and care for one another
  - A collaborative, cross-functional, hardworking, and joyful environment
- **Employee Enablement Support:** 
  - Laptop provided
  - A **one-time** $700 payment for remote environment setup; $200 stipend (in first paycheck) and up to $500 reimbursement, in accordance with our equipment policy
  - Cell phone and/or internet reimbursement of $50 per month
- **Professional Development:**
  - $500 annual (per calendar year) stipend towards professional development; prorated at time of hire
  - Up to $500 of professional development funds can be rolled over each year, up to a maximum of $1000
  - Training / guidance for staff required to utilize AI as part of their role, plus opportunities for employees to gain AI-related skills to support job and career growth
- **Retirement & 401k Plans:**
  - Employees receive a 100% employer match on the first 3% of contributions.
  - Employees with 3+ years of service receive an additional 50% match on contributions between 3% and 5%, for a maximum employer contribution of 5%
- **Medical:**
  - At least one no cost health insurance option for full-time employees for employee-only coverage
  - A minimum of 80% of the cost of dependent coverage
- **Remote Work:**
  - Code for America employees may work remotely across the US
  - Code for America employees main residence must be within the US
  - Full-time employees work 40 hours per week, Monday - Friday
  - **Collaborative working hours:** we aim to hold all **internal** meetings between 10 AM - 3 PM PT. We expect all Code for America staff to be available during these set working hours
- **Time Off:** 
  - Open personal time off (*subject to manager approval*), a minimum of 14 paid holidays, and an org-wide closure from Christmas Day through New Year's Day
  - Paid sick time; up to 96 hours annually
  - 17 weeks of paid parental and family leave
  - 3 weeks of paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

 

# **Timeline:**

From the time you are contacted by a Recruiter, you can expect a 1-2 month, or longer, hiring process. The specific hiring process and timeline goals for this role will be covered during the initial Recruiter phone screen. Code for America's standard interview process details are also available on our [careers page.](https://codeforamerica.org/jobs/#current-openings)

#   
**Equal Employment Opportunity:**  

Code for America is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, citizenship status, disability, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, medical condition or any protected category prohibited by local, state or federal laws.

#   
**Code for America Workers United:**

This position is covered by a Collective Bargaining Agreement between Code for America and Code for America Workers United, affiliated with OPEIU, Local 1010. The agreement was ratified on January 14, 2026, and is currently in effect.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
# About Clipboard

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top [_Y-Combinator company_](https://www.ycombinator.com/topcompanies/) and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

## About the role

We're looking for a Senior Product Designer to own up leveling the design of our core experiences across our worker and workplace apps.

You'll partner closely with product and engineering to define vision, build roadmaps, and solve real problems for our customers. You'll talk to customers regularly and use what you learn to form a clear point of view on how to build solutions for their needs. You'll explore multiple directions, design user flows, visuals, and interactions, build detailed prototypes to test them with customers, and iterate until what ships is polished, intuitive, and impactful.

This is an opportunity to build products in an industry that delivers real impact for our workers and workplaces and, enables better care outcomes for their patients. Beyond the features you own, you'll be working with other designers to dramatically raise the craft of everything we build. Sharper visual design, tighter interactions, more consistency across surfaces, and more care in the details throughout the experiences our customers use every day.

## **What you'll do**

- Own design for core features end to end across the worker and facility apps, from research and problem definition through specs and launch.
- Serve as the primary experience voice for your team, framing ambiguous problems clearly enough that partners can see the vision and build from it.
- Partner with PMs on planning and prioritization, using user needs and business context to decide what gets built and when.
- Set a high bar for craft and push visual and interaction quality across everything you design in our products.
- Build detailed, high-fidelity prototypes that show how an experience looks, moves, and feels.
- Design within our design system and contribute back to it, working with other designers and engineers to get new components and patterns built into the codebase.
- Talk to customers regularly to understand their problems, and use research and data to shape the experiences that solve them.
- Integrate AI throughout your process, from synthesizing research and analyzing competitors to generating concepts, writing copy, and building working prototypes.
- Take accountability for quality at every stage of a project, and above all for what ships.

## Skills you’ll need

- 5+ years of product design experience and a portfolio of shipped work that shows strong visual and interaction craft and clear end-to-end thinking.
- Experience owning a product area with little oversight, taking ambiguous problems from definition through launch and iteration.
- Deep attention to typography, layout, hierarchy, color, spacing, motion, and interaction detail.
- Fluency in Figma and AI-powered prototyping tools, with experience designing for iOS, Android, and web.
- Experience working within and contributing to a design system, including partnering with other designers and engineers to get changes built in code.
- Strong systems thinking, with the ability to design for interconnected flows and complex existing systems.
- Experience talking directly to customers, and using research and product data to inform design decisions.
- Credibility with engineering and product partners, built on clear communication and the ability to explain design rationale and influence direction.
- Clear, proactive written and verbal communication, with the ability to present work confidently and explain design rationale.
- Fluency with AI tools and a track record of using them to speed up your design work.
- Openness to feedback, with the ability to take critique, adjust, and keep work moving.

## **Nice to have**

- Experience with two-sided marketplaces, or products where both sides of a transaction depend on each other.
- Experience designing for healthcare, operations-heavy, or other high-stakes real-world domains.

###

## Location

- Preferred: San Francisco CA/Bay area
- Open to: US remote

**Quick Note on Scammers:**

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members [here](https://forms.gle/SyGaxHFbon7Hg9fW6).

description:

title: Deployment Lead, SaaS Implementation
description:
**About Economic Impact Catalyst**
We're a B2B SaaS company. Our platform, Catalyzer, is the software that government agencies, nonprofits, incubators, SBDCs, CDFIs, and economic development organizations run their small business programs on. It's used by organizations across 35+ states, supporting programs that have facilitated more than $200M in capital to underserved entrepreneurs.

**The Role**
This role reports directly to our CEO. When a deal closes, you become the client's project manager and the face of EIC. You own the rollout of Catalyzer from kickoff through go-live: building the plan, rallying our internal team around it, keeping client stakeholders engaged and on schedule, and making sure their staff go live confident on the platform.

Many of our clients are state agencies, SBDC networks, and municipal offices, so showing up matters. You'll lead in-person kickoffs, working sessions, and training, and you'll be the person on site when a client needs support. Expect to travel roughly half the time.

The right person for this seat gets a charge out of solving problems on the fly and out of meeting new people. Every deployment is a new organization, a new set of stakeholders, and a new set of wrinkles to work through. You should already have, or want to build, your own visible presence in this space: showing up at conferences, building relationships across the SBDC/CDFI/EDO world, and becoming someone clients and partners recognize and trust.

You'll start as a solo contributor with your own book of implementations. As our client base grows, this role is expected to grow into a lead position that helps shape how a future deployment team works.

**What You'll Own**
* Client-facing project management. Building and holding the deployment timeline, running kickoff, and keeping client stakeholders and internal teams aligned through launch.
* Rallying the team. Coordinating our product, technical, and client success teams across time zones so each deployment gets what it needs, when it needs it.
* On-site presence. Leading in-person kickoffs, working sessions, and go-live support for state agencies, SBDCs, and municipal offices.
* Training and enablement. Running live and virtual sessions for client staff, from program directors to frontline advisors, so they're self-sufficient at go-live.
* Data migration coordination. Working with our technical team and the client to scope, map, and validate the move from legacy systems and spreadsheets, so program history and reporting continuity carry over.
* Documentation and sign-off. Maintaining implementation records, decisions, and client approval at each milestone.
* Clean handoff to Client Success. What you deploy, our CSM team sustains. You're accountable for setting accounts up to succeed after go-live.
* Building the playbook and the brand. Helping define the processes a future deployment team will run on, while building your own reputation as a go-to voice in the economic development space.

**What We're Looking For**
* Energized by problem-solving. You like walking into a messy, half-documented situation and figuring out how to get it working.
* Genuinely energized by meeting people. New clients, new stakeholders, and a room full of program staff feel like an opportunity, not a chore.
* Mission-driven. You care about the outcome, not just the software. This work moves real capital to underserved entrepreneurs.
* Has, or wants to build, a personal brand in this space. Comfortable being the recognizable face of EIC at conferences, in client relationships, and across the SBDC/CDFI/EDO network.
* Strong project management instincts. You can hold a multi-week timeline together across internal and client stakeholders, and you keep momentum when things slip.
* A natural rallier. You bring people together and get a distributed team pulling in the same direction without needing formal authority.
* Polished, confident client presence, comfortable in the room with executives, program directors, and frontline staff alike.
* Comfort running live training for non-technical, sometimes lower-tech-fluency audiences.
* Working familiarity with data migration or system implementations — you don't have to write the scripts, but you can manage the process well.
* Comfort operating as a solo contributor from day one, with no scaffolding in place at the start.
* Strong written communication for implementation documentation and client updates.
* Public sector, grants, economic development, workforce, or nonprofit experience is a plus.
* Willingness to travel approximately 50% of the time.

title: Technical Account Manager, API Partnerships
description:
**About the role**

We're hiring a Technical Account Manager to own and grow our most strategic accounts. You’ll own the technical relationship with our API partners, from their first technical evaluation through implementation and ongoing support.

Reporting directly to the CRO, you’ll be the first dedicated post-sales professional at Shout About Us, responsible for making sure our biggest customers deploy, expand, and stay. Our ICP is founders, product teams, and engineering teams. 

This is a hands-on role. On any given day, you might join a prospect’s technical discovery call, troubleshoot an API request with a partner engineer, coordinate a fix with our engineering team, or improve a quickstart guide. You’ll also help build the documentation and processes that make each new integration easier than the last.

**Location and hours**

Remote, anywhere. Our standard working hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. US Eastern Time, including a lunch break. Occasional calls outside these hours are required for APAC partners and key implementation milestones.

**What you’ll do**

* Own a portfolio of 10-15 strategic accounts. Be the primary technical contact for API partners, keep stakeholders informed, and follow issues through to resolution.
* Support technical evaluations. Join sales calls, demonstrate API capabilities, understand the partner’s requirements, and explain how an integration would work.
* Lead partner implementations. Turn requirements into a clear integration plan, guide developers through setup and testing, and track progress through launch.
* Troubleshoot directly. Investigate requests, responses, logs, authentication issues, and integration behavior before escalating to engineering.
* Work closely with engineering. Provide clear reproduction steps, relevant evidence, and customer impact when an issue needs deeper investigation.
* Improve the developer experience. Create and maintain API guides, Postman collections, code examples, FAQs, and onboarding playbooks.
* Identify recurring friction. Share partner feedback and integration patterns that can inform product improvements.
* Lead expansion efforts. Cross-sell new features and products as a natural extension of the relationship, not a separate motion. 

**What we’re looking for**

* 4+ years in a customer-facing technical role or equivalent at an API-first or dev-tools company
* Strong practical understanding of REST APIs, HTTP, JSON, authentication, webhooks, pagination, and rate limits.
* Comfort using Postman or curl, reading logs, and writing or adapting small code examples in a language such as JavaScript or Python.
* Experience driving adoption inside complex orgs: navigating the gap between the buyer who signed and the team that deploys
* Strong follow-through. You keep track of open questions, set expectations, and make sure customers know what happens next.
* Startup experience at a company under 50 people. There's no support team behind you.
* Clear written and spoken English. You can explain the same issue to a developer and a nontechnical stakeholder.
* Owner mentality. "I'll make sure this gets done," not "I passed it to engineering."

**Why you should join**

* Own meaningful partner relationships from technical evaluation through launch and beyond.
* See the impact of your work in successful integrations and better customer experiences.
* You’ll own and drive every initiative you work on from start to finish. We fully trust you.
* Work remotely from anywhere while collaborating on a shared schedule.
* Work directly with the people selling and building the product.

**Why you shouldn't join**

* You are not comfortable working without a clear structure and playbook. 
* You need predictable hours. Most weeks are normal. Go-live weeks and APAC escalations aren't.

**Interview process**

Our process includes an introductory call, a short written exercise, a practical technical session, and a final conversation with our CEO. We’ll share the details and expected time commitment before each step.

**About Shout About Us**

Shout About Us is API-first review infrastructure for marketplaces and platforms.

Reviews are the most valuable decision signal in every transaction: which agent, which contractor, which property, which restaurant. Almost every platform that hosts those decisions rents that signal from Google, Trustpilot or Yelp. We give platforms the APIs and infrastructure to own it.

What you can build with our APIs:
* A verified first-party review engine: collection, verification, moderation and publishing under your brand
* Third-party review aggregation from Google, Yelp, Facebook and 80+ other sources
* AI review responses drafted and posted natively, without your customers leaving your platform
* Review solicitation and surveys triggered from events in your product
* Flagging, disputes, AI insight reports and competitor analysis

We’re a small team looking for someone who can make it easier for partners to understand, integrate, and succeed with our API.
