title: Fractional Head of Content + Acquisition
description:
[Techne] | Fractional contractor, output-based (not tracked by hours), with a path to full-time in-house | Remote, with regular monthly travel required for in-person work from any one of our three hubs: Boulder/Denver, Providence/Boston, or New Orleans | USD

**Focus:** Content is how people find out Beacon exists, and how they decide it's worth inviting their friends to. You own that engine — what gets made, who makes it, and whether it turns into activated circles. Paid tests, partnerships, and the invite loop still report through you, but they're in service of what the content proves is working.

**The mission**
We're building something that moves people off their phones and back into their neighborhoods. Our first version, Beacon, lets you tell the people you actually know, "I'm going to the farmers market, find me there." It only works if your friends are on it. We are starting with mothers in our pilot hub because they are the center of the local social graph. If it works there, we move to the next city.

We can build a great product and still fail if nobody's friends are using it, or if nobody outside our pilot hub ever hears what this actually is. This role exists so that doesn't happen.

**What you will own**
* Content, as the top of the funnel. Short vertical video is the acquisition channel — it's how this spreads before the invite loop ever gets a chance to. You decide what gets made, who makes it, and what it's trying to prove — not just "what's happening in town" but content built to convert a viewer into a circle. You select and brief creators, and you're accountable for view-to-join conversion, not view count.
* Circles, fed by content. The product works when existing groups — a school grade, a team, a neighborhood — move onto it. Content is now the main way you find and warm up the connectors who bring their circles in. Right now, this is ten ambassadors in our pilot hub. By February, it needs to be a playbook any city can run without us.
* The invite loop. We don't do follower counts or social proof. The only way we grow is through direct invites. You're responsible for how many people actually accept those invites, and for making sure content is feeding that flow with people who are primed to say yes. You'll work with the product lead on every screen that touches it.
* Paid acquisition, as a secondary lever. Meta and Instagram tests, mostly built on your best-performing content. This is a bridge, not the foundation. We run these against a strict cost ceiling with a "kill rule" if they don't perform.
* Partnerships, as a secondary lever. Organizations with active audiences — schools, charities, local groups. You open the door, structure the deal, and measure if their people actually show up. Content you've already made is often the thing that gets you the meeting.
* The scorecard. CAC by content piece and by creator, view-to-join conversion, and blended CAC across channels. You publish these numbers weekly. This scorecard decides where next month's money and creator hours go, and which creators get more briefs.

**Key outcomes (what success looks like)**
*You're inheriting a plan that's already in motion for September and October. Your job is to take it over and make it better. You will also have access to our copyrwriters and a small production team to execute your vision(s)*
* By December 15, 2026: A content engine that can point to specific pieces driving specific circle joins — not just views. 12 to 15 active circles in Boulder, Providence, Boston, or New Orleans with at least 40% of members accepting invites. The scorecard is live and being used for board evaluations.
* By January 31, 2027: A finished content and creator playbook for moving into a second city. We need to see at least one active circle in a new market, sourced primarily through content, where you weren't physically on the ground.
* By February 28, 2027: Content is the clear largest source of activated users, with paid and partnerships running consistently inside cost limits alongside it, all documented. You've built a solid list of local creators, ambassadors, and partners for the full launch.
* Ongoing: No "mystery" users. If we can't say where a user came from — including which piece of content — they don't count.

**Candidate profile**
* Content operator. You have built or run a content engine that grew a real audience and converted it into something — signups, members, customers, attendees. You've managed creators or made the work yourself. You know the difference between a video that gets views and one that gets people to act, and you can point to numbers that prove it. Ideally, you've done this for a product where the user brings the next user, and you know what an invite loop is and how content feeds it.
**You must also have:**
* Fluency in short vertical video as a distribution medium, either making it yourself or directing people who do. You know what makes a 20-second clip about a farmers market travel and what makes it look like an ad.
* Comfort being measured. You will be held to content-sourced circle activation, K, and cost per occasion, published weekly. If you prefer to be judged on reach and impressions, this is the wrong role.
* A record of closing. Content that shipped and converted, partnerships signed, ambassadors recruited. Not "worked on" or "supported."
* Proximity to the audience or a demonstrated ability to earn it fast. For example, you do not need to be a mother in one of our pilot hubs. You need to be someone a mother there would take a call from and then text her friends about.
* The ability to work alongside a product team and argue with them about screens. Growth in this product lives inside the invite flow, and you need to be in that conversation, not downstream of it.
* Comfort with a fractional, output-based arrangement now, with real interest in going full-time in-house as this proves out and scales.
* Dream-applicant shorthand: low-budget, culturally fluent, creator-led content that feels handmade and specific rather than produced — clever enough to stop a scroll, thoughtful enough to convert it into something real, not just views.

**What else you own**
*Everything below exists to make the content engine work — the same voice and story have to hold across every surface the content touches.*
* **Brand.** You own the brand system once the name clears trademark: identity, design direction, and how it shows up in creator content, on the site, in ads, and in the product. You brief designers and agencies; you do not need to be one.
* **Voice.** You write the voice guide and you enforce it, starting with creator briefs and ad copy. Every invite text, push notification, landing page, creator brief and ad reads like the same person wrote it, and that person is not a startup. The product's own copy sets the tone (short, plain, no engagement bait); you extend it to everything outside the app.
* **Comms.** You own what we say publicly and when: the marketing site, launch communications, press when it comes, and the cadence of what goes out on our own channels. You decide what gets said about the product before launch and you hold the line on what does not (no product name in public ahead of clearance, no donation asks ahead of fiscal sponsor confirmation).
* **Messaging.** One story about why this exists, told the same way in a piece of content, to a partner organization, to a creator, and to a funder. You write it and you keep it current as the pilots tell us what is true.

**What this role is not**
*Not the field operator.* Our current Field Operator recruits ambassadors and works circles on the ground in our pilot hub. You set his targets, give him the playbook, and read his numbers. You do not run his list. *Not the product lead.* Our current Product lead owns what the product does and how the screens work. You own how people arrive and what they see before they get there, and you are in the room for every screen that touches the invite flow. Disagreements are settled with data from the scorecard, not by title. *Not a designer or a video editor for hire.* You direct content, brand, and voice, and you can make things yourself. You are not the only person producing every asset — you're accountable for a slate of creators, not a one-person shop. *Not (yet) a full-time role.* This starts fractional and output-based. If it's working — for you and for us — the intent is to convert it to full-time in-house as the model scales past the pilot hub.

**Structure and engagement**
*Fractional independent contractor agreement, USD.* 
* Location: remote, with regular monthly travel required for in-person work from any one of our three hubs — Boulder/Denver, Providence/Boston, or New Orleans. 
* Output-based: no fixed weekly hours tracked; you're accountable to the scorecard and the key outcomes above, not a timesheet. 
* Compensation: $2,300 to $4,250 per month, paid as a monthly retainer. Performance component tied to the same milestones as key outcomes above, agreed in writing before start. No equity, token or phantom-equity compensation. All compensation approved through governance in a single decision before the engagement begins. Hub travel and field expenses covered. 
* Path to full-time: if the model is working by the Feb 28, 2027 checkpoint, this converts to a full-time in-house role, compensation renegotiated at that point.

**How to apply**
Send a note, not a cover letter, answering two things: the last time you built or ran content that got a stranger to do something specific (join, show up, sign up), and how you knew it worked. And a link to one piece of short vertical video you made or directed that you think worked, with the numbers. *Applicants who do not follow these instructions will not be considered.*

title: Head of Business Development - Logos Ecosystem
description:
**About Logos:**

Logos is building the technology and community required for a more sovereign, decentralised world.

Our technology stack spans decentralised infrastructure, communications and storage, with a focus on privacy, censorship resistance and permissionless systems. We work at the intersection of protocol development, Web3 infrastructure and ecosystem building.

We’re looking for a Head of Business Development to own and drive business development across Logos, while leading a team of two.

This isn't a traditional sales role. We're looking for someone who is deeply embedded in the Web3 infrastructure ecosystem, with a strong understanding of how decentralised networks operate and experience working with/launching privacy-focused protocols. Crucially, you'll have been through a mainnet launch and understand what it takes to build the partnerships, ecosystem and infrastructure relationships required both in the lead-up to launch and as the network scales post-mainnet.

**The role:**

As Head of Business Development, you will lead the development and execution of strategies to grow the Logos ecosystem. You will be responsible for establishing strategic partnerships, designing and executing growth strategies and building any relevant commercial relationships.

You'll identify where Logos technology can solve real problems, build relationships with protocols and infrastructure providers, and work closely with our technical teams to turn opportunities into integrations and long-term partnerships.

You'll also manage and develop a team of two, providing direction and prioritisation while remaining highly hands-on yourself.

A core part of the role is being able to operate credibly with technical stakeholders. You don't need to be an engineer, but you should understand the technology stack well enough to have substantive conversations with protocol teams, founders and engineering leaders without relying on someone else to translate the technology for you.

**Responsibilities:**

- Develop and execute Logos’ BD and partnership strategy, building strategic relationships ahead of mainnet and driving ecosystem growth and adoption through expanded distribution channels post-launch.
- Identify the ecosystems, protocols, infrastructure providers and applications where Logos technology can deliver the greatest value and bring users and volume to Logos network
- Build a focused pipeline of high-value opportunities rather than pursuing partnerships for their own sake.
- Establish clear priorities and success metrics for BD activity, owning the performance of BD goals against budget.
- Own opportunities from initial identification through technical evaluation, negotiation, integration and ongoing relationship management.

**Build technically meaningful partnerships:**

- Develop relationships across the Web3 infrastructure ecosystem, including wallets, centralised exchanges, on/off-ramps, oracles, indexers, DeFi protocols and aggregators, multisigs and other infrastructure providers, with a particular focus on those actively engaged in the privacy ecosystem.
- Identify opportunities for integrations, deployments, ecosystem partnerships and adoption of Logos technology.
- Understand prospective partners’ technical architecture and identify how Logos can complement their technology stack through its privacy capabilities, while attracting privacy-focused applications and protocols to build on the Logos ecosystem.
- Work with technical teams on both sides to move opportunities from conversation to implementation.
- Represent Logos credibly with founders, protocol leads, ecosystem teams and technical decision-makers.

**Understand the technology:**

You should be comfortable discussing concepts such as:

- L1s, L2s and modular blockchain architectures
- P2P and decentralised networking
- Nodes, validators and network operators
- Consensus and distributed systems
- Decentralised storage and messaging
- RPC and blockchain infrastructure
- Wallet and application infrastructure
- Token and network incentive models
- Testnets, mainnets and network launches
- Privacy-preserving and censorship-resistant technologies

You don't need to write production code, but you need genuine technical curiosity and enough depth to understand what we're building, why it matters, and how it can be used by others.

**Lead the team:**

- Manage, mentor and develop an existing team of two BD contributors.
- Set priorities and ensure the team is focused on the opportunities most likely to create meaningful adoption.
- Establish a disciplined approach to pipeline management, ownership and follow-through.
- Support the team on complex partnerships and negotiations.
- Create accountability without introducing unnecessary processes or bureaucracy.
- Remain hands-on with strategically important relationships and opportunities.

**Work across Logos:**

- Partner closely with protocol, engineering, product, ecosystem and communications teams.
- Bring market and partner feedback back into the organisation to help inform product and ecosystem priorities.
- Translate technical capabilities into clear propositions for different partners and use cases.
- Help technical teams understand the commercial and strategic context behind potential integrations.
- Ensure partnerships result in tangible outcomes rather than announcements alone.

**Required skills:**

- Significant experience in Web3, blockchain or decentralised infrastructure.
- Strong understanding of the technical architecture of blockchain networks and Web3 infrastructure.
- Experience in business development, ecosystem development, strategic partnerships or a closely related role.
- Evidence of building partnerships that resulted in real integrations, adoption, users, network activity or revenue.
- Existing relationships across the Web3 infrastructure ecosystem.
- Ability to communicate effectively with highly technical stakeholders.
- Strong commercial judgement and the ability to distinguish strategically valuable opportunities from noise.
- Experience managing or mentoring a small team.
- Comfortable operating autonomously in a remote, highly technical organisation.
- A builder mentality; you enjoy taking opportunities from an initial idea through to something that actually exists.

**We'd be especially interested in people who have worked within privacy focused ecosystems in areas such as:**

- Privacy focused L1 or L2 ecosystems
- Decentralised networking projects relating to messaging, storage and or Privacy tools and applications
- Wallets
- Experience in Open-source protocols is a must

**Hiring process:**  
  
Interview with our Talent team  
Interview with Martin, Ecosystem Development Lead  
Interview with Rahul, Partnerships Manager in Ecosystem Development  
Task  
Interview with Agata, Chief Legal Officer  
Interview with Co-founders, Jarrad & Carl

*We occasionally use cognitive tests and/or personality tests to gain insight into candidates' suitability with our org. The results provide an additional data point for us when making our hiring decisions. *   
  
*The steps may change along the way if we see it makes sense to adapt the interview stages, so please consider the above as a guideline.*

**Compensation:**

The expected compensation range for this role is negotiable, dependent on how we assess your skills and experience throughout our interview process. We are happy to pay in any mix of fiat/crypto

title: Regional Head - North America
description:

title: Virtual Assistant, Founder's Office
description:
**About us**
Revolve Realty works with hostel owners, property owners and investors in student housing. We fix running hostels that aren't filling up. We convert buildings into hostels and hand them over or run them ourselves. We also bring investors together to own and operate purpose-built student accommodation.

We're a small team that is growing quickly. We're building the core team now, and the people who join at this stage will shape how this company works.

**The role**
You'll be the person who keeps the founders' days running and makes sure nothing falls through the cracks.

Honestly, the job is "anything and everything." One hour you're booking a meeting with a developer. The next you're pulling together a list of co-living operators on LinkedIn. After that you're sending invites for an investor meet or building the weekly report. If something needs doing and nobody owns it yet, it lands with you.

This role is not for someone who waits for instructions. It's for someone who sees what needs to happen and gets it done.

**What you'll own**
1. Manage the founders' calendars. Schedule, reschedule and confirm meetings.
2. Set up appointments with prospective investors, developers, co-living operators, and our vendors and contractors.
3. Send reminders and share agendas and meeting links, so every meeting actually happens.
4. Research micro-markets and turn the findings into market reports, research reports and presentations.
5. Use LinkedIn to grow our network and connect with more stakeholders across real estate, co-living and investment.
6. Put together proposals, presentations and meeting briefs.
7. Manage emails, WhatsApp and calls for the founders where needed.
8. Maintain trackers for leads, meetings and follow-ups, and chase every open item until it's closed. 
9. Follow up with leads, partners and vendors until you get an answer.

**Who we're looking for**
1. Someone hands-on. You'd rather do it now than add it to a list.
2. Someone who takes ownership. When something is on your plate, it gets closed without anyone chasing you.
3. You're organised to the point where people rely on you to remember things.
4. You write clear, professional emails and messages in English. Hindi is a must, and Marathi is a plus.
5. You're comfortable with Google Workspace, Excel or Sheets, Canva and LinkedIn. Experience with a CRM or LinkedIn Sales Navigator is a plus.
6. You can research anything online and come back with something useful, not just a pile of links.
7. You're comfortable calling people you don't know and booking time with them.
8. You can be trusted with confidential information: deal terms, investor details and numbers.
9. You have 0–2 years of experience as a VA, EA, admin, coordinator or in a similar role. Freshers who are sharp and quick will be considered.

**What you get**
1. A seat in the Founder's Office. You'll work directly with the founders and see how deals, partnerships and decisions are made.
2. Exposure to developers, operators, brokers, investors, HNIs and UHNIs.
3. A role that grows with you. People who do this well can move into operations, BD or a Chief of Staff role as we scale.
4. Fixed salary

title: Director of Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
description:
### About the Role

As Thorn’s Director of Machine Learning & AI, you will lead and build the team responsible for applying machine learning and AI to some of the most difficult technical challenges in our mission. You will shape and lead the strategy for the function, develop its people and technical leaders, and ensure ML expertise is deeply integrated into Thorn’s products, technical innovation, and broader Build strategy.

You will lead an established core of passionate ML engineers with deep technical and mission expertise, while also having the opportunity to grow the team and shape the capabilities Thorn will need next. This role requires an exceptional people leader who can earn trust, build on the strengths already present, recruit outstanding new talent, and help the team evolve as Thorn’s needs and technical opportunities change.

As a member of Build leadership, you will report to the CTO and partner closely with Engineering, Product, and other teams across the organization to align ML priorities and technical direction with Thorn’s broader strategy.

### What You’ll Do

Technical Strategy and Innovation

- Shape and lead Thorn’s Machine Learning and AI strategy in partnership with Build leadership, Product, and cross-functional stakeholders, evolving technical direction as emerging technologies, research, customer needs, and the child safety landscape change.
- Identify promising ML and AI technologies and approaches, translating research and experimentation into recommendations about where Thorn should invest, partner, build, or evolve its product and technology strategies.
- Support Thorn’s Technical Innovation Roadmap through the exploration, prototyping, de-risking, and validation of new technical capabilities to advance mission impact and inform future product strategy.
- Ensure ML systems and practices meet Thorn’s expectations for privacy, security, responsible AI, regulatory compliance, reliability, and operational excellence, including appropriate oversight of sensitive datasets, external data annotation partners, and CSAM reporting processes.
- Partner closely with the Business Development and Strategic Impact (BDSI) team to inform Thorn’s technical research roadmap and enable exploration by connecting research questions, ML expertise, emerging opportunities, and product needs.

Develop an Exceptional ML Team

- Build on the strengths of an established, highly skilled Machine Learning team while developing the people, leadership, and capabilities Thorn will need next.
- Recruit, develop, empower, and retain exceptional ML talent, maintaining a high bar for technical excellence, collaboration, curiosity, and mission alignment.
- Lead, coach, and develop technical leaders and individual contributors of various levels, creating clear ownership and meaningful opportunities for people to grow their skills and their impact.
- Earn trust through curiosity, consistency, transparency, active listening, and strong follow-through.
- Thoughtfully evolve team culture and ways of working as Thorn’s needs change, preserving the strengths already present while strengthening collaboration, adaptability, and shared ownership.
- Foster psychological safety alongside high expectations, healthy disagreement, technical excellence, continuous learning, and accountability.
- Set clear expectations and provide timely, candid feedback. Recognize strong performance and address performance concerns thoughtfully and directly.
- Build leadership capacity throughout the team, delegating ownership and decision-making to the appropriate leaders and experts.
- Partner with People & Culture on hiring, onboarding, development, performance management, and succession planning, in ways that strengthen team cohesion, uphold our values, and support a culture of excellence and care.

One Build Collaboration

- Build deep partnerships across Machine Learning, Engineering, Product, BDSI, and other teams, strengthening collaboration across the SDLC so research, experimentation, product development, and production delivery remain connected throughout the lifecycle.
- Partner closely with Engineering leadership and teams to ensure ML capabilities are designed, built, deployed, and operated as reliable, scalable, production-ready systems, with shared technical context and clear ownership.
- Partner with Build leadership and Technical Program Management to align ML priorities, dependencies, investments, and capacity with Build’s broader strategy and roadmap.
- Help shape cross-Build technical decisions by bringing ML expertise and perspective, while strengthening collaboration across disciplines and empowering the appropriate teams and technical leaders to own decisions within their areas.
- Partner with Product, Engineering, BDSI, and customer-facing teams to ensure customer and ecosystem learning informs ML priorities and continuous improvement.
- Partner across Build to strengthen shared approaches to responsible data use, privacy, security, and ML governance.

Execution and Organizational Leadership

- Establish clear priorities, expectations, and operating rhythms that help the ML team deliver predictably while maintaining space for innovation and learning.
- Ensure sustainable ML development and operational practices that appropriately balance speed, quality, reliability, cost, security, and long-term maintainability.
- Empower technical leaders and senior individual contributors to own day-to-day execution while maintaining visibility into progress, risks, dependencies, and organizational needs.
- Partner with Finance and Build leadership on responsible resource allocation, headcount planning, infrastructure investment, and budget stewardship.
- Identify organizational or technical constraints early, make clear tradeoffs, and help teams align and move forward when priorities or perspectives compete.
- Serve as a member of Build’s leadership team, contributing to Build strategy, organizational planning, emerging threat response, investment decisions, and complex problem-solving.
- Represent Thorn’s ML work externally with customers, strategic partners, funders, conferences, advisory groups, and the broader technical community as appropriate.

### What We’re Looking For

Technical Strategy and Execution

- Significant experience leading ML, AI, Data Science, or related technical teams responsible for production capabilities at meaningful scale.
- Strong technical judgment across modern ML and AI, with the ability to guide direction, evaluate tradeoffs, and translate emerging technologies and research into practical capabilities and strategic direction.
- Deep understanding of AI/ML applications, content detection technologies, and software development.
- Experience developing and operating ML capabilities with appropriate attention to reliability, evaluation, monitoring, privacy, security, and responsible AI.

Team Culture and Cross-functional Collaboration

- Proven ability to lead, develop, and strengthen high-performing technical teams, including attracting, hiring, and retaining exceptional talent.
- Experience coaching technical leaders and individual contributors, delegating ownership appropriately, setting clear expectations, and providing candid, constructive feedback.
- Ability to earn trust with an established team and thoughtfully evolve culture while fostering psychological safety, accountability, inclusion, and high expectations.
- Track record of strong collaboration with Engineering, Product, Research/BDSI, and other cross-functional partners, including moving capabilities from research and experimentation into reliable production systems.
- Skilled at navigating complex stakeholder environments, creating alignment across teams, and providing direction and coaching where needed.

Leadership

- Ability to influence, drive change, and solve complex problems calmly and strategically.
- Strong communication skills, including asking critical questions, communicating key points clearly, and representing technical work externally through partner conversations, conferences, fundraising events, or advisory forums.
- Lead with empathy, humility, honesty, clarity, and a trauma-informed approach.
- Build relationships based on trust, transparency, accountability, and follow-through.
- You have a commitment to putting the children we serve at the center of everything you do.

**Compensation and Benefits**

A reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role is **$188,000 - $302,450/year**. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to location; skill sets; experience and training; licensure, and certifications.

Our remote-first work model is structured around working from home most of the time. But, there will be times that employees are expected to travel. For example, Thorn may host company-wide gatherings, and smaller teams may hold in-person meetings and team-building events, or require attendance at specific conferences.

At Thorn, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. [Learn more about what working at Thorn can mean for you](https://www.thorn.org/careers/).

title: Senior Support Engineer - Tooling & Automation
description:
Our Build Team develops and supports the products and tools that empower our industry and law enforcement partners to combat child sexual abuse online. - You communicate clearly, efficiently, and thoughtfully with both technical and non-technical audiences. We’re a highly-distributed team, so written communication is crucial, from Slack to technical documentation to Zoom calls.
- You have experience communicating directly with external users, and bring a strong commitment to delivering an exceptional customer experience.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Replication Foundations
description:
# **Role Summary**

We’re hiring a Staff Software Engineer to join the Replication Foundations team within Temporal’s Cloud Global Services (CGS) organization.

Replication Foundations owns and evolves Temporal’s core replication stack in Temporal OSS—the distributed systems backbone behind key Temporal Cloud capabilities such as High Availability namespaces, cross-cluster and cross-region failover, and migration products that enable customers to move workloads between self-hosted Temporal and Temporal Cloud. The team also builds foundational scalability and reliability mechanisms that support Temporal at scale.

In this role, you’ll help set the technical direction for Temporal’s distributed replication systems. You’ll lead complex, correctness-critical initiatives spanning architecture, design, implementation, rollout, and operations. You’ll work across teams to evolve reliable and scalable replication capabilities that support both the open source project and Temporal Cloud.

 
# **What You'll Do**

- Set the technical direction and evolve the architecture of Temporal’s OSS replication stack, from problem definition through rollout and operational support.
- Lead the design and implementation of replication protocols that power:
- High Availability namespaces
- Cross-cluster and cross-region replication
- Migration between Temporal clusters, including cloud-to-self-hosted and cloud-to-cloud scenarios
- Drive scalability and reliability initiatives such as:
- Multi-cell namespaces
- Enabling a namespace to span multiple clusters
- Improving load distribution and handling hot spots
- Define and communicate system-level guarantees, including consistency models, ordering, idempotency, failure recovery, performance, and operational behavior.
- Identify architectural risks and opportunities, and shape the technical roadmap for replication capabilities that support current and future cloud products.
- Partner with Cloud Enablement, CGS, Product, and other engineering teams to align OSS replication foundations with customer and product needs.
- Lead design reviews, raise the quality of implementation and testing practices, mentor engineers, and provide technical guidance across the organization.
- Lead or contribute to debugging complex production issues, incident response, and follow-up improvements related to replication and core system behavior.

# **What You'll Bring**

- A track record of designing and delivering complex production distributed systems, including systems where correctness, availability, and performance are critical.
- Deep understanding of distributed systems fundamentals such as replication, partitioning, consistency, fault tolerance, durability, concurrency, and failure recovery.
- Experience defining system architecture, protocol behavior, invariants, and trade-offs in ambiguous or evolving problem spaces.
- Experience debugging complex production issues, including concurrency bugs, data inconsistencies, partial failures, and performance bottlenecks.
- Proficiency writing production-quality concurrent code in Go; experience with Java, C++, or similar systems languages is also welcome.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex designs and trade-offs to both technical and cross-functional audiences.
- Demonstrated ability to influence technical direction across teams, build alignment without direct authority, and mentor engineers.
- A thoughtful and curious approach to understanding how systems behave under load, failure, and changing workload conditions.

# **Nice to Have**

- Experience designing or maintaining replication protocols or data-plane infrastructure.
- Experience with multi-cluster or multi-region architectures, including active-active or active-passive systems.
- Familiarity with database internals, log-based replication, or event-sourced systems.
- Prior contributions to large open source projects or distributed systems infrastructure.

Temporal Technologies is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Temporal Technologies does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. We embrace and celebrate differences and diversity.

Temporal is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. If you need to request a reasonable accommodation, please let your Recruiter know so we can assist.

title: Senior Frontend QA Analyst
description:
Job Overview 
We are seeking a Senior QA Analyst to own quality assurance across the frontend-to-middleware boundary of a multi-step web onboarding workflow.  
 
This role goes beyond scripted execution — it requires the analytical depth to design exploratory test strategies, apply structured testing techniques like equivalence partitioning, and validate that the workflow's step-by-step progression and submission states behave correctly under a wide range of input conditions.  
 
The candidate will review the evidence produced by the Manual QA Tester and convert observed frontend behaviour into a validated state model/FSM, including decision forks, equivalence classes, persona-specific behaviour, and boundary conditions. 
 
The ideal candidate is comfortable triaging complex defects and driving them to resolution. 
 
Project Details 
Title: Senior QA Analyst (Frontend) - (India) 
Rate: $6/hr 
Start Date: 19th October 
Duration: 4 Weeks 
Commitment: 40 Hours per week 
Location: India (Remote) 
Job Type: Freelance (with the possibility of full time employment based on performance and project needs in all opportunity)

Responsibilities 
1.	Design and execute advanced exploratory testing to uncover issues not captured by scripted test cases, particularly around how form-level validation carries through to submission behaviour 
2.	Apply boundary testing techniques to identify edge-case failures across frontend input handling and the middleware calls that consume that data 
3.	Use equivalence partitioning to design efficient, high-coverage test cases across valid, invalid, and edge-case input classes for form and workflow fields 
4.	Validate application behavior against defined state models (e.g., step progression, enabled/disabled action states, submission and confirmation states) to confirm correct transitions under both expected and unexpected input 
5.	Lead defect triage sessions, prioritizing issues by severity, impact, and reproducibility 
6.	Partner with developers to clarify root causes and confirm fixes against original defect conditions 
7.	Mentor junior QA testers on exploratory techniques and structured test design 
8.	Contribute to test strategy documentation and coverage planning for frontend/middleware features 
9.	Formalize and maintain the onboarding FSM/state-transition model based on observed application behavior. 
10.	Identify and document decision forks, state dependencies, persona-specific variations, and boundary conditions. 
11.	Validate coverage across the representative onboarding personas and identify gaps requiring additional controlled testing. 
12.	Produce a validated frontend/state-model evidence package for handoff to the Middleware SDET workstream. 
13.	Maintain traceability between observed UI behavior, FSM states, decision forks, and supporting evidence. 

Required Qualifications
1.	Solid 3-5+ years of experience as a QA Analyst with exposure to both frontend and middleware testing 
2.	Demonstrated expertise in exploratory and boundary testing methodologies 
3.	Practical experience applying equivalence partitioning and other formal test design techniques 
4.	Familiarity with state-machine / workflow-state concepts and validating multi-step systems against expected state transitions 
5.	Strong defect triage experience, including severity/priority classification and cross-team coordination 
6.	Analytical mindset with the ability to identify non-obvious edge cases 
7.	Effective communicator capable of guiding triage discussions and mentoring peers 
8.	Experience testing complex multi-step workflows, onboarding systems, registration flows, or account-creation processes is strongly preferred. 
9.	Ability to translate observed application behavior into structured state-transition models or equivalent workflow representations. 
10.	Working familiarity with browser and network developer tools is preferred; deep protocol-level expertise is not required.

title: Manual QA Tester
description:
Job Overview 
We are looking for a detail-oriented Manual QA Tester to execute frontend test operations with precision and consistency. This role sits at the client-facing UI layer of a complex web onboarding workflow and is responsible for validating form behavior, field-level validation logic, and error handling across browsers — all while following defined test runbooks and maintaining accurate, well-documented evidence of every defect or error state encountered.  
The primary assignment is to execute structured walkthroughs across representative onboarding personas and document the observed frontend constraints that will become inputs to downstream FSM/state-model analysis and evidence set. 
 
The ideal candidate thrives on process discipline and has a sharp eye for visual and functional inconsistencies in data-entry-heavy web applications. 
 
Project Details 
Title: Manual QA Tester - (India) 
Rate: $3.5/hr 
Start Date: 19th October 
Duration: 3 Weeks 
Commitment: 40 Hours per Week 
Location: India (Remote) 
Job Type: Freelance (with the possibility of full time employment based on performance and project needs in all opportunity)

Responsibilities
 
1.	Execute test cases strictly in accordance with documented test runbooks, ensuring no steps are skipped or altered without approval 
2.	Perform cross-browser UI testing to validate layout, functionality, and boundary conditions across supported browsers and devices 
3.	Validate client-side form field rules such as character-length limits, format/pattern (regex-style) validation, and required-field enforcement across form inputs (e.g., text fields, dropdowns, radio buttons) 
4.	Verify UI state behavior driven by validation outcomes — for example, error banners appearing on malformed input, or action buttons remaining disabled until all fields pass validation 
5.	Identify, capture, and log DOM-level screenshots and error states with clear, reproducible documentation 
6.	Track and report test execution status, flagging deviations from expected runbook outcomes 
7.	Maintain organized records of test evidence (screenshots, logs, error traces) for defect tracking and audit purposes 
8.	Escalate boundary and edge-case UI failures to senior QA or development teams with sufficient supporting detail 
9.	Collaborate with QA leads to refine and update test runbooks based on recurring issues or coverage gaps 
10.	Execute structured walkthroughs across the defined onboarding personas. 
11.	Document observed UI constraints, field limits, regex/pattern behaviour, conditional states, error states, and decision points. 
12.	Consolidate findings into a structured frontend constraint dictionary and evidence set for downstream FSM validation. 
13.	Maintain traceability between each observed behaviour, persona, test step, and captured evidence. 

Required Qualifications 
 
1.	Proven experience in manual QA testing, preferably in a frontend/UI-focused environment involving multi-field forms 
2.	Demonstrated ability to strictly follow and execute structured test runbooks 
3.	Hands-on experience with cross-browser testing tools and techniques (e.g., BrowserStack, native browser dev tools) 
4.	Working knowledge of DOM structure and browser developer tools for inspecting and capturing error states 
5.	Familiarity with client-side validation concepts (field length limits, format/regex validation, conditional UI states) 
6.	Strong attention to detail and disciplined documentation habits 
7.	Basic understanding of UI/UX boundary conditions and how they manifest as defects 
8.	Good written communication skills for clear, reproducible bug reporting 
9.	Ability to produce structured evidence that can be reviewed and reused by senior QA/SDET resources.

title: Full Stack Engineer (Flutter, Mobile & Web)
description:
**About FaithOnline**
FaithOnline is building a Gospel-centered digital ecosystem for real spiritual formation, honest connection, and grounded community online. We believe technology should serve growth in Christ, not distraction or noise.

We are pre-launch and moving quickly. Our platform is iOS and Android first, built for believers who want more than a scroll. Every engineer we bring on shapes both the product and the mission. We are not filling seats. We are looking for builders who care about what they build.

**The Role**
We need a full-stack engineer who can work across the whole stack: mobile, backend, and web. You will build a real product for real users, and your work will ship quickly and carry weight.

This is not a slow corporate role with layers of process. We move quickly, learn quickly, and adjust quickly. Everyone here owns their work and runs with it. No hand-holding required.

The role starts as a contract position at about 20 hours per week. Hours and scope can grow as the platform grows.

**What You'll Work On**
* Mobile (iOS + Android)
* Build and maintain features across our Flutter app
* Turn Figma designs into polished, performant UIs with Material Design components
* Keep the app stable, fast, and crash-free
* Support App Store and Google Play build, submission, and release
* Backend and Infrastructure
* Build and maintain backend services, APIs, and data pipelines
* Work across our core stack: Supabase (auth + database), GCP (infrastructure), Redis (caching), GetStream (social feed + messaging)
* Keep us fast, reliable, and scalable as we grow, and weigh in on architecture decisions
* Web and Admin
* Build and maintain our web admin dashboard and creator publishing tools
* Write clean, maintainable code across frontend and backend
* Build the internal tooling that keeps the platform running

**Working Together**

* Partner closely with product, design, and QA
* Take part in sprint planning and ticket refinement over Slack and Jira
* Raise issues early, propose solutions, and own your work end to end

**Our Stack**
You should be comfortable across most of this, or able to get comfortable quickly:

* Mobile: Flutter (iOS + Android)
* Design: Figma, Material Design components
* Social / Messaging: GetStream
* Auth + Database: Supabase
* Infrastructure: GCP (Google Cloud Platform)
* Caching: Redis
* Content CMS: Ghost
* Analytics: Mixpanel
* Testing: BrowserStack (App Live + App Automate)
* Project Management: Jira, Confluence/Notion, Slack
* Backend: Node.js + Express + Inversify

**Who We're Looking For**
***A true generalist.** You move comfortably across mobile, backend, and web, and you can point to things you have shipped end to end. Breadth matters more to us than any single specialty.
* **Strong mobile instincts**. Flutter experience is a big plus. If you have not used it yet but you learn fast and have shipped mobile before, we are glad to teach you.
* **You build with AI tools.** Using AI to move faster and write better code is a normal part of how you work, not an afterthought.
* **Still hands-on, and want to stay that way.** This is a build role, not a manage-from-above role. The best fit is someone deep in the code who loves being there.
* **Startup-minded.** You are comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities, and you take ownership without being asked.
* **A follower of Jesus** who wants every part of life, work included, to glorify Him, and who is looking for a place where His name is welcome rather than off-limits.

**Nice to Have**
GetStream or a similar social / activity feed platform

Supabase or Firebase-style backend-as-a-service

Ghost CMS or a similar content platform

App store submissions, TestFlight, and Google Play Console

A background in faith-based, mission-driven, or community-focused products

**What Success Looks Like**
You ship quality features across iOS, Android, and web that serve users and advance the mission

You move quickly through the stack without leaving technical debt that slows the team down

You work smoothly with design, backend, QA, and product

You own your workstream and you deliver

You grow with the platform as it scales from early traction into a thriving community of believers

**A Note on Who We Are**
FaithOnline is a Gospel-centered platform built on a clear Statement of Faith. We believe in the authority of Scripture, salvation through Jesus Christ alone, and the call of the Great Commission. We are building technology in service of the Church, not in competition with it.

The engineer we hire should share this foundation. You do not have to agree with every implementation decision we make, but you should believe in what we are building and why.

"Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord." (Colossians 3:23)

**Note to applicants:**
Please submit your application here: https://jobs.deel.com/faithonline/job-details/09d493ab-8ecd-4799-ad89-b7768c7b90bd/overview

title: Product Design Intern
description:
### About Nappr

Nappr is a marketplace that offers thousands of 2 to 12-hour hotel stays to help people catch up on rest and meet the demands of their unique schedules. Our network of 6,100+ global properties enables anyone to book rooms same-day at chains like Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, Sheraton and also many boutiques for up to 75% off the overnight rate - and with all of the amenities included. This also gives hotels the ability to fill their unused capacity and generate extra revenue with convenient, hourly scheduling.

We're on a mission to provide affordable access to quality sleep for those who tend to be exhausted in the middle of a hectic day and we're looking for some who can help us with our UI/UX and anything else design-related!

### About the Role

We are looking for a talented and highly motivated Product Design Intern to help us move faster across our mobile and web products.

This is a hands-on role with meaningful responsibility. You will work on real products used by real customers, contribute to active projects, and have the opportunity to see your designs move from idea to production.

We are looking for someone with a strong design eye who can also execute quickly, communicate clearly, and reliably get work across the finish line.

### What You'll Do

* Design and iterate on user experiences across Nappr’s mobile and web products
* Create wireframes, user flows, mockups, prototypes, and production-ready UI designs
* Work primarily in Figma using and expanding our existing design system
* Improve existing screens and identify opportunities to simplify the user experience
* Translate product requirements and feedback into clear, intuitive designs
* Collaborate with product, engineering, marketing, and company leadership
* Help maintain reusable components and consistent design standards
* Support occasional landing pages, marketing assets, and other visual design needs
* Take ownership of assigned projects and deliver them on agreed-upon timelines

### What We're Looking For

* Current student, recent graduate, or early-career designer in product design, UX/UI, interaction design, graphic design, or a related field
* Strong proficiency with Figma
* Solid understanding of UX/UI fundamentals, visual hierarchy, typography, spacing, and responsive design
* A portfolio demonstrating thoughtful digital product or interface design
* Ability to take feedback, iterate quickly, and turn ambiguous ideas into polished work
* Strong attention to detail
* Excellent communication and organizational skills
* Dependability and follow-through. If you commit to a deadline, we need to be able to count on you
* Comfort working independently in a fast-paced remote startup environment

### Bonus Points

* Experience designing consumer mobile apps or marketplaces
* Experience with travel, hospitality, e-commerce, or booking products
* Familiarity with user research, usability testing, or A/B testing
* Experience collaborating directly with developers
* Motion design, illustration, or lightweight graphic-design skills
* Interest in startups and building products from the ground up

### Why Nappr?

You will receive significantly more ownership than you would in a typical design internship. You will not spend your time working on hypothetical projects or sitting on the sidelines. You will contribute to real product challenges and help shape an ambitious consumer travel product as we grow.

This is a strong opportunity for a designer who loves making things, moving quickly, and seeing their work come to life.

### How to Apply

Please submit your resume, portfolio, and a short note introducing yourself and explaining why you are interested in Nappr. Include links to relevant product, UX/UI, or Figma work.

If you are interested in joining our team and are aligned with our mission to get people some more ZzZs, please apply!

[Website here!](https://www.nappr.io?utm_content=wf_design)

title: CEO-Designate / Fractional CEO — Consumer Marketplace
description:
Join before the Series A. Help raise it. Then lead the company.

OneStopSwap is building a next-generation consumer marketplace where people can buy, sell and swap goods, with significantly lower marketplace fees and social/live-commerce capabilities planned as the platform grows.

We're looking for an accomplished CEO-Designate to join us now on a fractional basis and transition into the full-time CEO role following our planned Series A financing, targeted within approximately 6–9 months.

We don't want to raise the Series A and then start looking for our CEO.

We want our CEO already at the table.

By the time we formally approach institutional investors, we want this executive to have spent months learning the company, shaping strategy, understanding the product and helping prepare OneStopSwap for scale.

The Role Today

This is initially a fractional position, approximately 8–15 hours per week.

Existing leadership will continue managing much of the day-to-day business. Your primary pre-funding role will be strategic and investor-facing.

You'll help:

Lead fundraising strategy and participate in investor meetings
Refine our Series A story and investor positioning
Strengthen our business model and marketplace economics
Work with product and engineering on major strategic decisions
Refine launch, monetization and growth strategy
Evaluate KPIs and financial assumptions
Develop relationships with investors and strategic partners
Help identify future C-suite and senior hires
Prepare the organization for institutional funding and scale
After Series A

Following completion of a qualifying financing, the position transitions into full-time Chief Executive Officer.

You'll assume overall leadership of the company, build and manage the executive team, oversee product commercialization and growth, execute the operating plan and lead future financing.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who has been here before.

Ideally, you've built, scaled, funded or helped lead a significant B2C marketplace, e-commerce, social-commerce or live-commerce company.

Experience at or comparable to eBay, Poshmark, Depop, Whatnot, TikTok Shop or another major consumer platform would be highly relevant.

We're particularly interested in former:

Founders | CEOs | COOs | CTOs | CPOs | GMs | Senior Marketplace Executives

You should:

Have significant consumer technology or marketplace experience
Be highly fluent in product and technology
Be comfortable working directly with engineers
Understand marketplace economics and growth
Have credibility with institutional investors
Ideally have successfully raised multi-million-dollar Seed or Series A financing
Be capable of recruiting and leading a world-class executive team
Compensation

Pre-Series A: Equity compensation; no cash salary during the fractional period. Equity vesting begins from your start date.

Post-Series A in 7-9 months: Anticipated base salary of $175,000–$225,000, plus continued equity participation and performance-based incentives.

Final equity, vesting, fundraising milestones and transition terms will be negotiated with the selected candidate.

The Person We Hope to Find

Maybe you've already built your company.

Maybe you've had an exit.

Maybe you've spent years inside a major consumer technology company and don't need another traditional corporate job.

Maybe you're consulting, advising, investing or semi-retired — but you'd get excited about helping build something again if the opportunity and ownership were right.

We're looking for experience, relationships, judgment and investor credibility now — and a full-time CEO after funding.

If that sounds like you, we'd like to talk.

Fundraising
Marketplace
B2C
Startup Leadership
Product Management
Business Strategy
E-Commerce
Venture Capital
Growth Strategy
Technology Strategy
Entrepreneurship, Executive Management, Go-to-Market Strategy, Consumer Internet, Social Commerce, Business Development, and Team Building.

The product is already under development, we have an experienced technical partner in place, and we are now preparing for our first seed financing round.

title: Senior Data Platform Engineer (Graph Serving)
description:
We're looking for a senior platform engineer to build and own the graph serving layer that sits on top of our data platform. Our main source of truth lives in the data lake. The graph database is built from it and can be rebuilt from scratch at any time. You'll build the pipeline that produces the graph and keep it current as new findings land. You'll also choose the graph store it runs on and build the query layer that analysts and downstream products read it through. You'll own the EKS infrastructure the team runs on as well.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll spend at least as much time writing pipelines and the query service as running infrastructure.

What you'll own

**The graph build pipeline.** Write the Spark pipelines that build the graph from lake tables and keep it current as new findings land. Make sure evidence that ages out is actually removed from the store. The graph must always be fully rebuildable from the lake. Once the data model shows its access patterns, you'll test candidate stores against them:
* traversals across several hops, with filters at each step
* queries against nodes with very high edge counts
* how fast a full bulk rebuild runs
* how efficiently data can be deleted as it ages out
You'll run the evaluation, make the recommendation, and then operate the store.
**The query and access layer.** Design and build the service and APIs that analysts and downstream products use to read the graph. This includes API contracts, versioning, authentication and authorization, and performance.
**Query performance.** Read query plans, design indexes and fix slow queries.
**EKS infrastructure.** Crossplane compositions, Argo CD applications, deployment pipelines and monitoring.
**Design leadership.** Write down the reasons behind architecture decisions, including the graph store evaluation, and take part in design reviews.

What we need

You have run a stateful data store in production, not just used one. That means sizing, upgrades, and a restore you performed yourself.
Kubernetes in production, and infrastructure as code.
Backend service and API development in Python, Go, Java or a similar language.
Enough Spark and lake table experience (for example Iceberg, Delta Lake or Hudi) to write the pipelines that build the serving layer.
Query performance work: reading query plans, designing indexes and fixing slow queries.
Strong debugging skills in distributed systems.
Must be a US citizen.

Nice to have

Graph database experience (for example Neo4j, Amazon Neptune, JanusGraph or TigerGraph). This is a plus, not a requirement. Distributed systems and operations experience is what matters most.
Hands-on experience with EKS, Crossplane or Argo CD specifically.
Running databases on Kubernetes (StatefulSets, Operators, persistent volumes).
Building data retention and deletion processes, or working in security-sensitive or regulated environments.

What this role is not

This is not a pure site reliability role. You'll spend at least as much time writing the pipelines and the query service as running infrastructure.

What success looks like

A graph store chosen based on test results, with the reasoning written down.
A graph that rebuilds reliably from the lake and stays current as new findings land.
Evidence that ages out is removed from the store on schedule.
A fast, well-documented query layer that analysts and products rely on.
EKS infrastructure that is defined in code, observable and resilient.

Why join us

Own a core platform component from the ground up, including the choice of its main technology.
Work on real production systems at meaningful scale.
Work closely with senior engineers, researchers and product leaders.
Build systems that value correctness, performance and maintainability.
