title: Sales Manager, North America (Toronto based)
description:
Hi, I’m [Matthias](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthias-markus-834aaa16b/) and I lead Sales at Modash

I’m in a need for a killer Sales Manager to take over our North America team.

### Background & reason for hiring

Today, I run the entire sales org & everyone reports to me - meaning the headcount I manage has grown out of hand. Not only that, but we’re expected to grow at least 70% in 2027. Making it impossible for me to effectively scale the team on my own.

For our NA AEs this today means that:

- They aren’t getting the depth of coaching & 1-1 development they need
- There’s nobody to actively join meetings & support key deals
- Their calls & deals aren’t actively reviewed and given feedback on

All in all this results in slower growth & delivering inconsistent customer experiences. I’m looking for someone to take full ownership over running our NA Account Executive team - **currently 6 people & growing**. You’ll be responsible for delivering the majority of the sales team revenue, since the NA team is the biggest.

### Scope of the role & some examples

**Example 1: Coaching**

You’ll run the day-to-day people management:

- Weekly 1:1s and individual growth plans
- Reviewing deals and call recordings, giving direct & specific feedback
- Tracking each rep’s attainment and stepping in early when someone is falling behind
- Running performance improvement plans when needed - you’ll need to be comfortable with hard conversations

**Example 2: Managing team performance**

- Running pipeline reviews
- Enforcing CRM hygiene, sales process & methodology
- Weekly/monthly reporting on attainment, risks & what needs to change
- Helping reps unblock key opportunities, including joining deal reviews and approving non-standard pricing or quotes
- Escalating compensation, tooling, enablement or resources issues
- Supporting hiring via sourcing, interviewing, and assessing future team-members.

### Team structure

You'll report to me & today you’ll get 6 direct reports yourself in the Toronto area.

You'll work closely with - Audrey & Steven, who are taking care of our AE Onboarding & Enablement + Sales Ops. They own the sales systems and the ramp curriculum. You’ll own making sure that the team actually performs to the highest degree.

You’ll also work with our marketing & success leads to ensure smooth experience across the entire customer journey for all our clients.

**The tools you'll use**

- **HubSpot** → CRM and pipeline management
- **Avoma** → call recording and reviews
- **Notion** → internal knowledge base
- **Slack** → internal communication
- **Calendly** → scheduling
- Custom internal tools for quoting and reporting

**Requirements**

- You have previously managed account executives (teams of 5-10+), not someone that’s doing it for the first time.
- Proper coaching ability - you can diagnose why someone is struggling and change their behavior within a few conversations
- You’ve run a full PIPs or handled hard performance conversations - not just given given feedback.
- Strong consultative sales skills to take over/assist in any live sales conversations.
- Comfortable building momentum in a remote environment - you’ll be managing a team that’s fully remote themselves. I am moving around a lot between Europe, North America & Asia, so I won’t be constantly looking over your shoulder & I need someone I can trust to hold high expectations for the team.
- B2B SAAS background.

**Nice to haves:**

- You’ve managed a sales team through a period of rapid growth & scale.
- Startup experience.
- Familiar with e-commerce & the creator economy.

**Benefits**

**Flexible working hours -** You’ll need to work primarily Toronto/ET hours to have overlap with your team. Otherwise, nobody is watching the clock as long as we deliver results..

**70/30 compensation split** ~180k-205 CAD OTE + stock options

**Unlimited paid vacation -** Rest when you need to. We mean it.

**Personal development budget -** Courses, books, conferences. If it makes you better at this job, we'll cover it.

**Real ownership -** You’re in charge of continuing to grow a team of high achievers. No red tape. Have an idea that you want to execute? Go for it.

### And a little more about us...

Founded in 2018 by a high-school dropout and a Canadian (yes, we’re also shocked it’s going so well), Modash is building a suite of tools that help brands scale partnerships with online content creators.

2,700+ companies like Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN already use Modash to manage and scale their influencer marketing work. And we're just getting started. Over the coming decade, brand investment in creators will continue to boom, and Modash will be at the centre of it all.

Modash is here to stay. We have 8-figures in ARR across two products, a [$12M series A investment](https://techcrunch.com/2024/10/30/modash-is-flipping-the-influencer-marketing-script-by-connecting-brands-with-the-long-tail-of-creators/), and we are default alive. We are building a company that will still be here in 20 years; not rushing towards an exit.

We’re almost 100 people distributed across 20+ countries, operating with a fast, async-first culture. If you join Modash, you’ll be surrounded by people who truly want to be the greatest at their craft. People who make you better. Interesting people too, who have done everything from building solar cars, to hanging out with Metallica and Bon Jovi.

Come join us. Be great, do great things, create great memories, all while making a great impact. Do it.

title: Product Manager Intern (U.S.A Only)
description:
React.js/Next.js, Typescript, Postgres, Docker, Microservices, AI/ML
Remote | Unpaid Internship | 6 months | 15–20 hrs/week | Master’s Degree Required
THIS IS NOT A SUMMER INTERNSHIP. Immediate hire only.

Please DO NOT APPLY if you are looking for a salary or monthly stipend. This is primarily an educational opportunity.

Master’s Degree in Engineering Management, Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, QA / Testing, or a closely related technical field preferred. Official QA Certification is a plus.

**About the Role**

We are seeking a Technical Product Management Intern to help lead delivery at the squad level by owning individual epics from requirements review through QA completion, MVP scoping, and production readiness.

This is not a general PM internship. It is a highly technical, execution-focused role for someone who can work closely with engineering, QA, and project leadership to make sure an epic is completed fully according to requirements, documentation, expected behavior, and release standards.

In this role, you will lead a small squad centered around one assigned epic. You will work closely with a QA teammate and an AI/full-stack vibe coding engineer, while collaborating with the Project Manager, Scrum Master, design team, and frontend team when needed. Your job is to make sure nothing is missing before an epic moves forward, that QA is completed against spec, that MVP scope is clearly defined, and that the work is ready for staging and production release.

This role is especially well-suited for someone who enjoys product operations, technical coordination, QA alignment, release readiness, agile execution, and making sure product work actually gets finished correctly.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Own one assigned epic at a time and help drive it from requirements alignment through QA completion, MVP scoping, staging readiness, and production release.

* Lead squad-level coordination across a small delivery team consisting of a Product Manager, QA teammate, and AI/full-stack vibe coding engineer.

* Collaborate closely with the Project Manager and Scrum Master to run squad meetings, track progress, remove blockers, and keep epic execution aligned.

* Ensure all epic requirements have been fully completed according to approved documentation, frontend requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases, data limitations, and related specifications.

* Review existing documentation and verify that the frontend implementation is completed according to the documented requirements rather than authoring all documentation from scratch.

* Work with engineers who follow internal SOPs to complete any missing frontend documentation needed for execution, including user stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases, data dictionaries, frontend requirements, and related implementation details.

* Validate that frontend and backend behavior match expected product requirements, workflow logic, business rules, and QA expectations.

* Partner with QA to ensure testing is completed thoroughly against specs and that nothing important is left unresolved before release.

* Help identify gaps, contradictions, incomplete states, missing requirements, weak UX handling, or unfinished implementation details that would prevent an epic from being production-ready.

* Collaborate with design when design support is needed and collaborate with frontend when additional polish or implementation cleanup is required.

* Support release flow by helping move completed work from development to staging for final QA, then helping scope the MVP version for production release.

* Participate in general product management tasks including MVP scoping, prioritization support, epic readiness review, and delivery coordination.

* Work with the client advisory board to collect feedback on product direction, validate usability and value, and help turn advisory conversations into actionable product input.

* Support outreach and recruitment for the client advisory board, including identifying, inviting, and onboarding new advisory members through an existing internal process and SOP.

* Help engage potential clients through advisory board participation so the team can gather stronger product feedback from real target users and potential paying customers.

**Qualifications (Required)**

* Currently enrolled in or recently completed a Master’s degree program in Engineering Management, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, QA / Testing, Product Management, or a closely related technical field.

* Strong ability to understand technical requirements, system behavior, workflow logic, APIs, and data flow across full-stack products.

* Strong ability to manage work across engineering, QA, and product stakeholders and make sure deliverables are completed according to spec.

* Experience working with user stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and software requirements in a real product or technical environment.

* Strong attention to detail, follow-through, and process discipline.

* Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to coordinate across technical and non-technical team members.

* Ability to think critically about release readiness, QA completeness, failure states, missing requirements, and real-world usage scenarios.

* Comfortable operating inside Agile or Scrum-based workflows and cross-functional squad structures.

**Preferred Backgrounds**

* Technical Product Management
* QA Analyst or Test Engineering
* Technical Business Analysis
* Systems Analysis
* Full-stack or Backend Engineering exposure
* Experience working in Agile or Scrum delivery teams
* Experience coordinating work across product, engineering, QA, and design

**Nice to Have (Not Required)**

* Familiarity with UX Design, microservices, and modern web application architecture.

* Familiarity with Figma, Jira, Linear, ClickUp, or similar planning and bug-tracking tools.

* Exposure to frontend QA, UI behavior validation, and release workflows.

* Exposure to AI-assisted software delivery or collaboration with AI coding tools.

* Interest in product operations, release management, UX logic, and client feedback loops.

**What You’ll Gain**

* Real-world experience leading squad-level product execution in a technical environment.

* Direct experience working with Project Managers, Scrum Masters, engineers, QA, designers, and client advisory stakeholders.

* Hands-on exposure to epic ownership, MVP scoping, QA coordination, release readiness, and production delivery workflows.

* Practical experience operating inside a modern full-stack product development workflow involving microservices, frontend requirements, QA validation, and agile execution.

* Strong resume experience for future roles in Technical Product Management, Product Operations, Technical Program Management, Business Analysis, QA Leadership, and Engineering Management.

**Internship Details**

* Duration: 4–6 months
 
* Commitment: 15–20 hours per week

* Location: 100% remote

* Compensation: Unpaid internship

* Purpose: Intended for academic credit, thesis alignment, or professional experience

* Schedule: Flexible hours with real responsibility and ownership


This internship is designed for graduate-level candidates who want real-world experience in technical product management, squad coordination, QA alignment, epic delivery, and production readiness within a modern software development environment.

title: Software Engineer Intern
description:
Contribute to real software projects in a supported part-time internship, with the opportunity to progress to a full-time Junior Software Engineer role after three months.

**About the role**
This internship sits within Architexor’s Software & Automation practice. You will work with experienced team members on client-facing and internal applications, learning how requirements become maintainable software and how engineering decisions are communicated across a multidisciplinary studio. We expect curiosity, reliable follow-through and a willingness to ask thoughtful questions—not prior mastery of every tool in our stack.

* Implement well-scoped application features and fixes with guidance from experienced engineers
* Write clear, maintainable code in TypeScript, React, Python, C# or the agreed project stack
* Test your work, investigate defects methodically and document what you learn
* Participate in code reviews and apply feedback to improve both the code and your engineering judgment
* Clarify requirements and communicate progress, questions and blockers early
* Contribute to technical notes, setup instructions and project handover documentation
* Work responsibly with source control, development environments and shared team workflows

**What we’re looking for**
* Foundational programming ability demonstrated through coursework, personal projects, open-source work or previous experience
* Familiarity with at least one general-purpose programming language and the fundamentals of web applications
* A basic understanding of APIs, data structures, version control and debugging

By the end of three months, you can deliver appropriately scoped work with growing independence, respond constructively to review, communicate risks early and leave code and documentation that another engineer can understand.

This role begins as a part-time internship. After three months, we will review delivery quality, learning progress, communication, reliability and collaboration. Strong performance may lead to an offer for a full-time Junior Software Engineer position, subject to business needs and mutual fit.

**Compensation**
Compensation, expected weekly hours and scheduling will be discussed during the interview process and will reflect the candidate’s location and experience.

title: Growth + Product Marketing Manager
location: California; Minnesota; North Carolina; Florida; Oregon; Washington; Michigan; Georgia; Nevada; Arizona; Indiana
description:
Organization: Mizzen Education, Inc. (501(c)(3) nonprofit) 

Location: Remote. This position is open to candidates currently residing in the following states: California, Oregon, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Georgia, Washington, Florida, Nevada, Arizona, or North Carolina. We are unable to consider applicants located outside of these states at this time. While the role is remote, candidates should be comfortable working primarily within Central or Eastern Time Zone business hours to support team collaboration.
Position type: Full-time  

Work Schedule: Agreed upon; Travel required 10 – 20%  
  
About Mizzen Education
Mizzen Education is a nonprofit edtech and youth development organization building technology, resources, and experiences that empower educators and inspire young people. We believe learning should spark curiosity, cultivate joy, and help young people see what’s possible for themselves and their world. That’s why we partner with the out-of-school time field to support educators and programs that create meaningful, engaging experiences for youth every day.

About the Position   
We are looking for someone as passionate about education, technology, and community as we are and who brings experience across product marketing, growth, and user engagement.
You’ll be the one shaping how our products are positioned, launched, understood, and adopted end-to-end.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move between strategy and execution. You might be developing the go-to-market plan and positioning for a new digital product one day, examining where users are dropping out of an onboarding journey the next, and then working with a designer or copywriter to bring a campaign to life through storytelling.

This role is part of the Engagement and Educator Experiences team and works closely with all Mizzen departments and contractors, focusing on turning first-time users into successful, engaged educators, not just growing signups. 

What You’ll Do  
- Campaign Strategy + Execution: Develop and implement integrated marketing campaigns across email, web, digital advertising, social media, events, partnerships, and other channels that support product, growth, and organizational priorities, with oversight and direction from the VP of Engagement + Educator Experiences.
- Growth + Engagement Marketing: Build and optimize segmented user journeys, communications, and campaigns across acquisition, onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, and re-engagement in line with the priorities set by the VP of Engagement + Educator Experiences to grow Mizzen’s community and help users discover greater value across our products and experiences.
- Product Marketing: Partner with the product development team and VP of Engagement + Educator Experiences to co-develop positioning, messaging, audience strategies, and go-to-market plans that successfully launch and drive adoption of Mizzen’s growing portfolio of free and paid products, features, and services, both on and off the platform. 
- Marketing Operations Management: Own Mizzen’s marketing calendar, workflows, systems, and day-to-day execution while managing branding and design, communications, and advertising contractors to keep marketing moving effectively.
- Performance + Optimization: Use marketing and product data to understand performance across the user journey, identify Mizzen’s biggest opportunities for growth and engagement, and prioritize where to focus, continuously improving conversion, onboarding, product and feature adoption, engagement, retention, SEO, and campaign effectiveness.
- Partnership Collaboration: Develop marketing plans with Mizzen’s partners that expand reach, create shared value, and introduce more educators and organizations to Mizzen.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with all Mizzen Education departments to ensure marketing strategies align with organizational goals, bringing user and market insights into organizational conversations and aligning teams around campaigns, launches, and growth priorities.
 
What You Need to Succeed  
- Marketing Strategy: Proven experience in independently crafting and executing multi-channel marketing strategies, managing user journeys, driving demand, and responding to shifting priorities and timely events through targeted campaigns. 
- Product Marketing: Demonstrated experience marketing digital products, platforms, or service solutions, including product positioning, go-to-market strategy, product or feature launches, and driving adoption.
- Project Management: Strong skills in managing multiple projects, familiar with tools like Asana, MailChimp, Retool, Slack, and Canva, or similar.
Content Development: Expertise in leading content creation, including digital ads, social media, blogs, and email campaigns, with experience managing designers and writers. 
- Analytical Skills: Data-driven approach to marketing, optimizing website performance, email, SEO, and conversion rates. 
- Collaboration: Experience working across teams and with external partners to align marketing strategies with organizational goals, with the ability to give and receive feedback, refine direction collaboratively, and move shared priorities forward.
- Creative + Strategic Thinking: Ability to think creatively and strategically, focusing on community engagement, retention, and brand growth. 
- Writing + Communication Skills: Excellent writing and communication skills for various marketing and collaboration channels, including email, social media, and web content. 
- People Management: Experience in managing contractors across time zones and fostering a positive work environment. 
- Adaptability: Agile, human-centered approach with the ability to pivot strategies and maintain focus on positive outcomes.
- Ownership + Initiative: Takes initiative, follows through, and is comfortable moving projects forward in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
- Startup Experience: Marketing experience at a fast-paced, high-growth startup is a plus. 

Work Environment + Requirements:  
- Work approximately 40 hours per week.   
- Flexible, remote position. Candidates should be comfortable working primarily within CST or EST business hours to support team collaboration.
- Manage two to three contractors (i.e., graphic design, copywriter, social media, and Google Ads) and potentially additional staff in the future. 

What We Offer You:  
- A work environment that encourages curiosity, growth, and learning alongside a human-centered, collaborative, purpose-driven, and creative group of professionals dedicated to advancing high-quality learning experiences for both educators and the youth they serve. 
- The salary range for this role is $75,000 - $85,000 per year, depending on relevant experience and work history.    

Mizzen Education, Inc. offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package.   
Comprehensive health coverage
401k matching  
Discretionary time off
Company-observed holiday pay (21 days in 2026) 
Monthly work-from-home stipend  
Flexible schedule (during work hours)   

Subject to change 

A Few Things to Know About Us:  
- We work at the intersection of technology, content, and community, creating solutions for the people and organizations that make learning in out-of-school time spaces possible.
- As we continue to build new free and paid offerings, both on and off the platform, we are thinking intentionally about how each product solves real problems for educators and organizations and how those products work together to create greater value.
- We are an 11-person, mission-driven team that cares deeply about both the people we serve and the quality of what we put into the world. We work with the energy and adaptability of a start-up: building, learning, and evolving as we grow.
- We believe great products and experiences begin with listening to and understanding our community, and we use what we learn to shape what we build next.
- We are evolving beyond being known primarily for our digital learning resource and lesson plan library, building a broader ecosystem of products and experiences that help educators and organizations discover learning resources, build and share organizational planning systems, coordinate teams, and create and manage their own content.

title: Sales Development Representative - Cannabis B2B SaaS
description:
Full job description
Sales & Growth Hire — Build Pipeline, Learn the Full Sales Cycle, Help Scale CCA

If you are not comfortable spending 4–6 hours per day prospecting, calling, emailing, following up, and advancing opportunities, this role is not for you.

**ABOUT CCA**

Cannabiz Credit Association (CCA) is the B2B credit bureau and risk intelligence platform built specifically for the cannabis industry.

We aggregate real accounts-receivable and payment data from cannabis companies across the country, helping businesses understand who pays, who doesn't, and where credit risk exists before extending terms.

CCA members use the platform to run credit checks, monitor customers, identify delinquency risk, and make better credit decisions using verified industry payment data.

Our network includes hundreds of cannabis operators and many of the industry's largest MSOs. We're now focused on turning that foundation into a scalable sales engine — and this hire will help build it.

**THE ROLE**

You'll work directly with CCA's Executive Director to create pipeline, grow membership, and help build our sales organization.

In a typical week, you'll:

Prospect into hundreds of cannabis operators, brands, MSOs, and financial institutions
Make outbound calls, send emails, and consistently follow up
Work inbound, closed-lost, and self-sourced opportunities
Run first-touch discovery and qualify prospects
Book qualified demos and participate in them
Help move opportunities through the pipeline
Maintain clean, accurate CRM data and next steps
This isn't designed to remain a traditional SDR role.

You'll shadow the Executive Director on demos, progressively take ownership of discovery and follow-up calls, learn to run demos, and ultimately close business yourself.

The goal is to develop a full-cycle salesperson while building the repeatable sales processes future CCA hires will follow.

CCA Deal Readiness Check

Right Company Type | Right Person | Right History of Delinquency | Right Market | Right Stakeholders

**WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT**

Build, don't just execute. You'll help improve target lists, outbound sequences, messaging, CRM processes, and sales strategy. What works becomes part of CCA's sales playbook.

Learn to close. You'll be exposed to the full sales cycle from day one, with increasing responsibility as you prove yourself.

Sell real data. CCA demos can use a prospect's actual accounts and verified payment behavior. You'll learn to have meaningful conversations with owners, CFOs, controllers, credit managers, and AR teams.

Grow with the company. As you ramp, you can become involved in partnerships, strategic accounts, tradeshows, and broader business development. Travel is required.

**WHO YOU ARE**

You're a builder who wants ownership and growth, not simply a list of leads.

You're hungry to learn the full sales cycle and eventually close business.

You're comfortable with high outbound activity and can build rhythm around consistent calling and prospecting.

You're coachable, disciplined about follow-up, and understand that strong CRM habits are essential to building a scalable sales organization.

You can become fluent in conversations around accounts receivable, delinquency, payment terms, write-offs, and credit policy.

Experience selling data, credit, fintech, payments, financial services, or into cannabis is a plus — but not required.

**HOW YOU'LL BE MEASURED**

Touchpoints: Meaningful outbound calls, emails, LinkedIn activity, and follow-ups.

New Leads: Workable prospects sourced and added to the pipeline.

Meetings Held: Qualified discovery calls and demos that actually occur.

SQLs: Opportunities that clear the CCA Deal Readiness Check and enter the closing pipeline.

New Customers & Revenue: Ultimately, activity needs to produce new members and revenue.

The CRM is our system of record. Every active opportunity should have accurate notes, deal stage, and a clear next step.

You'll meet weekly with the Executive Director to review activity, pipeline, conversion, coaching, and blockers.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

$54,000–$80,000 OTE, including commissions and bonuses.

Monthly healthcare allowance.

Company-paid travel for required conferences, tradeshows, and business development.

**HOW TO APPLY**

If you're still reading, don't just send us a résumé.

Email Mike at mike@cannabizcredit.com with a short Loom video explaining why you want to work at CCA, why you're a strong fit, and why you believe you'd be successful building pipeline and eventually closing business.

We're looking for someone who wants to help build a sales organization — not just fill a sales seat.

Job Type: Full-time

Pay: $54,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year

Application Question(s):

Why are you interested in this role? And what relevant experience do you have that you believe would make you the best fit?
Experience:

B2B sales: 3 years (Required)
CRM software: 3 years (Required)
Willingness to travel: To tradeshows and events (Required)
Cannabis industry: 2 years (Preferred)

title: Operations Manager (Part-Time)
description:
Part-time W-2 employee | 16–24 hours/week | $45–$50/hour | Fully remote within the U.S.
# Operations Manager (Part-Time)

**Location:** Fully remote (U.S.-based)  
***Preference for candidates in the Boston/Cambridge, MA area*** who can occasionally support in-person operational needs, such as mail handling.

**Hours:** Approximately 16–24 hours/week

## About Apollo

Apollo Quantum is a small, growing technology consulting firm working at the intersection of quantum computing and government. Our highly technical team helps government clients understand and evaluate emerging technologies.

We combine the agility of a startup with the operational rigor required in government contracting. As Apollo grows, we are looking for an experienced Operations Manager to take ownership of day-to-day business operations and help us build systems that can scale with the company.

## Why This Role

This is an opportunity to have meaningful ownership without committing to a traditional full-time schedule.

You will work directly with company leadership, have visibility across nearly every part of the business, and play an important role in shaping how Apollo operates as we grow.

Rather than stepping into a large organization with established processes, you will have the opportunity to improve systems, solve operational problems, and build lightweight processes that make the company run better.

We are looking for someone who enjoys bringing order to complexity, exercises strong judgment, and wants the autonomy to make things work.

## Position Overview

The Operations Manager will serve as the operational backbone of Apollo, enabling company leadership to focus on technical, client, and strategic work.

You will own recurring business operations and coordinate administrative, people, compliance, and internal processes across the company. Some systems are already established; others will need to be improved or built as we grow.

This is a high-trust role. We are looking for someone who can recognize what needs to happen, move work forward independently, and bring leadership in when a decision or escalation is needed.

## Key Responsibilities

### Operational Execution & Systems

- Own and improve internal workflows and administrative systems
- Ensure recurring operational processes run reliably and on schedule
- Maintain calendars, trackers, documentation, and recurring workflows
- Identify inefficiencies and implement practical, lightweight improvements

### Business Operations & Coordination

- Track internal priorities, deadlines, and deliverables
- Support execution of leadership priorities and company initiatives
- Coordinate with vendors, contractors, professional service providers, and internal team members
- Follow through on operational tasks from identification through completion

### Compliance & Documentation

- Maintain organized records for contracts, compliance requirements, certifications, and internal policies
- Coordinate administrative requirements related to government contracting
- Support documentation for proposals, audits, reporting, and other compliance activities
- Help ensure recurring requirements and deadlines do not fall through the cracks

title: Head of Product
description:
**About us**

Eli Health is making continuous hormone monitoring possible so users can support their daily and long-term health. No more waiting days to track key biomarkers—get results you can use within minutes. Eli’s flagship product, Hormometer®, is the first instant hormone monitoring platform to deliver results from saliva to mobile app—anytime, anywhere.

Developed over six years of R&D, over 2,000 iterations, and backed by a dozen patent-pending innovations, Eli’s award-winning platform turns hormones into measurable signals you can track and improve. Just as the thermometer and glucometer have transformed health for millions, Eli’s platform is poised to be the next major evolution in tracking changes in stress, endurance, sleep, and more. Our ambition is to make continuous hormone monitoring as ubiquitous as smartwatches, creating a new category that transforms how people understand and support their health.

**About the role**

Eli is looking for a Head of Product with the vision, ability to originate transformative product ideas, and drive to build a category-defining consumer experience. Reporting to Eli’s co-founder/CEO, you will own product across the company, with the expectation of taking full ownership of product vision and execution within your first three months. Over the next 12–18 months, you’ll deepen engagement and retention as we scale, and lead an ambitious, innovative roadmap across AI capabilities, current and future hormones, and B2B expansion.

This role can be remote. We strongly prefer candidates who can visit our Montreal office frequently for in-person deep dives with product, design, engineering, and scientific affairs. Your primary responsibilities will be to:

- **Set the vision and invent what comes next.** Make continuous hormone monitoring compelling to a mainstream audience, with innovations beyond incremental improvements. Originate major product ideas by connecting scientific and technological possibilities with unmet customer needs. Develop product opportunities that can change Eli’s trajectory, build conviction through intuition and evidence, and lead the team to make them a reality.
- **Build lasting value.** Own product discovery, combining customer research, product data, and scientific understanding to create experiences people love, use repeatedly, and keep paying for. Define success, test assumptions, and use cohort data to grow engagement, retention, and subscription revenue as we scale.
- **Own product and rally the team.** Bring product, design, engineering, and scientific affairs together around an ambitious direction. Make hard trade-offs and drive delivery without founders supplying direction, coordination, or momentum. Own product requirements, scope decisions, release readiness, and launch coordination with marketing.
- **Turn science into a compelling experience.** Partner with scientific and medical experts to make hormone data understandable and useful, grounded in evidence.
- **Deliver today and build for what’s next.** Pair meaningful near-term improvements with a bold roadmap across AI capabilities, current and future hormones, and B2B expansion.

This description is not exhaustive. We are looking for someone who can own and grow the product function independently.

**About you**

- **You’ve owned the whole product.** You’ve independently led a consumer subscription product from vision through delivery, rallying a multidisciplinary team and driving daily momentum.
- **You have exceptional product vision and a record of invention.** You’ve invented and shipped products people loved, starting from an insight you personally originated. You can explain what you saw, how you developed it with your team, and what happened when it reached customers. You can show the bold ideas, thoughtful details, and hard choices that made the experience compelling. You bring original product judgment and think from first principles, questioning established assumptions and developing an independent view of what is possible.
- **You’ve scaled beyond early adopters.** You personally drove the product changes that grew an initial audience of thousands of users into a substantially larger customer base, operating hands-on in a small team.
- **You’ve built recurring value that improved paid retention.** You can connect customer insight to what you shipped and demonstrate sustained results across cohorts.
- **You can learn the science and own the vision.** Ideally, you’ve translated scientific or biological concepts into a consumer health product. You work closely with experts while taking responsibility for product direction and respecting scientific realities.
- **You bring relevant experience across products or markets.** Ideally, you’ve worked on products such as wearables, hardware-software technologies, or health and wellness apps with a strong behavioural component.

If you don't exactly match the description but still believe you are the right person to join the team, please reach out. We value mindset and character.

**Why you’ll love working at Eli**

- **Create a category.** Help make continuous hormone monitoring as ubiquitous as smartwatches and shape how people understand their health.
- **Have real ownership.** Take the lead on product vision and execution, with the authority to make decisions and the space to invent.
- **Build at the intersection of science and consumer experience.** Work directly with engineering, design, scientific, and medical colleagues to turn new biological capabilities into products people love.
- **Shape the company.** Join a small, diverse team of fewer than 25 people where your decisions directly influence Eli’s trajectory.
- **Work with an exceptional, mission-driven team.** Many of our team members are former founders who have tackled some of the world’s most ambitious problems, from improving cancer treatments to making electric vehicles more efficient. Now, they’re focused on improving lifelong health at Eli.
- **Work with flexibility.** Remote work is possible, with a strong preference for candidates who can visit Montreal frequently for in-person collaboration.
- **Take care of yourself.** Health insurance covering medical, dental, vision, and more, four weeks of vacation, and unlimited free Bota Bota spa access for you and a guest.

**How To Apply:**

Sounds like you? Please apply using this link:[https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/eli](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/eli). Please note that we will not review applications made through other platforms. We look forward to learning about you!

title: Product Manager
description:
## About SleekSky

SleekSky builds and runs software for clients who want to scale their technology without heavy overhead. We work in dedicated teams with a startup-inspired culture and a bias for agility, ownership, and continuous improvement. We combine professional depth with real room to learn, decide, and build things that last.

## The role

Most product roles at three to five years hand you a backlog to groom and a roadmap someone else set. This one hands you part of a live product and asks you to work out what should happen to it.

You'll own areas of a healthcare platform we build and run for a US client, with real organisations using it all day and real patients on the other end. A problem might arrive as a complaint, a number that moved for no obvious reason, or an operations team doing something by hand forty times a day. You take it all the way:

- Work out what's actually happening
- Decide whether it needs an answer, a fix, or a change worth making
- Write the requirement engineering builds from
- Stay with it while it's built
- Go back and check it did what you said it would

It's part product management, part customer engineering, and part sitting with data until it tells you something. It's wide on purpose.

## What you'll own

- **Areas of the product, end to end.** You decide what happens next in a part of a live platform, and you're answerable for whether it was worth doing.
- **The customer's problem, from complaint to diagnosis.** Our customers are large US healthcare organisations, and their problems arrive as complaints, not specifications. Working out what's actually wrong is yours before anything else happens.
- **The requirement engineering builds from.** Written down, with product decisions made and engineering decisions deliberately left open, so engineers can start without you in the room and know which questions are still yours.
- **The numbers, watched rather than reported.** Nobody sends you a dashboard each morning. Knowing what normal looks like, noticing when it stops, and finding out why before a customer tells you is part of every day.
- **The decision about what not to build.** More requests arrive than can be built. Deciding which ones don't get built, telling the person who asked, and defending the ranking is the hardest part of the job and the one that matters most.

## What you'll bring

- **3–5 years in product management**, or an adjacent role where decisions were genuinely yours: business analysis, solution engineering, customer success with real product influence, or engineering where you owned the *what* as well as the *how*.
- **Curiosity that goes past the interface.** The strongest people here go and look at the data, the logs, the actual records, and the person doing the work, rather than asking someone to explain it. This is what we screen for hardest, and it's the thing we can't teach quickly.
- **Writing other people act on:** a spec, a decision memo, an incident write-up.
- **Comfort in front of an unhappy customer**, and the instinct to find out what's actually wrong before agreeing to anything. "I don't know yet, and here's when I will" is worth more than a fast answer.
- **Enough SQL or spreadsheet fluency** to answer your own questions instead of waiting on someone else.

title: Business Development Lead
description:
Two Words is a consultancy of designers, engineers, and operators. We work with enterprises on the products and platforms their business depends on — wealth platforms, tax workflows, pharma launches, internal tools that thousands of people open every morning. Work that has to clear policy, satisfy regulation, and still feel like one good idea.

We're a team of ten across Mumbai and Manchester. Clients include BCG, EY India, Novo Nordisk, Microsoft, and a handful of others under NDA. Most of our engagements run for years, not months.
We're hiring our first dedicated business development lead.

**The role**
You'll own the front of the funnel finding the right rooms, getting us into them, and turning first conversations into engagements.
That means:

* Building a pipeline of enterprise prospects across India, the UK, and adjacent markets — financial services, pharma, professional services, regulated platforms.
* Running outbound that doesn't feel like outbound. Email, LinkedIn, events, warm intros, conference rooms.
* Qualifying inbound. We get more than we can take on; you'll decide what's worth a first call.
* Sitting in on early-stage client conversations alongside the founders, helping shape proposals and scope.
* Owning the CRM, the follow-ups, and the rhythm of the pipeline.
* Closing Discovery sprints (2–4 weeks) and helping convert them into longer Projects and Embedded engagements.

You won't be selling alone. The founders are in every meaningful conversation. You will, however, be the one keeping the engine running.

You

* 3+ years selling something complicated to enterprise buyers — services, platforms, consulting, or SaaS to large accounts. Agency or consulting BD experience is ideal but not required.
* You can hold your own with a CXO. You've sat across from heads of design, CTOs, COOs, founders, and not flinched.
* You write well. Cold emails, follow-ups, proposal language — the words matter here, and we'll notice.
* You're organised in the boring, important ways. CRM hygiene, follow-up cadence, never letting a thread go cold.
* You understand that our work is craft-led. You're not going to pitch us as "scalable" or promise "10x growth" in a deck.
* You're comfortable with ambiguity. We don't have a playbook for you to inherit — you'll help build one.

Nice to have

* A network in financial services, pharma, or enterprise tech.
* Experience selling design, engineering, or AI services specifically.
* Background in operations, finance, or a non-sales discipline before moving into BD.

## **ABOUT TAVA**

At Tava Health, we believe mental health care should be as accessible and stigma-free as a checkup. We're reimagining the entire experience: from how people find a therapist to how providers deliver care, so more individuals can get the support they need, when they need it.

We’re a fast-growing team on a bold mission: to make high-quality mental health care available to everyone. If you’re passionate about using technology to solve meaningful problems and create lasting change, we’d love to meet you.

## **ABOUT THE ROLE**

The Delegated Credentialing Specialist owns the day-to-day execution of Tava Health’s delegated credentialing program across assigned payer relationships. This role manages payer audits, compliance reporting, audit-ready credentialing files, corrective action plans, provider-data reconciliation**_,_** and credentialing operations while partnering closely with internal teams and delegated entities. The role also supports day-to-day credentialing for Nurse Practitioners and group practices.

## **WHAT YOU'LL DO** 

**Payer Delegation**

- Oversee delegated credentialing activities for an assigned payer portfolio, including readiness reviews, ongoing compliance monitoring, recurring reporting, and annual audits.
- Monitor NCQA guidance, state regulations, and other accreditation updates; assess operational impact and implement necessary compliance changes.
- Prepare for and facilitate pre-delegation and annual credentialing audits in accordance with NCQA and payer-specific requirements; develop and track corrective action plans through resolution.
- Maintain complete, audit-ready credentialing records, including primary source verification, Credentialing Committee documentation, and adverse action logs.
- Prepare recurring deliverables for delegated partners and payers, such as provider rosters, audit materials, and credentialing activity reports.
- Monitor average time to credential and support targets by identifying delays, managing follow-up, and escalating issues as needed.
- Partner with Enrollment, Partnerships, Revenue Cycle, Legal/Compliance, and other teams to maintain accurate provider data and routinely reconcile internal records against delegated payer rosters.
- Serve as a reliable point of contact for payer communications related to delegated credentialing activities, audits, provider records, and follow-up items.
- Support the implementation of new delegated credentialing agreements, including the processes and controls needed to fulfill contractual requirements.

**Credentialing Committee**

- Serve as the operational lead for Credentialing Committee meetings in consultation with the Committee Chair, owning meeting preparation, execution, and follow-through.
- Curate and Maintain accurate Credentialing Committee meeting minutes, training materials, committee records, and follow-up items.
- NP and Group Practice Credentialing
- Lead credentialing for Nurse Practitioners, including application review, primary source verification, committee readiness, payer submissions, follow-up, and status tracking.
- Support credentialing for group practice providers by coordinating documentation, resolving application gaps, monitoring timelines, and maintaining accurate provider records.

## **REQUIREMENTS** 

- 2–5 years of credentialing and enrollment experience, including at least 2 years specifically focused on delegated credentialing.
- Certified Provider Credentialing Specialist (CPCS) certification.
- Ability to manage multiple payer relationships and responsibilities with minimal oversight.
- Self-motivated team player who thrives in multi-tasking environment and can adjust priorities.
- High attention to detail, strong organization, and excellent documentation skills.
- Outstanding written and verbal communication.
- High-growth/tech-enabled healthcare background preferred; behavioral health experience is a plus.
- Familiarity with CAQH, NPDB, PECOS, state licensing resources, credentialing software, and payer rostering tools.

## **WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING AT TAVA:**

- Competitive salary and stock options (so you share in the company’s success).
- Fully-covered medical and dental premiums for you and your family, plus voluntary insurance options.
- Free, generous Tava mental health benefit — of course!
- Monthly HSA contributions for qualifying enrolled employees.
- Generous PTO and paid holidays.
- Paid parental leave.
- 401(k) retirement plan.
- Weekly company-paid lunch via DoorDash and a personal DashPass subscription.
- Opportunity to make a meaningful impact at a high-growth, mission-driven company.

These states are Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Indiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Washington.

title: Growth Marketer
description:
Growth Marketer
Hybrid
Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Apparel Manufacturing runs on spreadsheets, WhatsApp threads, and email chains from 2014. Calico is replacing all of it, and nobody in the industry knows we exist yet.
That's the job.

**The gig**
You'll be our first marketing hire. There's no team to inherit, no playbook, no brand guidelines doc, and no "how we've always done it." There's a product with real customers, two revenue lines (software licenses and production), a social media lead who'll work alongside you, and a market full of product operators who've never been marketed to well.

Your job is to get their attention and turn it into a pipeline, using whatever works. The usual B2B playbook (gated ebooks, generic LinkedIn ads, a webinar nobody attends) won't cut it here. Sourcing managers don't read that stuff. You'll have to find the thing that does.

**What we'd love to see you try**
* These are examples of the kind of thinking we meant:
* A teardown series that gets forwarded in every sourcing group chat.
* A stunt at a trade show that gets people to your booth without a free tote bag.
* A scrappy, useful tool (a cost calculator, a template, a checklist) that operators actually bookmark.
* A cold outbound sequence so specific and human that people reply just to say "how did you know that?"
* A customer story told so well that their competitor calls us.
* Something we haven't thought of. That's the real point of this list.

**What you'll own**
**Pipeline**. Outbound, content, paid, partnerships, events. All of it, from first touch to qualified conversation. Test wide, kill fast, and go deep on whatever produces real conversations with apparel brands. Impressions don't count. You'll market both revenue lines, so figure out why a brand buys a license versus placing production with us, and build the offers and funnels for each.

**The story.** What we're called, how software and production become one coherent pitch, and what problem a brand recognizes as its own within ten seconds of landing on the site. You own the website, the pricing presentation, the sales decks, and the point of view we put into the world. This industry can smell a software marketer who just found a vertical, so sound like someone who gets it.

**The audience**. Build a following of apparel operators who read us because we're useful, whether or not they're buying. Set the content direction with our social media lead, who owns the daily presence while you own the standard. Turn customers into proof, and show up where sourcing decisions actually get made.

**The machine.** We run Unify, and we expect you to use AI everywhere: research, enrichment, sequencing, content, analysis. One person with great tooling should do what used to take four. Instrument the funnel, make the data trustworthy, and report honestly by revenue line: what worked, what flopped, what you're killing, what you're doubling down on.

**The team.** Show us where more capacity creates leverage, and we'll build the function around you.

**You're probably our person if...**
You've built something. A campaign, a newsletter, a community, a side project, a growth hack that made money. Big or small, it's yours, and you can tell us what happened and what you'd do differently. Bonus points if it flopped first.
You've been the whole marketing team, or close to it, with nobody to hand work to. Ideally 5+ years in, but if you've done more with less time, show us.
You get scrappy when there's no budget. Constraints make you more creative, not less.
You'd rather own the whole funnel than perfect one slice of it.
You think in pipeline and payback. You want your name next to a revenue number.
You find the bottleneck yourself and argue from data about where the next dollar goes.
You're competitive and you don't quit. When three channels fail, you try a fourth. When the fourth fails, you try something weird.

**Probably not a fit if...**
You want a playbook and a manager to tell you what to run.
You'd rather go deep on one channel than figure out ten.
You measure success in reach, not revenue.
"That's not my job" has ever come out of your mouth.

**Bonus points**
Category creation experience. An apparel, fashion, retail, or manufacturing background (you know what a tech pack is and why line sheets cause fights). B2B experience selling into an industry that doesn't think of itself as a software buyer. Experience marketing a business where the sale isn't purely self-serve.

**Why take this**
You'll own it. First marketing hire, strategy is yours, and the team is likely yours to build.
The story is untold. The gap between how sourcing works and how it should work is enormous, and almost nobody is telling it well.
The product is real. Brands are on the platform and production is moving. You're not marketing a promise.
No layers. Small team, direct line to the founders, and a short distance between what you learn and what we build.

**How to apply**
No cover letter. In 250 words or less, tell us the most creative, scrappy thing you've ever done to get results, plus the numbers behind it. 
Then tell us how you'd get Calico in front of 10 apparel brands in the next 30 days with almost no budget.

title: Business Development Executive Intern
description:
**About the Role**
CipherSchools is an EdTech company building technology-driven learning solutions, testing platforms, and various other Learning Products for Learning Individuals. Our flagship product is a Learning Management System (LMS) that lets students watch training content, write and execute code, solve programming problems, attempt tests and assessments, compete in coding contests, and access industry-oriented sessions - alongside 2-3 other products built to support institutions, faculty, and academic programs. We are the important hands for teaching and platform services.

We're looking for a Business Development Executive / Sales Intern to drive B2B outreach to colleges and universities. This isn't a telecalling job - it's a hands-on introduction to institutional sales, where you'll learn how real B2B deals get built: identifying the right stakeholders, pitching a genuine product, and moving a lead from first call to signed partnership.

**Key Responsibilities**
* Reach out to colleges and universities to introduce CipherSchools's products and solutions
* Identify and connect with relevant decision-makers Training & Placement Officers, Deans, HODs, Faculty Coordinators, and other stakeholders
* Understand each institution's needs and map our products to their requirements
* Generate and qualify leads through outbound calling and other outreach channels
* Schedule meetings and product demos between interested colleges and our senior/business team
* Follow up consistently with prospects after initial conversations
* Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of calls, leads, follow-ups, and meetings in the CRM or tracking system
* Build and manage a pipeline of potential institutional clients
* Coordinate with the internal team for a smooth handover of qualified leads
* Conduct basic market research to identify new colleges and business opportunities

**What You'll Do**
* Own the first mile of the sales funnel - from cold outreach to a booked demo
* Learn how to position and pitch a multi-product EdTech portfolio to institutional buyers
* Work toward weekly and monthly targets for outreach, lead generation, and meetings booked
* Get direct exposure to how B2B deals move through a real sales pipeline, from lead to handover

**Requirements / Who We're Looking For**
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* Confidence speaking with college representatives, faculty, and other professionals
* Comfortable with outbound calling and sales conversations
* A proactive, target-oriented mindset
* Ability to explain products clearly and professionally
* Strong follow-up discipline and relationship-building instincts
* Ability to work independently as well as within a team
* Basic working knowledge of MS Excel / Google Sheets and CRM tools
* Pre-Placement Offer (PPO) for a full-time role, based on your performance during the internship
* We are specifically looking for someone who can handle the Tamil Nadu region, preferably someone based in Coimbatore.

title: Strategic Account Director, B2B Distribution
description:
## **About Augment:**

Supply chain is broken. Let's fix it.

We are a team of engineers, product designers, and customer champions applying the most transformative technology of our times, AI, to one of the largest industries in the world. Augie, our AI agent, now runs end to end workflows for some of the largest B2B distributors in North America.

We are looking for a **Strategic Account Director** to own and grow our most important distributor relationships.

## **About the Role:**

You own Augment's growth inside a portfolio of strategic accounts. These are distributors with more than $5B in annual revenue.

You are the executive partner to each customer's leadership team. You find the next workflow Augie should run. You build the business case. You get the pilot live with our engineers. Then you turn the pilot into recurring revenue.

This is not a traditional sales role. Distribution executives do not want a salesperson. They want an advisor who understands their business model and delivers results.

You are one of the first people in this role. You will help write the playbook for everyone who joins after you.

## **What You'll Do:**

- Own ARR expansion across your accounts against an annual growth target
- Build trusted relationships with C-suite and VP leaders in purchasing, operations, logistics, sales, and IT
- Map each customer's workflows and find where Augie creates the most value next
- Build financial models and ROI cases that your champions can defend to their CFO
- Scope pilots and lead them to production with our Solutions Engineers, Customer Success Leads, and Product team
- Run executive business reviews and working sessions, onsite and remote
- Bring customer insight back to Product and help shape the roadmap
- Document what works and turn it into a repeatable strategic-accounts playbook

## **Who You Are:**

- 5+ years in strategy consulting, investment banking, corporate development, enterprise sales, or a founder role
- A track record of owning senior client relationships and driving measurable outcomes.
- Strongly analytical; you build models, work with messy data, and turn findings into clear decisions
- A second-order thinker. You connect today's priorities to long-term account strategy.
- Comfortable in ambiguity and with a product that changes fast
- Credible with executives, personable, and easy to work with
- Willing to travel to customer sites and industry events

## **Nice to have:**

- Experience in B2B distribution, supply chain, or ERP-heavy industries
- Hands-on use of AI or LLM tools
- An MBA or equivalent experience

## **Why Join Us?**

- Competitive Salary + Stock Options
- Comprehensive Health, Vision, and Dental Benefits
- Flexible PTO
- Monthly stipend
- Direct proximity to leadership
- Accelerated path into functional leadership

We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.*

title: Customer Support Associate
description:
**About BhuMe**
70% of India's Civil Court cases are property disputes. INR 2 lakh crore of real estate is frozen yearly because nobody can verify who owns what. BhuMe is building the source of truth for this broken system.

We are a fast-growing, AI-forward land records intelligence app rated 4.8+ by thousands of users. Built by a team from IITB, IIMA, and Amazon, we operate at the messy collision point between land records, transactions, and trust in India. Our mission is to give everyone from everyday property owners to local builders and factory runners absolute peace of mind.

**About the Role**
As we rapidly scale our platform especially across Maharashtra we are looking for a Customer Support Associate to own the end-to-end support experience for our Marathi-speaking users.

You will act as the first point of contact for our customers, resolving operational and technical issues in real time. This isn’t a standard script-reading role; this is a highly execution-focused position requiring deep empathy, raw problem-solving speed, and the ability to translate messy real-world property complexity into a seamless, trustworthy user experience.

**Key Responsibilities**
* Provide real-time support: Guide users in navigating our platform and understanding property insights in Marathi via WhatsApp, phone calls, and chat.
* Resolve core issues related to: 
	* App onboarding, account setup, and general navigation.
	* Understanding platform features, property reports, and search results.
	* Subscription, payment, and platform connectivity challenges.
	* General user queries, trust-building, and post-interaction follow-ups.
* Move comically fast: Customer has a crazy feature request or keeps hitting a UI bug? Spot it, flag it, and work with the team to ship a fix within 12 hours.
* Step on toes: You don't need permission to operate outside your functional area. We encourage Support to jam with Product, Design, and Engineering to fix whatever gets the job done for the customer faster.
* Document and scale: Track recurring issues accurately, update our internal tools, and build SOPs to continuously improve how we serve Bharat.
* Deliver peace of mind: Maintain high responsiveness and absolute empathy for users dealing with high-stakes property matters.

**What We're Looking For**
1. **Linguistic Proficiency:** Native or highly fluent in Marathi (speaking, reading, and writing) is strictly required. Excellent verbal and written communication in Hindi and English.
2. **Experience:** 1–3 years of experience in Customer Support, Customer Success, or Operations—preferably in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.
3. **Slope over intercept:** You come in with high energy and an immense capacity for growth. We will throw you as much rope as you're willing to catch.
4. **Humble & Service-Minded:** Strong filter for low-ego. You understand that our customers are the ones moving the needle, and you take pride in solving their problems.
5. **AI-Forward Mindset:** You are comfortable tinkering with modern software and AI tools to make your own workflow faster and more efficient.
6. **Composed under pressure:** Ability to remain calm and organized while handling multiple customer conversations simultaneously.
7. **Tech-Savvy:** Comfortable with CRM/helpdesk platforms, Google Workspace, and picking up new internal tools instantly.

We are expanding our team at The Legit and looking for motivated, proactive Sales Representatives to help us open conversations with business founders and executives.

title: VP Sales & RevOps (music industry)

### The Role

We’re looking for a VP of Sales and RevOps to lead our global sales and RevOps functions and drive sustainable revenue growth at DISCO.

This is a senior leadership role for someone who knows and understands both the music industry and scalable SaaS sales. We're looking for someone who can set a clear sales strategy, build a reliable go-to-market engine that produces consistent results, and lead a distributed team. You’ll be responsible for achieving and exceeding revenue goals, improving team performance, and making sure we have the right sales process, people, structure and operating rhythm in place.

This role requires someone who is comfortable operating at both the strategic and practical levels. You’ll need to be as effective thinking through long term TAM and revenue growth as you are with day to day revenue execution. Working closely with the Executive team and other leaders, you'll need to coach the team and hold them accountable; drive some bigger, more complex deals yourself; and stay close enough to the sales process to understand what’s working, what isn’t, and what needs to change.

This is a great role for a proven sales leader who is deeply versed in the music industry and has built and scaled sales in a B2B SaaS environment, understands how to create repeatable revenue, and is excited by the opportunity to lead growth at a much loved music tech company.

### Location

### What You'll Do

- Own the revenue number, including sales targets, pipeline creation, forecasting, and consistent attainment
- Lead, coach, and manage the global sales team, ensuring each team member has clear expectations, strong support, and accountability for results

- Review and improve sales tooling, reporting, CRM hygiene, dashboards, reporting, and team operating rhythms
- Build the sales playbooks, materials, training, and coaching rhythms needed to help the team perform consistently
- Help shape future sales team structure, hiring plans, compensation design, territory planning, and market expansion decisions
- Bring clear, data-informed updates to the executive team on performance, risks, opportunities, and priorities.

**Requirements**

- **5+ years in senior sales leadership roles, driving and being responsible for product sales and revenue growth**
- **3+ years leading a Rev ops function**
- **5+ years in the music industry, preferably B2B**

- A proven track record of leading B2B SaaS sales teams, ideally in music tech or adjacent creative industries
- Experience evolving and transforming sales teams - not just inheriting and maintaining
- Experiencing building and evolving effective RevOps teams and systems
- An autonomous and energetic approach to problem solving
- Collaborative, low-ego leadership style that fits a tight-knit exec team

**Benefits**

At DISCO, our employees have told us what benefits mean the most to them, and we've listened. So as a DISCO employee, you will work remotely from home (or a co-working space) whilst being supported by a friendly and fun international team.

In addition, you will receive:

- Two weeks of paid sick leave per year

title: Content Writer (Substack/Youtube)
description:
### **About This Week in AI**
[This Week in AI](https://thisweekinaiclub.substack.com) is an [AI media company](https://thisweekinai.club) covering the products, companies and ideas shaping the AI economy. We primarily target CxOs, Founders, Operators and in general people who want to build in AI.
We started with a newsletter and have built a growing audience of builders, founders and operators interested in understanding what is actually happening in AI — beyond the daily news cycle.
We're now expanding aggressively into YouTube and other media formats.
We're looking for someone who wants to help build that media company with us.
Someone who wants to build the machine.

### **The Role**
We're looking for a Content, Media Operator who can take an idea from:
Research → Insight → Story → Content → Distribution → Growth → Learning
You'll work directly with the founder and have significant ownership over the content and growth engine.
One day you might be researching an emerging AI company. The next, writing a newsletter section, developing a YouTube script, figuring out a better thumbnail, analyzing why a video didn't work, or experimenting with a completely new distribution channel.
You won't have a predefined playbook.
Part of your job is to create the playbook.

### **What You'll Do**
**1. Build the editorial engine**
Research and create content across our media properties. You'll:
* Track AI companies, products, research, markets and emerging trends.
* Read deeply across news, research papers, company announcements, technical documentation, earnings reports and online discourse.
* Find interesting stories and, more importantly, identify why they matter.
* Write newsletter content, social posts, scripts and other editorial formats.
* Turn complex ideas in AI, business and technology into content that is accessible and interesting.
* Develop recurring content formats and editorial franchises.
* Maintain a pipeline of ideas rather than waiting for the next assignment.


**2. Own YouTube end-to-end**
We're building YouTube as a major part of This Week in AI.

You'll help own the entire process: Idea → Research → Angle → Script → Production → Title → Thumbnail → Publishing → Analytics → Iteration

You'll work with editors and other collaborators where necessary, but you'll own the outcome.
You'll constantly ask:
* What should we make?
* Why would someone click?
* Why would they watch?
* Why would they share it?
* What did we learn from the last video?
* What should we do differently next time?


**3. Build our audience**
Content without distribution isn't a media business.
You'll experiment across YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Substack, Instagram, TikTok and whatever else makes sense. You'll:
* Develop distribution strategies.
* Experiment with formats, hooks, packaging and publishing.
* Understand platform-specific mechanics.
* Analyze audience and content performance.
* Identify what's working and double down.
* Kill things that aren't working.
* Find unconventional ways to get distribution.
We're looking for someone who sees growth as a creative problem, not just a dashboard of metrics.

**4. Think about the business**
This isn't a pure editorial role.
We want someone who understands that media is ultimately a business.
You should be curious about:
* Startups
* Business models
* Markets
* Economics
* Distribution
* Consumer behavior
* Technology
* The AI ecosystem
You should be able to look at a company, product or trend and ask:
"What's the business here?"
And when you see an interesting development in AI, you should naturally wonder:
"Why does this matter?"

### **Who We're Looking For**
The simplest description: **You're a creator who has become an operator.**
You've probably spent the early part of your career making things, building audiences, experimenting with the internet and figuring things out yourself.
You don't need to have worked at a major media company.
In fact, we're more interested in what you've built yourself.

Some preferences:
* ~3 years of professional experience, give or take.
* Experience creating content in some form.
* A track record of growing at least one social media channel, community, publication or audience.
* Demonstrated audience growth — the absolute starting or ending number matters less than what you actually achieved.
* Strong writing ability.
* Strong research ability.
* An instinct for interesting ideas and stories.
* A genuine interest in AI, technology, startups and business.
* Comfort learning new tools and platforms.
* The ability to work independently with very little hand-holding.

Most importantly:
**You are curious.**

You read things because you want to understand them. You go down rabbit holes. You learn things nobody asked you to learn. You try tools because you want to see how they work. You notice interesting patterns. And when you don't know how to do something, your first instinct is: "**Let me figure it out.**"

**The Most Important Trait: High Agency**

We don't want a path follower.
We want a path shower.
You should be comfortable starting with: "I don't know how we're going to do this."
…and ending with: "I figured something out. Here's what we should try."
You'll have a lot of freedom in this role.
That also means you'll have a lot of responsibility.
We won't give you a detailed checklist every Monday morning.
We'll give you a goal and expect you to figure out how to get there.

### You Need to Have Built Something
This is a non-negotiable.
You should be able to point to something you've grown.
It could be:
* A YouTube channel
* An X account
* A LinkedIn page
* An Instagram account
* A newsletter
* A community
* A niche publication
* A personal brand
* Or something else entirely

We don't care whether it has 10K, 50K or 500K followers. We care that you started somewhere and made it grow.

Tell us what you started with, what you did, what happened, and what you learned.

### What This Role Is NOT
This probably isn't the right role for you if you're looking for:
* A conventional 9–5 content job.
* A role where someone hands you topics and tells you exactly what to write.
* A social media job where success means publishing X posts per week.
* A job where you only operate within your existing skill set.
* A role with a clearly defined playbook.
* A large team where your individual contribution is difficult to see.

And we aren't particularly interested in:
* Where you went to college.
* How many followers your friends have.
* Whether you have connections at large technology companies.
* Whether you can name-drop people in the industry.

Show us what you've actually built.

### What Success Looks Like
2 months in, we'd want you to be someone who can independently say:
"Here's what's happening in AI."
"Here's the story we should tell."
"Here's how we should tell it."
"Here's how we're going to distribute it."
"Here's what the numbers say."
"Here's what I learned."
"And here's what I think we should do next."
That's the person we're looking for.

### Why Join?
You'll work directly with the founder and have a front-row seat to building an AI-focused media company from an early stage.

You'll get to work across: **AI × Media × Content × YouTube × Startups**
You'll have significant ownership, the ability to experiment, and the opportunity to build things that can become core parts of the company.

If you're someone who has always wanted to build something of your own but also wants the stability and resources of a growing company, this might be a particularly good fit.

I read every one.
— Adam, Founder & CEO
