title: Healthcare Data Engineer
description:
Data Engineers serve a unique and critical role in daily operations at Wider Circle. Customer and program data are the bedrock of our business, and Data Engineering is responsible for building and maintaining the systems that power analytics, reporting, and product intelligence.

We are looking for a hands-on, impact-oriented Data Engineer to build and maintain reliable data pipelines, modernize legacy workflows, and support analytics and machine learning use cases. You will primarily work within Amazon Web Services (AWS), supporting Amazon Redshift, Python-based pipelines, and lightweight AI/LLM integrations.

This role requires someone who ships production code, improves system reliability, and partners closely with analytics and data science to ensure data is trustworthy, well-modeled, and actionable. You will join a talented, fully remote Data Science, Engineering & Analytics team that handles customer data processing, automation, product analytics, complex integrations, and data-driven innovation.

**Company Overview**

Wider Circle exists to create pathways to lasting connection, belonging, and well-being by bringing people together in circles of trust to support one another and strengthen our social fabric. We partner with health plans and community organizations to connect members in small, relationship-driven groups, where they can build trust, support one another, and take meaningful steps forward. By combining peer connection, local facilitators, and data-driven insights, we help members stay engaged in their health while enabling our partners to drive better outcomes at scale.

 

**Responsibilities**

Core Data Engineering

  - Build and maintain scalable ETL/ELT pipelines using Python (pandas) and SQL
  - Ingest data from Amazon S3, APIs, Salesforce, and internal systems
  - Write performant SQL in Amazon Redshift (DDL, DML, stored procedures)
  - Manage schemas, views, permissions, and table evolution safely
  - Debug production data issues and performance bottlenecks
  - Ensure data quality, freshness, lineage, and observability
  - Document pipelines and datasets clearly
  - Ensure appropriate data safeguards for sensitive and regulated data, including PHI and PII

Orchestration & Automation

  - Migrate legacy cron-based workflows to more robust orchestration frameworks
  - Implement idempotent, retry-safe, production-ready jobs
  - Improve reliability and monitoring of existing pipelines
  - Use Git for version control and CI-friendly development practices

Analytics & Modeling Support

  - Partner with Analytics and Data Science to provide clean, modeled datasets
  - Support BI tools, reporting workflows, and Google Sheets integrations
  - Ensure internal SLAs for data quality and delivery frequency are met
  - Provide expert support for complex data integration challenges

AI / LLM Integration

  - Build lightweight AI-powered utilities (e.g., metadata extraction, SQL generation, anomaly explanation)
  - Integrate LLM APIs into existing data workflows
  - Focus on practical augmentation that saves analyst and engineer time

**What Success Looks Like**

- Data pipelines are reliable, observable, and well-documented
- Redshift schemas are clean, performant, and well-managed
- Analysts and stakeholders trust the data
- AI-powered tools meaningfully reduce engineering or analyst workload
- Internal SLAs for data delivery and quality are consistently met

**Requirements**

- 3–6 years of experience in data engineering or analytics engineering
- Strong Python skills (dataframes, file I/O, APIs)
- Strong SQL skills, including warehouse-specific optimization
- Hands-on experience with AWS (S3, IAM, Redshift)
- Experience using APIs for data ingestion and system integration
- Experience with Git and collaborative development workflows
- Comfortable working with imperfect data and legacy systems

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Experience replacing cron with modern orchestration tools (e.g., Airflow or similar)
- Experience with Salesforce API integrations
- Familiarity with Google Drive / Google Sheets APIs
- Exposure to LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
- Experience working with healthcare data (claims, eligibility, CDAs/HRAs)
- Experience partnering with Data Scientists to productionalize models
- Experience with tools such as Matillion, Mulesoft, or similar

**Compensation**

The expected base salary range for this position is $130,000 – $160,000 per year. Actual compensation will depend on experience, qualifications, and location.

title: Climate Analyst
description:
Founded in 2021, [Pulsora](https://pulsesg.com/) the “Enterprise Sustainability Platform”, is a well-funded Silicon Valley software startup.  It is dedicated to empowering purpose-driven enterprises to manage and improve their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) and overall sustainability footprint with an integrated, comprehensive, flexible, and innovative technology platform built for compliance, tracking, and insight. We are well funded, have amazing customers across industries and geographies, established strategic partnerships with leading ERP and consulting firms, and are growing fast! 

**About the Role**  
You sit between our customers and our product, and you own the carbon accounting. You'll work directly with sustainability leaders at enterprise customers as they build their programs in Pulsora - leading the methodology work behind inventory build, target setting, and disclosure. You'll own our emission factor library and calculation methodology, and you'll translate regulatory change into concrete product requirements. This is a hands-on methodology role. You will spend real time in activity data, emission factors, standard text, and calculation logic.

 

**Responsibilities**

- **Lead customer engagements:** Own the relationship with sustainability leads at enterprise customers across GHG inventory build, assurance, decarbonization planning, and voluntary and regulatory reporting. You do the methodology work behind the recommendation, the calculation behind the numbers, and you make sure what the platform produces survives the question "how was this number arrived at?" from an auditor, a CFO, or a regulator.
- **GHG Accounting & Decarbonization**: Shape product capabilities for greenhouse gas (GHG) accounting across Scopes 1, 2, and 3, decarbonization target-setting and tracking (e.g., SBTi, CDP), and audit-ready data lineage—ensuring our platform produces calculations and disclosures that hold up to third-party assurance.
- **Maintain the reference data:** Own the emission factor library end to end - sourcing, versioning, provenance, and retirement of superseded editions across DEFRA/DESNZ, EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub, IEA grid factors, and sector-specific sets. Manage GWP sets across IPCC AR4, AR5, and AR6 and the transition logic between them.
- **Client Engagement**: Serve as a subject matter expert on carbon accounting and sustainability regulations and standards, providing guidance and support to clients during onboarding, training, and ongoing usage of the platform.
- **Requirement Gathering and Prioritization**: Collaborate closely with clients, stakeholders, and internal teams to gather requirements and understand the needs of various users related to carbon accounting, sustainability compliance and reporting. Work closely with engineering, design, and other cross-functional teams to prioritize those requests.
- **Vibe Coding & Rapid Prototyping**: Use AI-assisted coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to independently build working prototypes, internal tools, and AI applications that accelerate discovery, validate ideas with customers, and deliver solutions.

**About you**

- Bachelor's degree in environmental science, business, or related field; Advanced masters degree or MBA preferred.
- Proven track record (5+ years) in climate consulting, or sustainability analyst roles, with significant experience in carbon accounting, sustainability consulting, sustainability framework advice, regulatory counseling, or related domains.
- Deep understanding of the GHG Protocol, ISO 1406X family of standards, sustainability regulations, frameworks, and standards, such as CSRD, CDP, SBTi, PCAF, GRI, SASB, TCFD, EU Taxonomy, SFDR, EDCI, and others.
- Hands-on experience building or auditing a full Scope 1–3 inventory under the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard and Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard..
- Fluency in emission factor sourcing and application: where factors come from, how editions differ, what breaks when a source revises, and how GWP set changes propagate through a restated inventory.
- Familiarity with sustainability assurance and audit practices (e.g., ISAE 3000/3410, AA1000AS, limited vs. reasonable assurance) and the data lineage, controls, and documentation customers need to pass third-party audits.
- Understanding of decarbonization strategy, science-based target setting (SBTi), CDP disclosures, marginal abatement cost curves, scenario analysis, and how companies translate net-zero commitments into operational reduction plans.
- Familiarity with AI-assisted “vibe coding” tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Replit) to build prototypes, internal tools, or working applications—deep AI/ML engineering background is not required, but you should be comfortable shipping real tools with the help of AI.
- Comfort operating in ambiguity at the intersection of regulated domains and fast-moving AI—making thoughtful trade-offs between accuracy, latency, cost, and compliance risk.
- A self-starter who takes ownership of opportunities and works well independently, manages multiple simultaneous projects, and deals well with ambiguity and last-minute changes.

title: Operations Specialist
description:
### Operations Specialist
Cruisebound is seeking an Operations Specialist to help shape the future of cruise booking. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for an early-career operator who wants broad ownership across AI, systems, content, and process in customer operations. You will own the tools and automation our support runs on, and you will see the results of your work in the customer experience.

This role is best suited for a systems thinker who is software-savvy, curious about AI, and able to balance rapid execution alongside projects that require deep, careful work.  This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports, though you will direct the day-to-day work of our Back Office agents employed by our BPO partners.

### Your responsibilities
**AI & Systems for Customer Support**
* Own the performance of our AI support agents. Configure, test, and continuously improve deflection flows and automated responses across chat, email, and voice.
* Own the content and response library that AI and human agents draw from (articles, macros, canned responses, templates, routing rules). Write, structure, and retire content so answers stay accurate, and improve it based on what the performance data tells you.
* Maintain CRM and support tooling configuration, including intents, workflows, tags, SLA rules, and reporting views.
* Own user provisioning and deprovisioning across our customer operations tools, for employees and BPO agents alike. Keep an accurate record of who has access to what, and revoke access promptly on departure.
* Run QA on customer and agent-facing AI output, and close the gaps yourself through content or configuration changes.
* Own automation reporting. Track deflection, resolution, escalation reasons, and contact volume by intent, and bring leadership a clear point of view on what should change.
* Scout and test new AI and support tools, run the pilot, and make the case for what we should adopt.

**Process & Documentation**
* Own the documentation and training materials that keep agents current on cruise line policy changes, product releases, and cross-sell updates.
* Document customer operations processes so they are clear, repeatable, and ready to be automated, measured, or handed off cleanly to internal teams and BPO partners.
* Direct the day-to-day work of our BPO Back Office agents on operational processes and product QA. Set queue priorities and quality standards, spot-check output against documented process, and raise quality or adherence issues with the BPO partner.
* Improve procedures for customer communication, booking modifications, transaction-related inquiries and errors, and cruise line escalations, and flag the ones that are not working.
* Partner with customer service, operations, supply, product and engineering to resolve customer operations issues.

**Product Collaboration**
* Give the product team direct feedback on bugs, feature shortcomings, and new ideas, based on your own usage of the product.
* Investigate booking inconsistencies, errors, and operational issues that come from product shortcomings (such as Pending Bookings), find the pattern behind them, and push for the systemic fix.
* Analyze customer needs, identify problems, and recommend solutions.
* Sample projects you might own
* Rebuild our AI for Agents knowledge base and agent configurations to increase breadth and accuracy and improve agent adoption 
* Audit the content library against what customers actually ask, retire what is stale, and write what is missing in an effort to increase AI resolution rates
* Stand up a QA sampling process for AI output, and report findings along with fixes
* Evaluate a new AI support tool end to end: run the pilot, measure it against what we have, and make the recommendation.
* Automate a repetitive Back Office process 

### The ideal candidate
* Has 1-3 years of experience in customer support, operations, or a systems and tooling role, or equivalent practical experience
* Is an early adopter: tries new tools on their own, has opinions about the ones they use, and pays attention to where AI is heading for customer support
* Has hands-on experience writing and iterating on prompts, and understands how wording, structure, examples, and context change the output. Tests a prompt change and reads the result rather than guessing at it
* Thinks in systems: comfortable with workflows, rules, tags, and intents, and finds the upstream cause rather than fixing the same thing twice
* Is curious, proactive, and self-directed, and does not wait to be told what to do
* Balances attention to detail with an MVP mindset and bias toward action
* Nice to have: admin experience with a modern CRM or support platform (Kustomer, Intercom, Zendesk, Salesforce or similar), comfort with business intelligence tooling

### Compensation and benefits
* The compensation package for this position comprises: (1) a base salary ranging from $60,000 to $70,000 depending on the candidate’s experience, knowledge, and skills, and (2) an employee stock option grant. In addition, we also offer our employees a comprehensive range of benefits including but not limited to:
* $1,000 annual cruise credit to use on Cruisebound.com and additional employee rebates
* Excellent health care insurance (medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, etc.)
* Generous personal paid time off (PTO) allowance beginning with 20 days in the first year, plus 2 additional days per year of tenure (up to 30 days total)
* 4 company-wide holidays (first Friday of each quarter) and 12 public holidays observed
* $100/month communication credit intended for cell phone and Wi-Fi expenses

**About Cruisebound**
Our mission is to help cruisers book their dream vacation by creating the best online booking experience for cruises.

We are customer centric: we focus on finding the fastest and most intuitive way to solve customer pain points. We are decisive: we don’t let perfect be the enemy of good. We are data driven: support every decision with data. We are one crew: we win and lose together, we are not afraid to make mistakes and learn from them.
Our founding team previously built and scaled Rocket Travel, a travel startup, to $900M in revenue. Rocket is now part of Booking Holdings, the world leader in travel. We are a diverse team from around the globe who have learned about the travel industry at places like Booking.com, United Airlines, McKinsey, BCG, Stanford, and MIT.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Classification and Detection (West Coast)
acceptedRemoteLocations: United States; Vancouver, British Columbia; British Columbia, Canada
description:
**This is a role for someone who trains models. Not someone who calls them.**
We are building classification and detection systems from scratch: fine-tuned transformers, entity detection over structured and unstructured content, and behavioral scoring against a taxonomy we defined ourselves. If your recent work is retrieval-augmented generation, prompt engineering, agent orchestration, or integrating a foundation model API, this is a different discipline and we would be wasting your time.

If you have owned a classifier in production, from data through training through evaluation through the retraining loop, please consider applying.

**About SmartVerify**
SmartVerify is building the data egress control plane for enterprise AI. We sit inline between AI agents and enterprise data, inspecting every query, enforcing policy in real time, and producing an immutable audit trail. 

This is a greenfield build against an existing spec. You have freedom to update the spec as you come in an evaluate the goals. You would be the only ML engineer on staff. You would report directly to the founder, who has a background in this space, and you would have a co-op available to own the evaluation harness and pipeline QA under your direction.

**What You Would Own**

• The behavioral classification model: multi-class classification of AI agent query intent against our internal taxonomy, producing labels, confidence, and supporting evidence rather than a bare score
• PII and PHI detection over query content and returned data, including span-level identification suitable for audit evidence
• Behavioral risk scoring, combining deterministic request signals with model-derived signals
• Model training, serving, and versioning on SageMaker within the asynchronous inspection path
• The evaluation harness, drift detection, and retraining loop, with a co-op supporting the harness work
• The classification output contract that downstream audit, enrichment, and dashboard consumers depend on

**What We Are Looking For**
Must-haves are genuinely required. Nice-to-haves are things we expect a strong candidate to pick up here

**Must have**
Production ML ownership: models you trained, deployed, monitored, and retrained in a live system
Transformer fine-tuning for text classification (BERT family, DistilBERT, or equivalent)
Sequence labelling or named entity recognition for structured entity detection
Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers
Evaluation rigour: you can explain how you chose thresholds and what you traded away
Comfort working from a written design spec rather than waiting for direction
Authorised to work in Canada or the United States, located in British Columbia or the Seattle area

**Nice to have, or will ramp up**
Bootstrapping labels through weak supervision, LLM-assisted labelling, or active learning
Anomaly or behavioural detection with sparse or absent labels
SageMaker training jobs and inference endpoints
Regulated domain experience: HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, or SOC 2
Fraud, abuse, or security detection background
Distillation or quantisation to hold an inference latency budget
Kinesis, Kafka, or other streaming pipelines
SQL and query structure parsing
Mentoring a junior engineer or co-op

**Who Does Well Here**
• You have shipped a model that other systems depended on, and you remember what broke
• You are honest about model limitations rather than defensive, because our customers are auditors and regulators
• You can read an architecture document, disagree with part of it, and say so with a reason
• You are comfortable being the only person in the company who understands this layer, and you document accordingly
• You want ownership more than you want a large team

**The Stack**
Intelligence layer: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, SageMaker training and inference, evaluation and drift tooling
Infrastructure: AWS, EKS, Terraform, Helm, Prometheus, Grafana

**Location and Compensation**
• Seattle area or British Columbia. Remote within those regions, with periodic in-person time with the team
• Existing authorization to work in United States is required. We can sponsor work visa and PR in Canada
• Below-market base plus meaningful early-stage equity. We discuss specific numbers early in the process rather than making you guess, and we will not ask you to name a figure first

## **What We’re Looking For**

- 5+ years of professional software engineering experience
- Experience owning and shipping **real production products**
- Meaningful experience building AI-powered products in production
- Strong Python and/or TypeScript/JavaScript skills with comfort across the stack
- Experience with modern AI architectures such as agents, tool use, RAG/retrieval, structured generation, and evaluation
- Strong product judgment and comfort operating with significant autonomy
- Clear communication with both technical and nontechnical stakeholders
- Genuine curiosity about AI—you actively experiment with new tools and continuously evolve how you build

We especially value engineers with **0→1 experience**, startup backgrounds, customer exposure, or ownership beyond a narrow technical specialty.

You don’t need to know everything. You do need to be **rigorous and deeply curious**.

## **How We Work**

Futureproofing is fully remote, with engineering talent primarily across Latin America and clients primarily in the United States.

Engagements may be part-time or full-time, with some US working-hour overlap. You’ll work closely with Futureproofing’s engineering leadership while working on a dedicated client founding team.

## **What Makes Futureproofing Different**

**Small, senior teams.** We build teams around problems, not seats.

**Real ownership.** Engineers participate in architecture, product decisions, tradeoffs, and client conversations—not just implementation.

**Production AI.** We care about systems that survive contact with real users, data, and business constraints.

**AI-native engineering.** We expect our engineers to experiment constantly with how AI changes the way software is built.

**Intentional matching.** We get to know our engineers and clients deeply rather than matching through keywords.

**Developer-first.** We’d rather build a smaller network of exceptional engineers doing meaningful work than optimize for placement volume.

description:
# Product Designer at Aios Medical — Remote, $90k-$150k/yr inc equity

# About AIOS

**AIOS is building the world’s first full-stack AI doctor.**  
We’re at $350M ARR, growing from $10M/yr 12 months ago. We’re the world’s fastest growing AI doctor.  
We’re faithfully serving \>150k/mo patients via Bolt Pharmacy, our main UK brand. We’re profitable.  
Our strategy exists at the intersection of two strong theses:

1. The AI doctor that wins will get to escape velocity using GLP-1s, the fastest growing consumer product in history.
2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

- **Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025**: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.
- **Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026**: Over the last 12 months we’ve grown from 3k to 150k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.
- **Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028**: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.
- **Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2031**: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.
- **Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035**: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.  
We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

You can read more about working with us here:[Working at AIOS](https://app.notion.com/p/Working-at-AIOS-5b5c0a584af44de78ac7fb9b2cf8d993?pvs=21)

## Being a Product Designer at AIOS

We are building a world-class team.

You’ll be taking on a senior, high-ownership role in product design at Aios Medical. We have multiple roles in the team across our clinical software and customer facing mobile app.

You’ll be stepping into a product that has grown fast and needs stronger design leadership, judgment, and structure.

Some of this work is visible and polished. Some of it is messy and internal. You’ll own projects end-to-end. That means taking loosely defined problems, talking to the right people, understanding workflows and constraints, and shipping solutions you can stand behind. We’re looking for someone who can run with a problem independently and be trusted to get it over the line.

The work often sits at the intersection of user needs, business goals, and real constraints. You might be working with engineers on a customer app flow, untangling a complex internal workflow that’s slowing teams down, reviewing CX tickets to understand where users are breaking, or defending a design decision.

You’ll report directly to our Head of Product Design ([Ryan Wu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryanhlwu/)) and work closely with our Head of Product ([Ben Dowdle](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bendowdle/)). You’ll also work alongside the rest of our Product and Design org, as well as our engineering and CX teams. You’ll be superb at collaborating and moving fast.

This is a full-time, remote role. We’re async-friendly and flexible with hours, but overlap with European and US time zones is expected.

## Key responsibilities

- Design ownership: You take ownership of design work across products and run projects independently, from problem definition to shipped solution.
- Customer apps: You design and improve customer-facing web and mobile app experiences. Mobile app work is a major focus area.
- Internal tools & workflows: You work on internal products used by clinical, ops, enrolment, and CX teams, focusing on workflow, usability, and efficiency.
- Complex problem solving: You work on products with real commercial and regulatory constraints. You understand that not everything can be changed freely.
- Business & user understanding: You start from the business problem and the user need. You can clearly explain what problem you were solving and why.
- End-to-end project ownership: You lead projects independently, including discovery, talking to users or internal teams, defining the solution, and shipping it.
- Clear communication: You can articulate your thinking, defend decisions, and hold your ground in discussions with strong opinions.
- Hands-on leadership: You’re comfortable being senior, helping shape how design works, and supporting other designers as the team grows, without stepping away from hands-on work.

## Need to have

Experience: You’ve spent **3+ years** designing digital products across **web or mobile**, including customer-facing mobile apps or internal tooling. What matters is that you’ve designed real products used by real people.

Robust Portfolio: Your portfolio shows real product work that shows off your design taste. We want to see the problem, the rules you had to work within, and the impact of your decisions - including polished screens of the output.

Ownership: You take loosely defined problems and run with them. You figure out what needs to be done, who to talk to, and how to move a project from idea to shipped solution. You don’t need constant direction, and you don’t get stuck in endless exploration.

Craft: You care about clarity and usability more than surface-level polish. You can work within fixed requirements, technical limitations, and existing systems, and still make meaningful improvements.

Clear thinking & communication: You can clearly explain what problem you were solving, why certain decisions were made, and what tradeoffs were involved. You’re comfortable defending your work and navigating discussions with strong opinions.

## Nice to have

Formal or equivalent design training: You’ve studied design, computer science, or a related field - or you’ve built the same depth of thinking through real product work.

Working in regulated and complex products: You don’t need experience in healthcare specifically. What matters is that you’ve worked on products where design decisions are shaped by regulation, compliance, legal requirements, or strong business rules. You understand that some copy, flows, or elements can’t simply be removed or redesigned, and that good design often means improving clarity and usability *within* those realities

Design that gets built: You’re comfortable working with engineers and thinking through implementation details. You understand how design decisions show up in real code and systems.

## Our cultural standards

We aim to make this your life’s work. This should be the most challenging, most rewarding role of your life. Accordingly, these are the core cultural standards to which we hold ourselves & our team-members:

1. Belief in the mission: We will have served 100 million patients by the end of 2035 and we transform the life of most patients who join. We have a lot of work to do. We are obsessed with our patients and are dedicated to the mission.
2. Unwavering integrity: We are at the frontier, so we often live in ambiguity with no trodden path. When we can’t look to others for guidance, we must maintain impeccable ethics and unwavering integrity.
3. Only the paranoid survive: Bad sh*t is coming. By joining us, you’re choosing to sail straight towards the storms with unhesitating conviction. However much we’ve already done, however far we’ve already come — it’s still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.
4. If we’re average we fail: We are only interested in “insanely great”, a focus on the quality of our execution that in everyday life would be considered pathological. We have a dedication to excellence and reject incompetence.
5. Commitment to candor: That which can be destroyed by the truth should be. You get full transparency from the company and the company expects full transparency from you. We never say anything about someone that we wouldn’t say to them directly. We give feedback with love and do not need to protect people from fleeting physical sensations.
6. A maniacal sense of urgency: We execute at an intensity that most people think is impossible. Speed is critical and we need things done yesterday. We all work very hard and in such a competitive world there really is no other way to win.
7. Enduring frugality: We are frugal. We hate being wasteful and we are anti-luxury. A culture of cheapness keeps us young. We spend our cash wisely & carefully — in a way that would make our grandmas proud.
8. Bulldozing barriers: The world is malleable and we shape it. We truly believe this and act accordingly. We are relentlessly resourceful and are at the mercy of no-one but ourselves. You’ll be shocked how capable you are and how much you can achieve.
9. Keep your head down: We’re boring people doing exciting work. We don’t chase short-term status — we ignore short-term dopamine hits and focus on what matters. Outsiders will underestimate us and we revel in that.
10. The power of focus: We live in a world of power laws and we cannot overestimate the unimportance of practically everything. Know your One Thing, and nail it.

🎯 *“You just build a f*ing amazing experience. Make each step amazing. Make every decision in the long term interest of the customer. Give the customer massively more value than you take.”*

## Compensation & Benefits

You get paid above market salary and you get early stage equity, so you get really rich if we nail this.

- *Compensation*: $90,000-$150,000 (inc equity)

### Benefits

The stuff below is cool as well.

- *Healthcare*: comprehensive medical insurance (if appropriate).
- *Vacation*: PTO with a yearly minimum (≥2wks/yr + local national holidays)
- *Personal development*: budget for books, courses, coaching.
- *Personal wellness*: budget for gym, health apps.
- *GLP-1s*: free membership with a clinic offering GLP-1s.
- *Equipment*: Macbook & work-from-home equipment provided as needed.
- **What are we missing?** We're still early so you get to shape our culture.

## How to apply

1. Apply on [Ashby](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/Aios/781c4075-21bc-4c06-ba74-9c8f2a7a3cfc)

title: Head of Finance
description:
**Location: Remote, US-based. Full time. Remote within the Eastern or Central time zones, with a preference for the NYC metro area. The work schedule is Eastern business hours. Travel to meet with the CEO in NY is expected, and is tied to the work need and opportunity.**

**About the Role**

Pawlicy Advisor is a venture-backed pet insurance marketplace that helps pet parents compare plans and choose the right coverage, distributed through veterinary clinics and partners nationwide. The business is profitable and growing. Pawlicy Advisor is hiring a Head of Finance to own the entire finance function and serve as the CEO’s operating partner. This is a hands-on role: on day one, you are the finance team, supported by outsourced accounting and tax contractors whom you direct and may bring in-house as the business case warrants. You will own cash, the monthly close, the operating model, financial reporting, and partner in operational and strategic decision-making. The role reports directly to the CEO and is designed to grow into an executive seat as the business scales.

**What You Own**

**Cash Management and Banking Relationships**

- Own the cash forecast and cash governance to proactively drive capital allocation and growth investment decision-making.
- Manage banking and investor reporting relationships.
- Assess capital options (equity, debt, non-dilutive) and recommend timing and structure with clear tradeoffs.
- Own the financial workstream for strategic transactions (financings, partnerships, M&A): models, data room, and investor and counterparty materials, in partnership with the CEO and counsel.

**Accounting, Close, and Control**

- Deliver a timely, accurate monthly close and GAAP-compliant financials; you review every close personally.
- Direct outsourced accounting and tax firms; hold them to defined deliverables, timelines, and cost.
- Own commission reconciliation and revenue assurance: carrier statement reconciliation, commission receivables, and revenue recognition to identify unpaid, underpaid, and misattributed commissions and recover what Pawlicy is owed.
- Maintain the chart of accounts and keep Brex, payroll, billing, and banking systems aligned with the general ledger.
- Oversee AP, AR, vendor payments, payroll, and federal, state, and local tax compliance.

**Operations, FP&A, and Board Reporting**

- Own the three-statement operating model, annual budget, and scenario planning for growth, profitability, and headcount.
- Deliver the monthly financial package to the CEO and Board: P&L, cash flow, variance analysis, and proactive recommendations.
- Prepare Board materials: actuals vs. budget, key business drivers.
- Serve as a key operator, galvanizing the team toward achievement of OKRs.
- Own LTV/CAC and payback analyses by acquisition channel and distribution segment.
- Support technical integration of financial data across companywide systems to help department heads understand and manage their budgets, and make the ROI of initiatives visible in real time.

**Finance Operating Model and Team**

- Own the mix of in-house staff and outsourced contractors. You have authority to restructure, replace, or bring work in-house, and you are expected to do so only when it lowers total cost or materially improves speed and accuracy.
- Every financial decision is rooted in a defensible, data-driven case: current fully loaded cost, proposed cost, what is the range of outcomes and their probabilities, and payback periods.
- Select and administer the finance systems stack (QuickBooks Online, Brex, payroll and PEO, banking, billing) with a bias toward automation over headcount.

**Where You Partner**

- Compensation and equity: comp modeling and leveling, developing Compensation Committee materials, optimizing incentive structures to align with company OKRs, preparing hiring plans including role scoping and ROI pressure-testing, and ensuring cap table accuracy in Carta, in partnership with HR and counsel.
- Legal and risk: corporate, commercial, and employment matters that intersect with finance; state registrations and compliance tied to payroll and operating presence.
- Commercial partnerships: financial terms, revenue share structures, and partner economics alongside the CEO, Chief Product Officer, and Partnerships lead. Additionally, you are eager to help lead business development initiatives as an externally-facing member of the team.
- Data and analytics: work with the Data team to connect product, marketing, sales, and financial data in Mixpanel and Tableau, building dashboards the whole company trusts.
- Company execution: contribute structured, data-driven recommendations on company OKRs and surface the highest-ROI opportunities and risks to the executive team.

**What Success Looks Like**

**First 90 days**

- Monthly close delivered on a defined schedule with a documented review process. You can explain every material line.
- Operating Model (forecast) is live, updated with actuals, and reviewed monthly.
- Become expert on company’s market, strategy, and operations.
- Audit of current financial workstreams complete, with scoped processes for completing needed workstreams and defined plan regarding contractors and bringing capabilities in-house.
- Transaction-ready data room with updated diligence materials.
- Support 2027 budget development as part of Operating Model build.

**First 12 months**

- The CEO and Board receive concise, accurate packages that drive decisions and show progress toward scalable growth.
- Channel-level LTV/CAC and payback are published, trusted, and used by department heads to allocate capital.
- Budget, hiring plan, and cash runway are always reconciled and forward-looking.
- Strategic opportunities are evaluated in days with rigorous analysis and a clear recommendation.
- Maintain active operational presence across the company, partnering on OKR development and guiding the business toward achievement of its OKRs.

**Requirements**

  - 7+ years in finance, including 2+ years as the second-in-command (Director or VP reporting to a CFO or founder) at a venture-backed company.
  - Hands-on ownership of the monthly close, GL, and financial statements; you have done the work, not just reviewed it.
  - Deep FP&A and three-statement modeling experience; fluency in scenario analysis, unit economics, and sensitivity modeling.
  - Direct experience with LTV/CAC, payback, and channel performance measurement in a multi-channel or B2B2C business.
  - Proven experience scaling a startup through a period of significant revenue growth.
  - Experience managing Board reporting and collaborating directly with venture firms.
  - Experience managing outsourced accounting, tax, and finance vendors to defined outcomes and budgets.
  - Strong systems orientation across QuickBooks Online, Brex, banking platforms, PEOs, Carta, and BI tools such as Mixpanel or Tableau.
  - Comfort working across HR, legal, and operations topics that fall outside traditional finance.
  - Preferred: familiarity with insurance distribution or commission-based revenue models.
  - Legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.

**How You Work**

- You are hungry to scale a company and have done high-paced operational work beyond finance.
- You do the work yourself first, then build process around it. You are comfortable being the entire finance function for a period.
- You are a clear, direct communicator who distills complexity into simple, actionable narratives for non-finance colleagues.
- You have a bias for action and move from analysis to decision to execution quickly.
- You are rigorously organized, document your work as a way of collaborating, and use digital task management tools (will use ClickUp daily for task management and AI tools such as Claude to compound your output) daily.
- You streamline and compound productivity with AI before hiring.
- You challenge assumptions and welcome being challenged in return.
- You treat every dollar of finance spend, including your own team, like any other investment: clear hypothesis, measured payback, and learnings that feed the next iteration.

**AI and the Hiring Process**

We embrace AI at Pawlicy and our work still relies on what the humans bring to it.

Prep with AI all you like, but in the room, we want your thinking, your questions, and your judgment. These stages exist so we can get to know you and how you'd work with our team. We're hiring you, not a model and it is you we want to see. 

To be concrete: no AI assistants or chatbots on any device during your interviews, and nobody else feeding you answers. If it turns out AI was used where we've asked you not to, it may end your candidacy.

If any part of our process is a barrier because of how you read, write or communicate, email careers@pawlicy.com before that stage and we'll talk through the options. The skills we're assessing stay the same; what changes is the format. Asking has no bearing on how we assess you.

**Interview Recording Notice**

By submitting your application, you acknowledge that interviews with Pawlicy Advisor may be recorded (audio, video, and/or transcript) to support a fair and consistent hiring process. Recordings are used only for hiring purposes and are accessible only to those involved in the hiring decision. You will be asked to confirm your consent at the start of any recorded interview.

**Benefits**

- Base salary $185,000 to $250,000, depending on experience and location.
- Target annual bonus tied to company and individual performance.
- Meaningful equity grant with a defined path to an executive title as the business scales.
- Top-tier health, dental, and vision insurance; 401(k) employer contributions; flexible vacation.
- Remote-first, with regular in-person opportunities to collaborate with the CEO.

**Career Path**

This role is scoped as Head of Finance with a path to CFO. The promotion is tied to outcomes: consistent, high-quality execution and ownership across finance and operations resulting in achievement of company goals. 

If you want to build and run the financial engine of a profitable, venture-backed, mission-driven company at an inflection point, and to act as a true partner to the CEO, Pawlicy would like to talk. Learn more at [https://www.pawlicy.com/about-us/](https://www.pawlicy.com/about-us/)

title: Technical Project Manager
description:
Certa ([certa.ai](http://certa.ai)) is an AI-native third-party risk management platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle, from onboarding through continuous monitoring and offboarding. Enterprises from the Fortune 500 to fast-growing startups use our no-code platform to manage vendors, suppliers, and partners across risk, compliance, and ESG. Trusted by Honeywell, Uber, MARS, and Boeing, we've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries.

We're looking for a Technical Project Manager to own the end-to-end delivery of complex enterprise software implementations. This is a client-facing role at the center of every engagement: you'll translate what a customer needs into a plan, drive a cross-functional team to build it, and keep both sides aligned from kickoff to go-live and beyond. You won't just track tasks, you'll understand the product deeply, engage in technical conversations with solution architects and engineers, lead the business requirement sessions, and make the decisions that keep delivery on track. The best person for this role thinks like an owner of the account, not a coordinator of it.

## What You'll Do

- **Own delivery end to end:** Run enterprise implementation projects from kickoff through go-live and stabilization, accountable for scope, timeline, budget, quality, and client satisfaction on every engagement you lead.
- **Build & manage the plan:** Break down complex, ambiguous requirements into a clear project plan with phases, milestones, dependencies, and owners, keeping it current and making trade-offs visible when reality shifts.
- **Lead requirements gathering:** Own the business requirement sessions end to end, facilitating discovery workshops that surface what the client actually needs, documenting requirements in a structured, unambiguous format, managing sign-off, and keeping them traceable through design, build, and testing.
- **Run the cross-functional team:** Coordinate solution architects, engineers, QA, and client stakeholders toward a shared outcome, removing blockers, resolving conflicts, and making sure everyone knows what they own and by when.
- **Own the client relationship:** Be the client's primary point of contact, leading status meetings, steering committee updates, and escalations, setting expectations early, and protecting the relationship even during hard conversations.
- **Manage scope, risk & change:** Hold the line on scope creep, documenting and quantifying changes before work starts, and manage risks and issues proactively with a live view of mitigation plans and early escalation.
- **Stay technical, report & improve:** Understand the architecture, integrations, and configuration decisions well enough to challenge estimates and speak credibly with engineers and technical buyers, produce honest, easy-to-read status reports and executive updates, and feed lessons learned back into delivery methodology.

## What Success Looks Like

- **On-target delivery:** Projects land on time, on budget, and within scope, with a clear plan stakeholders trust.
- **Trusted clients:** Clients feel informed and in control throughout the engagement, and would take your call for the next one.
- **Managed risk:** Risks surface early and get managed, so escalations are rare and never a surprise.
- **Aligned team & clean handoffs:** The delivery team is aligned, unblocked, and clear on priorities, and handoffs to support and account teams are clean, with nothing left undocumented.

## What You'll Need

- **Experience:** 5+ years managing technical or software implementation projects, ideally in enterprise SaaS, professional services, or a client-facing delivery environment, with a track record of delivering complex, multi-stakeholder projects on time and within budget as the primary delivery owner for enterprise clients.
- **Technical fluency:** You can read a solution design, understand integrations and data flows, and hold your own in a technical discussion without being the engineer.
- **Requirements & delivery craft:** Proven ability to run requirements and discovery sessions and translate them into clear, documented business requirements, plus solid command of project management fundamentals (planning, estimation, dependency management, risk and issue tracking, and change control).
- **Stakeholder management:** Excellent communication, comfort presenting to senior and executive audiences, and the ability to manage scope, timelines, and difficult conversations without losing the relationship.
- **Ways of working:** Organized and calm under pressure, you over-communicate rather than under-communicate, you're direct when a project needs a hard truth and diplomatic when a relationship needs care, and you own outcomes rather than pointing to a process.

title: Quality Assurance Team Lead
description:
# QA Lead — SleekSky

## About SleekSky

SleekSky builds and runs software for clients who want to scale their technology without heavy overhead: dedicated teams, a startup-inspired culture, and a bias for agility, ownership, and continuous improvement. We combine professional depth with real room to learn, decide, and build things that last.

## The Role

Most QA Lead openings hand you a quality function to run. **This one hands you the mandate to build it.**

You'll own quality end to end for a live US healthcare platform that our dedicated team builds and operates: the strategy, the automation that enforces it, the release process it gates, and the QA team that runs all three. Today, quality here is careful manual judgement applied late in the cycle. Your job is to turn it into a system applied continuously, and then be answerable for the result.

This is a construction job for at least the first year, and a player-coach role throughout. If you're looking for an established department to manage, this isn't it. If you want to build one and then run it, few roles will hand you this much room.

## What You'll Own

- **QA strategy, end to end.** What gets tested, where automation pays, and what must be true before software moves between environments. You'll build the mechanism that enforces it, not just the document that describes it.
- **The automation estate.** A suite already exists. Part of it encodes hard-won domain knowledge, and part of it is coverage on paper. A part-built migration to Playwright needs an owner who will finish it. Your first judgement call is telling those apart.
- **The release gate.** A short, fast, trustworthy suite wired into CI/CD, running on triggers rather than on someone remembering, and fast enough that nobody wants to skip it.
- **Quality metrics.** What escaped, where it should have been caught, and whether that's improving month over month. Making those questions answerable with data is part of the job.
- **Environments and test data.** Regulated health data changes what may appear in a fixture, a log, or a test environment. Test accounts, seed data, and that discipline are yours.
- **The team.** QA engineers report to you from day one, and you have the mandate to grow the function. You define what you're hiring for, and you hire it.

## What Makes the Problem Interesting

- **A platform of a dozen-plus applications**, several of them white-labelled. "The login test" is really a matrix of tests across customer configurations.
- **The most expensive defects aren't broken pages.** They're a malformed field in a file delivered to a partner. Testing that is data validation, not clicking.
- **Asynchronous behaviour everywhere:** background jobs, scheduled reminders, email, SMS, and automated voice calls. The thing you're asserting on often happens minutes later, in a system you don't control.
- **Real patients on the other end.** There is no quiet maintenance window in which to be wrong.

## What You'll Bring

- **5+ years in QA / quality engineering**, with at least two of them spent setting the test agenda rather than executing someone else's.
- **An automation suite you built that ran without you**, on a pipeline or a schedule, with other people depending on the result.
- **Test code engineers would accept in review.** JavaScript/TypeScript is our stack and Playwright is our direction. Cypress or Selenium experience transfers.
- **CI/CD fluency:** pipelines, gates, artifacts, and a real opinion about flaky tests.
- **SQL you can actually use.** Much of what needs verifying here never appears on a screen, including scheduled jobs, generated files, and data extracts delivered to partners.
- **Depth in API and integration testing**, and a method for deciding what *not* to test.
- **Experience mentoring or leading QA engineers**, and clear written English. You'll write the strategy, the release call, and defect reports a developer can act on without a follow-up question.

title: Founding Engineer, PhrasIQ
acceptedRemoteLocations: Canada; United States; Europe; Mexico; United Kingdom
description:
Location: Remote (or hybrid, open to discussion)
Stage: Pre-seed, equity-only until seed close or ARR milestone



**What PhrasIQ is**

PhrasIQ is an agentic FP&A and decision intelligence platform for enterprise finance teams. The core bet is that finance teams won't trust AI-generated numbers unless every output is auditable, traceable, and explainable back to source data. We call this reducing "alignment latency": the gap between an AI producing an answer and a human being willing to act on it.

The product is built on two layers:


1. Loktak — the deterministic backbone. Versioned finance ontology, canonical finance objects, data lineage, eval scoring. This is the system of record and the system of truth.
2. InsightOS — the orchestration layer. Agents, forecasting, narrative generation, UI. This is where the AI lives.


One rule governs everything: InsightOS never touches Loktak's database directly. It only ever goes through Loktak's API. No shortcuts, no unified credential set, no "just this once" direct query. If that constraint doesn't make immediate sense to you, or sounds like premature architecture for a pre-seed company, this probably isn't the right role.

We're hiring two founding engineer tracks. You can apply to either, or tell us which one you'd naturally gravitate toward and we'll figure it out together.


**Track 1: Founding Platform Engineer (Loktak)**

You'll build the deterministic backbone that everything else depends on.

**What you'll own:**


* Versioned finance ontology and canonical object models
* Data lineage: every number traceable to its source, every transformation logged
* Eval scoring infrastructure for AI-generated outputs
* The API surface that InsightOS is permitted to call — designing it to be strict enough that it's structurally impossible to bypass


**You're a strong fit if:**


* You've built systems where correctness and traceability mattered more than speed of iteration (fintech, healthtech, compliance-adjacent, data infrastructure)
* You think about schema design and versioning before you think about UI
* When someone describes a system with a "trusted" internal shortcut, your instinct is discomfort, not relief



**Track 2: Founding AI/Agent Engineer (InsightOS)**

You'll build the orchestration layer: the agents, the forecasting logic, the narrative generation, all of it operating strictly within the boundaries Loktak defines.

What you'll own:


* Multi-agent architecture across four scoped agents (Grounding/Retrieval, Modeling/Forecast, Variance/Anomaly, Narrative/Drafting), each with its own least-privilege credential scope into Loktak
* Forecasting and decision-brief generation logic
* The user-facing product surface


You're a strong fit if:


* You've built with LLM agents/orchestration in production, not just prototypes
* You default to asking "what should this agent NOT be able to touch" before "what should this agent be able to do"
* You've worked somewhere that made you care about explainability, not just output quality



What's true for both tracks

Comp: Equity-only until we close our seed round or hit ARR milestone, whichever comes first. We're telling you this now, not five interviews in, because we'd rather you self-select in or out early than waste your time or ours.

Stage reality: You will be the 2nd or 3rd engineer at the company. There's no scaffolding. You'll be making architectural calls that outlast this hiring round.

Path: For the right person on either track, there's a real path to a co-founder-level role, not just an early employee slot.

What we're actually testing for: Less "do you know the right frameworks," more "when you hit ambiguity, do you treat it as a product problem or just an engineering problem." The strongest people we've talked to instinctively ask who the output is for before they ask how to build it.


**Process**


1. Intro call (30 min) — mutual fit, equity structure surfaced up front
2. Technical deep dive (60-90 min) — architecture walkthrough, including a boundary/traceability scenario specific to your track
3. Take-home — mirrors an actual PhrasIQ problem (e.g., a Decision Brief Generator), intentionally underspecified in places
4. Founder conversation — vision, working style, path forward



**Before you apply here, please send us answers to the following prompt under "*What interests you about working for this company?*"**:
**Filter Questions (Screening)**


* This is equity-only with no cash until seed close or $250K ARR. What makes that worth it for you right now?

* What is a project you built that had to be correct, rather than just fast?
 
* What is one system you have worked on with a boundary or permission model you are proud of (or one you wish had existed)?

* Which track pulls at you more, and why?

description:
ABOUT US

The Estimator works closely with Operations, Procurement, and Business Development teams to ensure all proposals align with company pricing standards, client requirements, and profitability objectives.
The ideal candidate possesses strong cost analysis skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple estimates simultaneously while maintaining accuracy and consistency.

**What You’ll Do:**
•	Prepare accurate and competitive estimates, proposals, and quotes for reactive maintenance, preventive maintenance, service work orders, repairs, and capital improvement projects.
•	Support pricing and scope development for common maintenance and repair requests, including:
o	HVAC: AC not cooling, fan motor replacement, thermostat replacement, filter changes, coil cleaning, and system inspections.
o	Plumbing: Toilet clogs, pipe leaks, faucet replacements, fixture repairs, and water heater maintenance.
o	Handyman Services: Door repairs, drywall patching, ceiling tile replacement, hardware adjustments, building inspections, and general facility repairs.
•	Work within facility management platforms and client portals, including ServiceChannel, Corrigo, and similar systems used for work order management, proposal submission, and approval workflows.
•	Review scopes of work, technician findings, site photos, inspection reports, vendor assessments, and client requirements to determine labor, material, equipment, and subcontractor costs.
•	Develop pricing for facility maintenance trades including HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, automatic and overhead doors, handyman services, general repairs, and other commercial building systems.
•	Evaluate and process NTE (Not-to-Exceed) requests by preparing detailed cost breakdowns, supporting documentation, and client-facing justifications for approval.
•	Utilize historical work order data, market pricing, geographic labor rates, trade-specific costs, and vendor quotations to build accurate and competitive estimates.
•	Obtain, analyze, and compare multiple vendor and subcontractor quotes to ensure cost competitiveness while maintaining profitability and service quality standards.
•	Prepare detailed client-facing proposals including scope descriptions, exclusions, assumptions, line-item pricing, and supporting documentation.
•	Maintain and update pricing databases, labor rates, material costs, subcontractor pricing, markup structures, and historical cost records.
•	Analyze completed work orders and projects to identify pricing trends, improve estimating accuracy, and support continuous improvement initiatives.
•	Coordinate closely with Dispatch, Operations, Vendor Management, Procurement, and Project Teams to support quote development, service delivery, and project execution.
•	Identify scope gaps, pricing risks, operational concerns, and margin impacts prior to quote submission.
•	Maintain proper estimating documentation, version control, pricing records, and supporting files in accordance with company standards and client requirements.
•	Support dispatch and operational functions as needed, including vendor coordination, work order scheduling, service follow-up, and issue resolution to ensure timely execution and client satisfaction.
•	Contribute to the standardization of pricing methodologies, estimating processes, and best practices across all service lines and client accounts.

**What We’re Looking For:**
•	Experience in estimating, dispatching, construction, facility maintenance, or related operational support roles
•	Strong understanding of labor, material, and project pricing concepts
•	Ability to read and interpret scopes of work, vendor quotes, and repair assessments
•	Strong communication, coordination, and organizational skills
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, spreadsheets, and work order management systems
•	Ability to manage multiple tasks, vendors, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment
•	Detail-oriented with strong analytical and problem-solving skills
•	Knowledge of trades such as HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, or general maintenance is preferred
•	2–5 years of experience in estimating, dispatching, construction coordination, facility management, or related fields preferred
•	Experience working with vendors, subcontractors, and maintenance/service work orders is highly preferred
•	Experience in commercial property maintenance, construction, or facilities operations is an advantage

title: Cofounder, GTM | AI-native Recruiting as a Service
description:
I’m exploring what a recruiting company would look like if it were built from scratch today, with **AI and agents at the core rather than added on top of traditional recruiting workflows.**

The idea sits somewhere between **embedded recruiting and an AI-native service business.**

Companies get recruiting capacity embedded into their team, but instead of scaling the service by simply adding more recruiters, we build agents and automations to handle as much of the operational work as possible: research, sourcing, candidate enrichment, ATS management, follow-ups, reporting, interview support, and other repeatable workflows.

Humans stay focused on the parts where they actually add value: understanding the role, making judgment calls, talking to candidates, building relationships with hiring teams, and making decisions.

The goal isn’t to build another recruiting agency that happens to use AI.

It’s to figure out **what recruiting as a service looks like when humans and AI agents are designed to work together from day one.**

It’s early. There’s an existing recruiting operation to experiment with, real workflows, real searches and real clients, but the new model itself is still something to discover, validate and build.

### The setup

This is **not** a full-time role, and it’s **not** a salaried position.

We’d start building this alongside our current work, validate the model together, and see where it takes us.

* **Equity-based**: potentially 50/50, TBD together.
* **Part-time to start**: no expectation to quit your job tomorrow.
* **Remote**: Europe-based, so we can actually work together without fighting time zones every day.
* **Very early stage**: you’d be joining at the idea/validation stage, with real influence over what we build and how we build it.

I’m looking for a **cofounder, not an employee or a commission-based sales partner.**

### Who I’m looking for

A **GTM-minded cofounder with technical curiosity.**

Most importantly, you should genuinely enjoy GTM: talking to customers, testing positioning, selling something before it’s perfect, figuring out distribution, and turning messy feedback into a clearer business.

You **don**’t need to be an engineer.

But you should be genuinely hands-on with AI. I’m looking for someone who gets excited about figuring out what agents can actually do, where they break, and how we can redesign workflows around them.

Someone who isn’t afraid to open an automation tool, connect an API, experiment with agents, build a scrappy prototype, or learn whatever we need to learn to test an idea.

We don’t need to build perfect technology right now. We need to **build enough to learn.**

### Probably a fit if
* You’re strong in GTM, sales, growth, or business development.
* You’re genuinely hands-on with AI and curious about agents and automation.
* You like **0→1 **environments where the answer isn’t known yet.
* You’re comfortable starting scrappy rather than spending six months building before talking to customers.
* You want to build a company, not join one as an employee.

No laundry list of years of experience, degrees, or specific tools.

I care much more about **how you think, how quickly you learn, what you can figure out, and whether we enjoy building together.**

### About me

I come from People & Recruiting and have spent the last few years building recruiting operations, working with tech companies, and hiring across the US and LATAM.

I currently run a small recruiting operation, which gives us something particularly useful at this stage: **a real environment where we can experiment.**

We can take actual recruiting workflows and ask:

**Should a human be doing this? Could an agent do it? Should they do it together?**

Then build, test, measure, and repeat.

I’m not looking for someone to simply “do sales.”

I’m looking for someone who wants to **co-discover what this company should become and build it together.**

title: Founding GTM Partner
description:
# Founding GTM Partner

**Commonset** is building the management layer for reusable AI capabilities: skills, instructions, tools, workflows, and agents.

As companies adopt AI across more teams, models, and tools, those capabilities are starting to spread everywhere. Organizations need to know what exists, who owns it, which version is current, what has been reviewed and approved, and what people are actually using.

Commonset gives teams one place to manage that.

The product exists. Now I’m looking for the person who wants to build the commercial side of the company with me.

## The role

This is not a traditional sales job.

There is no mature pipeline to inherit, no established sales organization, and no finished playbook to execute. We are still early enough that a meaningful part of the job is figuring out what the playbook should be.

You’ll work directly with me across sales, positioning, customer development, pricing, packaging, partnerships, and GTM strategy.

You should expect to spend a lot of time with potential customers. You’ll identify opportunities, open conversations, run discovery, shape commercial offers, work through the buying process, and close business. You’ll also bring what you learn back into how we position and build the product.

Over time, the goal is to turn those early customer conversations and deals into a repeatable commercial motion.

This role has a lot of autonomy. It also has very little infrastructure around it. You need to be comfortable operating in both.

## Who I’m looking for

I care much more about what you’ve actually done than your title.

You might have been an early salesperson, founder, GTM lead, enterprise AE, commercial leader, or something else entirely.

What I’m looking for is someone who has operated close to the customer and close to the revenue. You should be comfortable working in an environment where the market, messaging, product, and sales process are still being shaped.

Enterprise software experience is useful. Experience selling to engineering, platform, security, AI, data, or technology leadership is particularly relevant.

You should be comfortable owning work end to end rather than operating within a narrow part of a larger sales machine. At this stage, there will be strategic work, customer conversations, outbound work, negotiation, follow-up, and plenty of things that do not fit neatly into a conventional sales job description.

I’m looking for someone who is ambitious about building a company, not simply taking the next sales role.

## What this could become

I’m deliberately calling this a **Founding GTM Partner** rather than VP of Sales.

If we work well together, I want this person to become a core partner in Commonset and own the commercial side of the company. That means real influence over positioning, pricing, customer strategy, product direction, fundraising, and eventually the team we build around GTM.

This is a cofounder-level role for the right person. The exact shape of that partnership should be earned by both sides through working together.

The exact shape of that relationship should be earned by both sides through working together.

## Compensation

This role is structured around ownership and results rather than a large guaranteed salary.

**Equity:** 5–10%, depending on experience, commitment, and fit, with standard vesting.

**Commission:** 12.5% of first-year collected revenue on business you directly originate and close.

**Salary:** No salary initially. As Commonset reaches the point where the company can support salaries, we would move to a normal executive compensation structure.

The commission structure is intended to provide meaningful near-term cash upside while we build revenue. The equity is meaningful because I’m looking for someone who wants to help build the company, not simply sell for it.

This will not be the right role for someone looking for a predictable base salary, an established pipeline, or a mature sales organization.

It may be the right role for someone who wants substantial ownership, enjoys working at the earliest stages of a company, and wants to build the commercial side rather than inherit it.

## About Commonset

Commonset is a control plane for reusable AI capabilities.

Teams are increasingly creating skills, instructions, tools, workflows, and agents across different models, repositories, and platforms. Commonset provides a place to discover and manage those capabilities, establish ownership and provenance, review and approve them, track versions and drift, and make trusted capabilities available across the organization.

The underlying model may change. The capability should endure.

We’re early. There is a real product, a large problem to solve, and a lot we still need to learn about how the market wants to buy it.

That is exactly what this role is here to help figure out.

title: Creative Intern, Brand + Content
description:
**LONA Beauty | NYC-Based
Part-Time | 10–12 Hours/Week | Academic Credit
Start Date: ASAP or Spring 2027**

### **About LONA**
LONA Beauty is skincare for people with more to do than skincare.

Built around High Standards, Low Maintenance, our adaptive, multi-use products combine high-performance skincare with a modern Western point of view. We believe beauty should fit into a full life, not get in the way of one.

We’re a small, founder-led team building LONA from the ground up, and we’re looking for a creative intern who wants to learn by being part of that process.

### **The Role**
We’re looking for an NYC-based Creative Intern, Brand + Content to work closely with LONA’s Co-Founder and creative lead across the visual world of the brand.

This is a hands-on creative internship spanning content creation, social, design, shoots, events, and brand creative. One day you might be editing a Reel, the next working on a social graphic, shooting product outside, pulling references for an upcoming campaign, or capturing content at a LONA event.

You’ll meet weekly with LONA’s Co-Founder and work directly alongside her, gaining exposure to the thinking and decision-making behind building a consumer brand. With nearly 20 years of experience across beauty, fashion, editorial, startups, and consumer brands, she’ll provide hands-on mentorship across creative direction, brand building, design, content, art direction, and social.

The goal is for you to leave the internship with a stronger portfolio, broader creative skill set, and a real understanding of how a brand develops ideas and brings them into the world.

We’re accepting applications on a rolling basis. Candidates may begin as soon as possible, provided their school can approve academic credit for the current semester, or join us for Spring 2027.

The initial commitment is one academic semester, with the opportunity to continue through the full academic year.

This is an unpaid internship for academic credit, so applicants must be currently enrolled in a college or university and eligible to receive credit through their school.

### **What You’ll Do**
Working alongside LONA’s creative lead, you’ll have the opportunity to:
* Shoot photo and video content for social, digital, events, partnerships, and other brand channels
* Edit TikToks, Reels, Stories, founder content, product content, and short-form video
* Support graphic design across social, email, events, presentations, and other brand touchpoints
* Participate in creative concepting and help develop recurring social and content series
* Attend shoots, events, partnerships, and activations to learn how to capture content in real time
* Build moodboards, creative references, shot lists, and visual concepts
* Assist with product and lifestyle photography
* Support layouts, decks, signage, printed pieces, and other brand creative
* Learn how creative work moves from initial idea through feedback, refinement, and execution
* Help organize LONA’s growing library of photo, video, and design assets
* Research emerging visual, social, beauty, fashion, wellness, and cultural trends
* Bring your own ideas, references, and creative discoveries to weekly working sessions
* Occasionally travel upstate or elsewhere nearby for shoots, events, and content

### Who You Are****
We care more about taste, curiosity, initiative, and creative instinct than a long résumé.
You might be a great fit if you:
* Are currently enrolled in a college or university and eligible to receive academic credit
* Are based in NYC and able to regularly collaborate and shoot in person
* Are studying graphic design, art direction, advertising, photography, film, communications, marketing, fashion, or another related creative field
* Have a strong visual eye and a point of view
* Are comfortable shooting content on an iPhone
* Understand how to make content feel elevated without making it feel overly produced
* Can edit short-form video in CapCut, Premiere, or similar tools
* Have experience with Adobe Creative Suite, Figma, Canva, or similar design tools
* Understand TikTok and Instagram but want to think beyond individual posts and learn about the larger brand
* Love beauty, fashion, wellness, travel, hospitality, culture, and the outdoors
* Like getting outside, exploring somewhere new, meeting people, and experiencing things
* Notice details and naturally want to photograph, film, save, or share them
* Are resourceful, curious, and comfortable trying things
* Can take creative direction while also developing your own point of view
* Are organized, dependable, and responsive
* Want to learn what it actually takes to build a brand from the inside
You do not need to be equally strong at photography, video, graphic design, and social. We’re looking for someone with a strong creative foundation who is excited to develop across all of them.

### The Kind of Person We’re Looking For****
LONA is about living more and doing less to get ready for it.

We want someone who connects with that.

Someone who likes getting outside. Who notices the light on a road trip, a great sign in an old motel, the texture of a vintage jacket, the packaging at a roadside store, or the way a product looks tossed into a hiking bag.

Someone who can go from a laptop to a shoot to an event to a weekend upstate and see creative opportunities everywhere.

You should be excited to live the brand as much as create for it.

### What You’ll Learn****
This internship offers direct access to the creative side of building an emerging beauty brand.
Through weekly working sessions, ongoing feedback, and hands-on projects, you’ll learn directly from a founder and creative leader with nearly 20 years of industry experience.
You’ll gain exposure to:
* Brand building and creative direction
* Art direction
* Social and content strategy
* Photography and video
* Graphic design and visual identity
* Creative concepting and campaign development
* Retail and partnership creative
* Events and experiential
* Founder-led brand building
* Giving and receiving creative feedback
* Taking an idea from concept through execution
* Building a cohesive brand across many different touchpoints
And importantly, you’ll have the opportunity to create work that actually goes live and can become part of your portfolio.

### Details****
Location: NYC-based. Regular in-person collaboration is required.

Start Date: ASAP or Spring 2027, depending on candidate availability and school requirements. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Hours: Approximately 10–12 hours per week, with flexibility around class schedules and academic commitments.

Schedule: Hours may shift slightly week to week depending on shoots and events. Some weeks may include evening or weekend events in place of regularly scheduled internship hours.

Commitment: One academic semester to start, with the opportunity to continue through the full academic year.

Compensation: This is an unpaid internship for academic credit. Applicants must be able to receive internship credit through their college or university.

Travel: Occasional local and upstate New York travel may be part of the internship. All required internship-related travel expenses will be covered by LONA, and travel/event time will count toward the internship commitment.

### How to Apply****
Please send us your resume or LinkedIn, social handles, and examples of things you’ve created.

That could be a portfolio, Instagram account, TikTok, photography, short film, design project, school assignment, moodboard, personal project, or something else that shows us your eye.

We care much more about seeing how you think, what you notice, and what you’re drawn to than receiving a perfectly polished portfolio.

And tell us one thing:
What have you seen, made, visited, watched, or discovered recently that inspired you creatively?
