description:
# Founding Account Executive, Local Partnerships

**Nearvana | New York City (Hybrid / Field Sales)**

## About Nearvana

Nearvana is building the future of local discovery — helping travelers discover the best restaurants, experiences, attractions, events, and hidden gems when they arrive in a new city.

Our interactive discovery kiosks are deployed in high-traffic destinations like airports and hotels, connecting travelers with local businesses at the exact moment they’re looking for what to do, where to go, and what to experience.

We’re starting in New York City and building a new discovery and advertising platform that helps local businesses reach millions of visitors.

## About the Role

We’re looking for our first Founding Account Executive to help grow Nearvana’s local business partnerships across NYC.

This is a hands-on sales role for someone who loves meeting customers, building relationships, and closing deals. You’ll work directly with restaurants, bars, hospitality groups, attractions, tour operators, experiences, and brands looking to reach travelers visiting New York City.

As our first sales hire, you won’t just sell — you’ll help build. You’ll work directly with the founders to develop our sales strategy, refine our messaging, understand customer needs, and create the foundation for Nearvana’s revenue engine.

This is a unique opportunity for someone who wants more ownership than a traditional sales role and wants to grow with an early-stage company.

* Conduct in-person visits, product demos, and relationship-building meetings with local businesses
* Own the full sales cycle — prospecting, outreach, presentations, follow-ups, negotiations, and closing
* Build relationships with restaurant owners, hospitality groups, marketers, tourism companies, attractions, and experience operators
* Identify businesses that benefit from reaching travelers, tourists, and new customers visiting NYC
* Develop repeatable sales processes, scripts, outreach strategies, and customer feedback loops
* Track leads, manage your pipeline, and consistently work toward revenue goals

## Who You Are

* You love talking to people and building relationships
* You’re comfortable walking into businesses, introducing yourself, and creating opportunities
* You’re energized by closing deals and helping businesses grow
* You understand how local businesses think and what drives their marketing decisions
* You’re resourceful, persistent, and comfortable figuring things out without a playbook
* You want to be part of building something from the ground up
* You’re excited about startups, travel, hospitality, and the future of local discovery

## Ideal Experience

* Experience selling directly to restaurants, bars, hospitality, entertainment, retail, or small businesses is strongly preferred

title: Director / Lead of Research-to-Market Coherence
description:
PromethistAI builds relational AI agents, digital humans, and human-to-AI interaction built on real behavioral science and economics research, not borrowed marketing language. We’re hiring someone to make sure that foundation, our product, and everything we say externally stay in sync as we scale.

**About the Role**

This is not a Head of Product or Head of Go-to-Market role, and it doesn’t report into either. You’ll sit across all three functions, our conceptual research, the product, and everything that carries it to the market (sales, marketing, partnerships, customer success) — and own the process that keeps them aligned. You’ll be the person who flags it when a product feature has no research behind it anymore, or when a public claim has outrun its evidence — including when that means pushing back on the CEO.

**What You’ll Do**

* Own and maintain a structured record of every research claim the company builds on, including its evidentiary strength and status (established, working hypothesis, unproven).
* Maintain traceability between that research and specific product decisions and external claims, and flag any that can’t be traced.
* Monitor market feedback — win/loss data, customer conversations, analyst and press reaction — and route it to the right owner: noise, a product issue, or a research question.
* Run a recurring cross-functional review that reconciles research, product, and go-to-market against each other.
* Translate technical or research-heavy material into language product and sales teams can act on, and translate ambiguous market signals into specific, testable questions.

**What You’ll Need**

* 3+ years combining applied research, editorial, or strategy work with hands-on execution — not research alone, and not strategy alone.
* Working fluency in how to evaluate evidence: distinguishing an established finding from a reasonable inference from an unproven claim, and comfortable saying which is which.
* Demonstrated ability to write clearly for a non-specialist audience without oversimplifying the underlying idea.
* Comfort operating cross-functionally without formal authority over the teams you’re coordinating.
* Advanced degree in a relevant field (behavioral science, economics, sociology, HCI) or equivalent practical experience.

**Nice to Have**

* Editorial experience at a publication that translates research for a business audience (e.g., Harvard Business Review, MIT Sloan Management Review).
* Background in applied forecasting or calibrated reasoning (e.g., superforecasting).
* Prior experience in a small company (<50 people) building a process like this from scratch.

**How to Apply**

In place of a cover letter, we’ll send you one dense claim from our own research. Take an hour and return two things: a version a salesperson could use in a customer conversation, and a version a product manager could act on — plus a short note on what additional evidence you’d want before fully trusting the claim. It’s a more accurate preview of the job than a résumé, and we’ll evaluate it the same way we’ll evaluate your work once you’re here.

**Location**
Remote

PromethistAI is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other legally protected status.

title: manual QA intern (android + iOS)
description:
we're a team of IIT Roorkee grads building bite-sized multiplayer games for 16-20 year olds, to be played in-person.

if you're alone and bored, you scroll. if you're together with your besties and bored, you all just... scroll. together, apart.

we believe screen time spent scrolling content has hit a peak. people increasingly want to be offline, doing shared experiences with friends. for college and school kids, a lot of their daily dead time is already spent together - so the question we're trying to answer is: can we convert that dead time into fun shared moments and experiences?

iykyk is our first shot at it: a fast-paced word-guessing game you play by passing one phone around, that captures funny clips for you to send to the group chat after.

if you get why this needs to exist, help us make sure it works on every phone, every time.

**here's what you'd do**:

title: Growth Marketer
description:
### **Internship Opportunity**

Halfyolk is hiring a Full Stack Growth Marketer who acts as an embedded growth partner for a specific Business Unit. This is not a support function—it is a high-impact, individual contributor role. You will sit alongside the Business Unit leader, translate their growth strategy into a campaign-ready Go-To-Market (GTM) plan, and execute it end-to-end.

Your primary mandate is digital marketing: designing, launching, and optimizing campaigns that drive qualified pipelines and measurable revenue. You will be supported by specialist teams for events, inside sales, marketing operations, and technology—but you are the one who connects strategy to tactics, tactics to pipeline, and pipeline to revenue. You run the campaigns and directly execute against your content calendar.

### **What you will own**

**Digital Campaign Strategy & Execution**
Design, build, and run digital campaigns from brief to deployment—including content marketing, email sequences, paid media, social amplification, webinars, and podcasts.

**Lifecycle Ownership**
Lead the full campaign lifecycle:  audience definition, messaging, channel selection, creative production, launch, optimization, and post-campaign analysis.

**Data-Driven Choices**
Use data to decide what campaigns to run, what to kill, and where to double down. You know the right questions to ask before the data tells you anything.

**Content Creation**
Produce compelling content—thought leadership, sales collateral, and digital assets—with a strong editorial eye. You can write a persuasive whitepaper and a tight email subject line for the same campaign.

**Account-Based Marketing (ABM)**
Run targeted 1:1, 1:few, and 1:many ABM campaigns within existing and new target accounts to land and accelerate new revenue.

**GTM Planning & Revenue Accountability** 

**Strategic Partnership**
Partner with the Business Unit leader to convert Business Unit goals into a concrete market plan with a clear Ideal Customer Profile (ICP), tailored messaging, optimal channels, and pipeline targets.

**Pipeline Metrics**
Own the marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline for the Business Unit—measured in opportunities created and revenue generated, not just activity volume.

**Funnel Tracking**
Track funnel conversion metrics (MQL → SQL → SAL), pipeline coverage, cost per qualified lead, and marketing-influenced win rates.

**Market Insights** 
Conduct gap analyses across value propositions, competitive positioning, customer demand signals, and industry trends to inform quarterly priorities.


**Collaboration & Alignment**
You will coordinate with and be supported by internal specialist teams—your role is to direct, brief, and ensure alignment, not to own these functions outright

**Event Planning** 
Brief the Events team on Business Unit-specific event strategy to build seamless, pipeline-feeding events.

**Inside Sales Coordination**
Align campaign follow-up sequences with the Inside Sales team to maximize lead conversion.

**Marketing Technology** 
Work with MarTech and Data Analytics for reporting, attribution, and platform support as a power user, not an administrator.

**Brand Ecosystem**
Ensure Business Unit communications are consistently on-brand, while activating partner and alliance marketing to amplify reach.

### What We Are Looking For****

**Strategy-to-Revenue Thinking**
You can take a business objective, translate it into a marketing strategy, decompose it into campaigns, and trace the outcome back to pipeline and revenue. You think in funnels, not just formats.

**End-to-End Execution**
You have personally built and run multi-channel campaigns—not just briefed them to an agency or external team. From audience targeting through creative production to performance analysis, you have done the legwork.

**Data-Driven Decision Making**
You are fluent in marketing analytics. You make investment decisions based on ROI, attribution, and pipeline coverage—not gut feel.

**AI-First Mindset**
You actively use AI in your daily workflow for content production, research, personalization, and campaign iteration. This is a core part of how you work. You will be enabled with Halfyolk’s internal AI platforms and agents to accelerate your impact.

**Industry Acumen**
You understand B2B professional services and technology verticals deeply enough to develop relevant messaging, target ICPs, and create compelling, industry-specific campaigns.

**Cross-Functional Partnership**
You thrive in a matrix environment—working across a Business Unit leader, a central marketing function, sales, solutioning, and external partners simultaneously.

### What "AI-First" Means at Halfyolk
This is not a checkbox. We expect you to actively use AI tools as a daily force multiplier. Halfyolk will provide you with AI platforms and custom agents as needed to support your marketing judgment. You will use AI to:

Draft, iterate, and personalize content at 3–5x the velocity of traditional approaches, focusing your time on defining the right message rather than manual content creation.

Synthesize market research, competitive intelligence, and account signals faster.Accelerate campaign production, reducing dependency on external agencies and specialist queues.

Analyze performance data to surface actionable patterns.

The right candidate is already working this way—experimenting with prompts, building workflows around AI tools, and rethinking how marketing gets done.

**Qualifications**
* No specific years of B2B, SaaS, or tech experience required—we care about your drive, capabilities, and output.
* A strong interest or foundational background in digital marketing, growth marketing, or full-stack marketing principles.
* Demonstrated ability to take a general marketing idea, break it down into tactical execution steps, and track its results.
* Hands-on proficiency with AI tools for content creation, brainstorming, or productivity (not merely awareness of them).
* Basic familiarity or an eagerness to learn modern marketing platforms (such as HubSpot, Salesforce CRM, ABM tools, or web analytics).
* Excellent writing ability and sharp editorial judgment.A massive bias toward speed, iteration, and execution. You ship.

title: Technical Customer Engineer (Product Support)
description:
**Team:** Customer Success / Engineering

**Mindset:** *Do you like writing code to solve customer problems? Read on.*

 

### **About Nametag**

Nametag is a category leader in identity verification, security, and account protection. We are building a world-class, remote-first team where engineers thrive in both technical depth and customer engagement. We value intellectual curiosity, collaboration, and a strong sense of responsibility in protecting enterprise security.

 

### **About the Role**

We’re hiring a Technical Customer Engineer to serve as the technical escalation point for customer-reported issues. This is an engineering-adjacent role focused on diagnosing complex integration problems, scripting and prototyping solutions, and collaborating directly with our core engineering team to drive fixes into production.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys debugging, writing lightweight code, and working closely with customers to unblock them quickly. This goes beyond ticket processing - it’s hands-on technical problem solving with real ownership.

 

### **Responsibilities**

- Act as the first technical responder for escalated customer issues, particularly those blocking integrations or deployments.
- Debug in the wild - inspecting API payloads, webhook logs, OAuth exchanges, and race conditions that surface only under real-world load.
- Provide interim solutions such as code snippets, pull requests, documentation updates, or configuration guidance.
- Bridge the gap between customer and engineering: reproduce issues, isolate root causes, and ensure fixes are fully validated before release.
- Gather structured context and relay actionable insights to engineering for long-term fixes.
- Recommend integration best practices across authentication flows, REST APIs, and IAM platforms.
- Improve internal support tooling, documentation, and runbooks based on recurring patterns.
- Surface common pain points and influence product priorities.

### **Tech You’ll Work With**

- You need to be comfortable in our primary languages (Go, Typescript), as well as some experience in a few of the other common platforms our customers use (Python, Ruby, that kind of thing).
- REST APIs, OAuth, Webhooks (reference: getnametag.com/docs)
- Authentication and identity workflows (OIDC, SSO, Token Exchanges)
- Scripting or debugging tools in Python, Node.js, Bash, or similar environments
- Identity platforms: Okta, Microsoft Entra, Duo, Auth0, Ping, and custom IAM stacks.
- Systems: AWS, CloudFormation, Postgres, Docker, GitHub Actions, modern observability stacks

 

### **Qualifications**

***Work Authorization (Required):** Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without current or future need for visa sponsorship. This is a firm requirement. The technical qualifications below are guidelines.*

- 2–5 years in technical support engineering, solutions engineering, DevOps, SRE, or adjacent engineering roles.
- Client facing experience - ability to communicate clearly and empathetically with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Strong debugging skills across APIs, backend integrations, or authentication workflows.
- Comfort writing lightweight scripts or tools to diagnose and unblock issues.
- Familiarity with IAM platforms such as Okta, Microsoft Entra, Duo, or similar.

 

### **Who Will Succeed in This Role If**

- You like solving real customer problems more than sitting behind abstract tickets.
- You don’t mind hopping between console logs, Slack threads, and cURL commands.
- You stay calm when something is broken, and you don’t stop until it’s understood.

### **Why Join**

You’ll join a fast-moving team where customer impact is immediate and visible. You’ll collaborate directly with engineering leadership, shape how we scale technical support, and build a reputation as a go-to problem solver.

If you’re the person others call when things break - let’s talk.

 

**Compensation & Benefits**

- Competitive salary: $120,000 - $160,000
- Potential equity in a high-growth company
- Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
- Flexible time off policies
- 401(k) program with employer matching
- Remote-first culture with opportunities for in-person collaboration during quarterly team off-sites

title: Senior Backend Engineer — E-commerce Platform
description:
**Position Details:**

Employment: Full-time, permanent W-2 employee.

Location: Fully remote within the United States; no office attendance or relocation required.

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 40 working hours per week. Saturday and Sunday off.

Working hours: Flexible start and finish times, with availability from 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Central Time for collaboration. Lunch breaks are outside working hours.

Base salary: $175,000–$205,000 USD annually, before taxes, paid biweekly.

**About the Role:**

You will design and develop the backend services behind ParcelNest Hub, with a focus on order processing, inventory synchronization, and third-party integrations. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with ownership of technical decisions, from initial design through deployment and ongoing improvement.

You will work closely with Engineering, Product, and Customer Support to turn real customer problems into reliable software.

**What You’ll Do:**

1. Build and maintain backend services and APIs for orders, inventory, and shipping workflows.
2. Develop integrations with e-commerce platforms and shipping providers, including authentication, webhooks, and data synchronization.
3. Design background processing that handles retries, duplicate events, and third-party service failures safely.
4. Improve database performance, data integrity, and the reliability of customer-facing features.
5. Own projects from technical proposal and implementation through testing, rollout, and monitoring.
6. Investigate production issues during working hours and address their underlying causes.
7. Review code, document important decisions, and mentor teammates through pairing and constructive feedback.
8. Work with Product to balance customer needs, delivery timelines, and long-term maintainability.

**What You’ll Bring:**

1. At least five years of professional backend software engineering experience.
2. Strong production experience with Python and a framework such as FastAPI or Django.
3. Strong SQL skills and experience designing, maintaining, and optimizing PostgreSQL databases.
4. Experience building APIs and integrating with external services.
5. Practical understanding of asynchronous processing, message queues, idempotency, and failure recovery.
6. Experience deploying and supporting applications in a cloud environment, preferably AWS.
7. Confidence writing automated tests, reviewing code, and using logs and metrics to diagnose problems.
8. Clear written and spoken English and the ability to collaborate effectively in a remote team.
9. Experience independently delivering a substantial feature or service from design to production

A computer science degree is welcome but not required. We value relevant experience and demonstrated engineering judgment.

**Nice to have:**

Experience with Shopify or WooCommerce integrations, fulfillment systems, multi-tenant SaaS products, Redis, Terraform, or application observability.

You do not need experience with every tool in our stack to apply.

Our Technology Stack

Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, AWS, Docker, Terraform, and GitHub Actions

**Compensation and Working Expectations:**

The base salary range is $175,000–$205,000. Your offer will reflect relevant experience, system design skills, and the level of responsibility you can take on. The same range applies across eligible U.S. locations.

This is a salaried position. The stated range is base pay and does not include the value of benefits. No variable bonus or equity award is included in this sample package. Compensation is reviewed annually.

We plan work around a 40-hour week. This position does not include an after-hours on-call rotation or scheduled evening or weekend work.

**Benefits:**

* Medical, dental, and vision: Coverage begins on the first day of the month following hire. ParcelNest pays 90% of employee premiums and 50% of dependent premiums.
* 401(k): Eligible after 90 days, with a dollar-for-dollar employer match on the first 4% of eligible pay you contribute. Employer contributions vest immediately.
* Paid time off: 20 vacation days accrued annually, plus 7 paid sick days and 10 paid company holidays.
* Parental leave: 8 weeks of paid leave after 12 months of employment.
* Life and disability insurance: Company-paid basic life and short-term disability coverage.
* Remote equipment: Company-provided laptop, monitor, and accessories, plus a one-time $750 home-office allowance.
* Internet support: $75 monthly reimbursement toward home internet.
* Professional development: Up to $1,500 annually for approved courses, certifications, books, or conferences.
* Paid onboarding: A structured introduction to the product, architecture, and development process, with an assigned engineering buddy.

**How We Work Together:**

We value thoughtful engineering, clear communication, and people who follow through. You will have room to work independently, with teammates available to discuss a design or help investigate a difficult problem.

We document decisions, keep meetings focused, and give feedback respectfully. Asking for help is welcome. When something breaks, we focus on understanding the failure and improving the system.

You can contribute fully whether you are outgoing or more reserved. Social activities are optional, and personal time is respected.

**Your First 90 Days:**

1. First 30 days: Learn the product and architecture, set up your development environment, and ship an initial improvement with support from your onboarding buddy.
2. By 60 days: Own a scoped backend feature or integration improvement through design, testing, and release.
3. By 90 days: Independently lead a project and contribute a practical improvement to reliability, performance, or the development process.

Success is measured by reliable delivery, sound technical decisions, maintainable code, and effective collaboration.

**Hiring Process:**

1. A 30-minute introductory conversation about your experience and expectations.
2. A 60-minute practical coding and debugging session using a small sample service.
3. A 60-minute system design discussion based on an e-commerce workflow.
4. A 30-minute conversation with the Head of Engineering about collaboration and ownership.

No unpaid take-home project is required. The target process takes two to three weeks, with time for your questions at every stage.

**Eligibility and Application:**

Candidates must reside in the United States and be authorized to work there. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

An English-language résumé is required. A LinkedIn profile, GitHub profile, or examples of relevant work are optional; a cover letter is not required.

ParcelNest welcomes applicants from different backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process.

title: Founding AI Research Engineer: Agent Harness & Model Systems
description:
**COMPENSATION — READ THIS FIRST **

Before launch and seed round (approx. months 4–6): equity-only. A founding-team equity grant negotiable based on experience, scope, and contribution. Standard vest and cliff. 
After launch and seed round: competitive base salary in the $220k–$320k range, ongoing equity participation through refresh grants, and other benefits. 
Why we lead with this: we value your and our time. We are looking for people who want to make their mark. Astoria is building the most ambitious product in the category. The pre-launch and pre-seed round phase is founder-mode: small team, high intensity, outsized equity. This role is for someone who sees the equity as the primary upside — not a supplement — because they believe what we're building will define the category. 

**The 90-Second Version **

We are in stealth and will help you with your diligence. Astoria AI is building an agentic runtime for human potential. Multiple specialized AI agents serve candidates and companies across the entire hiring and talent lifecycle: career strategy, networking intelligence, verified matching, compliance-native hiring, onboarding, engagement, retention, and workforce planning. 

We are attacking a market that is structurally broken in ways that damage real people. 44% of resumes contain fabrications. ATS keyword filters reject 88% of qualified candidates. 27% of posted jobs are ghost jobs. Meanwhile the regulatory wave — Mobley v. Workday, the EU AI Act, FCRA lawsuits against Eightfold — is forcing every enterprise buyer to ask whether their hiring AI creates legal risk or eliminates it. 

Nobody has fixed this. The incumbents can't, because their business models depend on the broken parts. That is the opening. 

Here is the technical thesis behind this role. Multiple agents making consequential decisions about people's careers do not become trustworthy because the underlying model is clever. They become trustworthy because of the harness they run inside — the runtime that governs how they call tools, assemble context, hand off to one another, fail, retry, escalate to a human, and leave a record you can replay in front of a regulator. Agent quality is dominated by harness quality. A good model in an excellent harness beats an excellent model in a bad one, every time, and we intend to have the evaluations that prove it. 

You own that harness. You also own the second half that feeds it: proprietary domain models that natively speak the language of work, and that are trained, tuned, and evaluated specifically for how they behave inside the harness rather than on a static benchmark. 

 
**WHAT WE MEAN BY "THE HARNESS" **

The harness is everything between raw model weights and an agent that can be trusted with someone's career. 
Concretely: tool-call contracts and schema-validated structured outputs; context assembly, compaction, and long-session memory; state and handoff between agents; routing decisions about which model serves which seat; retries, fallbacks, and a real failure taxonomy; latency and cost budgets enforced per call; guardrails and human-review gates on consequential actions; tracing and replay; and the in-loop evaluation that scores all of it continuously rather than at release time. 
In a hiring product, the harness is also where compliance lives. Under the EU AI Act, hiring is a high-risk category; post-Mobley, every enterprise counsel asks the same question. The ability to say "here is the exact trace of why this candidate was surfaced, which tools ran, what the model saw, and where a human signed off" is not a logging feature — it is the Compliance Shield, and it is built in the harness. What you build is simultaneously engineering infrastructure and the thing that closes enterprise deals. 

Most teams let the harness accrete as glue code between a framework and a prompt. We treat it as the core system of the company, and we are hiring a founding engineer to own it as such.  
What You'll Own 

**The harness **

The orchestration runtime: planner/executor and router/specialist patterns, multi-agent handoff, escalation paths, and the state model that makes long-running agent sessions coherent. 
Tool-call contracts: schema-validated structured outputs, function-calling reliability, a documented failure taxonomy, and retry/fallback behavior that degrades gracefully instead of hallucinating through an error. 

Context engineering: assembly, compaction, and retrieval policy for long sessions — deciding what the model sees, in what order, under what token budget, and proving those choices with evals rather than intuition. 

Model routing: which seat gets which model, with latency and cost budgets enforced per call, and the policy for escalating from the fast specialist to the deliberative model when the stakes warrant it. 
Guardrails and human-in-the-loop gates on consequential actions, with confidence thresholds that are measured, not guessed. 

Observability: tracing, replay, and structured decision records — so any agent action can be reconstructed months later for an audit, a customer escalation, or a regression hunt. 

In-harness evaluation as the company's quality bar: agents scored inside the live loop of tools, retries, and guardrails — not on static prompts — with harness-level regression gates in CI that block releases. 
The Compliance Shield surface: auditable traces and fairness instrumentation that ship as enterprise-facing product artifacts, documented and re-run on every release. 
The models 

Run the base-model bake-off: evaluate open-weight candidates (Qwen-, Mistral-, DeepSeek-class and peers) on our tasks, our license constraints, and — decisively — their behavior inside our harness. Write the recommendation memo the company acts on. 

Tool-use and agentic fine-tuning: train models that call tools correctly, respect schemas, know when to abstain, and behave predictably across multi-step sessions. This is where the two halves of the job meet. 

Build the data engine: corpus curation, deduplication, decontamination, PII scrubbing, quality filtering, and synthetic data generation for HR and recruiting domains. 
Run continued pretraining on the curated HR corpus, and instruction-tune (SFT) on Astoria's task formats — matching, screening, requisition drafting, structured extraction, career reasoning. 
Preference-tune on real hiring-outcome data (DPO-class methods and successors); own the choice of method and the honesty of the measurement. 

Distill and quantize the recruiting specialist to its serving budget; own tokens-per-second and cost-per-call as first-class metrics, and the inference stack (vLLM-class) it runs on. 
Own training infrastructure on rented GPUs: multi-node runs (FSDP/DeepSpeed-class), checkpointing, spot-interruption recovery, experiment tracking, and the training-cost budget. 
Maintain the model registry and versioning discipline: every deployed model has a card, an eval report, and a rollback path. 

Write it down: internal tech reports, runtime contracts, and decision memos the founders act on. When it serves the product, publish — we will support it. 
 
**A NOTE ON THE WORD "PROPRIETARY" **

Proprietary here does not mean pretraining a frontier model from scratch. Bloomberg spent millions training a 50B-parameter model from scratch and watched a general-purpose API model beat it on most public benchmarks within a year — while open-weight LoRA fine-tunes matched it for a few hundred dollars of compute.  
Proprietary means the things that actually compound: our harness (the runtime, contracts, and traces no competitor can copy off a model card), our data (a curated HR corpus and outcome-labeled hiring data nobody can buy), our post-training (recipes that survive any base-model swap), and our evaluations (task suites and fairness slices that define what "better" means in this domain). If that framing reads as obvious to you, you are who this posting is for.  
What You Bring 

**The must-haves **

- 4+ years of professional ML or software engineering, with recent hands-on work on agentic systems that ran in production and that real users or systems depended on. 
- AI harness experience — required. You have built or worked deep inside the harness that turns a model into a working agent: tool-calling loops, structured outputs, context management, state, retries, guardrails, human-review gates. You know from experience that a model is only as good as its behavior in-harness, and you evaluate accordingly. 
- Agentic architecture — required. You have designed, or trained models for, multi-agent systems: orchestration patterns, planner/executor and router/specialist splits, agent memory and state, tool routing, escalation between agents. You understand that a model is trained for the seat it occupies — a planner, a router, and a high-volume executor make different demands on the same weights. 
- Agent evaluation in the loop: you have built or run evaluations that score agents on multi-step trajectories, not single-turn outputs, and you have opinions about what makes such an eval trustworthy. 
- Production instincts for reliability: tracing, failure taxonomies, graceful degradation, latency and cost budgets. You have been paged for an agent that silently did the wrong thing, and you fixed the system, not the prompt. 
- Hands-on LLM post-training in the last two years — SFT at minimum; preference tuning in anger a strong plus; tool-use or function-calling fine-tuning ideal. 
- PyTorch fluency and the open post-training stack: Hugging Face transformers/datasets/PEFT and at least one of TRL, Axolotl, or LLaMA-Factory — or your own equivalent you can defend. 
- Real distributed-training experience: you have run multi-GPU jobs, debugged OOMs and loss spikes, survived checkpoint corruption and spot preemption, and can tell the story. 
- Data seriousness: you treat the corpus as part of the product — dedup, decontamination, PII handling, quality filtering are craft to you, not chores. 
- Paper-to-code speed: hand you a post-training or agent-architecture paper on Monday, see a working implementation against our system within the week. 
- Enough infrastructure to be dangerous: Docker, cloud GPU fleets, experiment tracking (W&B/MLflow-class), CI. 
- Clear async writing. Tech reports, model cards, runtime contracts, and decision memos are half this job's output. 

**Strong signals **

We are especially interested in candidates who can show: 

- An agent system you built that ran in production, described in the language of someone who owned its failures — what broke in the harness, what you changed, how you knew it was fixed. 
- Contributions to harness-layer tooling: agent frameworks, orchestration libraries, lm-evaluation-harness-class eval stacks, SWE-bench-style task harnesses, or tracing and observability tools for LLM systems. 
- An agent or model evaluation suite other people adopted — especially one that scores multi-step trajectories. 
- A model you tuned specifically for tool use or agentic behavior, with in-harness numbers to show for it. 
- A Hugging Face profile with fine-tuned models or adapters that strangers actually download — with model cards carrying honest eval tables. 
- A public reproduction of a post-training or agent paper, including where your numbers diverged from the authors' and why. 
- Contributions to the training stack: TRL, Axolotl, vLLM, llama.cpp, LLaMA-Factory. 
- Strong placements in Kaggle LLM competitions — bounded compute, leaderboard evals, maximum capability squeezed out. 
- Technical writing others cite: a blog, a tech report, a well-argued issue thread. 

**Nice to have** 

- Experience with MCP or comparable tool-integration protocols, and opinions about where they help and where they get in the way. 
- RLHF/RLAIF beyond DPO-class methods; reward-model experience; RL on agent trajectories. 
- Distillation and quantization to production (AWQ/GPTQ/GGUF-class) with measured quality-latency trade-offs. 
- Tokenizer work, corpus-scale data pipelines, or dataset releases. 
- Safety, red-teaming, or fairness-evaluation experience — especially anything adjacent to regulated domains. 
- Multilingual training or evaluation. 
- Workshop or conference publications. Nice. Genuinely optional. 

**What this role is not **

Not prompt engineering — that craft lives with our agentic engineer, and you will be building the system that makes prompts matter less. Not gluing together an off-the-shelf agent framework and calling it a runtime; we expect you to have opinions about where the frameworks fall short at this level of consequence. Not frontier-scale pretraining — there is no ten-thousand-GPU cluster here, and we think that's the right call. Not publication-first research — we will support publishing when it serves the product, but the product is the point. And not fine-tuning-by-managed-button: if your training experience is exclusively a closed platform's upload form, this will be a hard job. 

 
**How to Apply **

A short note — half a page is plenty. Not a cover letter. Tell us what you think of the harness thesis above, or push back on it. We are looking for a point of view, not enthusiasm. 
An agent system you have owned. Three sentences: what it did, how it failed in the harness, and what you changed in the system to fix it. 
A link to something we can inspect — a model, adapter, eval suite, or harness-layer contribution, with numbers attached. A model card, a W&B report, or a repo beats a resume line. 
 
Astoria AI is an equal opportunity employer. We especially encourage applications from engineers and researchers whose own career paths have been non-linear — you will understand this mission intuitively, because you have lived the problem we are solving. 

 
Astoria AI is the operating system for human potential. The place where potential finds its purpose.

title: Account Executive - EST/CST
description:
### About Pepper
Pepper is the system for food distributors’ critical business operations, serving the $1T industry we all rely on to feed us every day. Our customers are the family-owned, regional, and specialty wholesalers supplying the restaurants in your neighborhood.
We’re the category leader, and we just closed a $50M Series C, backed by Lead Edge, ICONIQ, and Greylock. Our agentic products handle the messy and manual workflows that the industry has run on for decades, rebuilding how distributors set prices, take orders, collect payments, and find new customers. Our platform marks a fundamental shift in what’s possible for distributors. We're growing quickly, with a large, untapped market in front of us, and a slew of new products on the way.

### Account Executive at Pepper
As an Account Executive, you’ll own a territory of independent food distributors and run full sales cycles from first conversation to signed contract. You’ll sell directly to the people who run these businesses—decision-makers who move quickly, expect you to understand their business, and partner with us for years when you get it right.

### What You’ll Do
* Own and close full cycles with independent food distributors: prospecting, inbound follow-up, discovery, demos, negotiation, and contracts.
* Learn how independent distributors actually run:ordering, pricing, collections, sales motions and show how Pepper can help distributors meet their goals.
* Sell an expanding platform: lead with the product that fits and set customers up for what we launch next across pricing, ordering, payments, and sales.
* Bring customer signals to Product and shape what gets built next.
* Work closely with SDRs, Sales Engineers, and Customer Success to turn pipeline into closed deals efficiently, and closed deals into successful customers.
* Keep HubSpot clean so the team can move with you.
* Use AI creatively to improve your workflows and outcomes for your customers.


### What You’ll Bring
* 2+ years in B2B sales with at least one year in a closing role, and a track record as a top 10% performer. 
* Experience selling to owner-led, mid-market businesses: you’ve sold to the owner-operator who signs the check and knows how to earn trust with people who don’t buy software often.
* Alignment with, or a strong trajectory toward, our deal profile: roughly $900K annual quota, $30K+ ARR deals, 60–90 day cycles. 
* Strong consultative fundamentals: discovery that gets to the real problem, demos that follow the conversation, and discipline to run a process end to end.
* Fluent in HubSpot and Gong, and creative with AI tools in your day-to-day.
* Vertical SaaS experience in blue-collar industries (restaurants, field services, trades, agriculture) is a strong plus—so is time in food distribution, foodservice, or supply chain, software or not.
* Hunger and resourcefulness: founding AE, entrepreneurial, or early-stage experience is a plus.

### Location
Remote-first within the US, with approximately 25% travel. This role covers a Southeast territory; Eastern or Central time zone candidates are strongly preferred.

### Why This Role

title: Security Engineer
description:
## **Join the Sleep Fitness Movement**

At Eight Sleep, we’re on a mission to fuel human potential through optimal sleep. As the world’s first sleep fitness company, we’re redefining what it means to be well-rested and building the most advanced hardware, software, and AI technology to make it possible. Our products power peak mental, physical, and emotional performance by transforming every night of sleep into a personalized, data-driven recovery experience. We are trusted by high performers, professional athletes, and health-conscious consumers in over 30 countries worldwide. Recognized as one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies in 2019, 2022, and 2023, and twice named to TIME's “Best Inventions of the Year.” We operate like a high-performance team: fast, focused, and motivated by impact. We don’t just ship; we iterate, refine, and obsess over the details that help our members sleep better and wake up stronger.

 

Every role at Eight Sleep is a chance to create cutting-edge technology, collaborate with world-class talent, and help shape a future where sleep isn’t passive - it’s a powerful tool for living better. If you’re tired of the ordinary and driven to build at the edge of what’s possible, this is your moment. Join us and lead the movement that’s transforming how the world sleeps and what we’re all capable of when we wake up.

 
## **High Standards. No Apologies.**

We operate with intensity because our mission demands it. At Eight Sleep, we bring the same mindset as the world’s top performers: focused, relentless, and always pushing to be in the top 1% of our craft. Think Kobe Bryant’s mamba mentality, applied to bold ideas, next-gen tech, and flawless execution. This isn’t a 9-to-5. Our team is deeply committed, often putting in 60+ hours a week –not because we’re told to, but because we’re invested. We’re here to build fast, push limits, and deliver without compromise. If you thrive under pressure and want to do the most meaningful work of your career, you’ll feel right at home. If you’re looking for something easier –this isn’t it.

 
## **The Role**

You will work very closely with backend, firmware, and data engineers, with R&D and clinical teams, and directly with the Head of Security.

We are looking for an experienced Security Engineer who embraces an AI-first culture to enable them to scale beyond themselves. This is a generalist role with real ownership from day one: various portions of the security program including corporate IT, identity, AI Security, enterprise, and cloud. The ideal candidate has been "the security person" on a small team before — someone who takes whatever comes up, automates the second occurrence of anything, and writes clearly enough that engineers, auditors, and executives can all act on their work.

 
## **How you’ll contribute**

- Google Workspace administration, device management, and the SaaS access lifecycle — onboarding, offboarding, and access reviews that hold up in an audit.
- Keep compliance green with code, remediate failing tests at the infrastructure level, extend Vanta with custom tests, and automate evidence collection.
- Partner with internal teams to find secure solutions to enable them to achieve the company’s goals.
- Vulnerability management and endpoint management on the company’s corporate fleet.
- Build processes for secure and ethical AI in corporate environments to minimize shadow AI/IT.
- Act as the security team's second brain: triage inbound requests, run security reviews of internal tools, and run point on incidents
- Tackle new security engineering projects.

## **What you need to succeed**

- AI-first mindset. We empower the team with the best tools available to scale beyond themselves
- 4+ years across security and/or IT engineering, including time on a small team where you owned whatever came up
- Experience operating a SIEM (Datadog Cloud SIEM, Panther, Splunk, Elastic, or similar)
- Corporate IT fluency: Google Workspace admin, MDM, identity lifecycle
- Scripting ability (Python or similar)
- Clear security writing and documentation: triage notes, runbooks, and audit evidence that engineers, agents, auditors, and executives can act on

## **Bonus points for**

- Vanta (or Drata) ownership through a real audit cycle for SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA
- Experience in a regulated or health-adjacent environment
- Incident response experience beyond tabletop exercises
 
## **Why join Eight Sleep?**

**Innovation in a culture of excellence**

Join us in a workplace where innovation isn’t just encouraged - it’s a standard. Our flagship product, the Pod, is a testament to our culture of excellence, beloved by hundreds of thousands of customers worldwide. At Eight Sleep, you will be part of a team that continuously pushes the boundaries of technology in sleep fitness.

 

**Immediate responsibility and accelerated career growth**

From your first day, you’ll take on substantial responsibilities that have a direct impact on our core business and product success. We are a small team that empowers you to own your projects and see the tangible effects of your efforts, enhancing both your professional growth and our company’s trajectory. Your path will be challenging but rewarding, perfect for those who thrive in fast-paced environments aiming for high standards.

 

**Collaboration with exceptional talent**

Work alongside other bright minds like you: at Eight Sleep exceptional intelligence and a passion for breakthroughs are the norms. Our team members are not only experts in their fields but also avid innovators who thrive in our dynamic, fast-paced environment.

 

**Equitable compensation and continuous equity investment**

We extend equity participation to every full-time team member, recognizing and rewarding your direct contributions to our success. This includes periodic equity refreshments based on performance, ensuring that as Eight Sleep grows and succeeds, so do you – perfectly aligning your achievements with the broader triumphs of the company.

 

**Your own Pod - and other great benefits**

- Every Eight Sleep employee receives the very product that defines our mission: a Pod of their own. If you join us you’ll get your own [Pod](https://www.eightsleep.com/), along with*:
- Full access to health, vision, and dental insurance for you and your dependents
- Supplemental life insurance
- Flexible PTO
- Commuter benefits to ease your daily commute
- Paid parental leave

*List of benefits may vary depending on your location

 

At Eight Sleep we continually celebrate the diverse community different individuals cultivate. As an equal opportunity employer, we stay true to our values by ensuring everyone feels they can flourish and grow. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

title: Senior Account Executive
description:
As an Account Executive, you will be responsible for proactively creating and closing new business with roofing contractors. You’ll own the full sales cycle — from prospecting and cold outreach through discovery, demo, negotiation, and close.

You’ll act as a consultant to contractors, uncovering the challenges they face when running their businesses and showing them how Roofr can help them work more efficiently, win more jobs, and grow their businesses. You’ll build and manage your own pipeline, develop strong relationships with prospects, and create a world-class buying experience from first touch through close.

### **What you'll get to do:**

- Own the full sales cycle from prospecting and outbound outreach through discovery, demo, negotiation, and close, while also working qualified inbound leads provided by Roofr to maximize every opportunity
- Build and maintain your own pipeline through consistent outbound prospecting across phone, email, and other channels
- Research target accounts and identify the right prospects, decision-makers, and business opportunities
- Create personalized outreach that speaks to the unique challenges and goals of roofing contractors
- Cold call and engage prospects to generate new conversations and qualified opportunities
- Qualify prospects through thorough discovery, uncovering their pain points, business needs, priorities, and buying motivations
- Conduct tailored demos that connect Roofr’s solutions to each prospect’s specific business challenges
- Educate prospects on Roofr’s products and services and clearly communicate the value and ROI of the platform
- Effectively manage multiple opportunities across different stages of the sales cycle and consistently follow up to move deals forward
- Develop and execute thoughtful closing strategies to convert qualified opportunities into customers
- Consistently achieve and exceed revenue and activity targets
- Work independently, effectively prioritize your time, and maintain a high level of outbound activity
- Maintain accurate CRM records, activity, and pipeline hygiene at all times
- Become a champion for Roofr’s products and stay up to date on our evolving solutions
- Partner with Customer Success, Partnerships, Operations, Engineering, and leadership to share customer insights and help improve the product and customer experience

### **What you'll bring to the role:**

- 3+ years of sales experience, with a strong track record in outbound prospecting and new customer acquisition
- Proven experience owning a full-cycle sales process, from prospecting through close
- Demonstrated success consistently achieving and exceeding quota
- A true hunter mentality — you’re energized by creating opportunities, picking up the phone, and turning cold prospects into customers
- Strong cold-calling and outbound prospecting skills, with the ability to consistently generate pipeline
- Experience selling SaaS technology and conducting consultative product demos
- Strong discovery skills and the ability to uncover both stated and unstated customer needs
- A thoughtful and effective approach to objection handling, negotiation, and closing
- Strong pipeline management skills and a disciplined approach to CRM hygiene
- Exceptional communication, organization, and time-management skills
- Highly self-motivated and comfortable working independently in a high-activity sales environment
- Coachable, curious, and eager to continuously improve your sales craft
- Enthusiasm for a fast-paced, adaptable startup environment
- Experience working with CRMs and sales tools such as Aircall, Outreach, Salesloft, or similar platforms

### **Bonus Points:**

- Experience selling to roofing contractors, construction companies, or other SMB trades
- Experience in SaaS, particularly high-velocity, lower-ARPU subscription sales
- Experience in a high-volume outbound sales environment
- Experience working at an early-stage or high-growth startup
- Existing knowledge of the roofing or construction industry
- Experience selling into SMB or owner-operated businesses

title: SEO/AEO Specialist
description:

You'll work across technical SEO, content optimisation, keyword research, and performance analysis to improve organic visibility in search and AI-powered engines

**Key Details:**

Role type: Full-time, Remote
Timings: 3 PM to 12 AM (IST)

* Strong understanding of search intent, entities, topical authority, semantic SEO, and content optimisation
* Comfortable with technical SEO fundamentals including crawling, indexing, site architecture, schema, and structured data
* Proficient with tools like GSC, GA4, Ahrefs/Semrush, Screaming Frog and/or other analytical tools to understand current performance and provide recommendations

title: Account Executive
description:
**About Us**

At Qase, we're building a modern, efficient test-management platform that helps engineering and QA teams move faster, collaborate better, and deliver higher-quality software. As we expand our go-to-market engine, we're looking for an Account Executive who can own revenue, build strong customer relationships, and turn opportunities into long-term partnerships.

This role is central to Qase's growth. You'll be building your own pipeline through high-volume outbound, closing deals, shaping the customer experience, and influencing how our product evolves. Outbound is the engine of this role: we expect you on the phones every day, making at least 50 calls. Like any fast-moving startup, our priorities shift as we scale. Adaptability, ownership, and strategic thinking are essential to succeed here.

We're seeking someone who can align at least part of their schedule with early Eastern Standard Time (EST) working hours (7:00–16:00).

**What You'll Do**

*Outbound Prospecting (Your #1 Priority):*
- Make a minimum of 50 outbound calls per day to prospects across Mid-Market and Enterprise accounts
- Self-source the majority of your pipeline through cold calling, supported by targeted email and LinkedIn outreach
- Research target accounts and personas (engineering, QA, and DevOps leaders) so every conversation is relevant and well-prepared
- Run multi-touch outbound sequences and follow up persistently until you get a clear yes or no
- Turn cold conversations into booked discovery calls and qualified opportunities
- Track and own your daily activity metrics (dials, connects, conversations, and meetings booked) and use the data to improve your conversion rates
- Protect dedicated call blocks in your calendar and treat them as non-negotiable

*Sales Responsibilities:*
- Meet or exceed monthly and quarterly revenue targets and quotas
- Build, manage, and grow a healthy sales pipeline across SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise segments
- Identify, qualify, and pursue new business opportunities with an outbound-first approach, complemented by inbound and partner channels
- Conduct discovery calls to understand client pain points, objectives, technical environment, and buying processes
- Deliver tailored product presentations and demos that articulate value clearly and persuasively
- Prepare and present proposals, business cases, and pricing packages
- Navigate complex negotiations and close deals efficiently
- Partner with Solutions Engineering and Product teams to deliver accurate technical information when needed
- Maintain detailed and accurate sales forecasts, reports, and CRM hygiene

*Client Relationship Responsibilities:*
- Build and maintain strong, trust-based relationships with both new and existing clients
- Understand customer needs in depth and propose solutions that meaningfully solve their problems
- Ensure customer satisfaction, retention, and long-term account value
- Identify expansion paths: cross-sell, upsell, additional seats, and feature adoption
- Act as a strategic point of contact for your accounts

*Market & Strategy Responsibilities:*
- Monitor industry trends, competitor activity, and emerging market opportunities
- Share insights with marketing, product, and leadership to influence roadmaps and GTM strategy
- Participate in continuous refinement of messaging, positioning, and sales plays

*Collaboration & Teamwork:*
- Work closely with Marketing on lead quality, messaging performance, and campaign outcomes
- Partner with Solutions Engineering, Product, and Customer Success to deliver a cohesive customer experience
- Participate in team meetings, pipeline reviews, and strategy sessions
- Share knowledge, learnings, and best practices with the sales team

**What You'll Bring**

*Sales Expertise:*
- Proven ability to consistently hit sales targets
- Confident, energetic cold caller who can open conversations and earn a meeting in the first 30 seconds
- Skilled in discovery, solution-selling, objection-handling, and closing
- Strong command of sales methodologies (MEDDIC, SPIN, Challenger, or similar)
- Ability to craft compelling narratives and business cases
- Experience navigating multi-stakeholder deals and technical buying committees

*Communication Skills:*
- Clear, persuasive communicator with strong presentation ability
- Confident handling technical and non-technical audiences
- Sharp written communication for proposals, follow-ups, and commercial docs

*Pipeline & Process Skills:*
- Strong CRM discipline and ability to manage pipeline with accuracy
- Comfort running parallel deal cycles
- Structured thinking with attention to detail

*Problem-Solving:*
- Ability to identify obstacles and move deals forward despite friction
- Comfortable dissecting customer needs and translating them into value propositions
- Strategic mindset with practical execution

**Experience**
- 3+ years of closing experience in B2B SaaS sales
- Experience selling to engineering, QA, DevOps, or technical teams is a plus
- Strong track record of exceeding quota in a high-velocity or hybrid sales environment
- Proven experience with high-volume cold calling (50+ dials per day) and building pipeline from scratch
- Familiarity with test management, QA tools, CI/CD, or DevOps ecosystems is beneficial
- Fluent in English

**Tools You'll Use**
- CRM platforms like HubSpot or Salesforce
- Sales engagement platforms and dialers (Outreach, Apollo, SalesLoft)
- LinkedIn Sales Navigator
- Proposal tools and contract automation systems
- Internal collaboration tools like Slack, Notion, and JIRA

**Soft Skills We Value**
- **Ownership:** you take responsibility for outcomes, not excuses
- **Adaptability:** you thrive in environments where playbooks evolve weekly
- **Strategic thinking:** you balance short-term wins with long-term account value
- **Resilience:** you pick up the phone for call #50 with the same energy as call #1, and rejection doesn't slow you down
- **Hunger:** you're self-motivated, competitive, and energized by building your own pipeline

**Key Deliverables**

- Consistently hit 50+ outbound calls per day and meet weekly meeting-booked targets
- Maintain consistent, high-quality pipeline coverage, primarily self-sourced through outbound
- Deliver compelling, high-impact sales presentations
- Close deals with precision and maintain strong relationships post-sale
- Provide actionable insights that strengthen Qase's GTM and product strategy
- Ensure clean, accurate CRM data and forecasting

title: Commercial Video Producer & Content Creator(UNPAID)
description:
Compensation: **Performance-Based Equity** (Transitioning to Full-Time Salary in 10–12 months)

Role Overview SkyTails.com is on a mission to revolutionize how pet parents save and invest for pets. As our Business Development Manager, you will be the primary architect of our partner network. Your goal is to identify, pitch, and onboard key partners—ranging from local animal shelters and national rescues to veterinary groups and pet-tech providers—to create a seamless value loop for our users.

We are looking for a highly creative and technical **Commercial Video Producer** to lead our visual storytelling. You won’t just be "making videos"; you will be crafting high-impact commercial assets that stop the scroll, drive conversions, and elevate our brand identity. You should be a "predator" (producer/editor/director) who can take a project from a rough whiteboard concept to a polished, professional delivery.

**Key Responsibilities**
* End-to-End Production: Lead all phases of video production, including concepting, storyboarding, scriptwriting, filming, and post-production.
* Commercial Strategy: Collaborate with the Marketing and Commercial teams to ensure every video aligns with specific campaign goals (e.g., brand awareness, lead gen, or product education).
* Multi-Platform Optimization: Create tailored content for diverse channels, including 15-second "hook-heavy" social ads (TikTok/Reels), 2-minute product deep dives, and high-fidelity brand anthems.
* Post-Production Excellence: Execute high-level editing, color grading, sound design, and motion graphics to ensure a premium look and feel.
* Equipment Management: Source and manage video/audio gear, lighting setups, and potentially coordinate with external freelancers or agencies for larger shoots.

**Qualifications & Skills**
* The Portfolio: A strong showreel demonstrating a "commercial eye"—clean compositions, intentional lighting, and rhythmic editing.
*  Technical Mastery: Expert-level proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud (specifically Premiere Pro and After Effects) or DaVinci Resolve.
*  Platform Knowledge: Deep understanding of social media trends, aspect ratios, and what makes a video perform in a digital-first landscape.
* Efficiency: Ability to balance high-concept "hero" videos with quick-turnaround social content without sacrificing quality.
* Communication: Strong ability to pitch creative ideas to stakeholders and translate complex business goals into visual narratives.

**Bonus Points If You Have:**
Experience in 3D animation (Blender, Cinema 4D).
A background in directing talent (actors or internal staff) to get natural, engaging performances.
Knowledge of AI video tools for workflow acceleration.

title: Sales Development Representative — Home Services (Remote)
description:
About HomeOtter / Blue Ink Digital

HomeOtter connects US homeowners with home service professionals — delivering ready-to-buy leads, inbound calls, and booked appointments to contractors in roofing, bath, windows, solar and a growing list of verticals. We run our own consumer sites and paid media, we own our demand, and we're building the self-serve platform that lets contractors buy customers directly from us instead of through the big marketplaces. Small team, fast decisions, growing every month — and you'd be our first dedicated sales hire.

The Role

You put contractors on our platform. Your day is outbound: calling and emailing US roofing, bath, solar and window contractors in the zip codes where our lead flow is already strong — and showing them, live, the customers we can send them. The demo is the pitch: you pull up their zip, show real demand, and sign them onto a self-serve account with no long-term contract.

What you'll do

Own top-of-funnel: high-volume cold calls and email sequences to contractor prospect lists, prioritized by live demand data from our media team
Run demo-pitches — every real conversation includes a live look at lead flow in the prospect's service area
Sign and onboard self-serve accounts; hand off to account management for retention
Keep a clean pipeline in our CRM — every conversation, stage, and follow-up tracked
Feed intel back to leadership: objections, pricing feedback, which verticals bite

Ramp & Targets

First 90 days: structured training on our products, platform, and pitch — working directly with the CEO, who built the demand engine you're selling
At ramp: 20 demo-pitches/week with decision-makers, scaling toward 30+
Success = signed, activated accounts — your performance pay is tied to accounts that go live and keep buying

Who You Are

1–3 years outbound sales/SDR experience — phone-heavy, high-activity, unbothered by cold outreach
Fluent, confident spoken English — you'll be calling US business owners all day
Gritty: contractors are on roofs and in crawlspaces; reaching them takes persistence and personality
Home services, lead gen, or local advertising familiarity a plus (not required — we teach the industry)
CRM-fluent, organized, honest with your own pipeline numbers
Available full-time on US business hours

What We Offer

$2,000/month base + performance commission on activated accounts — uncapped, structure finalized with the hire
Ground floor of a new sales org — the first rep who proves the motion is first in line to lead the team we build behind it
Direct access to leadership; real input into pitch, pricing, and playbook
Full tooling provided: dialer/outreach stack, CRM, warm prospect lists built from live demand data

How to Apply

Apply with your resume and a 60–90 second voice memo (Loom, Vocaroo, or audio file) telling us the hardest thing you've ever sold. Applications without the voice memo won't be reviewed — this is a phone role, and the memo is round one. We're interviewing immediately and hiring this month.

title: National Sales Executive
description:
We're [Scan.com](http://Scan.com). We're building America's national imaging network: the infrastructure that connects patients, providers, and payers to faster, better-value diagnostic imaging. Thousands of patients move through our platform every day, and each is a real person waiting for an answer to a healthcare concern. We exist to get them that answer faster.

We manage the medical imaging pathway end-to-end. Providers order through a single point of entry, and from there, we run the entire medical diagnostic pathway. Managing the full pathway, rather than brokering pieces of it, is what lets us deliver imaging faster, at higher quality, and at a lower cost than the fragmented status quo.

We’re looking for a **National Sales Executive (Workers’ Compensation)** at an exciting time — we’ve successfully launched multiple platforms and products, raised over $100m in VC funding, reached profitability, and have a growth trajectory of over 100% YoY.

Millions of people wait too long for a diagnosis. Come help us fix that.

## **WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE IN THIS ROLE:**

As a **National Sales Executive**, you will own a national book of business and lead full-cycle sales across key Workers’ Compensation segments. You will build and nurture senior stakeholder relationships, sell consultatively, and bring market feedback back into the business so we can continue to sharpen our product and go-to-market approach.

As a scaleup business, you can expect your role to develop over time. Here are some of the types of things you could be getting involved in:

- **Revenue generation and pipeline development:** Prospect, qualify, and close new accounts across payers, TPAs, self-insured employers, and managed care organizations. Build and manage a robust pipeline with defined targets tied to revenue milestones.
- **Strategic account management:** Develop and maintain relationships with key decision-makers including claims directors, medical directors, VP-level operations leaders, and C-suite stakeholders. Understand each account’s goals and pain points (claims costs, medical utilization, return-to-work outcomes) and position solutions accordingly.
- **Consultative selling and solution design:** Serve as a subject matter expert in Workers’ Compensation workflows, regulatory environments, and care pathways. Tailor proposals and presentations that connect solutions to measurable outcomes, such as reduced claim duration, lower litigation rates, and faster speed to care.
- **Market intelligence and competitive positioning:** Stay current on industry trends, state-specific regulatory shifts, network dynamics, and competitor offerings. Share insights with leadership to inform roadmap decisions and go-to-market strategy.
- **Cross-functional collaboration:** Partner with Strategy, Operations, Product, Marketing, and Legal/Compliance to ensure what is sold can be delivered. Support implementation handoffs, pilot design, and contract negotiations, including cooperative services agreements and SLAs.
- **Industry presence and thought leadership:** Represent [Scan.com](http://Scan.com) at national conferences (e.g., NWCDC, RIMS, WCI) and state-specific comp forums. Build a strong network within the WC ecosystem to generate inbound interest and referral relationships.
- **Reporting and forecasting:** Maintain accurate CRM data, deliver pipeline and forecast updates to leadership, and track KPIs including conversion rate, deal velocity, average contract value, and account retention.

## **WHAT YOU MIGHT BRING TO THE TABLE:**

You don't need to tick all the boxes to apply for this role. Whether it's your first role or your fifth role, we believe everyone can add value, learn, and grow. However, these might be some of the ways you are currently adding value:

- Experience owning full-cycle enterprise or mid-market sales, from outbound prospecting through close.
- Familiarity with the Workers’ Compensation ecosystem, including common buyer personas, workflows, and regulatory considerations.
- Familiarity with the role diagnostic Imaging plays in the injured worker care continuum.
- Strong consultative selling skills, including the ability to translate operational pain points into clear, outcome-based solutions.
- Confidence building relationships with senior stakeholders and navigating multi-threaded sales processes.
- Comfort working cross-functionally to shape pilots, implementation plans, and contract terms.
- Structured approach to pipeline management, forecasting, and CRM discipline.

## **AI REQUIREMENTS**

At [Scan.com](http://Scan.com), AI isn't a side project; it's how we work. We expect everyone to use AI to think faster, remove drudgery, and multiply their output. What we care about is judgment: knowing when AI makes you sharper, when it doesn't, and how to use it responsibly around patient data. We'll assess this in the way that matters for this role, using the tier below. You don't need to be an engineer. You need to reach for the best tool and get more done as a result.

Tier 2 — For this role, you're expected to be AI-Amplified. AI is part of your daily workflow for drafting, analysis, and research, and you know how to check its output and use it responsibly with sensitive data. (most commercial, marketing, finance, people, and G&A roles)

*One assessment principle across all tiers: we're testing judgment and adaptability, not whether you've memorized today's tools. Tools change quarterly; the ability to learn and apply them is what compounds.*

## **A VIEW ON OUR CULTURE**

We're building something that matters. Every scan we speed up is a real person waiting on an answer, and that urgency runs through everything we do. We move fast, we own outcomes, and take pride in our output. If you like ambiguity, working with ambitious people, and want your work to visibly move the needle, you'll feel at home here.

## **HOW WE WILL INTERVIEW YOU:**

We keep our interview process short and sweet. Here are the stages you can expect, but we might switch up the order depending on team availability:

1. 30-minute introductory phone call with a member of our Talent Team.
2. If it feels like there is an initial fit for all, we will invite you to a 45-minute video call with the hiring manager. This is a more structured interview that will deep-dive into the role and technical needs.
3. 'Scan Standard' interview, where our panel screens for values alignment and the success factors that matter at [Scan.com](http://Scan.com). You will also be assessed on your AI fluency at the stage and depth relevant to your role (see AI Requirements above).
4. Meet the founders and/or other team members. Again, the length varies depending on how many people are involved and whether in person or via video call.
5. Offer!

## **WHAT WE OFFER**

We go beyond the basics with our benefits package. Here’s what you can expect from us:

- Salary range of **$100,000 - $150,000 + Commission**
- Equity
- Flexible remote or hybrid work options
- Dedicated personal development budget
- Medical, vision, and dental coverage
- 28+ days of paid time off across PTO and wellbeing days, so you can show up at your best
- Paid parental leave
- 401k retirement plan
- All the equipment you need to do your best work
- Inclusive, people-first policies designed by our team, for our team

## **DIVERSITY AT** [**SCAN.COM**](http://Scan.com)

[Scan.com](http://Scan.com) is committed to eliminating discrimination and encouraging diversity within our team. We strive to provide equality and fairness for all job applicants and employees and never discriminate on the basis of gender, marital status, age, race, ethnicity, religion, or physical differences.

We are opposed to all forms of unlawful treatment and discrimination.

Our ambition is for our team to be representative of society's diversity, and for every employee to feel respected and able to bring their best selves to work.

If you need an accommodation to apply or interview, contact us at [people@scan.com](mailto:people@scan.com).

We look forward to receiving your application!

title: Product Manager
description:
We’re building Reflow, a workforce and workflow intelligence platform that helps teams understand and improve how work gets done. We’re at a stage where product decisions, execution, and delivery are inseparable — which means this role owns what we build, why we build it, and how it actually ships.

We’re looking for a founding Product Manager who can operate end-to-end: product strategy, prioritization, execution, and delivery. This is a hands-on role for someone who has built in very early-stage environments and thrives without guardrails.

## What you’ll do

Own product direction and outcomes:

- Own product direction, roadmap, and prioritization — making tradeoffs across customer value, speed, and technical constraints.
- Turn ambiguous goals into clear problems, scopes, and shipped solutions.
- Be accountable for outcomes, not artifacts.

Run product execution and operations:

- Drive planning, sequencing, and timelines with engineering.
- Manage dependencies, unblock progress, and keep delivery on track.
- Own release planning, testing, rollouts, and post-launch learning.

Be deeply hands-on:

- Write product specs, workflows, and acceptance criteria.
- Review builds, test flows, and iterate with engineers in real time.
- Make fast calls when things are unclear or breaking.

Stay close to customers and partners:

- Talk to customers constantly: discovery, validation, onboarding, and support.
- Translate feedback into priorities and concrete product changes.
- Support partner setup, onboarding, and early integrations when needed.

Build early product systems:

- Establish how roadmap, prioritization, and execution work.
- Create lightweight processes that increase speed, not bureaucracy.
- Document decisions and patterns so the product can scale.

## Who you are

- 5+ years of product management experience, with at least part of that in a very early-stage startup.
- Former founder, founding PM, or first/early product hire is strongly preferred.
- Proven ability to ship real products in ambiguous, resource-constrained environments.
- Comfortable owning execution details, not delegating them away.
- Strong technical and product judgment; engineers trust your calls.
- Bias toward action, clarity, and momentum.

## Bonus points

- Experience with B2B SaaS, data, analytics, workflow, or platform products.
- Technical background or deep technical fluency.
- Experience owning integrations or partner-facing features.

## Why join Reflow

- Founding-level ownership over product and execution.
- Direct access to founders and customers, zero layers.
- Real influence over product direction, roadmap, and delivery.
- Opportunity to grow into Head of Product as the company scales.
- Flexible setup (contract or full-time), high trust, high expectations.

This is a role for someone who wants to build the product, not manage around it — and who’s excited to do so in a true early-stage startup.

## Compensation:

We offer competitive pay based on the market and where you’re located. The salary ranges in our job postings are intentionally wide because they need to cover both U.S. and international candidates. Our final offer will depend on things like your experience, skill set, and location.
