title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
**📍 Locations: San Francisco (Hybrid), New York (Hybrid), Columbus (Hybrid), or Remote (US)**

The Forward Deployed Engineer is a perfect role for someone who is technical enough to sit in a customer's codebase and docs, curious enough to become the deepest product expert in the room, and wants to own the customer relationship at a fast-moving startup. You'll be on calls with enterprise engineering and docs teams every week, you'll own a book of accounts end to end, and you'll be the person who figures out how to make ReadMe work for whatever they're trying to do, not the person who files the ticket and waits.

At ReadMe the Sales team finds companies that we can solve problems for, and you take over from there. Your role is to oversee a swift and effective implementation, partner with the customer to have a successful first year, identify opportunities for growth and optimization, and make sure the right resources get tapped in to support whatever the customer needs to be successful with ReadMe. You'll solve most technical questions yourself, and know when and how to pull in Engineering or Solutions Architects for the rest.

## **🦉 What we do**

We're a small team of humans (and[ _one owl_](http://owlbert.io/)) working together to do big things, and that’s where you come in. In this role you’ll have a transformational impact on ReadMe across both the trajectory of the business and our thriving culture.

ReadMe helps more than 5,000 leading startups and tech companies build beautiful, personalized, and interactive developer hubs. If you’ve ever visited the developer docs for Amazon, Samsara, or Nvidia, you’ve used ReadMe!

We love what we do because it’s so much more than just documentation. We’re providing tools for teams to build a better developer experience and make their products and APIs easier to use. We’ve got great support from our investors at Accel who led our[ _Series A_](https://blog.readme.com/series-a/), and[ _our interview process_](https://blog.readme.io/how-we-designed-our-interview-process/) reflects the open, caring, and whimsical culture we want to maintain as we scale.

## **✅ What you’ll do here**

- Own a book of enterprise accounts end to end. Onboarding, adoption, renewal assistance, and expansion. Be the primary technical and strategic contact for each.
- Be on customer calls regularly, including: implementation kickoffs, working sessions, QBRs, and escalations. This is a customer-facing role, not a ticket-queue role.
- Act as the product SME for your accounts. Know ReadMe deeply enough to answer product questions in real time, and debug alongside customers when something isn't working.
- Get hands-on with the technical implementation. Review OAS files, help wire up CI/CD syncing via the ReadMe CLI or API, troubleshoot custom JS/CSS and auth setups, and prototype solutions before handing off to Engineering.
- Build AI into how you work. Use AI tools to draft implementation plans, analyze account health across your book, triage and summarize customer requests, prototype scripts, and automate the repetitive parts of the job so you spend more time solving real problems.
- Identify expansion and growth opportunities across your book and partner with Sales to close them.
- Advocate for customers internally, surface health risks early, and feed structured product and bug feedback to Product and Engineering.

## **💙 You’ll love this job if you are…**

- Passionate about working with others; you’d be collaborating with lots of new customers, and our Sales, Product, Support and Enterprise Engineering teams!
- An outstanding communicator, very organized, and able to manage multiple projects at once.
- Technical enough to read an OpenAPI spec, poke at a customer's HTML/CSS/JS, understand SSO and auth flows, and use Git and a CLI comfortably. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to hold your own with one.
- Someone who uses AI as a working tool. You've built prompts, workflows, or small automations that changed how you actually get work done, and you're eager to keep doing that.
- A problem solver who'd rather figure out the answer than escalate it. You enjoy the puzzle of making a product bend to a customer's real-world constraints.

## **🌱 How you’ll grow within one month**

- Learn and collaborate from people around the ReadMe org about our product and what it can do for customers.
- Start to develop relationships with your book of enterprise customers
- Sit in on customer calls with the team and start running your own kickoffs with new customers
- Complete a hands-on ReadMe build i.e., set up a hub from an OAS file, configure SSO, ship a custom page, so you've done what customers do.

## **🪴 Within three months, you’ll…**

- Be the first line of technical resolution for your accounts. You answer and debug most questions yourself.
- Have built at least one AI-assisted workflow that saves you or the team meaningful time each week.

## **🌳 Within six months, you’ll...**

- Be performing to the KPIs of the role - time to implementation, NPS scores, NRR, etc.
- Consult on how we can position our roadmap to maximize the enterprise experience in the long term.
- Identify expansion conversations in your book to forward to Sales

## **🛣️ What’s the hiring process like?**

1. We can’t wait to read your resume and (hopefully personality-filled) cover letter! Let us know what excites you about the role, and help us get to know you better!
2. If we think there could be a good fit, we’ll set up a 30-minute Zoom call with Kirby, one of our Account Executives. She’ll tell you more about the role and learn more about you and your experience.
3. Next, you’ll have a 30-minute Zoom interview with Dan, one of our TCSMs. You’ll dive a little deeper into your background and past customer experience.
4. Then, we’ll invite you to a virtual “onsite” over Zoom! You’ll meet members of our GTM team, people from across ReadMe, and dig a little deeper into your technical skills.
5. We’ll let you know how things went within a week! If it still seems like a good fit all around, we’ll extend you an offer! If not, we will update you to let you know so you aren’t left hanging.

**✨ Our benefits include…**

- Unlimited PTO with a three-week minimum. 🏝
- Fully covered medical, dental, and vision insurance for you, and your dependents. 🩺
- A One Medical membership. 🧑‍⚕️
- A wellness stipend for therapy of up to $350 per month for up to 6 months. 😌
- A wellness stipend of up to $150 per month. 🏋️
- One-to-one donation matching of up to $1,000 per year. 💸
- Twelve weeks of paid parental leave after the birth or adoption of a child. 🐣
- Work from home office stipend of $500. 🖥️
- Offsite retreats to get together with coworkers and plan for the quarter ahead. ✈️
- Take a look at our[_handbook_](https://readme.com/handbook) for more information on our benefits! 📘

Not sure if you’d be the right fit? Apply anyway! We’d love to see your application.

**At ReadMe, we’re committed to cultivating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome people of all different backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer and a pleasant and supportive place to work. We'd love to have you come join us here! ReadMe is open to hiring folks fully remote in the US, hybrid, or in-person at our New York, San Francisco, or Columbus HQ.**

title: Content Expansion Associate
description:
**Content Expansion Associate**

Project Expedition, a rapidly growing travel company, is seeking a Content Expansion Associate to join our Supplier Partnerships Team. This role is focused on onboarding new Tour Operators and suppliers, ensuring they are successfully launched and positioned for long-term success on our platform. If you enjoy building relationships, managing complex projects, working cross-functionally, and helping partners grow, this could be a great fit.

The right candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple onboarding projects simultaneously. You will serve as the primary point of contact for suppliers throughout the onboarding process, helping them navigate content requirements, technical setup, and platform best practices. This is a hands-on role that combines relationship management, content quality, operational execution, and problem-solving.

**Key Responsibilities**

Support supplier onboarding from initial engagement through activation

- Manage the onboarding process for assigned suppliers, ensuring a smooth and efficient launch experience
- Follow established onboarding processes, playbooks, and documentation to maintain consistency and quality
- Track and achieve onboarding KPIs, including time to launch, activation rates, and content quality standards
- Coordinate onboarding activities across multiple internal teams

Build and maintain supplier relationships

- Serve as the primary point of contact for suppliers throughout onboarding and early-stage development
- Provide guidance, training, and best-practice recommendations to help suppliers succeed on the platform
- Respond to supplier questions and proactively address onboarding challenges
- Escalate complex issues when necessary while maintaining a positive supplier experience

Manage content onboarding and quality assurance

- Review supplier content to ensure it meets platform standards and quality expectations
- Optimize product descriptions, inclusions, meeting points, imagery, and other content for conversion
- Conduct quality assurance reviews before products go live
- Partner with suppliers to resolve content gaps and improve overall product quality

Support technical onboarding and integrations

- Work closely with Supply Operations and technical teams to support supplier integrations
- Assist with onboarding-related technical tasks and connectivity validation
- Troubleshoot day-to-day onboarding issues and identify whether they are operational or technical in nature
- Collaborate with internal teams to ensure issues are resolved efficiently

Contribute to process improvement and reporting

title: Sr Cloud and Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Role : Sr Cloud and Infrastructure Engineer

Work mode : Remote / Hybrid in Vadodara

Shift timing : 3PM to 12 PM (May include night shift in future)

Notice max : immediate to 30 days joiners only

Budget : 20 lacs

POSITION SUMMARY

This is a hands-on, breadth-oriented role for an engineer who wants to run a real production environment, modernize how infrastructure is built and operated, and work closely with security and development to ship and run software safely. As lead infrastructure engineer for Omni’s multi-tenant Azure estate and Windows server fleet, this role works in close daily partnership with Omni’s Senior Security Infrastructure Engineer, who acts as the technical sounding board, security reviewer, and sign-off authority on significant infrastructure decisions. This role operates under a matrix reporting structure, with a functional reporting line to the CTO, Omni Agent Solutions (USA) and an administrative reporting line to the Associate Director IT (India).

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

- Operate as the lead infrastructure engineer in close daily partnership with Omni’s Senior Security Infrastructure Engineer, who provides technical direction, conducts security review, and signs off on significant infrastructure decisions before they reach production.

- Run and modernize Omni’s Azure environment, including compute, networking, identity, Azure App Services, Azure SQL, Microsoft WAF, Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365, and Azure Monitor.

- Own the Windows Server fleet end-to-end: provisioning, patching cadence, Group Policy and Active Directory operations, lifecycle planning, and end-of-support migrations.

- Own Microsoft 365 license allocation and Azure subscription management across Omni’s multi-tenant environment, including license assignment and recovery, subscription and tenant governance, cost visibility, and ongoing right-sizing.

- Modernize the infrastructure-as-code practice. Propose tooling and patterns for joint review with the Senior Security Infrastructure Engineer, and incrementally bring infrastructure under code with security guardrails built in from the start.

- Partner with the senior developer and broader development team to extend modern CI/CD patterns from application code into infrastructure deployment, and to design systems that scale securely as the business grows.

- Work closely with Omni’s security team and managed SOC on hardening, vulnerability remediation, identity controls, endpoint protection through SentinelOne, and compliance evidence.

- Cross-train into the security workstreams the Senior Security Infrastructure Engineer manages day-to-day, including endpoint detection and response, SASE and ZTNA networking, SIEM, and the managed SOC’s tooling, so the two roles can back each other up across disciplines.

- Manage observability across Datadog and Azure Monitor, including alerting, on-call signal hygiene, and runbook development.

- Maintain the homegrown line-of-business application infrastructure (Azure App Services, Azure SQL, and Microsoft WAF).

- Run day-to-day business continuity and disaster recovery operations within Omni’s defined RPO and RTO targets. Maintain DR runbooks and run periodic failover and tabletop exercises.

- Build and maintain runbooks, architecture diagrams, and change records so the environment can be supported by anyone on the team.

- Partner with Omni’s co-managed MSP as a shared delivery team across day-to-day operations and escalations, rather than treating the MSP as an outside vendor.

- Provide escalation support to internal end users for infrastructure-impacting tickets routed through the helpdesk and the co-managed MSP.

- Participate in an after-hours rotation covering monthly maintenance windows and incident response, and co-lead post-incident reviews. Formalizing the rotation is part of the role, in partnership with the Senior Security Infrastructure Engineer.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

- 8+ years of cloud engineering experience, with significant Azure depth.

- 3+ years operating Windows Server environments at production scale.

- Hands-on experience with hybrid identity, including Active Directory, Group Policy, and Entra ID, in a Windows-centric environment.

- Strong cloud and hybrid networking experience, including firewall change management, network segmentation, cross-tenant routing, IPsec and SSL VPN, NSGs, and subnet design.

- Experience operating to defined RPO and RTO targets, including DR runbook maintenance and failover testing.

- Strong infrastructure-as-code experience. Terraform preferred, with openness to Azure-native equivalents such as Bicep or ARM templates.

- Demonstrated ability to modernize engineering practices in close collaboration with security counterparts, partnering on the final shape of the practice rather than dictating it.

- Comfort operating in a role where a security peer reviews and signs off on significant infrastructure decisions, and where outcomes are defined jointly rather than independently.

- Comfort cross-training across infrastructure and security disciplines, holding a primary area of focus while providing secondary coverage of the other.

- Track record of partnering closely with security and development teams to ship and operate software safely and at scale.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Familiarity with Microsoft 365 Copilot or other enterprise AI rollouts.

- Exposure to NIST CSF, CIS Controls, or ISO/IEC 27001, and how these frameworks apply to both cloud and on-premises or Group Policy deployment.

- Familiarity with SOC 2 control operation and evidence collection.

- Working knowledge of California privacy regulation (CCPA / CPRA). HIPAA exposure also a plus.

- Microsoft partnership program exposure (CSP, Solutions Partner designations).

- Secondary cloud and SaaS familiarity beyond Azure, including Google Workspace, Google Cloud Storage, and Wasabi object storage.

- Exposure to thin-client deployments and cloud browser management.

- Cloudflare familiarity (edge, DNS, security).

- Next-generation firewall platform experience (Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet FortiGate, or comparable).

- Enterprise backup and DR platform experience (Veeam, Axcient, Azure Backup, or comparable).

- Experience migrating workloads from traditional VMs to serverless or cloud-native application platforms.

- SQL Server DBA exposure for day-to-day database operations (not a primary focus of the role).

- IIS management experience.

- AWS, Kubernetes, or serverless experience.

- Experience operating in a small infrastructure team where breadth matters more than depth in any one area.

title: Brand Designer (Digital)
description:
[Cloaked](https://www.cloaked.com) is a consumer privacy and identity platform on a mission to give people back control of their personal data. We let anyone generate unlimited identities - masked emails, phone numbers, and payment cards - scrub their information off data-broker sites, and shield themselves from spam, scams, and breaches, all from one app. Backed by a $375M Series B, we've protected 10M+ identities and removed 1B+ records from the data brokers who profit off personal information. Now we're building the AI-native future of privacy: autonomous agents that monitor, manage, and defend your digital footprint for you.

## **About the role**

We’re looking for a **Brand Designer (Digital)** to lead brand and visual design for Cloaked's white-glove protection offering - our concierge-led service for high-net-worth individuals, family offices, and top executives who've chosen dedicated protection over self-serve.  
  
This offering has its own identity, distinct from our core consumer product: premium, understated, and built to earn trust with an audience that expects it. You'll own everything a client sees, from the onboarding experience to the physical materials that arrive at their door, and steward the visual system that holds it together - working directly with the lead for the offering.  
  
This is a **four-to-six-month contract engagement** with the intent to convert to full-time for the right fit.

## **What will you do?**

*Build the visual system*

- Develop and steward the brand - typography, palette, logo and lockups, photography, layout language - so it reads as authoritative and premium, with restraint over flash
- Maintain the brand system and guidelines as a living reference the team can work from

*Design the client experience*

- Design the client-facing onboarding sessions: Figma presentations, screen recordings, and animations that make the concierge journey feel considered and easy to follow
- Explore and design product-interface concepts - UI mockups and flows for onboarding, interactive tutorials that teach the product, and the on-screen moments shown in client presentations

*Make the physical artifacts*

- Design tangible, high-touch collateral: leather-bound folders with foil-stamped logos, printed briefs and dossier presentation, and QR-to-digital experiences that bridge print to the app
- Design intentional, on-brand merchandise for clients and events - considered pieces that reinforce the positioning, not merch for merch's sake

*Work closely with the team*

- Meet weekly with the lead to review progress and set priorities

## **What skills and experiences will help you?**

- A portfolio showing brand systems you've built or substantially shaped, not just applied
- Strong typographic judgment and a point of view on what reads as premium versus what reads as loud
- Fluency in Figma, including presentation and prototype work
- Motion and animation skills sufficient to show product flows clearly
- Print production experience - you know how to prepare files that come back from the printer looking the way you intended
- Comfort designing UI, even if product design isn't your primary discipline
- Experience working independently as a contractor with minimal art direction

## **What's nice to have?**

- Work with luxury, private banking, high-end hospitality, or other high-net-worth audiences
- Specialty print experience: foil stamping, embossing, bookbinding, or bespoke packaging
- Experience designing sub-brands that sit alongside a parent brand without competing with it
- Exposure to security, privacy, or identity products
- Merch and physical product design
- Background working in a startup or high-growth environment

## **What do we like?**

- Self-starters who take ownership and proactively look for ways to improve things
- Restraint - the audience is sophisticated and can tell when something is trying too hard
- Comfort with chaos: priorities shift, context is incomplete, and you move anyway
- A pragmatic bias toward shipping and iterating over perfecting in isolation
- Strong communication, and the ability to explain a design decision rather than just present it
- Genuine care about craft, including in the details nobody asked about

## **What we offer**

Cloaked is a well-funded Series B startup based out of NYC.  
  
Although we are a distributed team, the NYC team operates with a hybrid model. We have two floors of our building, with two state of the art kitchens packed with drinks, snacks and everything else you'd need to get through the day.  
  
The Cloaked team has diverse interests and so we frequently embark on team outings and go out for socials!

 
## **Compensation and Benefits**

Compensation for this contract engagement will be discussed directly with candidates.  
  
For full-time US employees, we offer above market rate pay and equity based off of the market's best commercially available data. Your compensation will be a combination of salary, bonus and equity, plus a comprehensive benefits package: medical, dental and vision with Cloaked covering the majority of employee premiums, company-paid basic life, and a 401(k) with company match.  
  
We offer flexible work arrangements and the ability to work remotely as needed. Cloaked provides a home office stipend in addition to a new company laptop (and other tech depending on the role).

 
## **Perks**

**🌴 Competitive PTO:** PTO, floating holidays and sick days — and we push people to actually use them. We see time off as a preventative burnout measure, not a balance to hoard.

**👶 Parental Leave:** Paid leave for all new parents — birth, adoption, or foster placement — because the people building privacy deserve time with their families.

**🤸‍♂️ Monthly wellness & meals stipend:** Used for any kind of physical, mental or emotional care you'd like to take for yourself, be it a gym membership, a meditation app, or time with a personal trainer — plus lunch and coffee during the workday.

**🧠 Professional Growth:** Opportunities for career development and personal growth are provided to all employees who seek to further their knowledge and capabilities through an unlimited professional development fund. Additionally team members are encouraged to regularly attend conferences and industry events.

We are really excited about having you join our mission-driven team and help us build the future of online privacy!

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
### About Us:

[Ground News](https://ground.news/) is a platform that makes it easy to compare news sources, read between the lines of media bias, and break free from algorithms.

In a world where political polarization and media distrust are at an all-time high, Ground News offers people a better way to stay informed and see every side of the story. Our mobile app, web app, and browser extension are home to a community of mindful readers who use our news comparison platform to engage with news beyond their filter bubble.

Unlike most news companies, our values do not align with any specific political ideology. Unlike most tech platforms, we don’t rely on algorithms to keep users on our platform to sell more ads. We are supported by our readers who pay for a subscription to build a more nuanced understanding of the news, the world, and themselves.

 
### The Opportunity: Senior Data Engineer

As a senior Data Engineer, you'll build the analytical foundation that Ground News runs on. You'll sit within our ML chapter and work out of the Platform & Infrastructure pod, splitting your time between developing the integrations that bring data into our warehouse and analytical layers that serve KPIs for our Growth & Monetization, Core Experience, and Content Intelligence pods.

This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who thinks in reusable models across the org. You'll design scalable, conformed data models that let analysts answer their own questions without waiting on you, and you'll own the reliability of those models end to end: ingestion, data quality, accuracy, coverage gaps, and failures both upstream and downstream. When a number looks wrong, you're the person who can trace it from the event that produced it to the dashboard that reported it.  
  
You'll also be a key liaison between the people who ask the questions and the systems that answer them, translating what analysts, customer success, and product stakeholders need into data they can trust and reuse.

###   
What You’ll Do:

- Design and build scalable, conformed data models and analytical layers that serve experimentation and company KPIs.
- Own the connectors that land data in the warehouse end to end, from replicated backend tables to custom connectors you build yourself and third-party managed sources.
- Manage infrastructure as code and deployment workflows across AWS and GCP, using Kubernetes and OpenTofu (Terraform) to ship changes safely.
- Own the pipelines you build, monitoring freshness and responding to failures with urgency.
- Act as a senior voice in data architecture decisions, from selecting table types and datastores to designing the schemas from backend to semantic layers.
- Partner directly with analysts, ML engineers, and product stakeholders to turn business questions into data models they can self-serve from.
- Champion high engineering quality through testing, code reviews, observability, and thoughtful operational practices.

###   
What You’ll Bring:

- 5+ years of experience building and operating production data platforms and analytical models.
- Deep expertise in SQL and Python.
- Broad experience with dimensional modelling: grain, table types, conformed dimensions, and load patterns.
- Hands-on experience with modern data tooling: BigQuery, dbt, Dagster, and ingestion tools such as Fivetran, Airbyte, or Google Datastream.
- Experience with data stores and event-driven systems such as PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, and message queues or streams (Kafka, SQS, or Pub/Sub).
- SRE-oriented experience: monitoring, alerting, incident response, and performance optimization for data integrations.
- Experience shipping data and metrics safely, with the validation habits to keep wrong numbers off dashboards and an eye on the compute cost behind them.

###   
Why Work at Ground?

Co-founded by a former NASA engineer and Bain consultant, a position with Ground News provides an unparalleled learning experience both personally and professionally. At Ground, we prioritize growth: both for our business and team members. You’ll have the freedom to work remotely and play a key role in the development of Ground News products.

This is an opportunity to work with a growing and mighty team that is fighting every day to build a world where cooperative, civil debate is the norm, media is accountable, and critical thought is the baseline of our information consumption. Ground is based in Kitchener, Ontario, Canada, but this role is remote.

Our culture is one of collaboration, creativity, and diverse perspectives. If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding accessibility needs, please contact talent@ground.news, and a member of our team will be happy to help.

title: Strategic Initiatives Manager (Remote)
description:
Strategic Initiatives Manager (Remote)
(this is not a role with Dentistry Automation)
About The Role

I am looking for a highly capable, entrepreneurial, and execution-oriented professional to work directly with me across a wide range of business, investment, networking, philanthropic, and special projects.

This is not an Executive Assistant role.

This is not an administrative role.

This is not a project coordinator role.

You will help drive important initiatives from idea through execution, often with limited direction and incomplete information.

You should enjoy figuring things out, researching unfamiliar topics, coordinating people, solving problems, and ensuring projects move forward.

If you are looking for a structured corporate job with narrowly defined responsibilities, this role is probably not a fit.

⸻

Examples Of Projects You May Work On

* Researching and evaluating real estate opportunities
* Coordinating due diligence for potential acquisitions or investments
* Supporting philanthropic and foundation initiatives
* Building and maintaining strategic relationships and networking pipelines
* Researching new business opportunities and industries
* Coordinating meetings with founders, investors, operators, and advisors
* Organizing travel, conferences, and business events
* Managing special projects from concept through completion
* Identifying experts, vendors, consultants, and partners
* Tracking opportunities, commitments, and follow-ups across multiple initiatives

No two weeks will look exactly the same.

⸻

What You’ll Do

Research & Analysis

* Conduct research on industries, companies, investments, markets, and opportunities
* Prepare concise summaries and recommendations
* Gather information and organize findings into actionable insights
* Compare options and help support decision-making

Project Ownership

* Drive projects from initial idea through execution
* Coordinate stakeholders, vendors, consultants, and partners
* Create project plans, timelines, and accountability systems
* Ensure deadlines and commitments are met
* Proactively identify and resolve blockers

Relationship & Opportunity Management

* Track important relationships and follow-ups
* Coordinate meetings and introductions
* Maintain organized records of opportunities, discussions, and next steps
* Help ensure valuable opportunities are not lost due to lack of follow-through

Founder Support

* Help prioritize initiatives and commitments
* Organize information and reduce complexity
* Convert discussions and ideas into actionable plans
* Serve as an execution partner across a broad range of initiatives

⸻

What We’re Looking For

Required

* Exceptional organizational skills
* Strong written and verbal English communication
* High ownership and accountability
* Ability to operate independently
* Strong research and problem-solving skills
* Excellent follow-up and execution discipline
* Comfortable working with ambiguity
* Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously

Strongly Preferred

* Startup experience
* Consulting experience
* Founder’s Office experience
* Business Operations experience
* Program Management experience
* Experience supporting founders, entrepreneurs, investors, executives, or business owners

⸻

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is naturally curious, highly resourceful, intellectually sharp, and relentlessly organized.

You are someone who enjoys taking ownership, figuring things out, and making progress without needing detailed instructions.

You are comfortable saying:

“I don’t know, but I’ll find out.”

This role can be an excellent fit for:

* Former consultants
* Startup operators
* Founder’s Office professionals
* Program Managers
* Business Operations professionals
* Former entrepreneurs
* MBA graduates seeking broad business exposure

⸻

Working Hours

* Remote role
* Must have meaningful overlap with US Central Time
* Preferred overlap window: approximately 8:00 AM – 1:00 PM CST

⸻

APPLICATION PROCESS (READ CAREFULLY)

Many candidates will self-select out of this process. That is intentional.

We are looking for someone who can independently drive initiatives, solve problems, manage complexity, and create momentum with limited supervision.

Special Instruction

To confirm you carefully read this posting, the FIRST line of your application must be:

Strategic Builder

Applications that do not follow this instruction will not be reviewed.

⸻

Step 1: Video Submission (Required)

Applications without a video submission will be automatically rejected.

Please submit a single video (10–15 minutes maximum) answering ALL of the following questions:

1. Tell me about yourself and your career journey.
2. What is the most complex project you personally owned from start to finish?
3. Describe a time you had little direction and had to figure things out yourself.
4. Tell me about a time you failed. What happened and what did you learn?
5. Tell me about a time you had to push back on a founder, executive, client, or manager.
6. What are the three accomplishments you are most proud of professionally?
7. What is the hardest problem you have solved in the last three years?
8. Tell me about a project where you delivered an outcome despite missing information, limited resources, or unclear requirements.
9. What books, podcasts, newsletters, or thought leaders do you follow regularly?
10. What do you want your career to look like in 5–10 years?
11. Why are you interested in this role specifically?

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Product Engineering
description:
**Location:** Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory

##   
Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.

##   
What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

**Month 1: Ship.** Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.

**Month 2: Make the team faster.** Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

**Month 3: Own hiring.** Take over engineering interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.

##   
What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is management and the technical decisions. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.

You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

- **Speed.** You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.
- **Quality.** Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.
- **Team and hiring.** Team structure, growth conversations, the hiring process, and eventually the next manager.
- **AI in the craft — and in the management.** Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

## What success looks like

**At 6 months:** The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.

**At 12 months:** The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've found and/or coached the EM Nr. 2 to support growth.

##   
How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

- **Focus is sacred.** Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our [thoughtful communication](https://www.notion.so/33448601ddf88090b8e5dce0875087f7?pvs=21) and [our remote culture](https://www.notion.so/33348601ddf880f8930adfe6f044040c?pvs=21); give it a read.

To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:
- **Small, temporary teams.** A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.
- **AI is already part of the craft.** We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it [here](https://www.notion.so/Building-production-grade-product-with-AI-in-2026-33448601ddf8808997bafcc9f4ec83df?pvs=21).
- **Zero-bugs.** We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.
- [**We build what customers need**](https://www.notion.so/33448601ddf880b89f0dd9e1b29da3b4?pvs=21)**, not what they ask for.** Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

## This role is for you if:

- **You've managed a real team and made it ship faster.** You've hired for it, run the hard conversations, and know what breaks as it grows — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.
- **You know what great engineers look like.** You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.
- **You have an exceptional IC track record before becoming a manager.** You were a senior/principal engineer before you started managing — you didn't skip into management early because coding wasn't working out.
- **You have product taste.** You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.
- **You hold people to a high standard.** You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations about performance.
- **You're hands-on with AI-assisted development.** You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.
- **You've worked in startups.** You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."
- **You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale.** You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.
- **You communicate proactively in writing.** In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.

##   
What we're looking for

### Required

- 8+ years as a software engineer, including 4+ years managing a team of 8+ and hiring for it yourself
- You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data
- Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't
- You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt
- You're an engineer at heart. You were senior or principal before you managed, and you can still hold your own in a design review, a debugging session, or building a feature
- You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook
- Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK

### Nice to have

- You've grown a team to 15+ at a VC-funded startup
- Managed tech leads or a second manager
- Previous experience at a fully remote company

## Interview process

We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:

- **30 min** — Intro call with our talent team
- **45 min** — Interview with Grigory
- **45 min** — Technical interview
- **1.5 hr** — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI
- **2 hr** — Leadership session with the founders

Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.

##   
What Secfix gives you

- **Remote:** 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather
- **Salary:** Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)
- **Equity:** Generous package — we're all owners here
- **Development budget:** €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better
- **Workspace:** Remote workspace support + co-working access
- **Holidays:** 26 days + local public holidays
- **Health insurance:** Comprehensive coverage
- **Annual retreat:** Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands
- **Tech:** MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latest

title: Fractional Laboratory Informaticist
description:
**About Us:**

Lunar is a stealth technology company building a new type of software platform for health systems. We are on a mission to revolutionize healthcare with cutting-edge, AI-powered software designed to help every hospital deliver world-class care for their patients. Our platform is already the core backbone of health systems today, transforming clinical and operational workflows at scale with the world’s first AI-native hospital information system.

This next-generation platform is a fundamental rebuild of the information infrastructure that runs health systems. All of it – from doctors, nurses, pharmacists, lab technicians, coders, billers, supply chain, and even patients – Lunar’s software powers everything, soup-to-nuts. We believe that this mission is the moon landing of healthcare – something so consequential and ambitious that most people believe it to be impossible.

Backed by Silicon Valley’s preeminent venture capital firms, we believe in the power of a high performance team of seasoned professionals operating at the peak of their abilities. We value people who are driven, curious, have sound judgement, and care about doing the best work of their careers.

We are looking for an experienced Laboratory Informaticist to help us set up our laboratory configuration and optimize workflows in Lunar as we look to shape the future of healthcare. Come join us and play a pivotal role in this exciting and important mission.

**Over the next 6 months, here are some ways you can make an impact:**

- **Lab Order and Test Configuration:** Configure laboratory orders, tests, and specimen rules tailored to specific departments and hospital configurations to ensure accuracy and compliance in laboratory operations.
- **Translate Traditional LIS Workflows to Lunar:** Bridge the gap between Lunar's next-generation platform and traditional laboratory information system (LIS) workflows, ensuring smooth adoption and user understanding.
- **Training and Documentation:** Create comprehensive training materials and provide guidance to hospitals, translating complex lab ordering, resulting, and workflow processes into clear and practical resources.
- **Interfaces and Result Edits:** Define and compile rules for laboratory interfaces and result edits, including critical value flags, reflex testing logic, units, and reference-range mapping. Oversee the setup and testing of these rules within the system.
- **Quality Assurance:** Configure and establish QA processes within Lunar's LIS and tailor them to individual customer configurations.
- **Interface and Workflow Review:** Review and refine laboratory interfaces and resulting workflows for each hospital partner, ensuring seamless integration with analyzers and reference labs.

**Your Experience:**

- **Experience:** Approximately 10 years of clinical laboratory experience across multiple domains such as hematology, chemistry, immunology, microbiology, etc.
- **LIS Implementation:** Proven track record of leading or supporting successful LIS implementations or interface builds.
- **Product Intuition:** Deep understanding of laboratory information systems with the ability to intuitively navigate and optimize software for enhanced performance and usability.
- **Laboratory Standards:** Deep understanding of laboratory coding and terminology standards (e.g., LOINC, SNOMED).
- **Problem Solving:** Complex problem-solving abilities in laboratory operations and systems environments.
- **Training & Communication:** Strong skills in translating complex processes into clear, concise training materials, and communicating effectively with hospital teams at all levels.
- **Passion for Healthcare:** Enthusiasm for improving laboratory operations through cutting-edge software solutions that drive both operational efficiency and quality.

*At Lunar, we know our greatest strength is the diverse blend of backgrounds, experiences, and ideas that our team members contribute. We’re passionate about healthcare, but we are also passionate about creating an inclusive workplace where every unique talent and perspective is not just respected, but celebrated. We thrive on embracing differences and are fully committed to fostering a fair, supportive, and dynamic environment where everyone has the opportunity to shine. All applicants will be considered for employment regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.*

There’s a lot of work to be done; a confident, collaborative, and curious leader will maximize leverage, make tough prioritization decisions, and advocate for a strong marketing and communications team in a deeply engineering-minded organization.

We are a small team with big goals. Your primary responsibilities will include:  

* Product marketing. MLCommons has some exciting product developments underway in both performance measurement and reliability measurements. These initiatives demand a shift in communications, from a primarily standards-oriented, community-centric communications model to one that incorporates B2B product marketing. Your role will be to help the organization make this shift, while remaining true to its roots in open, collaborative engineering.
* Community cultivation. As a member-driven organization, we depend on the financial and engineering investments our members and contributors make. And our efforts can benefit tremendously from leveraging the capacity and credibility of our members’ own marketing and communications.. You will be responsible for unlocking these resources with a strategy and plan to deeply engage our members in our work. Imagine bringing together the grassroots and highly technical nature of developer relations, the high-touch, high-stakes nature of corporate relations, the softer side of community cultivation, and the nitty-gritty of relentlessly driving membership growth. All in an organization that prides itself on values of openness and collaborative engineering.
* Thought leadership and brand awareness. We are not an advocacy organization, and we do not have a consumer-facing brand nor a strong PR practice. But we do have a (sometimes strong!) point of view about what will be required to accelerate AI development and adoption over the coming decade; given how the benchmarking field has evolved, it’s essential that our perspective be sought and heard. In this role, you will help us craft and communicate our point of view in ways that resonate with our key audiences, building MLCommons a reputation as a key thought leader in AI. Along the way, we also expect you to develop opinions about our brand and help evolve it.

You won’t be doing this alone. We have great people working directly and indirectly on marketing tasks, and we have some budget to build a team.

There is a lot of detailed work that goes into each of these focus areas, and we will look to you to help define the objectives, strategy, and tactics for driving that work forward.

MLCommons is a fully remote organization, and we support flexible working environments and situations.

The target salary range for this position is $175–200k, plus benefits.

### About You
You are a seasoned marketing leader with experience managing product and brand narratives and cultivating relationships on behalf of organizations. Ideally, you have experience in product marketing at companies selling enterprise solutions. These are some qualifications you might have, but none of these are prerequisites for the role — if you’re excited by the opportunity outlined above, we want to hear from you!

We are looking for someone who:  

* Is a structured and clear communicator. Ideally, you have a demonstrated track record of making novel ideas a reality within organizations or communities. You structure problems clearly, enabling leaders to make informed decisions.
Has a bias for action. You take pride in getting things done efficiently and effectively, with buy-in from your key stakeholders.  
* Is a quick study. AI moves fast, and our community of technical experts is working at the cutting edge of many disparate areas of research and across many different industry verticals. You have a beginner’s mind and can build trust with the most expert contributors in our community.
* Is well-informed about AI. You may not be the earliest adopter of AI tools, but you follow the industry closely, know the key players at all levels of the AI stack, and are familiar with the basics of their business models. You enjoy trying out the latest models and apps, and are deeply curious and thoughtful about the impact AI will have on the world.
* Loves building community and partnerships. You enjoy building relationships with people from all kinds of backgrounds and with all kinds of expertise. In particular, you get along well with engineers and have an appreciation for the complexities of large tech companies, civil society, and government regulators.
* Has 10-15+ years of experience in tech, several of which in marketing. Product marketing experience in particular is most valuable; developer relations, community management, product management, or enterprise sales/partnerships/business development are all great experiences to bring too.

### How We Work
How we pursue our mission matters as much as what we build. Our team shares a set of operating values that describe how we work together, and we look for people who embody these values:

* Say the difficult thing directly. We name problems plainly and early, even when it would be easier not to.
* Default to generosity. We read each other’s intentions in the most generous light and assume good faith.
* Default to transparency. We share what we know and work in the open, so others can build on it.
* All voices count, then commit as one. We make room for every voice in the decision, and once we decide, we move together.
* Say it, own it, do it. We deliver what we said we would and take ownership of the outcome.
* Try, learn, adapt. We experiment, learn from what happens, and adjust as we go.
* Together, not territory. We work for the shared mission rather than individual status or turf.

### Interested? Apply Now.
To apply, send your resume or LinkedIn profile, and three professional references that can attest to the quality of your work to: jobs@mlcommons.org. Please note the job title in the email subject line. (Note: references will not be contacted without your permission).

MLCommons is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to building a team that reflects the global community we serve.

title: Senior Security Engineer (Remote, EU/CET)
acceptedRemoteLocations: Portugal; Spain; Netherlands; United Kingdom; Ireland
description:
## About Maze

**Maze is the user research platform that helps companies build the right products faster by making user insights available at the speed of product development.**

In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the *right* product. That’s where Maze comes in.

We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.

Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.

That’s why Maze was recently named the **#1 user research platform** in [UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey](https://www.uxtools.co/survey/user-research/user-testing-overview)—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.

Maze is a **Series B** company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce [driven by our core values](https://maze.co/about-us/).

## Senior Security Engineer

**Location:** Remote*,* preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal. *Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales.*

## About the Role

We’re hiring a **Senior Security Engineer** to take the lead on security at Maze. You’ll own two closely connected areas:

- The corporate IT foundation every Maze employee relies on
- The security controls that keep our cloud, code and SaaS environment secure and auditable

Identity, devices and access sit right at the intersection of IT and security. This is an opportunity to own that space end to end. Your job is to automate the IT side so well that most of your time goes to corporate security engineering. You own the budget and tooling to automate the IT layer, and the helpdesk scope stays deliberately small, so the role stays an engineering role.

You’ll report to our **Senior Manager, Platform Engineering** and work closely with teams across Maze.

## 

## As a Senior Security Engineer at Maze, you will:

- Own identity and SSO in Google Workspace, including groups, SCIM provisioning, MFA and access policies
- Run our macOS fleet through Iru, including enrolment, configuration, patching and compliance
- Automate joiner, mover and leaver flows from Rippling so new hires are fully provisioned on day one and leavers lose access within hours
- Own SaaS licensing and app provisioning, while keeping internal support lightweight through automation and self-service
- Own security controls across AWS, GitHub, Kubernetes and our SaaS environment, including role based access, IAM hygiene, cloud guardrails, network boundaries and secrets management
- Run vulnerability management end to end, taking findings from Intruder, Socket and pentests through remediation and verification with clear owners and SLAs
- Run regular access reviews and generate audit evidence through Vanta, making compliance thorough, timely and low effort
- Bring a security perspective to incidents and post-incident reviews, turning what we learn into stronger controls
- Use AI-assisted and agentic workflows to reduce manual work and investigate issues faster

## What you won’t own

Application code review and threat modelling, sales questionnaires, customer security calls or other customer-facing security work. These sit with our Senior Manager, Platform Engineering today and will move into the Infosec function as business needs grow.

## What we’re looking for

- You have a strong software, infrastructure or security engineering background and are comfortable using code and infrastructure as code to automate repetitive work
- You’ve owned identity, MDM and joiner and leaver automation at a remote company and can speak to the impact your automation had
- You’ve secured a modern AWS or GCP environment and can explain the trade-offs behind your IAM decisions
- You’ve run vulnerability management or access reviews in an environment with external audits
- You have experience with SOC 2 or ISO 27001 controls and know how to turn a control into an automated check
- You care about the employee experience and are comfortable saying no when needed while providing context and a better path forward
- You’re excited about AI-assisted development and actively use modern AI tools in your work

## Our stack

- **Identity and people systems:** Google Workspace, Rippling
- **Devices:** Iru (formerly Kandji), macOS
- **Cloud and infrastructure:** AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker
- **Security and compliance:** Vanta, Intruder, Socket, Datadog Security, Riot
- **Network:** Cloudflare Zero Trust
- **CI/CD:** GitHub Actions, Depot CI, Argo CD
- **Observability:** Datadog
- **Collaboration:** Slack, Notion, Linear, GitHub, Zoom
- **Application:** TypeScript, Node.js, React

You don’t need experience with every technology in our stack. We care more about strong fundamentals, an engineering approach to both IT and security and excitement about making Maze secure by default as we scale.

## Inclusivity and Pay

At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture. 

Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package.

Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.

## Why Maze is unique

- **Early-stage startup:** You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.
- **Market disruption:** We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.
- **Product-market Fit:** Maze is used by 100,000+ brands across 4,000 companies, from SMB to enterprises, and in the last fiscal year, we saw 6.5M questions answered, supporting 25K decisions

## Benefits

- Health insurance with international coverage, vision, and dental: 100% of the team member premium paid

  - For some locations, coverage options vary, please see our [benefits pages](https://mazedesign.notion.site/Benefits-Full-Time-Team-Member-fac6236ca0d6452dbc659a1947d89317) for more information
- Free access to proper mental health care, unlimited virtual therapy sessions (with a human) and 24/7 access to resources
- Life and Disability Insurance, 100% of the team member premium paid
- Flexible time off
- Meaningful equity
- Company retreats, fully paid for by Maze
- New MacBook (laptop), paid for by Maze
- Paid Family leave: 16 weeks for birth or adoptive parents
- $500/month to be used for dependent health insurance coverage

  - If you don't have dependents to add to your plan, you will still get access to this money to be used at your discretion to get the benefits that matter to you with our flexible a-maze-ing benefits - gym memberships, co-working spaces, food, travel, whatever!
- $1,500 remote work setup fund to ensure you can set up a productive work space
- Flexible work schedule where you manage your own working hours
- Monthly [Bonus.ly](http://Bonus.ly) points that are awarded to others to recognize teamwork, dedication and helpfulness - points can be cashed out for gift cards and more
- Virtual social engagements randomly throughout the year
- SWAG, we have some really cool swag
- Open, transparent culture that includes virtual: coffee chats, bi-weekly all-hands meetings, and more

Check out all of our a-maze-ing benefits [here](https://mazedesign.notion.site/Benefits-fac6236ca0d6452dbc659a1947d89317). 

## Outreach Notice

We understand you might be excited about the job you’re applying for, we are excited you are interested! However, please **refrain from reaching out to our current team members on LinkedIn** for referrals. Our policy is that referrals can only be provided by team members who personally know the candidate. With the high volume of interest in our roles, contacting our team members who are not involved in recruitment can be overwhelming. Additionally, please **avoid submitting support tickets regarding your application**, as our support team is not involved in the hiring process. Rest assured, our recruitment team is diligently reviewing all applications and will reach out directly if there is a match.

title: Product Designer — UX & AI Implementation
description:
Only Farmers is hiring two Product Designers to improve the quality and user experience of our app and web products. You will work directly with Ted and Wolfe, who set overall product direction, and take ownership of turning that direction into thoughtful, reliable experiences.

Salary: £40,000–£55,000 per person, depending on relevant skills and experience.

Location: Remote within the United Kingdom. You must be based in the UK.

Employment: Full-time.
Two positions at the same level; this is a hands-on individual contributor role.

## ABOUT ONLY FARMERS
We connect farmers with people who want to discover farms, book experiences and stays, and participate in farming communities. Our product includes customer experiences and the tools farmers use to manage their businesses.

Explore [Only Farmers](https://onlyfarmers.co.uk/).

## THE ROLE
This is a hands-on UX and product design role. Your core work is understanding users, identifying usability problems, designing user journeys, and refining the layout, interactions and visual details of our app and web products. You will turn user feedback into clear design decisions and test whether your designs make the experience easier to use.

You will also bring those designs to life by directing coding agents in Codex or Claude, then checking and refining the implemented experience. No prior professional coding experience is required; strong UX/UI design skills and practical experience working with coding agents are essential.

## WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Identify friction through user feedback, conversations, product data and hands-on testing.
- Design clear journeys across discovery, bookings, community and farmer tools.
- Improve interaction design, visual hierarchy, content, accessibility and consistency across mobile and web.
- Turn problems into clear briefs and acceptance criteria for agents, then guide implementation using Codex or Claude.
- Challenge agent output, investigate unexpected behaviour and iterate until the result works well.
- Test complete journeys and relevant screen sizes, including loading, empty, error and permission states.
- Maintain shared design patterns and a prioritised UX improvement backlog with the team.
- Document what changed, how it was checked and any remaining limitations, following the team's review and release process.

## WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
- A strong UX/UI portfolio showing usable, coherent products and the reasoning behind your decisions.
- Practical experience delivering working changes by managing coding agents through Codex or Claude. Personal and independent projects count.
- Good visual and interaction design judgment, with close attention to the details that make an app feel clear and dependable.
- The ability to break work into manageable steps, communicate precisely and recognise when an agent's output is incomplete or wrong.
- Confidence speaking with users and prioritising the problems that matter most.
- Careful testing and a willingness to keep refining your work.

No prior professional coding experience is required; practical experience delivering changes with coding agents is essential. You do not need a computer science degree or a particular educational background. Experience with mobile apps, marketplaces, accessibility or design systems is useful, but not required.

## WHY JOIN
Your designs will become working product improvements, and you will be involved through implementation and verification. You will work closely with the founders, help shape a product serving real farming communities, and develop your practice of designing and building with agents.

## HOW TO APPLY
Send your CV or professional profile and portfolio. Include one example of something you improved or built using Codex or Claude: the problem, your decisions, what the agent did, and how you checked the result. A link, screenshots or a short written walkthrough is fine. Please do not share confidential work or customer data. Tell us your UK location, availability or notice period, and whether the salary range fits your expectations. No cover letter is needed. Put these details in your application response or attach them with your CV.

Applications may be organised and reviewed with AI assistance. Ted and Wolfe make hiring decisions.

## OUR PROCESS
1. Review of your application, portfolio and agent-assisted work.
2. Selected candidates complete a paid practical exercise: up to two hours, paid £110 regardless of the hiring outcome, in a prepared test environment. We assess design judgment, agent direction and verification. This is an assessment, not unpaid production work.
3. A 45-minute conversation with Ted and/or Wolfe to discuss your work, decisions and the role.
4. Three references, contacted with your permission, followed by a hiring decision.

Please let us know if you need an adjustment to take part in the application or assessment process. We assess evidence of relevant skills and judgment, and welcome different routes into product design.

title: Buy-Side Equity Analyst or Portfolio Manager: Paid User Testing
location: San Francisco; London; Toronto; New York
description:
Mercata is looking for a few experienced **buy-side equity analysts and portfolio managers** for **early user testing** of our **AI-native Research OS** for hedge funds and alternative asset managers. One **30-minute session**, **paid** for your time, with the option to do more (also paid) sessions later if it's interesting to you. NOTE: this is a short user-testing engagement, not an employment role.

### About Mercata

title: Physical Product — Co-Founder | Equity Only
description:
Important: this is a physical consumer product role. It is not a UX, UI, software, digital product or product management role.

We’re looking for someone to join Blankwerk as our third co-founder and take ownership of the physical products we build.

You should have experience taking a physical consumer product from an idea through design, prototyping, manufacturing and into customers’ hands.

Experience in oral care, beauty, personal care, cosmetics, wellness, lifestyle or other physical consumer products is particularly relevant.

If most of your experience is in UX/UI, apps, SaaS, websites or digital product design, this probably isn’t the right role for you.

This is an equity co-founder seat, not a paid job. You’d own a real piece of what we build, in exchange for building it with us from the start.

**The company**

We’re Blankwerk — a startup building a new kind of oral care brand, starting with one of the most disposable objects in the world.

Our first product is a toothbrush made to last. A precision stainless steel handle where only the brush head is replaced. It’s designed to be something you keep rather than throw away, and built for people who care about how things are made and how they feel in their hands.

4.7 billion toothbrushes are thrown away every year. We think there is a better way.

We’re building a range of physical oral care products around the same idea: products that are considered, durable and genuinely good to use.

**Where we are**

We have early interest from real users, live validation already running, and the first products taking shape.

We’re one founder (Dentist - CEO), with a strong co-founder (COO) joining soon. You’d be the third person and the physical product co-founder. We’re focused on getting ready to raise funding and moving quickly.

**The role**

You’re not joining to manage a product roadmap. You’re joining to create the physical products themselves. You’ll own physical product development from the first idea through to production and launch. You’ll work across:

1. Product and industrial design
2. Physical product development
3. Materials and finishes
4. Prototyping and testing
5. Product functionality and durability
6. Finding and working with manufacturers
7. Suppliers and production partners
8. Manufacturing and quality
9. Cost and production trade-offs
10. Building the product development process as we grow

You’ll be involved in deciding what we should make, how it should work, what it should feel like, what it should be made from, who should manufacture it and how we get it into customers’ hands.

The job is hands-on. You’ll be looking at prototypes, talking to suppliers, solving manufacturing problems, making design decisions and testing things in the real world.

**What we’re looking for**

The strongest signal is simple:

1. You’ve made physical products before.
2. You’ve taken something from concept to prototype to manufactured product and shipped it.
3. You understand the difference between a nice-looking concept and something that can actually be produced at the right quality and cost.
4. You know how to work with manufacturers and suppliers. You understand materials, production constraints and the compromises that come with making something in the real world.
5. You can move between the details and the bigger picture. You can look at a product and think about how it works, how it feels, how it will be made and whether people will actually want to use it.
6. You should be comfortable with the uncertainty of zero-to-one and with making decisions without having every answer first.
7. Fluent English is important. It’s our working language.

**Who this isn’t for**

1. This isn’t a UX or UI role.
2. It isn’t a digital product role.
3. It isn’t a product management role where you’ll mainly manage a roadmap, write requirements or coordinate a software team.
4. It isn’t a role where you’ll hand designs to somebody else and wait for the product to be made.

We need someone who wants to be close to the physical product and own what happens to it.

**Reasons not to take this job**

1. There’s no salary yet. If you need income now, this isn’t for you.
2. This is full-time and all-in. It’s not a side project you fit around other work.
3. Work you did last month might get thrown away when we learn something new. We build it again.
4. There is no predefined schedule, only deadlines we set ourselves. It runs on trust before proof.
5. There is risk. The company might fail. The product might fail. The market might not behave the way we expect. We’re asking you to bet on this early, exactly as we’re doing.

If that sounds frightening, don’t apply.
If it sounds exciting, we should talk.

**What you get**

1. A real co-founder seat from the beginning.
2. Co-founder-level equity with standard vesting. You’re the physical product co-founder, and the specific number is a conversation we have with serious candidates.
3. Full ownership of physical product development and a genuine say in what we build.
4. A clean slate. No legacy product team, no layers of approval and no ten-year roadmap written before you arrived.
5. You’ll help shape the products, the company and eventually the team around them.

If you’ve spent your career making physical products and this sounds like the kind of thing you’d want to build, we’d love to hear from you.

If you know someone who might be a good fit, please share this with them.

**We’re committed to building an inclusive company from day one. We welcome people of all genders, backgrounds, ethnicities, ages, abilities and circumstances. Different perspectives make a product and a team genuinely stronger.**

# Business Directory Acquisition Partner (Independent Contractor)

## Position Overview

This role focuses specifically on finding businesses, organizations, agencies, and professionals who would benefit from paid directory listings and converting them into active, paying subscribers across all listing tiers (Basic through Elite).

You are not selling internal services—you are building revenue for the **Business Directory ecosystem** by onboarding external businesses into the platform.

This is a commission-only independent contractor role with recurring income potential tied to subscription renewals and tier upgrades.

Your primary responsibility is to:

* Find businesses that need visibility
* Convince them to join the JUS Business Directory
* Drive ongoing subscription revenue through listing tiers

* Track conversions, renewals, and upgrades.
* Encourage tier upgrades for increased visibility benefits.
* Build repeatable outreach systems and lead sources.
