title: Mercor AI Research Fund Grants
location: San Francisco; London; New York; Mexico City
description:
# **About Mercor**

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.

**Mercor AI Research Fund Grants $5M**

One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical.

Mercor is committing **$5 million** to fund AI research. Award size and mix depend on the project. The grant supports:

- The time of experts from Mercor's platform
- Researcher hours
- API costs
- Stipends for event and conference attendance

This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply[ _HERE_](https://www.mercor.com/careers/a0a98be0-d856-4129-b500-c0a3e412ef01/)) and our $5m of safety funding awards (apply[ _HERE_](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/mercor/1d59ce50-4207-4d95-b7fd-5a01e90b0897)).

**What we're looking for**

- **Real-world evaluations:** measuring whether benchmark performance translates into reliable performance on realistic tasks and workflows
- **Environments:** building high-fidelity, interactive environments that capture the complexity of real-world work
- **Long-horizon tasks:** evaluating and improving models’ ability to plan, execute, and adapt across extended workflows
- **Agentic capabilities:** tool use, coordination, memory, and autonomous execution
- **Reasoning and problem-solving:** improving performance on complex, ambiguous, or underspecified tasks
- **Post-training:** developing better data, rewards, and training methods to improve model capabilities
- **Evaluation methodology:** creating more robust measures of capability, reliability, and real-world utility

**Why us**

- Funding for researcher time, API costs, and event attendance
- Where useful to the work: access to Mercor's expert network for human grading and annotation: lawyers, accountants, engineers, scientists, clinicians
- Access to Mercor's internal evaluation infrastructure, subject to review
- Introductions to Mercor's network of researchers across frontier labs and academia

### **Who should apply**

- Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.
- People with a specific, well-scoped question: the grant is built around your proposal, not a generic research rotation
- Applicants based in the United States or the United Kingdom
- Bonus: researchers with experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, and post-training.

We expect grantees to publish – such as a paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.

**Award terms**

Selected grantees will sign Mercor’s research award agreement. Key terms include:

- Grantees keep ownership of their work and grant Mercor a non-exclusive license to use it, including commercially.
- Mercor may identify grantees and their institutions as award recipients, including by name and logo. Grantees may use Mercor’s logo with Mercor’s approval.
- For benchmark and evaluation projects, Mercor receives early access to the benchmark before public release and the exclusive right to build and host a private held-out test set, at Mercor’s cost.
- Grantees agree not to work with specified Mercor competitors on substantially similar benchmarks or evaluations during the award and for 12 months afterward.
- Grantees are free to publish their findings. Mercor reviews drafts in advance only to remove its confidential information.
- Awards are subject to tax documentation, sanctions screening, and periodic progress reports.

**How to apply**

Submit an Expression of Interest. We expect to see a one- or two-page document. It should contain at least a section on your team, background, and research accomplishments; a section on your proposed research project; and a section on the outputs and impact of the project, with directionally correct timelines and resource requirements. Please do not include confidential or proprietary information in your Expression of Interest. Submitting an Expression of Interest does not obligate Mercor to make an award.

title: Creative Lead, Artist Experiences, Growth & Operations
description:
### We’re looking for a designer-turned-operator to find extraordinary artists around the world, win their trust, and turn their creative worlds into VAWAA experiences people will travel for.

Someone with a trained eye for design and craft, strong relationship instincts, and the commercial instinct to know which artists and experiences will resonate — and the drive to get them onboarded and launched.

[**Apply via this link**](https://vawaa.breezy.hr/p/fef1bb83e8e2-creative-lead-artist-experiences-growth-operations?)

### We are building [**VAWAA**](https://vawaa.com). The platform for human creativity in an AI world.

It’s a global platform where people travel to learn directly from master artists in their studios for multi-day apprenticeships, stepping into the real rhythm of their practice and leaving changed. We are defining a new category at the intersection of travel, creativity, learning, culture, and transformation.

VAWAA artists are extraordinary ceramicists, painters, weavers, chefs, sculptors, shoemakers, woodworkers, designers, and Indigenous makers around the world.

Our guests are curious humans who want to make something with their hands, learn from someone extraordinary, and experience a place through its creative culture.

95% of our guests describe their experience as life-changing. 98% of the VAWAA artists have stayed on the platform. People come to us when they want something more meaningful than another vacation.

Demand is outpacing supply. On the other hand, we have 1,200 artists on the waitlist. Our team is small (just 5) and we’re just trying to keep up with the demand. We’ve built a really good product. Our founder built VAWAA after two decades in design and tech, and a life built around learning and traveling across 65+ countries. Our angel investors are great too, and repeat VAWAA guests.

If you’ve played the startup game before, you know that nothing in life is certain. That said, we have strong fundamentals, we believe our mission for human creativity is meeting the moment, and our business is working.

We are now growing our artist community across art forms, cultures and geographies.


### The role

We’re looking for a **Creative Lead, Artist Experiences, Growth & Operations** to own the growth of VAWAA’s artist supply—from identifying exceptional artists to building the relationship, shaping their VAWAA and getting them successfully launched.

This is not a traditional recruiting, sales, curation, editorial or operations role. It combines elements of all five.

You’ll need enough creative judgment to recognize what makes an artist exceptional, enough curiosity to uncover what isn’t obvious from an application, enough commercial instinct to shape an experience people will travel for, and enough operational discipline to move dozens of artists through a complex process without losing the human relationship.

Our immediate goal is to build the systems and pipeline to launch approximately 20-30 exceptional artists over four months, without compromising the quality bar that makes VAWAA distinctive.

The role will begin as a **3–4 month consulting engagement**. During this period, you’ll take ownership of a priority artist pipeline while helping us build and improve the systems for curation, onboarding and launch.

You’ll initially own the artist journey end-to-end. As we grow, we’ll add specialist support around you. Your role is both to do the work and help build the systems that allow it to scale.

This is a hands-on, computer-based role that does not involve travel. You should enjoy both creative decisions and daily execution: following up, editing copy, selecting images, maintaining the CRM, and meeting launch deadlines.


### What we're looking for

Our strongest candidates will likely be designers who became operators. It is essential that you have trained creative judgment, experience producing excellent work, and the ability to operate commercially and get things shipped.

* **Trained in architecture, interior architecture, industrial or product design**, or another discipline where you developed a strong understanding of materials, making, creative process and visual quality is essential. You can distinguish between work that is competent, work that is interesting and work that is genuinely distinctive and why it belongs on VAWAA.
* **At least 2–3 years of professional experience in a high-pace, high-standards creative environment** such as a design or advertising agency, multidisciplinary studio, technology company or creative startup, including experience in a computer-based role requiring responsiveness, self-direction, and reliable delivery.
* **Relationship management experience** through outreach, partnerships, onboarding, account management, or client support. You can manage multiple relationships at once. You’re warm and curious, but can also challenge someone constructively, build trust, establish expectations and move conversations toward decisions.
* **Commercially thoughtful.** You can respect an artist’s practice while thinking clearly about guest demand, pricing, positioning and what makes an experience compelling.
* **Strong editor with writing and visual judgment.** You can identify the story inside a large amount of messy information and can turn an artist’s practice into clear, compelling content.
* **Highly organized AI-native operator and systems thinker.** You can manage many moving relationships, deadlines and details simultaneously. You have experience maintaining a CRM, setting project timelines and can improve how information and work are organized. You’ve already used AI and automation to coordinate multiple projects, build workflows, manage information, or increase team capacity.
* **Careful execution and effective prioritization.** You work efficiently, catch details, manage competing deadlines, and take responsibility for the quality of finished work without repeated reminders.
* **Independent judgment and an ownership mindset.** You form an original point of view, explain your reasoning, make thoughtful decisions, and balance artist needs, guest experience, and business priorities.
* **Openness to feedback.** You advocate for ideas constructively, adapt when another direction is chosen, and remain engaged in making the work successful.
* **Cultural sensitivity, curiosity, and mission alignment.** You communicate respectfully across backgrounds and traditions and want to build a career helping a creative business grow.
* **Comfortable being hands-on.** You may negotiate with an established artist in the morning and edit their page copy in the afternoon. 

This role will become more specialized as the team grows. Initially, you need to be comfortable building while doing.

We expect most successful candidates to have **approximately 6+ years of relevant professional experience**, although we care more about what you’ve owned than a specific number of years.

An existing network of artists, designers, makers, or cultural organizations, as well as international or cross-cultural work experience, is a plus.


### What you'll own

**Find and curate exceptional artists**

* Review applications, research artists and build priority shortlists based on creative quality, distinctiveness, geography, art form and guest demand.
* Lead video conversations to assess artistic mastery, communication, teaching ability, studio environment, hospitality, reliability and overall VAWAA fit.

**Build relationships and move artists forward**

* Be a primary face of VAWAA to prospective artists.
* Build trust, understand motivations and hesitation, answer objections, establish clear next steps and help the right artists confidently decide to join.

**Shape VAWAA experiences that people will travel for**

* Work with artists to turn their practice into a compelling multi-day experience.
* Think about what makes the artist distinctive, what access a guest could have, what makes the experience worth traveling for, and how to balance artistic integrity with guest desire and business viability.

**Develop and launch the story**

* Review artist submissions, identify gaps, research missing context, write and edit profiles and experience descriptions, and select images that communicate the artist, process and place.
* Manage contracts, content, approvals, follow-ups and launch deadlines so artists move from interest to live experience without things falling through the cracks.

**Build systems as you go**

* Improve how we screen, research, prioritize, follow up, onboard and launch artists.
* Use AI and automation thoughtfully to increase your capacity while knowing where human judgment and personal relationships matter.

You'll help build the operating system that future team members can work within.


### What success looks like during the 3-4 month pilot

* Launched 20–30 exceptional new VAWAA artists, while maintaining our quality bar.
* Built a strong forward pipeline of artists already committed, contracted, or moving toward launch.
* Demonstrated that you can independently identify and prioritize strong VAWAA artists and make sound decisions about who should move forward.
* Built trusted relationships with artists and successfully moved the right ones from interest to commitment to launch.
* Strengthened the quality and commercial potential of their VAWAAs through your creative and business judgment.
* Created clear ownership and momentum throughout onboarding, so artists know what’s needed and continue moving forward without unnecessary delays.
* Built a repeatable process capable of supporting 8–10+ high-quality launches per month with significantly less Founder involvement.
* Identified the biggest remaining bottleneck and recommended the next hire or system needed to scale.


### Other things to know

We are remote, but need New York working hours, with candidates living in US/Canada time zones.

**Role begins as a 3-4 month paid consulting engagement ($7-$8K/month),** with compensation based on experience.

This is a substantial, hands-on engagement with ambitious goals. You should have sufficient capacity during the 3–4 month pilot to own the scope and deliver the agreed outcomes.

The engagement offers flexibility in how the work is structured, with reasonable overlap with the VAWAA team and artist schedules to keep the pipeline moving.

For an exceptional long-term fit, we expect the role to transition to full-time employment.

Upon conversion to full-time:

* $95,000–$110,000 salary, depending on performance and scope.
* 0.25%–0.5% equity or profit sharing options
* Health insurance
* 1 Free and discounted VAWAA experiences
* Work closely with our founder and community of artists and guests in 50+ countries + a mission that matters

**Growth path:** In 2–3 years, this role could evolve into Head of Curation / Artist Development & Supply / Artist Success with responsibility for team, strategy, systems, and growth.


### Why you shouldn’t work at VAWAA

VAWAA is small, global and evolving. We’re working toward an ambitious goal. If you’re looking for a comfortable, highly structured job, or one that feels exciting simply because it involves travel and art, this is probably not the role for you.

We value people who don't complain, keep commitments, ask clear questions, give direct updates, receive feedback without defensiveness, take responsibility when something slips, and learn quickly from mistakes.We’re remote, which requires trust, responsiveness, and strong follow-through.


### Apply

Apply via [this link](https://vawaa.breezy.hr/p/fef1bb83e8e2-creative-lead-artist-experiences-growth-operations?). 

We are based in New York, but open to remote applications within the US and Canada.

Tip: You’ll stand out if you include a link to a short video telling us why you want to do this and why we should hire you. Let us see your personality.

A quick note from me (founder):

I’ll be personally reviewing every application — and as a very small team juggling everything from fundraising to product to growth to support, my bandwidth is limited.

That said, this role is mission-critical. I'm eager to find the right person fast, and will reach out quickly if there's a potential fit.

I may not be able to respond to everyone, but I want to thank you in advance for your time, care, and interest in joining VAWAA. I’m excited to hear from you.

title: Founding Community & Creator Growth Lead
acceptedRemoteLocations: Vancouver, British Columbia; Toronto, Ontario; Waterloo, Ontario
description:
**Remote · Part-time · Equity-only: 0.5%–1.5%**
**Vancouver preferred, but open to the right person anywhere in North America**

### About Palette

Palette is a consumer travel product that turns the places people discover online into organized, searchable, and shareable trips.

Instead of losing a restaurant, hotel, activity, or destination inside TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, or a group chat, people can save it to Palette, see it on a map, organize it into an itinerary, and share the finished guide with others.

We are in an early beta and are focusing our initial growth on **travel creators and people who already curate and share trips with an audience**.

### The role

We are looking for a **Founding Community & Creator Growth Lead** to join Palette’s core team.

This is not a freelance content-production role, a social media coordinator position, or a job where you inherit a finished marketing playbook. You will work directly with the founders, designers, and engineers to build that playbook with us.

You will be on the ground speaking with creators and early users, testing acquisition ideas, shaping Palette’s positioning, identifying product gaps, and building the community and growth systems that future team members will inherit.

Our immediate opportunity is to help travel creators turn scattered social content into useful, polished Palette guides that they can share with their audiences. Your first major question will be:

> Can Palette help travel creators turn their content into genuinely useful trip guides—and can those guides become a repeatable source of new users?
> 

### What you will own

- Identify promising travel creators and build a focused outreach pipeline.
- Turn selected creator content into polished Palette ShareLinks and trip guides.
- Approach creators with something valuable already made—not a generic partnership pitch.
- Build genuine relationships with creators, early adopters, and travel communities.
- Work with interested creators to refine, publish, and distribute their guides.
- Develop creator campaigns, collaborations, ambassador ideas, and community programs.
- Produce lightweight short-form content that demonstrates creator guides and real Palette use cases.
- Test outreach messages, hooks, calls to action, collaboration formats, and distribution channels.
- Speak regularly with creators and early users, then turn their feedback into positioning, onboarding, and product recommendations.
- Track the funnel from creator outreach → published guide → guide views → sign-ups and imports.
- Document what works and turn early experiments into repeatable systems.
- Help recruit and onboard future community, content, and growth contributors as Palette expands.

### Why this is a founding role

You will not be joining at the edge of the company simply to manage social accounts. You will help shape how Palette grows and what we build.

As a core team member, you will:

- Work directly with Palette’s founders and product team.
- Participate in product and go-to-market discussions.
- Help define our initial creator and community personas.
- Influence the roadmap through direct conversations with creators and users.
- Design Palette’s first repeatable community-led acquisition engine.
- Establish the voice, partnerships, processes, and metrics that future hires will inherit.
- Help determine when and how Palette expands from creators into group travel and the broader consumer market.
- Have meaningful autonomy and equity reflecting the risk and responsibility of joining early.

### What success could look like in the first 60 days

Together, we would refine the exact targets, but an effective first 60 days might include:

- Define and validate the initial travel-creator persona.
- Build a focused pipeline of 50–100 relevant micro-creators.
- Create 10–15 strong example creator guides.
- Hold meaningful conversations with at least 10 creators.
- Secure the first 3–5 creator collaborations.
- Identify which creator segment and outreach approach respond most strongly.
- Publish initial creator-led campaigns and measure audience response.
- Establish a simple funnel for creator outreach, guide publishing, audience activity, and attributable sign-ups.
- Deliver clear product and onboarding recommendations based on creator feedback.

These are initial hypotheses to shape together—not rigid quotas imposed before we understand the channel.

### You may be a good fit if

- You understand TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, creator culture, and how online communities form.
- You have built an audience, managed creators, run partnerships, grown a consumer community, or helped an early product find its first users.
- You are comfortable with thoughtful cold outreach and consistent follow-up.
- You can create credible short-form content using tools such as CapCut, Canva, or equivalent tools.
- You know the difference between activity metrics and meaningful growth.
- You enjoy testing ideas, reviewing results, and improving the next experiment.
- You can turn informal community conversations into useful product insight.
- You are comfortable operating independently in an early-stage environment with limited resources.
- You communicate openly when something is working, failing, delayed, or unclear.
- You care about travel discovery, curation, creator tools, or community-led products.
- You can realistically commit approximately 10–15 hours per week.

You do not need to match every point. Evidence of initiative, judgment, consistency, and genuine community-building ability matters more than a conventional marketing résumé.

### Compensation and commitment

This is currently an **equity-only, part-time founding role**. Palette is pre-revenue and cannot offer a salary yet. Please apply only if that arrangement genuinely works for your current circumstances.

The anticipated equity range is **0.5%–1.5%**, depending on relevant experience, weekly commitment, scope of ownership, and mutual fit. The role begins with a 60-day mutual working period so both sides can evaluate the collaboration before finalizing a long-term agreement. Any equity arrangement, vesting terms, responsibilities, and expectations will be documented in writing.

If Palette reaches the financial milestones required to support salaries, converting core roles to paid positions will be a priority. However, candidates should not join based on an assumed date for cash compensation.

### How to apply

Please send:

1. Two or three examples of content, creator partnerships, communities, campaigns, or growth programs you personally worked on.
2. A short explanation of your specific contribution and the result of each example.
3. One travel creator or creator segment you think Palette should approach first—and why.
4. Your realistic weekly availability.
5. Why an equity-only founding role makes sense for you at this point in your career.

No long cover letter is required. We care more about what you have built, who you have brought together, and how you think.

### About the team

Palette is a remote, async-first team working across product, design, and engineering. Most team members currently contribute alongside other professional or academic commitments. We organize around clear goals and outcomes rather than tracking hours.

Because we are early, priorities will evolve as we learn. We value people who are comfortable with ambiguity but who also improve clarity for everyone around them. Open communication, ownership, and long-term alignment matter as much as raw output.

title: Founding Backend Engineer — Product Infrastructure & Data
acceptedRemoteLocations: North America; South America; Canada; United States; California, United States; New York City, New York; Vancouver, British Columbia; Toronto, Ontario; Calgary, Alberta; Saskatoon, Saskatchewan
description:
**Location:** Remote; North American time-zone overlap preferred
**Commitment:** Part-time, approximately 8–15 hours per week
**Compensation:** Equity-only, anticipated range 1%–3%
**Apply:** Through Wellfound

## About Palette

Palette turns travel content people discover online into organized places, maps, and shareable trips.

Instead of losing a restaurant, hotel, activity, or destination inside TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, a notes app, or a group chat, people can save it to Palette. Our system turns that content into structured travel cards, matches it to real-world locations, displays it on a map, and helps users build and share itineraries.

We are an early, remote team working across product, design, and engineering. Palette has a working product and an existing backend. We now need a founding backend engineer to take long-term ownership of the systems that make capture, organization, sharing, collaboration, and trustworthy travel-intent data possible.

## The role

This is a hands-on founding-team role—not a fixed-scope consulting project, an AI research position, or a job focused primarily on installing analytics tools.

You will inherit a working TypeScript, Node.js, Express, and MongoDB backend. Your job is to understand it before replacing it, identify the highest-risk architectural gaps, and improve it incrementally while the product continues to develop.

You will work directly with the founders, frontend engineering, and design. You will help translate changing product requirements into durable backend decisions, communicate technical trade-offs in plain language, and establish the foundation that future backend contributors will inherit.

The right person enjoys both architecture and the unglamorous work required to keep a real system dependable: debugging, migrations, retries, monitoring, tests, documentation, and production support.

## What you will own

### Product data architecture

- Redesign how canonical place and content data relate to user-saved cards, trip-specific card instances, notes, dates, ordering, creator commentary, and group context.
- Solve the current Master Card propagation problem so itinerary-specific changes do not overwrite a user’s original saved inspiration.
- Design schemas and migration paths that support ShareLinks, copied trips, group planning, and future creator experiences.
- Balance data integrity, development speed, and query performance without introducing unnecessary complexity.

### Capture and processing reliability

- Own the pipeline that receives social and web content and turns it into structured travel cards.
- Improve input validation, duplicate prevention, idempotency, retries, partial-failure recovery, and error visibility.
- Introduce background jobs or queues where they solve a real reliability or performance problem.
- Improve structured metadata extraction, multi-location handling, language support, and location resolution.
- Build graceful fallbacks when external platforms, AI providers, or place APIs fail or change.

### Product infrastructure and security

- Design and maintain APIs, authentication, authorization, and access controls.
- Support secure ShareLink permissions such as public read-only access, copying, commenting, collaboration, and access requests.
- Improve database indexes, connection handling, migrations, rate limiting, caching, and third-party API integrations.
- Establish practical logging, monitoring, alerting, and production-debugging workflows.
- Keep the system understandable and maintainable for a small, distributed team.

### Trustworthy behavioral data

- Help define a reliable event model covering the journey from saving content to creating, sharing, importing, and eventually booking a trip.
- Decide which events should be recorded by the browser versus the backend.
- Maintain consistent identifiers across users, cards, trips, ShareLinks, and external sources.
- Prevent duplicate or misleading events caused by retries, anonymous sessions, failed jobs, or inconsistent naming.
- Start with a lean analytics setup and recommend more infrastructure only when product needs and usage justify it.

## What the first 60 days could look like

The exact plan will be shaped together after reviewing the current system.

### First 30 days

- Learn the product, users, current architecture, and social-content capture flow.
- Audit the Node.js, Express, and MongoDB backend for reliability, security, schema, testing, and observability risks.
- Document how data currently moves from an incoming link to a saved travel card and itinerary.
- Identify the highest-risk technical issues and propose an incremental plan rather than defaulting to a rewrite.
- Establish basic visibility into processing failures and production errors.
- Agree on the first set of critical product events and data definitions.

### Days 31–60

- Implement the highest-priority architectural improvement, likely the Master Card versus trip-specific instance model.
- Improve capture reliability with validation, idempotency, retries, and clearer failure states.
- Add or improve background processing where needed.
- Add tests around critical capture, card, trip, and sharing flows.
- Document important decisions so another engineer can understand and maintain the system.
- Recommend the next phase for ShareLinks, group collaboration, creator tools, and behavioral data.

## What we are looking for

### Core experience

- Strong TypeScript and Node.js backend experience.
- Experience with Express or a comparable API framework.
- Experience designing document-database schemas with MongoDB or a comparable database.
- API design and third-party integration experience.
- Authentication, authorization, and role- or scope-based access control.
- Background jobs, asynchronous processing, queues, retries, and idempotency.
- Logging, monitoring, debugging, and production failure recovery.
- Automated testing and safe schema or data migrations.
- Evidence that you personally owned a meaningful backend in production.

### Valuable, but not mandatory

- Next.js familiarity.
- Geospatial data, map APIs, or location search.
- Social-content parsing, scraping, or browser automation.
- Structured LLM output, validation, and model-provider fallbacks.
- Product analytics and event architecture.
- Real-time collaboration or WebSocket systems.
- Affiliate attribution or booking integrations.
- Consumer, creator, or travel-product experience.

We care more about backend judgment and production ownership than a perfect match to every tool in our current stack.

## How you work

You may be a strong fit if:

- You investigate an existing system before proposing a rewrite.
- You can distinguish what Palette needs now from what may be useful after significant growth.
- You can explain architecture, risk, and trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical teammates.
- You build with an early-stage budget and understand the operating cost of your choices.
- You are comfortable making progress from a high-level product goal rather than waiting for a complete technical specification.
- You communicate assumptions, decisions, progress, and blockers proactively in an asynchronous team.
- You care about user and business outcomes—not only technically interesting systems.
- You are willing to own routine maintenance and production reliability after the initial architecture work is complete.
- You hold strong technical opinions but change your position when evidence supports a better approach.

## Why this is a founding-team role

You will not be joining simply to complete a backlog of backend tickets. You will:

- Own Palette’s backend as an ongoing product responsibility.
- Participate in product, data, and architecture decisions.
- Help prioritize new capabilities against reliability, technical debt, and user value.
- Shape the engineering practices and documentation that future hires inherit.
- Help evaluate, onboard, and mentor future backend contributors.
- Work directly with a non-technical founder and technical co-founder.
- Influence how Palette’s creator, group-travel, personalization, and monetization ideas become real systems.

We are looking for someone who wants to build Palette with the team over time—not treat Palette as another consulting client or temporary portfolio project.

## Commitment and compensation

This is currently an **equity-only, part-time role**. Palette is pre-revenue and cannot offer a salary today. Please apply only if that arrangement genuinely works for your circumstances; we cannot guarantee a date when cash compensation will become available.

The anticipated equity range is **1%–3%**, depending on experience, commitment, role scope, and mutual fit. The role begins with a 60-day mutual working period. Proposed equity, vesting, responsibilities, and long-term expectations will be reviewed and documented in writing as part of that process.

Most team members currently contribute alongside other professional or academic commitments. We expect approximately 8–15 dependable hours per week, one recurring team meeting, and consistent asynchronous communication. We do not track hours or prescribe a daily schedule; we agree on outcomes and expect open communication when availability, priorities, or timelines change.

## How to apply

Apply through Wellfound and include concise answers to the following:

1. Describe one production backend you personally owned. What did it do, what did you build, and what broke after launch?
2. Describe a messy system you inherited. How did you decide what to fix, what to leave alone, and whether to rewrite anything?
3. How would you process a submitted social link asynchronously while preventing duplicates and recovering from partial failure?
4. Which technologies have you used that you would deliberately avoid at Palette’s current stage?
5. How would you keep an early production backend and analytics setup lean and affordable?
6. How many hours can you consistently commit, and what other work competes for those hours?
7. Why do you want to join a founding team rather than complete a defined consulting project?
8. What would happen to your Palette commitment if you received a demanding paid contract or full-time offer?
9. Share one code sample, architecture diagram, or public project that reflects your own backend work. Clearly explain what you personally built.

We prefer concrete evidence and honest trade-offs over a long cover letter or a list of technologies.

title: Technical Support Specialist
Educational Content Manager
description:
# 🎼 Who we are 🎼

Flat is the online music editor offering the most intuitive experience to write, learn and share music. Founded in 2015 by 4 developers and music lovers under the company name **Tutteo**, we've been profitable and independent since 2017.

Today we serve 6M+ musicians (**Flat**), tens of thousands of schools (**Flat for Education**), and power embedded music notation across the web (**Flat Embed**). We're bootstrapped, profitable, and building for the long term.

# 🚀 The Challenge 🚀

We're looking for a **Educational Content Manager** to own how Tutteo creates, distributes, and implements content within Flat for Education.

This is a hands-on, teacher-first role that requires strong project managment skills. Flat for Education is used in tens of thousands of schools, and teachers increasingly ask us for more than a great notation tool: they want ready-to-teach lessons, standards-aligned sequences, and assessments they can trust. In Texas specifically, that means content built on the TEKS (Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills) and assesments that fit local standards. You'll be the person who builds that content, gets it through the formal review processes, and makes sure it actually works in a real music classroom.

You'll draw on your own teaching experience to decide what a good lesson looks like, then design, write, and structure the resources yourself. You'll also lead the effort to reorganize our existing resource library so teachers can find what they need, and you'll be a bridge between our Customer Success Managers and the content: answering curriculum questions, joining calls with district leaders, and turning what you hear from teachers into new material.

You'll do this with real leverage: a product teachers already love, a Customer Success team talking to schools every day, and a founding team that wants to hand education content to someone who can take it further. You'll report to the Head of Growth and work closely with Customer Success and Product.

# 🎩 What you'll own

**Texas-aligned content:** design and write TEKS-aligned lessons, units, and assessments for music education on Flat for Education, and own the TEKS alignment and submission process end to end.

**Assesment creation:** build and maintain the assignments that support teachers and districts participating in the assesment allotments in the USA.

**The resource library:** audit, restructure, and grow our existing teaching resources so they're organized by standard, grade band, and skill, and easy for a busy teacher to pick up and use.

**Content projects from brief to delivery:** scope the work, set timelines, coordinate with designers, Customer Success, and Product, and ship on schedule.

**Teacher training and presentations:** run webinars, record walkthroughs, and present at trainings and conferences so teachers know how to get the most out of the content and the product.

****Customer Success support:**** be the curriculum expert our CSMs can lean on to support with trainings, onboardings, or other places where capacity is needed. 

# 🛠 What you need to be a good fit 🛠

**You've taught.** You have 3+ years of real classroom teaching experience, in music and ideally in Texas, and you know what a lesson looks like when it lands and when it doesn't.

**You've designed curriculum.** You've written lesson plans, unit sequences, or full courses from scratch, aligned them to standards, and revised them based on what happened in the room. Familiarity with the TEKS, and with TIA, is a strong plus.

**You have strong project management skills.** You can take a large body of content, break it into a plan, hold yourself and others to deadlines, and keep several projects moving at once without dropping threads.

**You're comfortable in front of other teachers.** You've presented at PD days, led trainings, or run workshops, and you can explain a new tool or approach clearly to a room (or a Zoom) of educators.

**You write clearly.** Your instructions are easy to follow, your rubrics are unambiguous, and your emails to a district administrator read like they came from a peer.

**You're comfortable with technology.** You can learn a new platform quickly, you're at ease with Flat for Education (or will be fast), and you're curious about how software can make teaching easier.

**You operate independently.** You drive the highest-leverage work without being told what it is, close loops without being chased, and escalate a stuck item rather than repeating it for a month.

**Full professional proficiency in English.** You like music and believe the sheet music industry is ready for a change.

# 🏡 The Tutteo Approach 🏡

- When big projects come along, we all pitch in. Doing the dirty work is what we thrive on.
- We value feedback, honesty, and transparency.
- We're open to failure. A growth bet that doesn't move the metric is a valid result; a fix that doesn't ship is a process failure, and we know the difference.
- As the company grows, so do we.
- Talent has no borders. We're remote-first, rooted in Europe.

# 💶 Compensation & Benefits

- **Base salary: €65,000 to €80,000**, based on experience and seniority
- **performance bonus** tied to the growth targets of the company
- 100% remote, asynchronous, with no daily or weekly meeting overhead
- Health insurance, paid sick leave, generous paid time off
- Annual company retreats plus regular online gatherings
- Financial support to build your ideal work setup

*The salary range is indicative. The actual gross offered is adjusted to your location and contract type so the package stays fair and competitive wherever you are.*

# 🤝 How to apply 🤝

Please begin your note with the words "Music for All" so we know you've read this far.

Then answer the following questions:
1. Which of the Texas 6th grade TEKS do you feel would be the most difficult to build/assess within a digital platform and why? 

2. What is your experience with developing full curriculums within music educaiton.

title: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) Scientist
acceptedRemoteLocations: India; Europe; United States; Germany; France; United Kingdom; Italy
description:
About Carbon Trail

The world's leading retail brands are facing a wave of new sustainability regulations that carry significant financial and reputational risk. They need to measure, manage, and report on the environmental impact of their products, but the process is manual, slow, and complex.

Carbon Trail is the AI-powered platform built to solve this. We automate product impact assessment for fashion brands and retailers, turning a painful compliance chore into a source of strategic advantage. We are a fast-growing, founder-led company with a strong base of enterprise customers (including global leaders like Aditya Birla Fashion & Retail, Mammut, L.L.Bean, Deichmann). 

The Opportunity: Shape the Future of Sustainable Fashion Retail

As our Sustainability Scientist, you won't just be running calculations; you will be the scientific core of our platform and the trusted expert for our clients. You are the bridge between deep climate science, cutting-edge technology, and real-world impact in the fashion & retail industry.

This is a unique opportunity to move beyond traditional, manual consulting and scale your expertise through a data-driven SaaS platform. You will directly influence our product roadmap, empower brands to make meaningful decarbonization decisions, and establish Carbon Trail as the gold standard for environmental footprinting in fashion & retail.

What You Will Do

1. LCA & Climate Science Leadership (40%):

* Serve as Carbon Trail's in-house subject matter expert on LCA methodologies, with a laser focus on the PEFCR 3.1 for Apparel & Footwear.
* Build and refine complex LCA models for various fashion products (from cotton T-shirts to leather sneakers), integrating both primary supplier data and secondary database information.
* Stay on the bleeding edge of regulatory changes (e.g., PEFCR, Ecobalyse, Digital Product Passports) and translate them into actionable product requirements.
* Conduct deep research on material impacts (e.g., recycled vs. virgin fibers, new dyeing technologies) to ensure our platform's data is accurate and defensible.

2. Product & Technology Integration (30%):

* Work hand-in-glove with our CTO and Product teams to codify LCA logic, data structures, and calculation models into the Carbon Trail platform.
* Champion the use of advanced tools; leverage programmatic approaches (e.g., using Brightway/Python) to automate and scale our modeling capabilities.
* Validate product outputs, ensuring the software’s calculations are scientifically robust and compliant with relevant standards.
* Provide the "voice of the scientist" in product strategy sessions, ensuring our roadmap aligns with scientific best practices and market needs.

3. Client Strategy & Enablement (30%):

* Partner with the Customer Success team to lead technical deep-dives and workshops with our clients, educating them on LCA principles and the insights from our platform.
* Analyze client-specific supply chains to identify and quantify the most effective decarbonization "hotspots" and opportunities.
* Act as the ultimate technical authority during complex client onboarding and support escalations, building deep trust and credibility.
* Author whitepapers, blog posts, and webinars to establish both your personal brand and Carbon Trail’s position as a thought leader.

What Will Make You A Great Fit

You are the bridge between deep environmental science and our fast-moving, software-driven platform. We're looking for a unique blend of scientific rigor, technological curiosity, and a passion for driving real-world change.

Core Experience & Scientific Foundation (Must-Haves):

* Domain Expertise: 5+ years of hands-on experience conducting Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs), with a strong preference for work in the textile, apparel, footwear, or consumer retail industries.
* Methodology Mastery: Deep, practical knowledge of key standards. You must be able to apply PEFCR for Apparel & Footwear (EF 3.1) and ISO 14040/14044. 
* Carbon Accounting Fluency: Solid experience with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol and a clear understanding of how PCFs feed into corporate Scope 3 reporting.
* LCA Modeling from Scratch: Proven ability to build detailed LCA models, mapping greenhouse gas emissions and material flows across the value chain, using both primary and secondary data.
* Strong Communication Skills: You are confident and articulate, capable of leading workshops and acting as a trusted advisor to our clients.

Technical & Product Aptitude (The Enablers):

* Tool Proficiency: Hands-on experience with LCA software and databases. You should be familiar with tools like SimaPro, GaBi, or openLCA and databases such as Ecoinvent or Textile Exchange.
* Education & Mindset: A Bachelor's degree or higher in environmental engineering, sustainability science, or a related field is preferred, but we believe deep practical experience can be just as valuable. You have a startup mindset—proactive, adaptable, and eager to take ownership.

Bonus Points (These will make you stand out):

* Next-Gen Tooling: Experience with (or a strong, demonstrated desire to learn) programmatic LCA tools like Brightway. This signals you're ready to help us scale.
* Product Collaboration: You have previously worked with software/product teams, translating complex scientific requirements into product features.
* Public Voice: You have a public profile (e.g., publications, conference talks) in the sustainability space or a passion for building one.

If you have demonstrated this capability and believe you are a right fit, please do reach out at hello@carbontrail.net.

title: Staff/Principal Software Engineer — AI Platform (contract)
description:
Just Whole Care (JWC) is a California health-equity consulting firm building Assessment Lab (AL), an AI-assisted platform our team uses to turn complex organizational, financial, clinical, policy and operational evidence into assessments, decision tools, financial models and client deliverables.

We are looking for a genuinely senior software engineer for a bounded, part-time contract engagement to stabilize and simplify AL and help us successfully deliver the next phase of the product for two active client engagements.

This is not a greenfield build and not a mandate to redesign the platform.

AL already works across Python, Google Cloud Run services and jobs, Google Cloud Storage, Google Apps Script and Sheets, document retrieval and parsing, multiple LLM providers, cached model artifacts, durable job state, release bindings and AI-assisted development through Cursor.

Our immediate need is an engineer senior enough to understand that system as a whole, make it substantially more reliable and simpler to operate, and say no when more code or architecture is not the right answer.

**Initial engagement**

We expect approximately **60–70 hours of work**, generally **5–10 hours per week**, with somewhat heavier involvement at the beginning and flexibility around releases or production incidents.

Target contract rate: **$150–$165/hour**, depending on experience.

There may be follow-on work if it is valuable to both sides, but this is not being presented as a full-time position.

**Your first mandate: make AL boring**

Before adding significant new functionality, you will help us make the existing system predictable:

**Make assessment runs reliable.**
A new real-world organization should be able to enter AL, progress through its stages, checkpoint safely, resume when necessary and complete without routine engineering intervention.

**Make recovery simple.**
Failures should be diagnosable and recoverable without stale workers, stuck state or manual command-line archaeology.

**Make releases routine.**
We want one reproducible, safe release path with automatic agreement across the relevant Cloud Run, job and Apps components, clear rollback and fewer environment- or credential-specific surprises.

**Improve observability.**
We should be able to tell quickly where an assessment is, how long it has been there, what it has cost, what failed and whether a human actually needs to intervene.

**Freeze important interfaces.**
Help us stop repeatedly changing core data, evidence and product contracts while client-facing capabilities are being built on top of them.

**Reduce complexity.**
Identify experimental, duplicate or unnecessary paths that do not help current client delivery. Turn them off, defer them or recommend later removal rather than building around them.

**Then help us finish the client-critical product work**

Once the critical run/release foundation is dependable, you will help productize the specific AL capabilities required for our current Safe & Sound and Compass engagements.

These include structured baseline and data-quality outputs, funding and billability decision tools, non-duplication and funding-braid logic, useful financial modeling and pro formas, implementation tools, cross-assessment synthesis and related staff-facing workflows.

Our healthcare, policy, finance and consulting experts own the domain meaning. Your role is to turn those requirements into dependable software without creating unnecessary platform complexity.

**How we use AI development tools**

JWC uses Cursor and advanced language models extensively in engineering.

We are not hiring someone simply to type code that an AI agent can produce.

We need someone who can:

* determine the smallest correct engineering change;
* give AI coding agents clear, bounded work;
* review what they actually built;
* identify system-level failure modes that local code review misses;
* stop unnecessary refactors, frameworks and speculative development;
* decide when existing behavior should be reused instead of rebuilt;
* get approved work through testing, release and production verification; and
* reduce total engineering and model spend rather than adding another management layer.

A major measure of success is that the CEO spends less time coordinating ChatGPT, Cursor, releases and engineering incidents.

**What we're looking for**

You likely have:

* 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, with Staff-, Principal- or equivalent senior technical ownership.
* Strong hands-on Python experience.
* Strong backend and distributed-systems judgment.
* Production experience with Google Cloud Platform or comparable cloud infrastructure.
* Experience with containerized services, asynchronous jobs, durable state, checkpointing/retry patterns and distributed failure recovery.
* Strong experience with CI/CD, release engineering, observability and production incident response.
* Experience debugging systems that cross application code, cloud infrastructure, APIs, storage and external services.
* Strong automated testing skills and the judgment to know which tests actually prove production behavior.
* Comfort inheriting substantial existing code and simplifying it without breaking working behavior.
* Excellent judgment about when not to build something.
* Ability to communicate technical decisions clearly to a non-engineer CEO and domain experts.
* Willingness to take a problem from diagnosis through tested, deployed resolution rather than handing off implementation fragments.

**Helpful but secondary**

Experience with any of the following is valuable, but we would choose excellent systems judgment over narrow expertise in these areas:

* modern LLM APIs and AI-enabled applications;
* RAG, document retrieval or evidence-grounded AI;
* AI coding agents such as Cursor;
* Google Cloud Run, Cloud Build and GCS;
* Google Workspace APIs, Google Sheets or Apps Script;
* structured LLM outputs, model evaluation and provider failover;
* document extraction or Document AI;
* healthcare, Medicaid or other regulated/sensitive-data environments;
* spreadsheet or financial-modeling applications.

**This role is not a fit if**

Your instinct when inheriting a complicated system is to start over.

It is also probably not a fit if your primary expertise is prompt engineering, ML research, frontend design or infrastructure in isolation.

We need an engineer who enjoys taking a system that has accumulated too many moving parts and making it smaller, clearer and reliably useful.

**What success looks like**

By the end of the initial engagement:

* ordinary AL assessments complete without routine engineering intervention;
* stalled work has a straightforward recovery path;
* releases are reproducible and substantially less fragile;
* we can quickly see assessment state, failure, duration and meaningful cost;
* important interfaces stop changing underneath client-facing development;
* unnecessary development paths have been identified and deferred or disabled where appropriate;
* the Safe & Sound and Compass capabilities that actually require engineering are working;
* Cursor and model spend are materially better controlled;
* development requires substantially less CEO orchestration; and
* AL is easier for the next engineer to understand than it was when you arrived.

title: Performance Marketing Manager
description:
**Role Summary **

Own paid user acquisition for companie's US business end to end: channel strategy, budget 
allocation, creative testing velocity, and measurement. You scale spend profitably 
against deposit and GMV payback targets, and you defend every dollar with 
incrementality logic. 

You decide where the money goes, what gets tested, and why. Creative, data, and 
product teams are your partners; the CAC-to-payback outcomes are yours. 

**Key Responsibilities **

**Channel Strategy and Scaling **

● Own performance channels end to end: Google App Campaigns, Meta App Install 
Campaigns, Apple Search Ads, and emerging channels (DSPs, OEM, 
influencer-performance, playable networks). 
● Plan and control the full UA budget: allocation across channels, campaigns, and 
geos, tuned weekly against payback data. 
● Scale what works and kill what doesn't, fast. Document the why either way. 
Real-money gaming compliance in UA 
● Operate within RMG ad certification and policy frameworks on Google, Meta, 
and Apple, including state-level targeting restrictions in the US.

responsible gaming requirements.

advantage. 

**Measurement and Incrementality **

SKAN/post-ATT measurement, and web-to-app flows. 
● Design and run incrementality tests: geo holdouts, PSA tests, and audience 
splits. Report what's truly incremental, not what platforms claim. 
● Build the CAC-to-payback view by channel and cohort: cost per first deposit, 
GMV payback windows, and contribution-margin breakeven. 

**Creative Testing Engine **

● Run a high-velocity creative testing loop with the creative team: hypotheses, 
batch testing, and structured readouts. 
● Develop audience-creative fit: what converts casual players vs. competitive cash 
players, and where fatigue sets in. 
● Feed winning angles back into concepting; kill losing angles with data, not 
opinions. 

**Economy Guardrails & Analytics **

● Define target segments and how to reach them: lookalikes, broad + creative-led, 
and re-engagement of lapsed depositors. 
● Own the paid funnel jointly with product: install → registration → first game → 
first deposit. Diagnose leaks, brief fixes. 
● Coordinate with LiveOps on event-led acquisition moments and seasonal spikes. 

**What You Bring **

**Experience **

● 4+ years driving growth through digital acquisition channels, with 2+ years 
hands-on managing large-scale app campaigns on Google, Meta, and Apple 
Search Ads. 
● Strongly preferred: experience in real-money skill gaming, social casino, 
iGaming, or F2P gaming, where you owned revenue-based payback targets. 
● Experience managing large budgets with full planning and budgetary control. 
● Proven track record of scaling acquisition profitably: meeting or exceeding 
revenue and payback goals, not just install targets. 
Measurement craft 
● Deep hands-on experience with MMPs (AppsFlyer, Adjust, Kochava) and app 
attribution, including SKAN and post-ATT reality. 
● Demonstrable experience running incrementality and structured testing 
programs: bidding, audience, creative. 
● Strong analytics fluency: cohort analysis, LTV modeling, payback curves; SQL is 
a strong plus. 

**Mindset **

● Self-starter who executes under deadlines without being chased. 
● Startup-culture comfort: ambiguity, speed, and owning outcomes with a small 
team. 
● Experience scaling acquisition geographically and managing agile growth 
processes. 
● Intellectual honesty: you report incrementality even when it makes your channel 
look worse. 

**Good to have **

● US market UA experience, including familiarity with state-level RMG advertising 
restrictions. 
● Experience managing or mentoring a growth team. 
● Exposure to web funnels and PC/cross-platform acquisition. 
● Creative strategy instincts: you can brief a winning concept, not just measure 
one. 

**What This Role Is Not **

● Not a brand marketing role. This is performance: every dollar has a payback 
target. 
● Not a reporting seat. You operate campaigns hands-on and own the budget, not 
the dashboard. 
● Not install-count growth. Success is measured in deposits, GMV payback, and 
contribution margin.

* Speaker Diarization

Applicable legal protections, including protections against discrimination and harassment, continue to apply as required by law.

description:
About the role
MAX is an AI astrology assistant serving thousands of members through a FastAPI backend. It combines Swiss Ephemeris, retrieval and LLMs to answer questions about natal charts, transits and forecasts. We handle tens of thousands of LLM calls each week across free, basic and paid tiers.
We're looking for an experienced engineer to reduce LLM serving costs by at least 40% without reducing answer quality or accuracy.
This is not a prompt-tuning or model-selection role. Changing models is not an option. The focus is on finding savings within the existing model setup through better use of tokens, caching, request flow and deterministic alternatives.

What you'll do
Audit LLM spend by model, stage, tier and endpoint using raw logs and SQL.
Identify and cost potential savings before implementing them.
Optimize caching, prompts, payloads, request flow and unnecessary LLM calls.
Identify opportunities to replace deterministic work with code where appropriate.
Ship changes incrementally through staging and validate cost, quality and accuracy before production.
Document what worked, what didn't and why.

What we're looking for
Proven experience working with LLMs at scale and reducing LLM serving costs.
Strong understanding of token economics, caching and API pricing.
Strong SQL and production debugging skills.
Experience with Python/FastAPI and Anthropic or similar LLM APIs.
A measurement-first approach. We care about evidence, not assumptions.

Please don't apply if you haven't worked with LLMs at scale or directly reduced LLM serving costs.

Success
40%+ reduction in LLM serving cost
No regression in answer quality or factual accuracy
Savings verified against deduplicated production logs

Format
Contract, scoped engagement. Remote.
To apply, send your background and relevant experience to leonard@greatawakener.com.

title: Google Ads Support Specialist
description:
# Google Ads Support Specialist

**Remote | Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising**

## About Slaymaker Marketing

Slaymaker Marketing is a growing digital advertising agency managing paid-media campaigns for e-commerce and B2B clients. We combine senior-level strategy with hands-on execution across Google, Microsoft, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, and other advertising platforms.

We value honesty, improvement, respect, ownership, selflessness, and results. We are looking for someone who communicates clearly, pays close attention to detail, and takes responsibility for producing accurate work.

## About the Role

We are hiring a Google Ads Support Specialist to support campaign implementation, optimization, QA, analysis, and reporting across Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising.

You will work alongside experienced account leads who own client strategy and communication. Your role will be to translate that strategy into accurate campaign execution, monitor account performance, maintain organized documentation, and proactively surface opportunities and concerns.

This role is ideal for someone with strong Google Ads fundamentals who wants to develop into an independent account manager and strategist.

## What You’ll Own Day to Day

* Build and update Search, Shopping, Performance Max, Demand Gen, Display, and YouTube campaigns
* Conduct keyword, search-term, competitor, audience, and placement research
* Develop and implement keyword lists, match types, negatives, audiences, and targeting
* Draft and upload responsive search ads, extensions, assets, and other ad variations
* Make approved changes to bids, budgets, targeting, exclusions, and campaign settings
* Monitor spend pacing, CPA, ROAS, CTR, CVR, impression share, and other relevant metrics
* Review search terms and identify negative keywords or expansion opportunities
* Conduct routine account checks and flag unusual performance or delivery changes
* Pull and organize data for client reporting and internal analysis
* Prepare performance notes, insights, and recommended actions before client calls
* Support Google Merchant Center and product-feed troubleshooting
* Maintain campaign naming conventions, labels, tracking templates, and UTMs
* Review conversion actions, attribution settings, URLs, and campaign goals
* Document completed changes, test results, open questions, and next steps
* Implement campaigns and changes in Microsoft Advertising when needed
* Proactively identify opportunities instead of waiting exclusively for assigned tasks

## QA Expectations

Every campaign build or major change must receive complete QA. You will be expected to verify:

* Campaign type, objective, bidding strategy, budget, and schedule
* Keywords, match types, negatives, audiences, and exclusions
* Geographic, demographic, device, network, and language settings
* Ad copy, assets, final URLs, tracking templates, and UTMs
* Conversion actions and campaign-level conversion goals
* Merchant Center products, feed settings, and product-group structures
* Brand exclusions, account-level negatives, and suitability settings
* Naming conventions and reporting consistency
* Alignment with the approved strategy and client instructions

## Required Qualifications

* Hands-on experience building and optimizing Google Ads campaigns
* Strong understanding of Search campaign structures and keyword strategy
* Familiarity with Shopping and Performance Max campaigns
* Ability to interpret performance data and identify meaningful trends
* Strong attention to detail and commitment to pre-launch QA
* Clear written English and dependable internal communication
* Strong organization and time-management skills
* Ability to manage work across multiple accounts and deadlines
* Willingness to document work and communicate progress proactively
* Ability to identify concerns and suggest solutions before escalating them

## Preferred Qualifications

* Experience supporting both e-commerce and B2B lead-generation accounts
* Familiarity with Microsoft Advertising and Google Merchant Center
* Experience with GA4, GTM, Looker Studio, Shopify, and HubSpot
* Understanding of conversion tracking and offline conversion imports
* Experience with product feeds and feed-optimization tools
* Familiarity with value-based bidding, attribution, and lifecycle-stage reporting
* Experience working with monthly advertising budgets of $50,000 or more
* Familiarity with project-management and team-communication platforms

## What Success Looks Like

* Campaigns and optimizations are completed accurately and on schedule
* Every launch receives thorough QA
* Search-term reviews and account checks are completed consistently
* Reporting data and call-preparation notes are accurate and useful
* Performance issues are identified and escalated early
* Account leads have clear visibility into completed work and blockers
* Recommendations are supported by data and aligned with client goals
* You gradually progress from execution support toward independent ownership of smaller accounts

## What We’re Looking For

The right person is analytical, dependable, organized, and proactive. You should be comfortable following a defined strategy while also thinking critically about whether the requested implementation makes sense.

We do not want someone who blindly completes tasks. We want someone who checks their work, raises concerns, investigates performance changes, and contributes ideas for improvement.

To apply, please provide:

* A brief overview of your Google Ads experience
* The campaign types and monthly budgets you have managed or supported
* Examples of e-commerce or lead-generation accounts you have worked on
* An example of an optimization or QA issue you identified
* Your experience with GA4, GTM, Merchant Center, and Microsoft Advertising
* Your availability and preferred working hours

title: Social & Content Lead (Equity Only)
description:

The product is live (v1), and we’re now focused on early growth and distribution.

We’re looking for someone to take ownership of social and build it for the product and the brand.

The role:
- This is not a typical “social media manager” role.
- You will define how the brand shows up, what content we create, and test what actually drives attention, engagement and growth.
- You’ll work directly with the founder and a marketing strategist (currently focused on SEO, blogs, analytics, email) with no pre-defined playbook.

Current status:
- v1 live and iterating based on user feedback
- Partnerships live with accommodation groups in Colombia and Peru
- Distribution via high-footfall locations (QR / physical presence)
- Small, focused team (Founder, CTO, Designer, Marketing Strategist, Part-time sales/marketing support + advisors)
- Founder has been based in Latin America for 5+ years

Existing content:
- We’ve already started building and testing content on @lyosapp
- Early content is live - we're looking for someone to take this further and scale it into a consistent growth channel

Content approach:
- Travel and brand-led content
Original content built around travel, long-term travel and the ideas behind Live Your Own Story. This could include travel observations, humour, questions, opinions, experiences and the broader themes of independence, expectations, identity and making your own choices.
- Founder-led content
Stories, opinions, experiences and other original material from the founder. The founder can provide a strong source of content and participate in filming, but the strategy should not depend on the founder being the face of every piece of content.
- Creator collaborations
Work with relevant travel creators to develop content that fits their audiences and gives LYOS access to new communities. Identify creators, develop collaboration ideas and build ongoing relationships.
- User-generated content
Real travel stories, experiences, photos and videos from LYOS users and the wider travel community. Find ways to encourage, source, curate and repurpose this content.

The goal is to build a consistent content engine, not a single personality channel.

What you’ll do:
- Own TikTok and Instagram as primary channels
- Edit and publish short-form content
- Develop repeatable content formats
- Work with the founder on filmed content (direction, editing, posting)
- Identify and reach out to relevant travel creators for collaboration
- Build and manage a pipeline of creator relationships
- Build and maintain a consistent posting cadence while continuously testing quality, formats and volume

Organic first: Build content that earns attention organically. Paid distribution may come later, but we want to understand what resonates before putting meaningful budget behind it.

Who this is for:
- You’re proactive and comfortable operating without structure
- You’re comfortable editing and producing short-form content
- You’re comfortable directing or working with someone on-camera (not required to be the face)
- You’re comfortable both creating content and proactively reaching out to creators
- You’re comfortable shipping content quickly and iterating based on performance
- You want ownership, not just execution

Bonus if you’re currently based, travelling, or have spent time in Latin America.

Compensation:
- Equity accrues based on time contribution and converts at the first funding event in line with investor terms.
- Transition to paid (part-time → full-time) as the company scales

Details:
- Fully remote
- English required


This role is suited to someone who wants to build and own a growth channel from an early stage, not manage pre-defined social channels.

title: Chief Technology Officer (Head of Engineering)
description:
Energytech Cypher exists to use technology to accelerate clean energy commercialization by using technology to connect innovators, investors, and strategic buyers by giving them the insight they need to find and build meaningful commercial relationships.  We do this by facilitating authentic connections, providing critical resources, and providing organizational development; this is enabled by leveraging modern AI and proprietary data sets.  

Energytech Cypher is hiring its first full-time technical leader. This person owns the architecture, engineering practice, and technical direction of our platform as we scale from early customer deployments to a production system serving the energy and industrial sector.

In addition to strategy, this is a hands-on building. The CTO is the functional Head of Engineering: hands on the keyboard (with Claude Code), in architecture reviews, and deploying to production - working as the direct counterpart to our Head of Product. We are looking for someone who has run a small, high-output engineering team (3-6), has recently written and reviewed production code, and is ready to take on additional scope as the company grows.

**Core Responsibilities**
*1. Platform Architecture & Technical Direction*
* Architecture Ownership: Defining how the platform must function over the next two to five years, and making the trade-off decisions as we service our stakeholders
* Infrastructure & Data Decisions: Owning cloud and database strategy and deployment implementation with a clear view of cost, operational burden, and scaling behavior. You should be able to tell us what our infrastructure looks like as we grow our customer base an order of magnitude
* Technical Judgment: Bringing lived operating experience to decisions currently made on best-available industry practices.
*2. Engineering Team Leadership & Operations*
* Hands-On Engineering: Writing code, reviewing pull requests, and working directly alongside the engineering and coding teams. 
* Engineering Operations: Establishing platform and engineering best practices - environments, release process, testing, observability, incident response - and knowing what to do when things break.
* Team Development: Assessing the skill gaps on our current engineering team and building a deliberate plan to close them. Growing early-career developers into stronger ones is a core part of this role.  Hiring and building a team and facilitating a strong performance culture.  
*3. Cross-Functional Partnership & Communication*
* Product Partnership: Serving as the technical counterpart to our Head of Product - answering the engineering questions that shape product decisions, and reflect on the state of the art for agentic interaction in product design.
* Stakeholder Influence: Explaining technical direction and trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders - executives, investors, customers, and partners - and building alignment around them.
* Customer-Facing Engagement: Participating directly in technical discussions with enterprise and industrial customers during evaluation, integration, and deployment.
*4. AI-Enabled Product Development*
* Applied AI Direction: Setting the strategy for how AI and large language models are used inside our platform and inside our own engineering workflow.
* Tooling & Technique: Maintaining active, current fluency with AI platforms, prompting approaches, and evaluation methods, with a bias toward measurably better output rather than novelty.


**About Energytech Cypher **
Energytech Cypher connects innovation to industry and is pioneering new ways to use AI to accelerate commercialization partnrships. We connect the dots between emerging technologies, industry adopters, and financiers through novel search tools, curated content, and deep industry insight. Our mission is to accelerate the transition of energy by breaking down the barriers between innovators and their early adopters.
