Bachelor's

title: Account Executive — B2B Fintech
description:
ApolloX Technologies
Remote — Canada / United States
Commission-Based | Uncapped Earnings

ApolloX is building AI-native financial infrastructure for business payments.

We’re starting with Canadian businesses managing recurring Canada–U.S. payment flows and combining payment execution, FX, financial workflows, reporting, and Atlas our intelligence layer within one platform.

The product is live. Now we’re building the commercial engine.

We’re looking for a high-performing B2B salesperson who can prospect, run discovery, build relationships with senior decision-makers, and close meaningful business.

This is not an SDR role, and it is not a role where leads simply appear on your calendar.
You will help create revenue.

What You’ll Own
- Build and manage your own pipeline of qualified B2B prospects
- Prospect into Canadian and U.S. businesses through outbound calling, email, LinkedIn, referrals, and strategic outreach
- Run discovery calls with founders, CFOs, controllers, finance leaders, and business owners
- Understand a prospect’s current payment, FX, reconciliation, and financial workflow challenges
- Position ApolloX around the customer’s actual financial operations rather than delivering a generic product pitch
- Conduct product demonstrations and guide prospects through the buying process
- Handle objections, negotiate commercial terms, and close new customers
- Maintain disciplined follow-up across longer B2B sales cycles
- Work directly with ApolloX’s Founder & CEO on messaging, objections, pricing, and sales strategy
- Feed customer insights back into the company as we refine our GTM playbook


Who We’re Looking For
You should already know how to sell.
We’re particularly interested in candidates who have:
- Proven experience closing high-value B2B products or services
- Experience managing a deal from initial outreach through close
- Strong outbound prospecting ability
- Excellent discovery and objection-handling skills
- Confidence speaking with executives and financial decision-makers
- Experience with multi-call sales processes rather than purely transactional sales
- Strong CRM and pipeline discipline
- The ability to operate independently without a heavily scripted sales organization
- A track record of consistently following up and moving deals forward
- Experience in fintech, payments, banking, treasury, FX, financial services, B2B SaaS, accounting software, ERP, or business finance is strongly preferred.
- Existing relationships with CFOs, controllers, accounting firms, importers/exporters, finance teams, or mid-market companies are a major advantage.


What This Is Not
This is not primarily:
- Consumer sales
- Retail sales
- An inbound-only closer position
- Selling coaching programs or digital courses
- A role where ApolloX provides every lead and you simply take calls
We are looking for someone who can create pipeline and close it.

Compensation
This is a performance-driven, commission-based opportunity with uncapped earning potential.
Compensation will be tied to business you successfully bring to ApolloX and may include:
- Commission on closed customer revenue
- Ongoing commission tied to qualifying customer revenue
- Additional incentives for larger accounts
- Performance bonuses for commercial milestones
- Potential opportunity to grow into a larger sales leadership role as ApolloX scales
Exact commission structure will be discussed with selected candidates.

The principle is simple:
Create meaningful revenue for ApolloX, participate meaningfully in the value you create.

Why Join ApolloX
You’d be joining before the sales organization has been fully built.
That means you will have unusually direct influence over:
How we sell.
Who we target.
What customers respond to.
How the playbook evolves.
You’ll work directly with the founder and have the opportunity to establish yourself as one of ApolloX’s earliest commercial hires.
We’re looking for people who want responsibility, ownership, and upside — not simply another sales job.

How to Apply
Along with your résumé, send us a short answer to these four questions:
1. What is the largest B2B deal you have personally closed?
2. What were you selling and who was the buyer?
3. Did you source the opportunity yourself?
4. Walk us briefly through how you moved the deal from first contact to close.


ApolloX Technologies
Understand. Decide. Execute.
AI-native financial infrastructure for how businesses move money.

description:

Ability to make a global impact with your work, leading innovations in Conversational AI, Energy/Utilities, ESG, HealthTech, IoT, Risk/Compliance, CyberSecurity, PLM and more.

title: Content Manager (India)
description:

title: VP of Finance & Operations
description:
### **About Us**
Rilian is an agentic systems integrator built for the AI-native era of security. Its platform,
Caspian, gives defense and security teams a single command layer across their entire stack —
pre-trained agents amplify every analyst, capture institutional knowledge, and deploy into
air-gapped, sovereign, and compliance-restricted environments in days, not years. Founded
by lifelong practitioners, Rilian's mission is to enhance global security by promoting
cutting-edge cyber and defense capabilities among the U.S. and its Allies.

**About the Role:**
We're looking for a hands-on VP of Finance & Operations to build the operational foundation
of a growing, well-funded seed-stage company. This is an operations-first role: roughly 80%
operations, 20% finance. You'll bring structure and discipline to a fast-moving business —
spanning day-to-day operations, financial planning, and the systems and processes that let
us scale — while staying close enough to the work to execute it yourself when needed.
You'll work directly with the founders and leadership team, and because Rilian serves
defense, government, and critical infrastructure customers, you'll also touch the operational
complexity that comes with that.

**What You’ll Do**

Operations (primary focus)
● Own and continuously improve day-to-day business operations — efficiency,
accountability, and scalability
● Build the processes, systems, and operating rhythms an early-stage company needs,
without over-engineering for a stage we haven't reached yet
● Drive cross-functional initiatives spanning people, technology, vendors, contracts, and
general company operations
● Identify operational gaps and personally close them — designing a process, standing
up a system, or doing the work directly
● Support government contracting, compliance, and international deployment logistics
as they arise
● Serve as a trusted operating partner to the founders as the company grows

Finance (supporting)
● Own the annual operating plan and rolling forecasts — budgeting, forecasting, and
variance analysis
● Build financial models covering revenue, headcount, and cash flow to support
planning decisions
● Establish KPIs and dashboards that give leadership and the board clear visibility into
performance
● Partner with outside accounting / fractional CFO resources on more technical
accounting, tax, and compliance work

**What We're Looking For**
● ~10 years of progressively broader experience in business operations at an early-stage
startup or similarly lean, high-growth environment
● Demonstrated ability to build processes and infrastructure from scratch, not just
manage established functions
● Working knowledge of financial planning — budgeting, forecasting, financial
modeling, and resource allocation
● Direct experience partnering with founders or senior leadership on company-wide
priorities
● Comfort moving between strategic thinking and hands-on execution, with high
ownership and judgment
● Experience in cybersecurity and/or government contracting
● Experience managing international operations or foreign entities

**Why Join Us:**
● Mission-driven team and culture.
● Competitive salary and performance-based bonuses.
● Opportunity to work with a passionate and forward-thinking team in a growing
industry.
● Continuous learning and professional development opportunities.
● Be at the forefront of cybersecurity innovation, helping clients protect their most
valuable assets.

title: Family Office Operations Manager
description:
Full-Time | India | Remote | Directly Supporting Founder & Family Office

The Role

I am looking for a highly capable, resourceful Family Office Operations Manager to help manage a diverse set of business, investment, financial, property, and family-office priorities.

This is not a traditional Executive Assistant role, and it is not purely a strategy or investment role.

You will work directly with me across multiple areas: investments, real estate, new business ventures, a growing dental platform, banking and financial administration, India-related matters, charitable initiatives, properties, travel, vendors, and selected personal/family projects.

The common thread is simple: things need to get figured out and completed.

I need someone who can take an unclear problem, determine what needs to happen, find the right people or information, present sensible options, and then drive it through completion.

What You Will Work On

1. Family Office & Financial Operations

You will help coordinate and track matters involving:

* Investments and investment opportunities
* Banking and financial administration
* Account opening, documentation, remittances, and follow-ups
* Coordination with accountants, lawyers, bankers, wealth managers, and other advisors
* Insurance and important financial documents
* Entity and compliance-related matters
* Charitable/foundation projects
* India and U.S. financial administration
* Maintaining organized records of important assets, accounts, entities, contacts, and deadlines

You are not expected to personally provide legal, tax, or investment advice. Your job is to make sure the right experts are involved, questions get answered, decisions are documented, and nothing falls through the cracks.

2. Investments, Real Estate & New Ventures

Projects may include:

* Researching potential investments
* First-pass financial analysis and underwriting
* Real estate opportunities
* Evaluating businesses for acquisition
* Building acquisition target lists
* Finding brokers, lenders, operators, lawyers, or other specialists
* Comparing financing alternatives
* Researching new business ideas
* Preparing concise decision memos
* Tracking deals from initial idea through decision and execution

Strong financial skills are helpful, but intellectual curiosity and the ability to learn quickly matter more.

3. DSO & Business Projects

I am building several businesses and initiatives, including a dental platform.

Projects could include:

* Dental practice acquisition research
* DSO/MSO development
* Market research
* Competitive research
* Financial modeling
* Recruiting executives or operators
* Finding acquisition targets
* Coordinating diligence
* Working with outside advisors
* Following up on important business initiatives

You will not be responsible for running the day-to-day operations of my existing companies. This role sits primarily on the owner/family-office side.

4. Personal & Family Operations

This is an explicit part of the position.

Projects may include:

* Managing projects related to family properties
* Coordinating contractors, interior designers, vendors, or property managers
* Major purchases and vendor comparisons
* Travel research and coordination
* Handling documentation and administrative matters
* Coordinating family-related projects
* Solving unusual one-off problems

These are not “side tasks.” They are part of managing a family office.

If you are interested only in corporate strategy and consider personal or administrative execution beneath you, this role will not be a good fit.

5. Project Management & Follow-Through

One of your most important responsibilities will be creating order around many simultaneous projects.

You will maintain a simple Family Office Control Center showing:

* Active projects
* Next action
* Owner
* Deadline
* Current status
* Blockers
* Decisions required from me

I should not have to repeatedly ask:

“Whatever happened with that?”

You should already know.

How We Will Work Together

I operate quickly and often have many projects moving simultaneously.

Sometimes I will give you a well-defined assignment.

Other times I may simply say:

“Figure out how we can accomplish this.”

You should be comfortable turning that into a structured project.

I do not want lengthy reports unless they are necessary. I prefer:

Problem → Options → Recommendation → Cost → Next Step

When something can be handled without me, handle it.

When you need a decision from me, make the decision easy.

Working Hours

This role is based in India and is not a U.S. night-shift position.

Most work can be completed during reasonable India working hours.

However, because you will work directly with me in the United States, some overlap is necessary.

You should be comfortable with:

* Flexible working hours
* Occasional evening calls
* Being available up to approximately 1:00 AM IST when necessary for important discussions or urgent matters

This does not mean working until 1:00 AM every day.

The role is primarily outcome-driven rather than clock-driven. I care much more about ownership, responsiveness, and execution than watching someone sit online for eight particular hours.

Who I Am Looking For

You will probably be unusually good at this job if you:

* Are extremely organized
* Follow through relentlessly
* Write and communicate clearly
* Are comfortable speaking with senior professionals
* Can research unfamiliar subjects quickly
* Understand basic financial statements and Excel
* Can compare alternatives logically
* Know when to research something yourself and when to find an expert
* Are comfortable managing several unrelated projects simultaneously
* Don’t need detailed instructions for every task
* Are willing to pick up the phone and solve problems
* Can respectfully challenge an idea when the facts don’t support it
* Protect confidential information
* Have excellent judgment

Experience in family offices, investment banking, consulting, PE/VC, founder’s offices, real estate, finance, or high-level operations is useful but not mandatory.

Exceptional execution ability matters more than pedigree.

What This Role Is NOT

This is not:

* A traditional personal assistant position
* Pure investment banking
* Pure private equity
* Pure corporate strategy
* A research-only job
* A job where someone gives you a checklist every morning

It is a hybrid Family Office + Investments + Special Projects + Personal Operations role.

Some days you may analyze an acquisition.

Another day you may resolve an India banking issue.

The next day you may coordinate a property project, evaluate an investment, find a specialist, or help plan a new business.

That variety is the job.

What Success Looks Like

After 90 days:

* I have one reliable place to see every important family-office project.
* Important deadlines aren’t being missed.
* Projects continue moving without me constantly following up.
* Advisors and vendors receive timely responses.
* Research comes back with conclusions rather than piles of information.
* Problems reach me with proposed solutions.
* My involvement shifts increasingly toward decisions rather than administration.

Ultimately, I am looking for someone who becomes the person I can say:

“Please own this.”

And then stop worrying about it.

Application

Please send:

1. Your résumé or LinkedIn profile.
2. A short introduction explaining why this unusual role interests you.
3. One example of a complicated project you personally drove from ambiguity to completion.
4. Your current and expected compensation.
5. Your current location in India.
6. Your notice period / earliest possible start date.
7. Whether you are comfortable occasionally being available until approximately 1:00 AM IST.

title: FP&A Consultant, Loyalty Programs
description:
### About Us 

KYROS is the only actuarial firm solely focused on loyalty programs. We’re a small, boutique, fully remote consulting firm built by actuaries and technologists who wanted to rethink how actuarial work is done. 

We help your favorite frequent flyer program, hotel, bank or retail loyalty program measure and optimize the economic value that the program creates through a modern, highly technical combination of actuarial theory, machine learning, and big data technology. 

As a lean and growing team, we operate much more like a startup than a large consulting firm. We move quickly, expect a high level of execution, and rely on team members to take ownership of their work end to end. This is an environment for people who work efficiently, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and enjoy delivering high-quality work without layers of process or bureaucracy. 

We also leverage AI in service of human potential -- not to replace our people, but to amplify what they’re already great at. It’s freed our team up to spend more time on the work only a person can do: solving hard client problems, pushing into new territory, and building real relationships. If you’re comfortable working alongside AI as part of the job, you’ll fit right in here. 

Likewise, if you thrive on variety, enjoy coming to work not always knowing exactly how your day will unfold, and get energized by balancing multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment, this role is for you. 

### The Role 

**Salary range**: $150,000-$200,000

We’re looking for a highly motivated finance and analytics professional to help us manage and grow a portfolio of client relationships. This role is best suited for someone who has spent their career close to a loyalty, rewards, or points program — in FP&A, financial analysis, or a similar role inside an airline, hotel, retailer, bank, or other loyalty-driven business — and who is ready to bring that perspective to a wider range of clients. This is a place where you can make a real impact, as opposed to getting lost as one more cog in a big machine. 

You’ll act as the primary point of contact for a set of clients, partnering with our analysts and data scientists to scope and execute quantitative analyses rooted in machine learning. This includes estimating and forecasting loyalty program liability, customer lifetime value (CLV), and other key drivers of program economics. You don’t need to write the code yourself, and you don’t need to come from an actuarial or traditional consulting background — but you already understand how a loyalty program shows up on a company’s books and in its financial planning, and you can translate that fluency for our clients. 

Just as important as the domain fluency is the entrepreneurial mindset it takes to work here: clients bring us open-ended business problems with no existing solution, and you’ll need to be comfortable building a solution in the ambiguity rather than waiting for one to be handed to you. 

Even within our specialty, no two engagements look alike. Airline, hotel, retail, gaming, and ticketing loyalty programs all behave differently. If you’ve spent your career on the inside of one of these industries, this is a chance to use that experience across many programs instead of just one, while also being at the forefront of innovation that will take loyalty program analytics to the next level. 

### A Day in the Life 

No two days look exactly the same, but here’s what the work typically looks like: 

- You’re the first call for a set of assigned clients, fielding quick ad hoc questions one moment and steering a multi-week project the next

- You work with analysts and data scientists to translate a client’s business problem into a structured quantitative analysis, then build and manage the project plan to keep it on track

- You dig into the outputs of predictive models to sanity-check the results and understand what’s really driving them, not just what the model produced

- You synthesize those results into a clear narrative: building the slides, the talk track, and the recommendation that helps a non-technical client make a real business decision

- You present to clients directly, fielding questions in real time and adjusting the story based on what matters most to them

- In between, there’s always ad hoc work, from a client question that needs a quick turnaround to a problem nobody at KYROS (or elsewhere) has solved before

- You stay connected through a steady cadence of team standups, a structure that keeps our fully remote team organized and workloads manageable

There’s also real opportunity to shape how we work: to improve our client deliverables, contribute to internal tools like our KPI validation platform, and help define what a great client engagement looks like as we grow. 

**Requirements**

### Basic qualifications

- **Years of Experience**: At least 5 years of professional experience, ideally in FP&A, financial analysis, or a related finance/strategy role
- **Education**: Bachelor’s degree in math, statistics, economics, finance, or another quantitative field; candidates with strong analytical experience and a different academic background are also welcome to apply
- **Industry Background**: Direct experience with a loyalty, rewards, or points program — ideally at an airline, hotel, retailer, bank, or similar company — with a real understanding of how the program works and what drives its economics
- **Analytical Rigor**: Comfortable working with large transactional datasets, aggregating, structuring, and interpreting data to find the story inside it
- **Project Management**: Demonstrated experience owning relationships end-to-end, setting expectations, managing scope, and delivering results on tight timelines
- **Business Sense**: Ability to connect technical or financial analysis to a client’s business goals, understanding not just what a model says, but what it means and why it matters
- **Skills**: Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, complex formulas, large dataset manipulation) and strong PowerPoint skills; a sharp sense for what makes a good chart, slide, or client story, including the ability to direct and critique AI-generated visuals and decks; experience with project management tools and data visualization software (e.g., Power BI)
- **Modeling**: Working understanding of predictive modeling concepts, sufficient to guide, question, and validate work performed by analysts and data scientists
- **Communication**: Ability to clearly distill complex, technical concepts into language non-technical audiences can understand and act on
- **Other**: Strong communicator, growth mindset, comfortable operating with ambiguity and little day-to-day guidance
- **AI Fluency**: Comfortable, and enthusiastic, about using AI tools as part of the daily workflow

### Bonus points if you have

- Prior experience in a client-facing consulting or advisory role
- Actuarial background or exam progress
- Prior experience in a small or startup-like consulting environment

**Benefits**

- Retirement Plan (401k with employer match)
- Qualified Small Employer Health Reimbursement Arrangement (QSEHRA)
- Discretionary PTO
- Fully remote

title: Catch-Up Accountant
description:
Catch-Up Accountant
EFS Group is hiring a Catch-Up Accountant to lead one of our highest-demand services: bringing client books up to date, accurate, and ready to move forward. This is a dedicated, specialized role for someone who enjoys solving the puzzle of incomplete, inconsistent, or inaccurate historical records, not simply maintaining books that are already clean. You'll own each catch-up engagement from intake through delivery, working directly with clients to resolve open items and ensure the financials are accurate, complete, and reliable for both the client and our team. As you grow into the role, you'll also take on responsibility of new client onboarding, helping ensure a smooth transition from signed proposal through the start of ongoing accounting services.

Responsibilities
- Own catch-up bookkeeping engagements from kickoff through delivery, rebuilding books for clients whose records are incomplete, inaccurate, or behind.
- Manage bank and merchant data imports for each catch-up period, ensuring completeness before reconciliation begins.
- Reconcile bank and credit card accounts across the full catch-up period, tracking down and resolving every discrepancy between books and statements.
- Review existing bookkeeping, client-maintained or from a previous provider, to catch miscategorizations, duplicate entries, and missing transactions before rebuilding the ledger.
- Apply cash and accrual accounting methods as each engagement requires, following IFRS/GAAP standards throughout.
- Meet regularly with clients to resolve open items and keep engagements moving on schedule.
Scope and estimate catch-up projects accurately, flagging complexity early to protect timelines and budgets.
- Reconcile historical payroll allocations and sales tax liabilities against filings already made, identifying and documenting any gaps.
- Document the reasoning behind historical entries clearly, and keep engagement documentation organized in the Teamwork portal.
- Liaise with the tax department after catch-up completion to confirm the books are ready and viable for filing with federal entities where necessary.
- Deliver every engagement within EFS's budgeted timeframe, communicating any potential adjustment to the completion timeline to the client and EFS team as early as possible.
- Own closing calls to wrap up each completed engagement with the client.

As you grow into the role, take ownership of new client onboarding, managing the process end to end.

Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Accounting or a related field, or a minimum of two years of professional-level work experience in accounting.
- Proven experience with catch-up or cleanup bookkeeping engagements, not just steady-state monthly maintenance.
- Comfortable working in both cash and accrual accounting, with a solid grasp of IFRS/GAAP standards.
- Strong judgment working through incomplete, disorganized, or conflicting historical records.
- Proficiency in payroll allocations and reconciliations using various payroll software integrations.
- Sharp attention to detail, with the discipline to fully reconcile every period rather than approximate a close.
- Familiarity with a variety of cloud bookkeeping technologies and tools.
- Strong project management skills, with the ability to scope, sequence, and drive a multi-period catch-up to completion on deadline.
- Confident communicator, comfortable leading client meetings and requesting documentation directly.
- Able to manage multiple concurrent catch-up projects independently in a fast-paced environment.

How To Apply
To apply, please email your resume and cover letter to careers@efsgllc.com. Be sure to include the job title in the subject line of your email.

About the Company
EFS Group, PLLC is a fast-growing and highly entrepreneurial group of virtual outsourced accountants and fractional CFOs. Inc. Magazine named EFS Group, PLLC #1064 on the 2023 list of the 5,000 fastest-growing privately held companies in the United States. We specialize in serving million-dollar retail and service businesses led by women entrepreneurs seeking growth and scalability. Our expertise lies in preparing these businesses financially, enabling them to secure funding and investment capital. We are renowned for our strong client relationships and our dedication to addressing their unique financial requirements.

description:
### Who We Are

**About leafplanner**
We’re pioneering the intersection of WealthTech, family office management, and professional services technology. Our platform—built on over 30 years of wealth advisory and risk-management expertise—helps ultra-affluent families and their advisors organize both “hard” and “soft” information, identify blind spots, and streamline the succession-of-information. By combining cutting-edge software with emotionally intelligent guidance, we empower families to preserve their legacies and make informed decisions, generation after generation.

**Our Mission**
At leafplanner, we believe that true financial stewardship extends beyond numbers. We’re dedicated to educating, engaging, and empowering families so they can leave an enduring legacy. Through innovative tools and thought leadership, we help clients uncover opportunities, prevent gaps, and build lasting peace of mind.

**Recognition**
We’re proud recipients of four Family Wealth Report Awards, and our insights have been featured in Forbes, Spear’s, Crain Currency, Wealth of Wisdom 2.0, Family Offices: The STEP Handbook for Advisors, and top industry podcasts.

### The Opportunity

We're looking for a Client Success Manager to build out and own the client success and support function for our HNW/UHNW clients and the professional service firms (RIAs, family offices, estate attorneys, CPAs) who serve them.

This is a newly defined role. Historically, client-facing work at our company has been handled through a concierge model—high-touch, largely manual, data-entry-heavy support delivered by our Concierge Team. As we scale, we need someone who brings traditional Client Success and Support rigor, proactive account health monitoring, structured onboarding, ticketing discipline, renewal/retention ownership, and client communication cadences — while still being comfortable rolling up their sleeves on concierge-style work when white-glove service calls for it.

You'll partner closely with our Implementation Manager on onboarding and leafplan build-out, and with our Director of Concierge Services (upon her return from leave) to establish a clearer division of labor between "Client Success" and "Concierge" going forward. During the Director's 6-week maternity leave, you will also help ensure continuity of service for existing concierge clients.

### Who You Are

* 4+ years in a Customer Success, Account Management, or Client Support role, ideally at a B2B SaaS company; experience serving high-touch, high-expectation clients (wealth management, legal, financial services, or similar) strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to build or mature a support/CS function — not just execute within an existing one.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable communicating directly with UHNW individuals, family offices, and professional advisors with appropriate discretion and polish.
* Hands-on experience with HubSpot (CRM/communication tracking) and JIRA (ticketing/workflow) required; Stripe familiarity a plus.
* Empathetic, calm under pressure, and detail-oriented — HNW/UHNW clients often bring sensitive, high-stakes situations.
* Comfortable with some hands-on/administrative work (data entry, plan building) even while primarily focused on strategic CS work.

**Nice to Have**
* Prior experience in estate planning, wealth management, or working alongside RIAs/family offices/attorneys.
* Experience designing client coaching/adoption programs or lifecycle communication sequences.
* Prior experience at a small company (<20 employees) where roles span broadly.

### Key Responsibilities

**Client Success & Support**
* Own the end-to-end post-sale client experience through onboarding, adoption, retention, renewal, and expansion for a portfolio of HNW/UHNW clients and professional service firm accounts.
* Build and manage a real support function in HubSpot and JIRA — triaging, prioritizing, and resolving client tickets/requests with clear SLAs, rather than ad hoc handling.
* Establish and track account health indicators (usage, engagement, satisfaction, risk signals) and proactively intervene before issues escalate.
* Manage the client communication cadence—check-ins, QBRs, education, renewal conversations—using HubSpot to track relationship history, touchpoints, and pipeline/renewal status.
* Serve as an escalation point for complex or sensitive client issues, particularly those involving billing (Stripe) or account status.

**Concierge & Onboarding Support**
* Partner with the Implementation Manager on new client onboarding, including leafplan build-out, configuration, and data setup.
* Step in on concierge-style, white-glove tasks as needed, particularly for top-tier UHNW relationships where a more hands-on, done-for-you approach is expected.
* Help define where "Client Success" ends and "Concierge" begins, and document those handoffs so the distinction is clear to the team and to clients.

**Client Communication & Coaching**
* Design and deliver leafplan completion and coaching plans including structured outreach sequences that drive clients toward full plan completion and sustained engagement.
* Create clear, professional client-facing communications (emails, guides, check-in scripts) that reflect the trust and discretion HNW/UHNW clients and their advisors expect.
* Train clients and professional service firm contacts on platform functionality, best practices, and how to get the most value from leafplanner.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration**
* Work with the Technical Product Manager to route and prioritize product feedback, bugs, and feature requests surfaced through client interactions.
* Partner with Engineering (Sr. Software Engineer / Software Engineer) on troubleshooting escalated technical issues.
* Provide input on internal tooling and process (HubSpot, JIRA workflows) to improve visibility into client health and support volume.
* During the Director of Concierge Services' leave, coordinate with the Implementation Manager to maintain coverage across both concierge and CS responsibilities.

### Our Culture and Benefits

leafplanner is built on the pillars of trust, communication, empowerment, and transparency. We are dedicated to fostering a culture that embodies these values at every level. Our team enjoys competitive salaries, healthcare stipends via ICHRA, unlimited PTO, and flexible remote work options, reflecting our commitment to their well-being and professional growth.

**Commitment to Diversity & Accessibility**
We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and abilities. Reasonable accommodations are available throughout the hiring process—please let us know how we can support you.

**Ready to shape the future of family office technology?**
Apply today and join us in helping families preserve their legacies, one meaningful relationship at a time.

title: General Application
description:
### About Wunder

Wunder is building a Modern Energy Company.

We were founded with one simple vision: to address the greatest crisis of our generation by accelerating the deployment of solar energy. In doing so, we help businesses, municipalities, and schools save money by delivering clean on-site power. We convert simple warehouses into electrified industrial platforms built for the future. We enable the nation’s leading commercial and industrial real estate firms to capture the benefits of solar across their properties. We align ESG goals with revenue targets, and the renewable energy assets we’re deploying today will power America’s tomorrow.

Wunder is actively developing hundreds of commercial solar projects across the country. Our team has evaluated more than 30,000 properties for solar across all 50 states to meet our customers where they are—which is everywhere! Our customers have a national footprint and so do we. Wunder’s proprietary technology platform enables us to develop solar at scale, across a portfolio that includes everything from self-storage facilities and schools to data centers and industrial logistics facilities. Our average solar system—about 430 kilowatts in size—can offset 350,000 pounds of coal burned each year of system operation!

* * *

### General Application Overview

We’re thrilled you’re interested in joining our team! If you don’t see an open position on our Careers Page that fits your unique background, you are invited to submit your resume and cover letter for consideration via this General Application. 

If we have a position available that fits your skill set, we will get in touch. If you are interested in a specific posted position, please apply directly to the appropriate role.

* * *

### Some Benefits To Look Forward To

Wunder provides one of the only tangible opportunities to truly save the planet - and that’s hard work! Your job impacts nearly every facet of your life, so we provide an extensive compensation and benefits package to ensure Wunder has a positive impact on your life, both personally and professionally. 

#### Salary & Equity

Wunder determines the successful candidate's compensation package, including equity in the form of stock options, throughout the interview process based on experience and expertise. The final compensation package will be discussed with the candidate during the final stages of the interview process.  

#### Benefits & PTO

Wunder truly cares about your happiness and well-being, so we strive to ensure our benefits offerings are of top quality. We offer the following benefits to all team members:

- 100% employer-paid medical, dental & vision insurance for all team members
- 50% employer-paid medical, dental & vision insurance for dependents
- Employer-paid short-term disability, long-term disability & life insurance
- 401k Matching (Wunder offers a 50% match with a max of 2% company contribution to your 4% employee contribution)
- Health Savings Account (HSA), Medical FSA, and Dependent Care FSA
- Up to 14 weeks fully paid Parental Leave for childbearing parents; 6 weeks fully paid Parental Leave for non-childbearing parents
- 11 paid holidays & unlimited PTO

#### Culture

Wunder believes connecting with your team members is instrumental to job satisfaction and your ability to solve complex problems. You’ll find our team taking coffee walks or solving problems at a whiteboard, while also cycling, hiking, climbing, skiing, camping, and dining all over our mile-high home: Colorado. Here are some of the ways we facilitate a flexible yet cohesive work environment:

- A big, bright, modern office located in Downtown Boulder; in-office meals and a fully stocked kitchen
- Commitment to diversity, equity & inclusion through company principles, programs, and events (see below for even more details)
- In-person monthly events, team offsites, and company retreats
- Annual professional development budget and unlimited book budget
- And so much more!

#### Commitment to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI)

Wunder is focused on providing a happy, productive workplace, and we’re constantly improving it! We’re committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive workplace in which all team members have an opportunity to contribute to the success of our mission. At Wunder, people are valued for their skills, experiences, and diverse perspectives, and we encourage all individuals to apply, even if they don’t check every box in the ‘About You’ section above. 

Our commitment to equity is embodied in company policy, but it’s also evident every day in how we conduct business and the internal initiatives and programs we provide for our team. Here are some of the ways we strive to ensure everyone feels welcome, safe and free to be themselves at Wunder:

- A holistic, actionable DEI learning strategy that enables all team members to advance inclusivity in a meaningful way
- Inclusive, objective recruiting processes and partnerships with diverse candidate pools & organizations
- Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), events and initiatives focused on inclusivity
- Equitable Compensation Principles that ensure every team member is paid fairly and equitably
- An environment that values feedback, active listening, flexibility and open communication

title: Co-Founder — Technical & Product
description:
# Co-Founder — Technical & Product

**Cairn · Open AI/Data Infrastructure**
**Website:** cairndev.sh
**Role:** Co-Founder
**Type:** Founding / Equity
**Focus:** ML Infrastructure · Distributed Systems · Open Source · Product

## About Cairn

Cairn is building an open-source, vendor-neutral control plane for AI and data infrastructure.

Modern AI workloads span Kubernetes, cloud GPUs, training frameworks, workflow engines, data systems, model registries, storage, evaluation, and multiple infrastructure providers.

Cairn provides a common control layer for composing this heterogeneous infrastructure into **governed, reusable, installable pipelines**—without locking users into a particular cloud or technology stack.

We're looking for a co-founder to help turn this technical foundation into a widely adopted product and company.

## The Role

We're looking for a **technical co-founder with strong product and business instincts**.

You'll work across:

**Engineering → Product → Users → Business**

This is a hands-on founding role. You'll help shape the architecture, build the product, talk to users, define what we should build next, and help establish the company's direction.

## What You'll Do

### Build

* Shape Cairn's core architecture and technical direction.
* Build ML/data infrastructure and developer-facing systems.
* Work on capabilities, operators, contracts, pipelines, execution, and integrations.
* Design systems that work across Kubernetes, cloud, on-prem, and different AI infrastructure providers.
* Write production code and review architectural decisions.

### Product

* Talk directly with ML/platform engineers and understand their problems.
* Turn infrastructure pain points into simple product abstractions.
* Define Cairn's APIs, developer experience, and workflows.
* Decide what belongs in the core platform versus integrations and extensions.
* Prioritize what to build based on real user needs.

### Business

* Identify early adopters and design partners.
* Develop Cairn's initial go-to-market strategy.
* Explore commercial models around the open-source project.
* Build partnerships and integrations.
* Help define Cairn's positioning and long-term company strategy.

### Open Source

* Help grow the Cairn open-source ecosystem.
* Build integrations and extension points.
* Work with contributors and early users.
* Communicate Cairn's architecture and vision to the community.

## What We're Looking For

### Must Have

* Strong software engineering background.
* Experience with **ML, infrastructure, or distributed systems**.
* Ability to understand complex technical systems quickly.
* Strong product sense.
* Genuine interest in building a company, not just a product.
* Comfortable operating with significant ambiguity and ownership.

### Particularly Relevant Experience

Experience with one or more of:

* ML infrastructure / MLOps
* Kubernetes
* Distributed systems
* Cloud infrastructure
* Data platforms
* Model training / evaluation
* Developer platforms
* Workflow/orchestration systems
* Open-source infrastructure
* AI developer tools

You don't need to be an expert in everything above.

We're much more interested in someone who can **bridge ML, infrastructure, product, and business**.

## The Mindset

You naturally ask:

> What problem are we actually solving?

> Who has this problem?

> Is this abstraction useful beyond our own code?

> How do we make this dramatically easier for the user?

You care about technical quality, but you also care about adoption.

You can move from:

**architecture diagram → code → customer conversation → product decision**

without needing someone else to connect the dots.

## Why Now?

AI infrastructure is becoming increasingly heterogeneous.

Teams are combining different:

* models and providers
* training systems
* compute platforms
* data systems

title: Community Engagement Coordinator
description:
**A mission worth building for, on a model you should understand before you apply.** FiNC is changing how politics works in America, and we are Crowd-Starting it. **Contributor roles are not paid yet; compensation is deferred.** Full details in the Crowd-Starting section below.

## About FiNC

We're assembling a coalition to change how politics works. Forever.

3 middlemen decide which candidates you ever hear about: big money, party gatekeepers, and media manipulation. They control the money, the access, and the visibility every candidate needs to win, so they decide who wins before anyone votes. The system isn't broken. It's rigged, and it works exactly as it was built to.

FiNC (Future is Now Coalition) is the way around it. Citizens say what they care about, candidates say who they are, and the 2 sides connect with nobody in between. Our work is the human side: outreach, PR, social, and citizen buy-in. We're not marketing a website. We're campaigning for a better way to choose leaders.

We're largely neurodiverse, direct by default, and soft on hierarchy. Team members here are partners and co-architects, not employees. Full mission and culture at futureis.org.


## IMPORTANT: This involves DELAYED COMPENSATION -- Please read carefully

To maintain our independence and avoid conflicts of interest, we are not accepting investors or financing that comes with strings attached. Instead, **we are Crowd-Starting FiNC: building it together from the ground up**.

***We ask team members to contribute 15 to 20 hours per week during this phase, with compensation deferred until we are operational. That includes the Founder, who has not drawn a salary and will not until the team does.***

This model only works if you see it as a **short-term investment for a long-term return**. Contributors who build this with us **earn an ownership stake in FiNC**.

We are an LLC today because we needed a legal home to start from. We are **building toward something akin to a nonprofit cooperative, where the people who build the organization own it, and we operate not for profit in the meantime**.

This model filters for people who believe in the mission deeply enough to build alongside us. It is not for everyone, and that is okay.

## Culture and Employment

**A New Kind of Organization for a New Kind of Democracy**

- Neurodiversity and diversity-of-thought are strengths, not obstacles
- Servant leadership, dynamic team structures, and shared ownership
- Purpose over profits, value over hours, and respect for work-life balance
- We reward authenticity, passion, and commitment, not conformity
- We support individual weaknesses to enhance collective strengths
- Continuous role assessments, long-term growth opportunities, and real career sustainability

From your first 2-way interview, you will see (and feel) how radically different we are.

# Community Engagement Coordinator

## The Role

We're looking for a **Community Engagement Coordinator** to be the person citizens actually talk to.

People show up in our comments every day on Reddit, TikTok, Instagram, and everywhere else we post. Some are curious, some are skeptical, and some are angry at a side they assume we're on. All of them deserve a real answer from a real person.

This is a flexible seat. You would start in the comment sections and our subreddit, and move to wherever citizens are talking to us that month.

## The problem you would solve

Most people have stopped expecting anyone to answer. Everyone you can reach has no power, and everyone with power is unreachable, so after a while people stop asking.

Our comments are one of the few places where that isn't true. A good reply can turn someone who came in ready for a fight into someone asking a better question. No reply, or a canned one, confirms what they already believed about every political group online.

We're getting real attention, especially on Reddit. What we're short on is the person who meets it.

## What you would do

- Reply to comments across Reddit, TikTok, Instagram, and the other platforms we're active on, quickly and like a person
- Help run conversations in our subreddit: start threads, keep them on track, and make it a place people actually want to post
- Collect real stories from real citizens, in their own words and with their permission, about why the old way stopped working for them
- Share our micro-actions and help people follow through on them: small, quick things that make a real difference
- Bring back what you're hearing. The questions that keep coming up, the objections, the posts that land, so the team builds on what's real
- Move with the work. When a new citizen effort goes live, you're likely one of the first people on it

## What success looks like in 90 days

- **Nobody who asks a real question in our comments goes unanswered**
- **At least 1 subreddit thread you started or ran** turned into a real conversation
- **A running list of what citizens keep asking us**, sorted so the rest of the team can use it
- **A handful of real citizen stories**, collected with permission

## Who we're looking for

- 1+ years running an online community, moderating, managing social for an organization, or something close enough that you can show us the work
- **Warm with strangers who show up angry.** You can take the heat out of a comment without taking the bait
- **You disagree without talking down.** Nobody here gets made to feel stupid for what they believed yesterday
- **You don't take sides in the comments.** We host every position and take none, and people test that constantly. You can be critical of both parties' leadership in the same breath and mean it
- **Consistent.** A comment section is a daily beat. It rewards the person who's there every day far more than the one who's brilliant once a week
- **Good judgment on when not to reply.** Some comments want a fight, not an answer. Knowing which is half the job

**Drawn more to the partner side?** Apply anyway. We're hiring for both halves of our Outreach Team, citizens and partners, and we'd rather sort out the fit together than have you guess.

description:

That's what we're building at Hyatus: fully autonomous apartments.

Something breaks, someone needs to fix it, and someone else needs to make sure it actually got fixed. We want software and AI agents to coordinate the people, tools, and services behind all of that, end to end.

We run real apartments, so we get to build against real problems and see whether it works. We're close. We need a great builder to help us get the rest of the way.

You know backend. You've gone all in on AI.

You've spent years building backend systems and cloud infrastructure. You understand APIs, databases, queues, deployments, and what happens when production gets messy.

And the way you build has changed. You use coding agents constantly. You know how to split up work, give agents the right context, get them working together, and check the result. You're always experimenting with how much further you can take it.

What you'll build

- Agent workflows that coordinate guest service, maintenance, cleaning, and day-to-day apartment operations.

You'll own problems all the way through: figure out what should happen, ship it, watch it work, and fix what doesn't. That includes the unglamorous parts: retries, permissions, evals, and knowing when to bring in a human.

Move fast. Use the best tools you can find. Bring ideas we haven't thought of.

Show us how you work

Send something you've built: a demo, a repo, a short walkthrough. Tell us what the agents did, what decisions you made, and what broke along the way.

We care about strong engineering judgment, curiosity, and the ability to turn an ambitious idea into something that works.

Remote, worldwide.

Help us make apartments run themselves.

title: SENIOR MOBILE ENGINEER (FOUNDING TEAM)
description:
**ABOUT ZAHLN**

Zahln, by Zysygy, is building Germany's zero-fee payment network. Merchants pay zero transaction fees. We route payments directly over SEPA Instant, bypassing Visa, Mastercard, and the entire card network chain. No hardware. No card reader. Just a phone.

Nearly every digital payment in Germany today moves over infrastructure owned outside Europe, and a share of each one leaves the continent as fees. We are building the alternative on European rails: a fully software-based merchant POS and a consumer super-app for everyday financial life, payments, transport, utilities and government services in one place, settling account to account over SEPA Instant, with European data residency by design. Think what UPI did for India. We are doing it for Germany, on infrastructure Europe controls.

We start on campus. Students pay in the mensa, at city merchants, and for university services from one wallet, and the institution pays no transaction fee. Everything they touch to do that is an app on a phone. This role owns it.


**EXIST FUNDING**

This role is open to students and recent graduates (within the last 5 years) of German universities who are eligible for EXIST Gründerstipendium funding.


**LOCATION**

Remote within Germany, with regular time in Augsburg. English is our working language. German is useful and not required.


**ROLE OVERVIEW**

You own the app. iOS and Android, one codebase, from an empty repository. Nobody hands you a specification and nobody reviews your architecture before you commit to it.

Students will never read our deck or look at our architecture. They open the app in a mensa queue with eleven people behind them and either pay in three seconds or they do not. That moment is the whole company and it belongs to this seat.

One constraint shapes everything else here: you cannot hotfix a phone. A bad build sits in review for days, and a share of your users will never update at all. So the app has to be built on the assumption that you will sometimes be wrong. Kill switches, feature flags, staged rollout, forced update, configuration driven from the server rather than baked into a binary. You decide how that works in your first weeks and it stays decided for years.

There is a second frontend seat, based in India, covering web. That person also works inside the app. You set the mobile architecture and the standards, they build to them, and you review each other. The division is not permanent and we expect both of you to cross it.


**WHAT YOU WILL DO**

*The consumer app, first priority*

- Onboarding and KYC, PIN and biometric setup, device binding, session handling.

- Wallet and balance, top-up, withdrawal, transaction history, search, transaction detail, dispute reporting.

- Notifications and security alerts, GDPR data export, account deletion.

- Identity as it appears on a phone: document capture, liveness, eID over NFC where we use it, and the handover to and from a partner's identification flow. The hard part is not the capture. It is what a user sees when their onboarding is stuck inside someone else's system.

*The payment moment*

- QR scan, NFC tap, merchant and amount confirmation, biometric authorisation, receipt. Measured in milliseconds and optimised above everything else in the product.

- Strong customer authentication in practice: which actions require re-authentication, what happens when biometrics fail, how a session survives an app switch without becoming a hole.

- Campus wifi will drop a request after the money has already moved. How the app behaves in that second is a design decision, and it is yours.

*Merchant acceptance*

- What sits on the till: dynamic QR with amount, live confirmation, refund from the device. A screen, not a dashboard.

*Release, reliability and security*

- Store submission and review for both platforms, signing, versioning, staged rollout, rollback, forced update.

- Crash and performance monitoring, real user metrics, and product instrumentation good enough to tell us where people abandon onboarding without shipping personal data out of Europe.

- Certificate pinning, keychain and keystore, integrity checks, screenshot handling on sensitive screens, logging that never puts a token or a balance in a crash report.

- Automated testing that runs on real devices, and a regression pass before every release.

- Accessibility built in from the first screen rather than retrofitted. Consumer payment services in Germany carry legal accessibility obligations and our institutional clients are public bodies with their own.

*Later, as we grow*

- P2P, split bills, scheduled and recurring payments, contact handles.

- The digital student ID and university services in one authenticated session: semester fee, mensa top-up, library, exam registration.

- The full merchant app, with KYB, staff shifts and catalogue.

- Transport, telecoms and utilities inside the wallet.

None of that is pilot scope. All of it is why the decisions you make in month one matter.


**OUR STACK**

React Native with Expo, TypeScript and NativeWind on mobile. React, TypeScript and Tailwind on web, sharing design tokens, API types and validation with the app through a TypeScript monorepo. Go, Node.js, Python and PostgreSQL behind it, REST over SEPA Instant rails. Sentry for errors and performance, Maestro for device-level end-to-end tests.

We chose React Native so that two engineers can work in one codebase and cover for each other. You will have real influence over everything above, and we would rather you argued with it than inherited it quietly.


**WHO YOU ARE**

- Eligible for EXIST Gründerstipendium funding: enrolled at a German university, or a graduate of one within the last 5 years.

- Around three to five years building production software, with genuine depth in React Native. Not React with some exposure to mobile. You have shipped to both stores, handled a rejection, and lived with what you released afterwards.

- You think in states rather than screens. Pending, failed, expired, insufficient balance, refunded, disputed. Asked to describe a payment screen, you describe all of them.

- You have worked on unreliable networks and know why an automatic retry on a payment request is dangerous.

- You are comfortable at the device layer: NFC and its platform limits, biometrics, camera and QR, push reliability, deep links, background states, secure storage. You know when dropping below the React Native layer is the right call and when it is showing off.

- You measure performance instead of asserting it. Cold start, frame rate, time to confirmation.

- You have taste and you defend it. You will push back on a design, or on a founder, when the product would be worse.

- You use AI tooling seriously in your workflow and you know where it produces confident nonsense.

- Comfortable with ambiguity and early-stage risk. There is no playbook yet. You will help write it.


**STRONG BONUS (NOT REQUIRED)**

- You have worked on a fintech, banking or payments app, or anything else where a bug costs someone money rather than time.

- You have shipped NFC on iOS or Android and know exactly what Apple permits a third party to do.

- You have built or maintained a design system inside an app.

- You have run a release train under pressure: versioning, phased rollout, rollback, an emergency fix on a Friday.

- You have made an app genuinely accessible and know what a screen reader does to a layout you thought was fine.

- You design as well as build, in Figma or directly in code.


**BENEFITS**

- Be part of a founding team eligible for EXIST Gründerstipendium, a grant from the German government that funds you to build.

- You own the consumer surface of the company. Not a feature team, not a queue of tickets, not someone else's architecture.

- Thousands of students on the first campus, using what you built, telling you about it the same day. Feedback in weeks rather than quarters.

- This is European payment infrastructure rather than a skin on somebody else's. The rails, the data and the supervision stay in Europe, and the app is where that turns into something a person can hold.

- Flexible hours and remote within Germany, with regular time in Augsburg. We expect you in the mensa at 12:15 sometimes, watching people use it.

- Early stage means something here. Small team, real ownership, no queue of forty pull requests ahead of yours.

- You will work with people who left stable paths to build a faster, simpler way to move money in Germany. Less bureaucracy, more momentum.

- For the right person who grows with the company, equity is a conversation we will have when the time is right.


Connect with the Founder
www.linkedin.com/in/shabbir-maimoon

title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer
description:
### **About the Role**

As a Staff ML Engineer at Thorn, this role will design, build, deploy and maintain world class models, classifiers and algorithms to increase Thorn’s capabilities to achieve our mission of the elimination of child sexual exploitation. They will be the go-to expert in one or more domains of machine learning and provide critical guidance to multiple teams across legal, engineering, product, business development and external affairs. They will directly contribute to the Machine Learning team’s critical function in Thorn’s mission - building automated solutions that:

1. Reduce the time it takes to identify a child sexual abuse victim, elevating the most vulnerable and high risk victims from an ocean of online content
2. Enable the removal of child sexual abuse material from the internet, finding known and new content
3. Prevent online abuse from happening in the first place, detecting abusive content before it spreads

They are responsible for ensuring that their work is high quality, as well as mentoring other ML Engineers. They will thrive in highly ambiguous problem spaces and be able to creatively design and build scalable solutions with minimum direction. They will demonstrate persistence and strong technical expertise to navigate legal, product, and technical constraints. They are responsible for partnering with the engineers, product manager and designers across different products to drive requirements, as well as any and all relevant external partners, taking into account all stakeholder needs.

### **What You’ll Do**

- Own end-to-end model development: design, build, test and maintain machine learning systems and algorithms
- Lead machine learning system designs, set engineering standards, lead technical meetings and proactively engage and mentor other engineers
- Help debug, do code review, and support general machine learning initiatives led by other members of the Machine Learning team.
- Define data sourcing and labeling strategy for your technical domain, proactively identifying future data needs and partnering with the Sr. Technical Program Manager to drive planning and prioritization
- Work closely with specialists at Thorn to create data labeling guides and support labeling efforts. This may involve engaging with sexually explicit material that is not child sexual abuse material
- Look for opportunities to streamline and reuse work, proactively identifying cross-team dependencies. Anticipate technical risks across ML systems, define architectural guardrails, establish best practices for scalability and reliability
- Represent Thorn as a technical thought leader at conferences and other external forums, advancing the field and strengthening strategic partnerships
- Collaborate with engineers, product managers, product owners, and designers to drive requirements, define scope of work, engage with users, and translate user needs into features and deliverables
- Collaborate with engineers on product teams to maintain and deploy models, algorithms and model serving infrastructure
- Look for opportunities, in collaboration with the Sr. Technical Program Manager, to improve the innovation -\> impact cycle across product, academic collaborations, and other external partnerships
- Build relationships and collaborate with external partners
- Look for opportunities to improve systems, author tools and introduce policies/patterns that raise productivity for the Machine Learning team
- Clearly communicate and document problem formulation, feature/model design, training, and evaluation results to technical and non-technical audiences
- Identify new problem spaces within online child safety. Stay abreast of technical developments and breakthroughs with an eye towards applying solutions to our issue space.
- Drive roadmap planning and cadence of maintenance vs. new feature development for your areas of ownership
- Conduct data analysis as needed to improve cross-functional understanding
- Collaborate closely with Product and Engineering during planning, software design, model development, and time-sensitive customer support efforts.

### **What We’re Looking For**

- You have a commitment to putting the children we serve at the center of everything you do
- You have a willingness to learn about online child safety and victim identification.
- You have 8+ years background in machine learning and/or artificial intelligence, with 3+ years experience in building production-scale computer vision and/or NLP machine learning systems and pipelines
- You have a Ph.D or master’s degree in a quantitative field, or equivalent professional experience.
- You have an ability and interest in learning and adopting new technologies quickly
- You can work with ambiguity, shifting requirements and collaborate with cross-functional internal and external stakeholders
- You have a passion for machine learning and an aptitude to work in a collaborative environment, can demonstrate empathy for our team and strong advocacy for our users, while balancing the vision and technical constraints of engineering. Success on this team requires humility, curiosity, and a willingness to both teach and learn.
- You excel at identifying unique opportunities and translating them into scalable solutions that align cross-functional stakeholders around a clear, compelling, and actionable vision
- You communicate clearly, efficiently, and thoughtfully. We’re a highly-distributed team, so written communication is crucial

### **Technologies We Use (for relevant roles)**

- AWS
- Python
- Pandas
- PyTorch
- scikit-learn/scipy
- Terraform
- CI/CD Pipelines
- Tensorflow with Keras
- Hugging Face Transformers/Diffusers
- OpenCV
- FAISS or other vector stores
- ONNX/onnxruntime
- Kubernetes

**Compensation and Benefits**

A reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role is **$171,000-$235,750/year**. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to location; skill sets; experience and training; licensure, and certifications.

Our remote-first work model is structured around working from home most of the time. But, there will be times that employees are expected to travel. For example, Thorn may host company-wide gatherings, and smaller teams may hold in-person meetings and team-building events, or require attendance at specific conferences.

At Thorn, we know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and offer employees a broad range of benefits. [Learn more about what working at Thorn can mean for you](https://www.thorn.org/careers/).

title: Venue Database, Partnerships & Booking Coordination Specialist
description:
Help finalize Crave Locally's Loudoun County venue database, visit venues in person, build relationships with wineries, farms and lodging partners, and help shape itineraries and customer bookings.

About Crave Locally
Crave Locally is an agritourism discovery and booking platform connecting visitors with wineries, farms, breweries, lodging, dining, and other countryside experiences across Northern Virginia.

With support from Loudoun County, Crave Locally is developing a comprehensive and highly structured database of local agritourism venues designed to make it easier for visitors to discover experiences that match their specific needs and interests.

At the center of this work is Crave Locally's proprietary venue database, which captures 214 structured data fields per venue and supports personalized discovery, itinerary development, curated packages, and booking.

Objective of the assignment
Crave Locally is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and personable Venue Database, Partnerships & Booking Coordination Specialist to support the continued development and finalization of the Loudoun County venue database, coordinate with local tourism businesses and stakeholders, assist in creating visitor itineraries and packages, and support customer bookings.

This is not solely a research or data-entry role. The assignment requires someone who is comfortable speaking directly with venue owners, tourism partners, concierge teams, and customers — building relationships, asking questions, following up, and coordinating multiple parties to deliver a strong visitor experience.

Database research and quality assurance
In-person venue verification
Venue and partner outreach
Itinerary and package development
Booking fulfillment and customer coordination
Stage 1 — Primary data collection
Venue profiles are developed through structured desk research using public and online sources. Research covers core information across Crave Locally's database, including venue characteristics, amenities, visitor policies, family and pet suitability, accessibility, food and beverage offerings, activities, event capabilities, booking requirements, sustainability features, and other factors relevant to visitor decision-making.

Stage 2 — Site visits & verification
Selected venues are visited in person to confirm what desk research cannot: the feel of the place, seating and shade, accessibility in practice, how families and dogs are actually received, and the details that make an itinerary work on the day.

Qualifications & skills
Excellent research, fact-checking, and organizational skills
Strong attention to detail and ability to work with structured data
Experience with Airtable, databases, CRM systems, spreadsheets, or similar tools
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Confidence speaking with business owners, hospitality professionals, tourism partners, and customers
Comfortable making phone calls, conducting outreach, asking follow-up questions, and building professional relationships
Strong customer-service orientation
Ability to coordinate multiple businesses and moving pieces simultaneously
Good judgment and problem-solving skills
Familiarity with Loudoun County, Northern Virginia, tourism, hospitality, wineries, farms, lodging, or agritourism is highly desirable
Ability to conduct site visits within Loudoun County
Reliable transportation for assignments requiring in-person visits
Working arrangement & compensation
The assignment combines remote research and database work, partner and customer communications, and targeted in-person venue visits within Loudoun County. Work will generally be organized around assigned venues, outreach priorities, customer requests, and package-development needs.

Compensation is $20 per hour. Scheduling is flexible, although some assignments may require availability during normal business hours, evenings, or weekends depending on venue operations, customer bookings, and scheduled site visits.

Structured venue database
Research and data definitions
Existing venue records
Site-visit questionnaires
Venue outreach and onboarding materials
Itinerary and package information
Booking and partner coordination materials
What you'll gain
Hands-on exposure to Loudoun County's tourism and agritourism ecosystem
Direct interaction with wineries, farms, lodging providers, hospitality businesses, and tourism stakeholders

Experience supporting real customer bookings and visitor experiences

Potential for continued work in venue partnerships, customer experience, business development, community engagement, or tourism operations as Crave Locally grows

title: Founder's Office Intern
description:
Mango Giraffe builds AI filmmaking infrastructure for long-form storytelling. We work with major studios. Our product handles the parts that break when a studio tries to make a film this way: keeping a character's face the same across 200 shots, giving a director control over a camera move, getting from a locked script to footage a studio will put on screen.

Adoption takes more than tools, though. There's the pipeline, the cost structure, and the people inside a studio who want this to work and don't know where to start. We're working on all of it. This role exists because there's more of it than three founders can carry.

The work

- Decks. Investor, studio, partner. You write the argument and the slides.
- Cold outbound to studios and production heads, here and abroad. Find the person, write the mail that gets a reply, get the meeting.
- Fix what's broken. A delivery slipping, a process nobody owns, a number nobody tracks. You take it and hand it back working.
- Build systems for the fires that keep coming back, so they stop needing a person.
- Chase answers out of people who don't report to you. Founders included.


Who we're looking for

- You break a problem down to its constraints before you look at how anyone else solved it.
- High agency. You've built or run something nobody asked you to, and it had your name on it.
- You write well. Most of this job happens in writing.
- You finish. Handing work to someone else doesn't close it.
- One to three years somewhere demanding. Or none, if you've built something we can look at.


You don't need a film background. You do need to find the industry interesting.

What this isn't
Calendars, travel, meeting notes, inbox. This isn't an EA role with a better title.

Why take it
A few months here shows you fundraising, studio sales, hiring, pricing and delivery from the inside. People who do this well tend to leave and start their own companies. If that's your plan, say so when you apply.
