title: DevSecOps Engineer
description:
## **About Us**

At Tradeify, we're building a high-performance trading ecosystem that empowers traders around the world with capital, technology, education, and community. We operate across futures and crypto markets and partner with platforms like NinjaTrader and Tradovate to deliver a best-in-class trading experience.

We're a rapidly scaling fintech serving a global trader community, and technology is at the center of everything we do. If you want to work on infrastructure and security where performance actually matters — where a 200ms lag on a dashboard is a real problem for real traders — this is a good place to do it.

##   
**About the Role**

We are seeking a hands-on DevOps/SecOps Engineer to own the infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and security posture behind Tradeify's trading platform. This role splits evenly between building and hardening: shipping CI/CD and infrastructure improvements that let the engineering team move quickly, and running the security practices — monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response, compliance — that protect trader data and platform integrity.

This is a great opportunity for a DevOps/security professional to take real ownership of a live trading platform's infrastructure and security program, working closely with engineering and leadership to make both a competitive advantage rather than a bottleneck.

This role is fully remote (U.S.-based) and reports to the Head of Engineering / CTO.

##   
**What You Will Do**

- Design, build, and maintain CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions + OIDC) across services and repositories.
- Manage and scale cloud infrastructure on AWS (EC2, S3, SES, ECR, Parameter Store, IAM).
- Own containerized deployments with Docker/Docker Compose, including reverse proxy and TLS termination (Caddy).
- Build and maintain infrastructure-as-code for repeatable, auditable environment provisioning.
- Improve observability across services — logging, metrics, tracing, and alerting for production systems.
- Support database operations (PostgreSQL, Redis) including backups, failover, and performance tuning.
- Own vulnerability management: scanning, triage, patching cadence, and remediation tracking across infrastructure and application layers.
- Design and enforce access control, secrets management, and least-privilege practices across cloud and CI/CD systems.
- Build and monitor security detection and alerting (intrusion detection, anomaly detection, log-based threat monitoring).
- Lead incident response: develop runbooks, coordinate response to security events, and drive postmortems.
- Support compliance and audit readiness relevant to a financial services/fintech environment.
- Perform security reviews of new infrastructure, integrations, and deployment changes before they ship.
- Champion secure-by-default practices across the engineering team (dependency hygiene, secrets scanning, hardened base images).
- Partner with engineering to reduce deployment friction and improve release reliability.

##   
**What You Bring**

- Experience owning both infrastructure/DevOps and security operations responsibilities, or a strong track record in one with real depth in the other.
- Production experience with AWS (EC2, S3, IAM, ECR, Parameter Store or equivalent secrets management).
- Strong Docker/containerization experience, including writing and hardening Dockerfiles and Compose configurations.
- CI/CD pipeline design and maintenance (GitHub Actions or equivalent), including OIDC-based cloud authentication.
- Experience with vulnerability scanning, patch management, and remediation workflows.
- Solid understanding of network and application security fundamentals (TLS, firewalls, IAM, least privilege).
- Experience with PostgreSQL and Redis in production, including operational concerns (backups, monitoring, scaling).
- Comfort with Linux systems administration and shell scripting for automation.
- Incident response experience — able to lead through an active issue, not just document it after the fact.
- Independent work capability in a startup environment with high ownership and minimal hand-holding.
- Strong written communication — comfortable documenting runbooks, postmortems, and security findings clearly.

##   
**Nice To Have**

- Fintech, trading, or other regulated-industry experience.
- Familiarity with the broader Tradeify stack: Next.js/React, Python/FastAPI, TypeScript, BullMQ + Redis for background jobs.
- Experience with SIEM tooling, SOC workflows, or managed detection and response platforms.
- Exposure to compliance frameworks (SOC 2, PCI DSS, or similar).
- Infrastructure-as-code tooling (Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation, or similar).
- Experience with reverse proxies and TLS automation (Caddy, nginx, Traefik).
- AI-assisted development workflow familiarity (Claude Code or similar).

##   
**Why Join Tradeify**

- Join a professional-grade futures trading firm at a pivotal stage of growth.
- Real, fast-moving trading platform serving thousands of traders where performance and security genuinely matter.
- High ownership from day one — shape infrastructure and security practices rather than inherit rigid process.
- Small team structure with direct influence on architecture and tooling decisions.
- High-performance culture that rewards ownership, curiosity, and results.
- Competitive base salary, performance bonuses, and comprehensive benefits.
- Be a foundational member of the infrastructure and security function at a growing fintech company.

##   
**A Note on Our Hiring Process**

*At Tradeify Futures, we use AI-assisted tools as part of our recruiting process, which may include resume screening, application review, and candidate communication. We want all applicants to be aware of this upfront so you can make an informed decision about applying. Final hiring decisions are always made by a member of our team.*

title: Talent Lead at AIOS- Remote, $100-200k inc equity
description:
# About AIOS

**AIOS is building the world’s first full-stack AI doctor.**

We’re at $400M ARR, growing from $10M/yr 12 months ago. We’re the world’s fastest growing AI doctor.

We’re faithfully serving \>200k/mo patients via Bolt Pharmacy, our main UK brand. We’re profitable.

Our strategy exists at the intersection of two strong theses:

1. The AI doctor that wins will get to escape velocity using GLP-1s, the fastest growing consumer product in history.
2. The $2T European healthcare market is overlooked by the most talented builders.

Our master plan:

- **Step 0 → $100M/yr by end of 2025**: We went from $10M to $100M in 6 months serving the UK GLP-1 market.
- **Step 1 → $1B ARR by end of 2026**: Over the last 12 months we've grown from 3k to 150k UK active GLP-1 patients. We’ll continue this growth curve to hit $1B ARR.
- **Step 2 → $10B ARR by end of 2028**: Blitzscale Europe. We’ll be Europe’s largest GLP-1 provider.
- **Step 3 → $100B/yr by end of 2031**: Get regulatory approval across Europe for our Full Autonomous Prescribing (FAP) system. Win contracts at scale with European payers to mass replace human labor. We’ll be the dominant full-stack AI doctor in Europe.
- **Step 4 → $1T/yr by end of 2035**: With one line of code and zero human time, you can use AIOS to treat any patient globally with any medication.

In so doing, we’ll become the world’s first trillion-dollar healthcare company.

We’re a young, founder-led company. This is still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.

You can read more about working with us here: [Working at AIOS](https://app.notion.com/p/Working-at-AIOS-5b5c0a584af44de78ac7fb9b2cf8d993?pvs=21)

## Being a Talent Lead at AIOS

We’re building a world-class team. As Talent Lead at AIOS, your fundamental role is to supercharge our talent (recruiting) function, ensuring that a lack of key hires never blocks growth. You’ll help define what a killer sourcing process looks like while leveraging frontier tooling to increase your throughput and velocity as you recruit best-in-class operators.

You’ll work across a variety of roles: traditional direct-to-consumer Growth roles (Performance Marketing), technical roles (AI + SWE Engineering & Product), and clinical roles — flexing deftly between more junior roles all the way up to the most senior roles in the org.

This is a full-time, fully remote role, and you’ll work mostly async in the timezone of your choice — as long as you’re around until midday Pacific Time every weekday. You’ll have flex in your calendar for kids if you have them — many of our team have kids so we’re kid-friendly.

This is an individual-contributor role — no direct reports, full-cycle sourcing/screening/closing, hands dirty in the trenches. You’ll report directly to Cierra Olsen (Head of Talent).

You’ll also work closely with the rest of the Talent Team: Zoe Wheeler (UK Talent Lead), Mika Mansilla (Founder Associate), and Jordan Pellikan (VP Ops).

## Key responsibilities

- Full cycle: Own searches end to end from sourcing, outbound, screening, interview coordination, calibration, and closing (recent examples: Head of InfoSec, Head of Creative, Senior Media Buyer, Affiliate Lead).
- Sourcing: Build repeatable sourcing engines for hard-to-fill roles. Run LinkedIn X-ray searches, build target-company lists, and do the outbound headhunting yourself. Our best hires won’t come inbound.
- Processes: Constantly sharpen our hiring bars (seniority, industry fit, recency, builder pattern) consistently across every search you’re DRI for. Help improve interview processes across the org.
- Hygiene: Keep pipelines, stages, and candidate communication clean and current in Ashby so nothing stalls and our time to hire continually improves.
- Calibration: Flag pipeline risk early, bring calibration questions before they become misses, and constantly align with leaders across the org to improve our processes.
- Closing: Manage candidate experience through to signed offer, including comp conversations.

## KPIs

- Time-to-fill on your owned searches, without sacrificing the bar
- Sourced (outbound) candidates as a % of your total pipeline — we want you building your own pipeline, not living off inbound
- Offer-accept rate on closed candidates
- Ashby pipeline hygiene — stages and candidate status always current

## Need to have

- Excellence: You have 5+ years experience personally recruiting (sourcing, screening, managing, and closing) great candidates across difficult searches. You can point to hires that materially raised the talent bar of the teams they joined.
- Hunter: You can turn a vague candidate profile into target companies, search strings and a high-quality outbound pipeline. You do not depend on inbound applicants or agencies to fill roles.
- Senior hiring: You have successfully recruited senior leaders and understand how sourcing, assessing and closing them differs from junior hiring.
- Judgment: You can distinguish exceptional people from candidates who simply have the right companies, titles or polish on their CV. You develop conviction quickly and can clearly articulate why someone does or does not meet the bar.
- Range: You can move between very different searches without losing depth. You learn unfamiliar markets quickly enough to recruit credibly within them.
- Multi-workstream: You can run several searches simultaneously while keeping sourcing quality, candidate communication, follow-ups and pipeline hygiene exceptionally tight.
- Urgency: You push searches forward without waiting to be managed, surface problems early, and change approach quickly when a pipeline is not working.
- High bar: You care more about making an exceptional hire than filling a seat, and you are comfortable challenging hiring managers when you do not believe a candidate meets org standards.

## Nice to have

- Startups/Scale-ups: You’ve recruited in a fast-moving startup or scale-up where priorities shift quickly, roles evolve mid-search, and there isn’t always an existing playbook.
- Technical recruiting: You’ve successfully recruited for Engineering, AI, Data, Product or other technical roles and can credibly assess candidate quality beyond surface-level credentials.
- Regulated industries: You’ve recruited in healthcare, financial services, or another highly regulated industry where candidate requirements and operating constraints are more complex.
- AI-native: You actively use AI and automation to improve sourcing, research, outreach, screening, and recruiting operations.
- Systems builder: You’ve helped build or materially improve recruiting processes, tooling, scorecards, sourcing systems, or interview loops rather than simply operating an existing process.
- Network: You have an existing network of exceptional operators, builders and leaders you’d be excited to bring into AIOS.

## Our cultural standards

We aim to make this your life's work. This should be the most challenging, most rewarding role of your life. Accordingly, these are the core cultural standards to which we hold ourselves & our team-members:

1. Belief in the mission: We will have served 100 million patients by the end of 2035 and we transform the life of most patients who join. We have a lot of work to do. We are obsessed with our patients and are dedicated to the mission.
2. Unwavering integrity: We are at the frontier, so we often live in ambiguity with no trodden path. When we can't look to others for guidance, we must maintain impeccable ethics and unwavering integrity.
3. Only the paranoid survive: Bad sh*t is coming. By joining us, you're choosing to sail straight towards the storms with unhesitating conviction. However much we've already done, however far we've already come — it's still Day 1 and all our work is ahead of us.
4. If we're average we fail: We are only interested in "insanely great", a focus on the quality of our execution that in everyday life would be considered pathological. We have a dedication to excellence and reject incompetence.
5. Commitment to candor: That which can be destroyed by the truth should be. You get full transparency from the company and the company expects full transparency from you. We never say anything about someone that we wouldn't say to them directly. We give feedback with love and do not need to protect people from fleeting physical sensations.
6. A maniacal sense of urgency: We execute at an intensity that most people think is impossible. Speed is critical and we need things done yesterday. We all work very hard and in such a competitive world there really is no other way to win.
7. Enduring frugality: We are frugal. We hate being wasteful and we are anti-luxury. A culture of cheapness keeps us young. We spend our cash wisely & carefully — in a way that would make our grandmas proud.
8. Bulldozing barriers: The world is malleable and we shape it. We truly believe this and act accordingly. We are relentlessly resourceful and are at the mercy of no-one but ourselves. You'll be shocked how capable you are and how much you can achieve.
9. Keep your head down: We're boring people doing exciting work. We don't chase short-term status — we ignore short-term dopamine hits and focus on what matters. Outsiders will underestimate us and we revel in that.
10. The power of focus: We live in a world of power laws and we cannot overestimate the unimportance of practically everything. Know your One Thing, and nail it.

🎯 *"You just build a f\**ing amazing experience. Make each step amazing. Make every decision in the long term interest of the customer. Give the customer massively more value than you take."

## Compensation & Benefits

You get paid above market salary and you get early stage equity, so you get really rich if we nail this.

- *Compensation*: $100k-$200k/yr, incl equity

### Benefits

The stuff below is cool as well.

- *Healthcare*: comprehensive medical insurance (if appropriate).
- *Remote*: our team is fully distributed across the world and functions fully remotely.
- *Personal development*: budget for books, courses, coaching.
- *Personal wellness*: budget for gym, health apps.
- *GLP-1s*: free membership with a clinic offering GLP-1s.
- *Health coaching*: free biweekly health coaching so you stay healthy.
- *Work coaching*: free biweekly work coaching so you stay sharp + calm.
- *Equipment*: Macbook & work-from-home equipment provided as needed.
- **What are we missing?** We're still early so you get to shape our culture.

title: Founder Operations & Customer Intelligence Lead
location: Brazil; United States; New York; Remote
description:
Skip is building an AI operating system for entrepreneurs and small business owners.

More than 1 million entrepreneurs have used Skip to find funding, build their businesses, create content, launch products, grow their online presence, and get guidance from their AI Cofounder.

We're looking for one exceptional person to work directly with Skip's founder across customer intelligence, operations, AI, and product.

This is not a traditional customer support role. It's also not a traditional executive assistant, operations, or product role.

It's a high-autonomy, high-expectation role for someone who is unusually curious, sharp, proactive, and good at figuring things out.

You won't have a tightly defined task list, and you shouldn't expect someone else to consistently tell you what deserves your attention.

We expect you to notice what others miss.

If a customer says something unusual, investigate it. If several customers encounter the same problem, figure out why. If a process is repetitive, determine whether AI should automate it. If a potential partner contacts us, understand the opportunity before escalating it. If something in Skip doesn't make sense, question it.

You'll work directly with Skip's founder, and one of the clearest measures of your success will be whether you reduce the amount he has to notice, investigate, follow up on, and manage himself.

This role will be an unusually good fit for a small number of people—and probably a poor fit for most.

**What you'll own**
**~40% — Customer Intelligence & Human-in-the-Loop**

Skip increasingly uses AI and automation to handle routine customer needs. Your job isn't to sit in an inbox answering every message. You'll own the human judgment around that system.

You'll handle situations where a thoughtful human genuinely adds value, investigate unusual customer issues instead of simply forwarding them, and understand what customers are actually trying to accomplish.

But an equally important part of the job happens after the individual conversation.

Why did this customer get confused? Is anyone else experiencing it? Is this a product problem? Is our AI getting something wrong? Is there a bigger pattern? Should we change the product rather than answer the same question again?

**You'll:**

* Own customer situations that genuinely require human judgment.
* nvestigate issues deeply before escalating them.
* Talk with customers by email, chat, video, or phone when useful.
* Identify patterns across customer conversations.
* Turn customer feedback into clear product findings and recommendations.
* Help improve how our AI handles customer interactions.
* Recognize when a customer message contains valuable business or product context.
* Make good judgment calls about when not to respond or intervene.
* Bring Product and Engineering evidence rather than vague feedback.

Closing support tickets isn't the goal. Learning from customers and solving underlying problems is.

**~30% — Founder & Company Operations**

You'll work directly with Skip's founder on whatever is most important.

One day that might mean qualifying a potential partnership. Another might mean investigating an unusual customer situation, coordinating with a grant winner, researching an opportunity, following up on something important, or making sure a project actually gets finished.

We don't want someone who simply forwards things to the founder.

We want someone who can independently come back and say:

Here's what happened. Here's what I investigated. Here's what I learned. Here's what I think we should do.

You'll gradually build enough understanding of Skip, our customers, and how the founder thinks that you can take more and more off his plate.

**~30% — AI, Automation & Product Feedback**

Every repetitive task should make you wonder:

Why are we still doing this manually?

We're an AI company. We expect you to use AI constantly—not simply to write nicer emails, but to research, investigate, analyze, automate, and accomplish substantially more than one person traditionally could.

You don't need to be an engineer. You do need to be deeply AI-native and curious about what's now possible.

**You'll:**

* Find repetitive customer and operational workflows we can automate.
* Help determine where AI should act independently and where humans should remain in the loop.
* Test new Skip functionality yourself.
* Identify confusing, broken, or underwhelming product experiences.
* Use customer conversations to discover product opportunities.
* Work directly with Product and Engineering when you find something important.
* Help evaluate and improve AI output and workflows.
* Constantly look for ways one exceptional person + AI can accomplish what historically required a much larger team.
* The kind of person we're looking for

We're much more interested in how you think than whether you've held this exact title before.

You may have worked in operations, customer experience, product, at an early-stage startup, alongside a founder, or in something completely different.

Being responsive, organized, friendly, and hardworking is necessary—but not sufficient for this role.

We're looking for unusually strong curiosity and judgment.

You should be someone who naturally thinks:

That's strange. Why did that happen?

I've seen this more than once. Is there a pattern?

Why are we doing this manually?

Does the customer actually need a response?

How do we know that's true?

What are we missing?

I don't know yet. I'll figure it out.

**You'll probably thrive here if you:**

* Are exceptionally curious.
* Have excellent written and spoken English.
* Have strong instincts about products and people.
* Learn complicated products extremely quickly.
* Notice inconsistencies other people overlook.
* Ask good questions without being told which questions to ask.
* Investigate before escalating.
* Can separate important signals from noise.
* Form opinions rather than merely summarize information.
* Are comfortable respectfully challenging assumptions.
* Use AI extensively and continuously experiment with what's possible.
* Can communicate naturally with an upset customer, a potential partner, an engineer, and a founder.
* Take ownership without waiting for permission.
* Enjoy ambiguity and responsibility.

We don't expect you to always be right.

We do expect you to think.

**This role probably isn't for you if...**

You're looking for a traditional support role where success means working through assigned tickets.

You need your manager to consistently tell you what to work on next.

Your instinct when something unusual happens is to forward it to someone else.

You prefer executing established processes to questioning whether the process should exist.

You use AI mainly to draft emails or rewrite things.

You aren't naturally interested in understanding how the entire product works.

Or you want responsibilities that remain neatly inside a predefined box.

Skip moves quickly. Our product changes constantly. This role will too.

**Why Skip**

You'll have unusual access and responsibility.

You'll work directly with Skip's founder and closely with Product and Engineering. You'll interact with entrepreneurs using Skip every day and often see problems and opportunities before the rest of the company does.

When you discover something important, we expect you to do something about it.

This is a role where someone relatively early in their career can take on an enormous amount of responsibility very quickly.

As Skip grows, the role can grow substantially with you.

**How to apply**

We know this application asks more of you than most job applications.

That's intentional.

This role offers substantially more ownership than most roles at this level. We're looking for someone excited by that—not someone looking for the easiest application process.

Before applying, spend meaningful time learning about Skip.

Visit our website. Research the company. Create an account. Use the product. Explore our AI Cofounder and other functionality. Develop some opinions.

If you haven't spent meaningful time researching Skip and using the product, please don't apply yet.

Email careers@helloskip.com with the subject:

Founder Operations & Customer Intelligence Lead — [Your Name]

Include your résumé or LinkedIn profile and answer the following five questions.

**1. Why Skip, specifically?**

Tell us what you think Skip is trying to build, why that interests you, and one thing you think we may be underestimating or getting wrong.

Generic answers about loving startups, AI, small businesses, or entrepreneurship won't tell us much.

We want your actual opinion.

**2. Give us your mini product assessment.**

Spend real time using Skip.

Tell us the three most important things you noticed.

They can be problems, opportunities, things you loved, confusing experiences, business observations, product ideas, or something we haven't considered.

Rank them #1–#3 and explain why each one matters.

Then tell us one thing you initially noticed but ultimately decided wasn't important enough to prioritize—and why.

We're interested in your judgment, not the number of bugs you can find.

**3. What did we not ask you?**

After researching and using Skip, tell us something you became curious about that none of these application questions prompted you to investigate.

What did you notice? Why did it make you curious? What would you investigate next? How would you figure it out?

We use AI extensively at Skip and expect you to as well. You're welcome to use AI to research, organize your thinking, or improve your application. Generic AI-generated answers, however, won't tell us much about you.

There is no perfect format for a great application.

We're hiring for curiosity, judgment, initiative, product instinct, and the ability to form your own point of view. Show us how you think.

title: Head of Operations
description:
***See full description [here](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/PRISM?utmsource=rkZvvbw025https://).
*

**Details**

*     Location: Cambridge, UK strongly preferred; open to remote (US/EU with overlap with UK hours) – open to sponsoring UK visas.
*     Type: Full-time (part-time options will also be considered)
*     Reports to: CEO
*     Compensation: Salary commensurate with experience, typical range of $100,000 - $160,000

**Overview**

PRISM is entering a period of growth, and we're looking for a Head of Operations to help us scale without losing what makes us effective. You'll take ownership of the operational backbone of the organisation (HR, finance, systems, and compliance) so that the people running our core programmes can focus on the work itself. This is a senior, high-trust role for someone who can build durable systems, exercise good judgement under uncertainty, and grow an operations function as the organisation expands.

**About PRISM**

PRISM (Partnership for Research Into Sentient Machines) is a UK-based registered charity helping to build the field of digital minds. We support research and educational initiatives that prepare society for the challenges posed by AI consciousness, digital minds, and AI moral status. We raise awareness among non-expert audiences, develop talent to help the field grow, and convene the researchers and experts for important conversations.

Field building sits at the heart of our direction. As a young field, digital minds needs infrastructure: ways for newcomers to orient themselves, and spaces that keep researchers and practitioners connected and collaborating. Our programmes span a podcast, the Beginner's Guide to Digital Minds, a quarterly newsletter, a community slack channel, fellowships, an online course, and expert workshops. A key part of the role is our partnership with Cambridge Digital Minds, with whom we run Fellowships and an Online course. You'll be central to making that collaboration run smoothly and scale well.

**What you'll do**

*     Help us through a period of growth. Anticipate the operational challenges that come with scaling; more people, more programmes, more complexity. Lay the foundations so that growth is an opportunity rather than a bottleneck.
*     Take ownership of HR and Finance. Own people operations end to end: hiring logistics, onboarding, contracts, policies, and day-to-day HR. Lead the collaboration with our accountants across budgeting, payroll, bookkeeping oversight, funder and grant reporting, Charity Commission filings, and compliance. Bring in specialists where it makes sense and manage those relationships.
*     Implement systems. Design and roll out the tools and processes the organisation needs, running recurring processes, and maintaining a CRM for donors, candidates, and partners. Build systems that fit how people already work.
*     Support the staff working on our core programmes. Make sure the teams delivering our programmes have the operational support they need to succeed, removing friction and handling the logistics so they can concentrate on the substance.
*     Maintain policies and support governance. Keep policies current and identify gaps, prepare materials for board or governance meetings, and keep the organisation's housekeeping in order.
*     Grow the operations function. Over time, bring functions in-house where appropriate and build and manage a small operations team as PRISM scales.

**Who we're looking for**
You may be a good fit if you have:

*     5+ years of experience in operations, finance, HR, or a related role (e.g. chief of staff, head of operations).
*     Experience scaling an operations function through a period of organisational growth: building systems and processes that held up as headcount and complexity increased.
*     A proven track record of owning detailed and high-stakes work (budgets, filings, contracts, payroll).
*     Reliability across a broad, busy workload. You will keep various projects moving and rarely drop the ball.
*     Good judgement under uncertainty. You know when to handle something yourself, when to bring in a specialist, and when to escalate.
*     A bias toward clarity and simplicity, and the ability to build systems that work with people's existing workflows.
*     Strong people-management instincts and readiness to build and lead a team as we grow.
*     Genuine care for PRISM's mission.

**Strong candidates may also have:**

*     Familiarity with UK-charity finance and regulatory requirements
*     Experience with grant management or funder reporting
*     Experience running or supporting fellowships, courses, or other talent programmes
*     Familiarity with the AI safety or digital minds ecosystem.

**Compensation and benefits**

 *     Salary: $100,000 to $160,000 per annum
 *     8% pension / 401(k) employer contribution
 *     25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays
 *     Wellbeing budget of up to $3,500 a year
 *     Support for setting up a productive work environment
 *     Personal development budget
 *     In-office meals, snacks and drinks (when in office)

**Hiring Process**

*     Application Review
*     Screening Interview
*     Paid Work Test
*     Team Interviews
*     Reference + Offer

To guarantee that your application receives full consideration, please apply by Wednesday, September 30th (11:59 PM UK time).

Please apply [here](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/PRISM?utm_source=rkZvvbw025https://).

title: Account Executive, Azure
description:
*Note: this role is remote, but preference given to candidate based in the Greater Austin, Dallas, or NYC areas. This role involves on-site meetings at Microsoft’s offices. Previous experience selling Azure or another cloud (AWS/GCP) is required.*

**About Us**
Sela is a global cloud partner, dedicated to guiding our clients in their cloud journey. With deep partnerships across AWS, GCP, and Azure—and a growing practice at the intersection of cloud and AI—we help enterprises modernize infrastructure, migrate workloads, and build intelligent, resilient systems. Our team has over three decades of experience delivering excellence and thought leadership to clients. We take pride in our strong engineering culture, our drive for excellence, and our supportive team.

**What We Are Looking For**
We're looking for an Account Executive to join our growing sales team. This is a strategic, field-driven role with Azure as your primary cloud focus. You'll own relationships with Microsoft’s field teams at their regional offices, drive net-new business, and expand existing accounts across cloud migration, modernization, data, and AI workloads. You'll work closely with Sela's technical team to scope and sell meaningful professional services engagements, not just licenses or resale. You're someone who genuinely loves technology, builds credibility with engineers and executives alike, and thrives at the intersection of sales and solutions.

**Responsibilities**
* Own the full sales cycle for cloud professional services engagements (migration, application modernization, DevOps, data, and AI/ML workloads) from prospecting through close
* Build and maintain deep relationships with Microsoft’s field sales teams (especially SMEC and Scaling AI), acting as a trusted co-sell partner
* Identify and develop new business opportunities with startup and mid-market clients across cloud migration, modernization, and managed services
* Collaborate with Sela's architects and engineers to scope solutions, develop proposals, and support technical discovery
* Manage and grow a portfolio of existing accounts, identifying expansion opportunities across new service lines
* Maintain accurate pipeline and forecasting in CRM tools
* Represent Sela at Microsoft and cloud industry events
* Bring market and customer insights back to the team to help shape offerings and go-to-market strategy, particularly around AI and cloud-native workloads

**Requirements**
* 2+ years of B2B technology sales experience
* At least some hands-on experience selling Azure, GCP, or AWS — you've carried a number tied to cloud and know how the hyperscaler motion works
* Demonstrated success hitting targets and a self-directed approach to building pipeline
* Working knowledge of Microsoft Azure and real interest in going deeper: you understand the basics of the platform and the partner ecosystem, and you're eager to learn the field motion
* Comfortable selling services rather than products, or ready to learn how: you can hold your own in conversations about migrations, modernization, and technical scoping alongside our architects
* Genuine curiosity about technology and the credibility to earn trust with vendor field teams, customer technical leaders, and our engineering team
* Clear, confident communicator who can hold a room with senior stakeholders
* Coachable, resourceful, and comfortable operating without much structure (we're a small US team)
* Available for regular on-site engagement at local Microsoft offices

**Preferred Qualifications**
* Azure as your primary platform, with fluency in the ecosystem and partner motion
* 5+ years in B2B technology sales, including cloud professional services or infrastructure
* Experience selling data, AI/ML, DevOps, or cloud-native modernization work
* Existing relationships in the Microsoft partner organization, especially SMEC and Scaling AI
* Familiarity with Microsoft co-sell motions and funding programs
* Background in professional services, systems integration, or consulting sales
* Azure certifications or Partner accreditations
 
**Why Join Us?**
* Be part of a technical, high-integrity team working on meaningful cloud and AI projects
* Sell with the backing of a strong engineering team; you'll have real solutions to bring to customers
* Help shape Sela's go-to-market as we grow our AI and cloud practice
* Strong relationships with Microsoft field teams that create real co-sell momentum
* Opportunities for growth in sales leadership as the team scales

**Benefits**
* Remote-first workplace
* We offer top medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents (with options for 100% covered)
* FSA and HSA plans available
* Retirement matching (3%)
* Unlimited PTO
* Occasional lunch and learns and happy hours
* Home office stipend
* Occasional team get-togethers
* Modern tools to get your job done (MacBook, etc)
* Collegial workplace focused on individual growth

*This is a remote, full-time position open to candidates located in the United States. This role will frequently involve on-site work at Microsoft’s Austin or Dallas offices. Expected base salary range is $110,000–$150,000, commensurate with experience. This role includes a performance-based commission plan, with expected OTE of $250,000–$300,000 and additional upside for overachievement.*

title: Founding GTM Lead / Sales Co-Founder
description:
**About Relay**
Relay is building operations software for companies where work happens across facilities, equipment, frontline employees, departments, and multiple locations.

Our platform gives operational teams a structured way to report problems, establish ownership, coordinate work and communication, escalate unresolved issues, and identify recurring operational patterns.

We're initially focused on operationally complex industries including manufacturing, warehousing and distribution, property operations, and multi-site businesses.

The product is built and live. We have industry-specific demos, pricing and onboarding in place, along with an internally developed CRM, prospect research, outbound infrastructure, sales sequences, engagement tracking, and other GTM tooling.

We're now looking for an experienced B2B SaaS salesperson to build the commercial side of the company alongside the founder.

**The Role**
This is a hands-on founding sales role.

Initially, you'll personally build pipeline and work accounts from cold prospect through close. That means prospecting, calling, outbound email, discovery, demos, follow-up, pilots, negotiation, and closing.

We're not looking for someone whose experience is primarily managing an established sales organization. We're looking for someone who knows how to sell when the company is early, the playbook is still being developed, and there isn't an SDR team filling the calendar.

You'll also have significant involvement in developing Relay's overall go-to-market strategy: who we target, how we position the product, how we price and package it, how we run the sales process, and what commercial infrastructure we build.

The goal is for this person to eventually build and lead the commercial organization as the company grows.

**What You'll Do**
* Build outbound pipeline from target accounts
* Cold call, email, and prospect directly into organizations
* Identify champions, operational buyers, economic buyers, and other stakeholders
* Run discovery calls and product demonstrations
* Develop account strategies and multithread opportunities
* Structure and manage trials and pilots
* Handle objections, negotiation, and closing
* Establish a repeatable sales process
* Refine our ICP based on actual market response
* Help develop positioning, messaging, pricing, and packaging
* Build sales enablement, qualification, and objection-handling processes
* Turn prospect conversations into useful product and market feedback
* Help determine what should be added or changed in our internally developed CRM and GTM tooling
* Eventually recruit and lead additional commercial talent

**Who We're Looking For**
* You should have meaningful experience personally selling B2B SaaS or enterprise software.
* We're particularly interested in someone who has:
* Personally generated pipeline through outbound prospecting
* Cold-called prospective customers
* Run discovery and software demonstrations
* Managed multiple stakeholders within B2B accounts
* Structured pilots or trials
* Negotiated and closed software deals
* Worked effectively without a large marketing or SDR organization
* Helped develop or improve a sales process rather than simply following one
* Early-stage or founding sales experience is strongly preferred.
* Experience selling software into manufacturing, operations, maintenance, facilities, property management, logistics, field service, or other physical operational environments would be particularly valuable.

**Compensation & Equity**
Relay is early-stage, and we are not currently in a position to offer the market-rate base salary that an experienced SaaS salesperson could receive from an established software company.

Initial compensation will therefore be heavily performance-based, with substantial commission/revenue participation on business generated.

For the right person, there is a path to meaningful founder-level equity and a genuine commercial co-founder role.

We don't intend to make that decision based solely on interviews. We want to work together first, establish that the partnership works, and determine whether there is a strong long-term founder fit.

As recurring revenue grows sufficiently to support it, the role is expected to transition to a conventional executive compensation structure with base salary and performance compensation.

**Longer Term**
Relay is the company's first commercial software product, but it is not intended to be the last.

The longer-term objective is to build additional B2B software products and a commercial organization capable of taking those products to market.

For the right person, this is an opportunity to become the commercial counterpart to a product-focused founder and help build that capability from the beginning.

Location: Indianapolis, IN / Remote
Role: Founding GTM Lead / Sales Co-Founder
Experience: B2B SaaS sales experience required; early-stage experience preferred

title: Principal Software Engineer, Health Data & Interoperability (Remote)
description:
### **About the Company**
Verto Health is a health technology company solving some of healthcare’s most complex data fragmentation and interoperability challenges. Our patented, AI-enabled platform brings together structured and unstructured clinical data across disparate EHRs, claims, and payer systems to create a unified, actionable view of patient populations.

We work with health systems and value-based care organizations across North America to turn fragmented healthcare data into personalized patient journeys, automated workflows, and more accurate risk adjustment. By connecting data to action, Verto helps healthcare providers reduce manual work, improve operational efficiency, and deliver more proactive, data-driven care at scale.

### **About the Role**
As Principal Software Engineer, Health Data & Interoperability, you will be the senior technical voice on our engineering team and the owner of the data architecture underneath the product. You’ll set the bar for what good code looks like, build the AI-assisted development pipeline the team works through, and own the canonical model and the pipelines that feed it.

This is a hands-on role. You'll write code, review everyone else's, and design the ingestion and transformation that turns fragmented and inconsistent healthcare data across HL7 v2, FHIR, claims, and third-party sources into something the product can depend on.

Reporting into the CIO, you'll largely interface with four teams. The engineering team owns application architecture and software development, and will operate the pipelines you design. The AI engineering team owns AI system design and evaluation, and will depend on you for reliable modelled inputs. The product and delivery team owns the roadmap. The implementations team owns client projects and integration delivery.

### **What You'll Do**
#### Engineering Leadership & R&D
*  Set and hold the code review bar, and raise the standard of what ships rather than only reviewing what arrives.
*  Build and drive our AI-assisted development pipeline, from the agentic harnesses themselves through to daily use of frontier coding tools across the team.
*  Own technical R&D and spikes: evaluate what is worth adopting, prove it, and bring back something the team can use.
*  Hold the line on technical debt and resilience, including retiring legacy code and fixing projects that only one person understands.
#### Data Architecture
* Own the canonical healthcare data model covering patients, encounters, providers, claims, and clinical events, fit for longitudinal records, cross-source analytics, and EMPI.
* Own the semantic terminology service, the platform APIs applications consume, and the datasets the application and analytics layers depend on.
* Set the standards for data quality, lineage, and standardization, and build provenance in outputs informing a clinical or financial decision can be traced to source.
* Own decision rights on the data model and data standards, and make the data-side calls in the Architecture Review Board.
#### Interoperability & Data Pipelines
* Design the ingestion and ETL that brings HL7 v2, FHIR, claims, and third-party data into the platform, and keep it working as sources change.
* Work with federated query engines such as Trino and with ingestion patterns that span many source systems.
* Optimize pipelines for throughput, cost, reliability, and latency, and own root cause when a feed breaks.
* Build for operability so the engineering team can run what you design without you in the loop.
* Keep ingestion patterns reusable across clients rather than rebuilding them for each client.

### What You Bring
#### Knowledge & Experience
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Health Informatics, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 7+ years in software and data engineering, including 4+ years hands-on building and operating production systems on a team that reviewed each other's code.
* Strong current Python and SQL, with excellent software engineering craft. You will be writing code and reviewing everyone else's.
* Hands-on HL7 v2 and FHIR experience with real EHR and claims data, including designing the ingestion behind it. You have debugged live feeds, not only read the specifications.
* Experience designing canonical data models, schemas, and ETL at scale across multiple source systems, rather than a single integration.
* You’ve set and held a code review bar on a team, and are comfortable leading through influence without direct reports.
* Hands-on with AI-assisted development tooling, with an interest in building the harnesses rather than only using them.
* Cloud data platform experience, ideally Azure, and working knowledge of PHIPA, PIPEDA, or HIPAA as they bear on health data.
#### Preferred
* Experience with interface engines such as Mirth Connect, Rhapsody, or InterSystems, and standards including HL7 v3, C-CDA, IHE, DICOM, or X12 claims files such as CCLF.
* Experience with clinical terminologies including SNOMED CT, LOINC, and ICD-10, or analytical modelling such as OMOP CDM.
* Familiarity with the Canadian digital health landscape, including Ontario Health, provincial health information exchanges, or Canada Health Infoway.

### How You Work
* A strong communicator who can align a room on a complex system and explain it just as well to a client executive as to an engineer.
* At ease finding the simplest workable route through a messy integration, in a company where scope is broad and resources are lean.

### What Success Looks Like
* Pipelines that hold: ingestion keeps working as sources change, and cost and latency improve rather than drift.
* The bar rises: code quality, review standards, and AI-assisted development adoption visibly improve across the team.
* Architecture that holds: the canonical model and semantic layer absorb new clients and sources without a redesign each time.
* Data trust: quality, lineage, and standardization standards are met and demonstrable, with audit evidence ready when asked.
* Knowledge shared: architecture decisions are documented and technical depth is growing in the team, not concentrated in one person.

### Where You'll Work
* This role is remote and open to candidates anywhere in Canada.
* We hold in-person team days at our downtown Toronto office roughly once a quarter.

### Why Verto
* Own the data foundation everything we sell depends on, in a product used by health systems across North America
* Genuine architectural ownership without leaving the code
* Shape how AI-assisted engineering is practiced across the team
* Work on some of the hardest data interoperability problems in healthcare, with the autonomy to actually solve them
* Generous professional development support and flexible work options

### Compensation
The salary range for this role is $165,000 to $190,000 CAD per year, depending on experience, skills, and alignment with the role.

In addition to base compensation, Verto Health offers a comprehensive benefits package, which may include health and dental coverage, paid time off, professional development support, and flexible work arrangements.

Compensation is reviewed regularly to ensure fairness, market alignment, and internal equity.

### Ready to Apply
If you’re eager to tackle some of healthcare’s hardest data problems, own the architecture that turns fragmented data into something teams can actually build on, and shape how AI-assisted engineering works across a growing team, we’d love to hear from you.

Do you have 70% of the qualifications we're looking for? That's enough. Apply anyway.

If you have come across this post through an external job board, we strongly encourage candidates to apply directly through [our careers page here](https://vertohealth.applytojob.com/apply/ruJJhusE1x/Principal-Software-Engineer-Health-Data-Interoperability-Remote?source=Wellfound).

Verto Health is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible experience for all applicants. If you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know and we'll work with you to meet your needs.

### Use of AI in the Hiring Process
Verto Health uses artificial intelligence-enabled tools during the recruitment process to assist in screening, assessing, and selecting applicants for this position. This includes tools to evaluate candidate skills, experience, and qualifications against the role requirements.

AI tools are used to assist our hiring team, not to make final hiring decisions. All candidate applications and interview outcomes are reviewed and evaluated by people. If you have questions about how AI is used in our hiring process, please reach out.

title: Head of Business Development
description:
# About Ataraxis AI

Ataraxis is a clinical AI research lab working at the intersection of multi-modal AI and precision medicine. Our goal is to make disease predictable. To accomplish this, we develop new AI methods that predict patient outcomes and treatment response, and build clinical tools to assist physicians in selecting the most optimal treatments for their patients.

Our AI research lab discovers and develops methods to recognize patterns and predict outcomes across complex, multi-modal clinical data. This spans our [causality](https://www.ataraxis.ai/research-causality) (Ataraxis™ Tau), [foundation model](https://www.ataraxis.ai/research---representation-learning) (Falcon and Kestrel for digital pathology), and [survival analysis](https://www.ataraxis.ai/research-survival-analysis) research.

Our first clinical products, such as [Ataraxis™ Breast](https://www.ataraxis.ai/ataraxis-breast-overview) for breast cancer, already help patients get the most appropriate treatment across the best academic institutions and community clinics worldwide.

At Ataraxis, you will have a unique opportunity to shape not only the future of our company, but also the future of healthcare. You will join an exceptional team at the forefront of clinical AI research and deployment. Our advisors include AI pioneers such as our founding advisor, Yann LeCun, and distinguished oncologists from top cancer research institutions, all united by the mission to redefine precision medicine.

Ataraxis has raised over $24 million in funding, including a $20 million Series A led by top venture capital funds such as Thiel Capital/Founders Fund (OpenAI, SpaceX, Palantir), Obvious Ventures (AMI Labs, Inceptive, Radical Numerics, Recursion), and AIX Ventures (Hugging Face, Perplexity).

We are an company with a flat organizational structure, where every team member is empowered to actively contribute. Leadership roles are earned by those who demonstrate initiative and consistently deliver exceptional results. Strong work ethic and the ability to prioritize ruthlessly are essential.

## **Responsibilities**

You will build Ataraxis's pharma partnership business from the ground up. Ataraxis has developed prognostic and predictive AI models validated in breast cancer, with potential applications across drug development, such as companion diagnostics, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and trial rescue. This role owns pharma as a revenue stream alongside our diagnostics business. In that process, you will:

- Identify target companies, map the decision unit inside each, run outreach, and lead negotiations to signature.
- Construct novel applications of our technology against each company's development pipeline and translate them for scientific, clinical, and business audiences.
- Build and maintain relationships with the people inside pharma who sponsor and fund partnerships.
- Bring pharma priorities and unmet needs back to our research and product teams.
- Work with research, clinical, product, and legal to scope what we commit to, structure the terms, and get agreements signed.
- Work directly with the CEO on pipeline, forecast, and deal strategy.

## **Qualifications**

- 8+ years in pharma and/or diagnostics business development, from inside pharma or from a diagnostics or technology company selling into pharma.
- Preferred: MD, PhD, PharmD, NP, or a Master’s degree in cancer biology, molecular biology, cell biology, biomedical sciences, pharmacology, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related life sciences field.
- Documented track record of leading or co-leading pharma deals in companion diagnostics, biomarkers, patient stratification, or similar. If you did not formally lead one, we want evidence you were pivotal in getting it done.
- Built a pharma partnership pipeline from scratch, or decided from the pharma side which partnerships got funded.
- Fluency in how pharma makes partnership decisions: who decides, where the budget sits within a business unit, and how deals actually get pushed through.
- Relationships across large and mid-cap oncology pharma that you can activate now.
- Comfortable doing deep on technical material, with a history of finding non-obvious applications for it.
- Bias for action.

title: Senior Account Executive (Enterprise)

description:
# **About Glacis**

We’re on a mission to revolutionize the supply chains of global giants like Tesla and Coca-Cola through AI agents that think, plan, and act. Backed by legendary Silicon Valley VCs behind Flexport, Databricks, and Perplexity, we’re empowering supply chain teams across the world to automate complex logistics workflows, integrate processes seamlessly with existing systems, and supercharge efficiency.

We’re a team of seasoned entrepreneurs, Y Combinator alumni, and ex-Googlers; if you’re ready to change the way a trillion-dollar industry operates, join us on Day 1.

## **The Role**

As our Senior Account Executive, you'll run complex, multi-stakeholder deals across mid-market and enterprise manufacturers and distributors where supply chain performance is a board-level priority. You'll have end-to-end responsibility: Actively do outbound and build pipeline, turn those leads into signed contracts, and help build a repeatable sales process along the way.

Your buyers are VP-level operations and supply chain leaders who have been in the industry for decades. You need to speak their language, understand their problems, and show them exactly how Glacis solves them.

## **Key Responsibilities**

- **Own the full sales cycle.** From qualifying inbound leads and running your own outbound, through discovery, technical validation, AI committee signoff, procurement, and close. You don’t hand off, you see it through.
- **Sell consultatively, not transactionally.** This is not copy-and-paste SaaS. Our customers run complex, deeply embedded operational processes and AI is new to nearly all of them. You'll need to understand the challenge and complexity within each organization, identify where AI can make a real difference, and collaborate closely with our team of forward-deployed engineers to configure a solution that addresses the customer's actual needs.
- **Earn credibility in the room.** Your buyers are VP-level operations and supply chain leaders at global manufacturers and distributors. You’ll win by understanding their real operational challenges: breakdowns in communication with suppliers, missed deadlines, ad hoc firefighting and connecting them to outcomes Glacis delivers.
- **Build and refine the go-to-market playbook.** There is no ready-made setup. You'll work across a mix of mid-market and enterprise deals, and every deal teaches us something: what messaging resonates, which industries convert, what objections come up. You document what works, share what doesn’t, and help shape the methodology that scales.
- **Maintain disciplined pipeline management and accurate forecasting.** You’ll run 3-12 month sales cycles with meaningful deal sizes. The business depends on knowing what’s closing, when, and at what value.
- **Bring market signals back to the product.** You’re in front of customers daily. When you hear consistent feedback on integrations, pricing, or onboarding, you bring that back so we build what actually closes deals.

# **Are You the Right Fit?**

***Experience***

- You've sold software into supply chain, procurement, or logistics teams at mid-market or enterprise manufacturers and distributors, and you understand the domain, not just the software layer, but the operational reality underneath it.
- You have 5+ years experience closing mid-market or enterprise deals with US or European buyers with a minimum of $75k ACV, multiple stakeholders, 3+ month cycles, technical validation, executive sign-off.
- You have owned and successfully operated in the past the full lifecycle from building your own pipeline to rollout with customers.
- Ideal but not required: you've worked in supply chain operations, logistics, or procurement or have done consulting for those teams before moving into sales. You've managed the chaos yourself.

***Mindset***

- You're a self-starter who doesn't need structure to be effective. You're comfortable building the process as you go, being wrong sometimes, and iterating fast.
- You're intellectually honest about your pipeline. You disqualify deals that aren't real. You name what's stuck and fix it. You don't manage expectations by hiding problems.
- You want to help build a company, not just carry a quota. The opportunity to shape how the company sells and to share in what that builds - matters to you.

## **Who Might Not Be a Good Fit**

- If you've spent most of your career in short-cycle, transactional sales, the pace and complexity here will feel very different.
- If supply chains are unfamiliar to you. Our buyers have decades of operational experience and expect conversations grounded in their domain.
- If you do your best work inside a structured organization: clear territory, a BDR handing you qualified leads, an enablement team running playbooks; this isn't the right time. We're building that from the ground up.
- If ambiguity makes you uncomfortable. Incomplete information is the default at this stage.

# **Why Join Glacis?**

- **High Ownership & Real Impact:** Shape critical solutions used by global enterprises, directly influence supply chain performance at scale.
- **Entrepreneurial Growth:** Ideal stepping stone if you've considered founding your own company - learn firsthand from seasoned entrepreneurs and ex-Googlers.
- **Learn Fast in Enterprise B2B:** Deep exposure to supply chain, logistics, and AI; you’ll learn how to communicate complex operational problems and solutions.
- **Foundational Team:** Join at an early stage, contribute directly to company-building, and share the journey of rapid scaling.
- **Mission-Driven Culture:** Fast-paced, ambitious environment with collaborative colleagues committed to delivering meaningful, impactful technology.

description:
## About Share

Share is a venture-backed internet infrastructure network building Africa’s backbone. The company aggregates underutilised telecom infrastructure, fiber, subsea cables, and data centers, and provides ISPs with scalable access to bandwidth without traditional upfront costs. Through an open-access model, local internet providers can deliver dramatically faster speeds to their subscribers without raising their own costs.  
  
The platform team builds the software that makes this work: billing, payments, subscriber management, RADIUS-based network authentication, and integrations with ISP billing systems and mobile money providers. We are replacing legacy, non-API systems with a modern API platform, and real money is already flowing through the system. This is a small, high-intensity engineering team building core infrastructure under real deadlines. You will own entire domains, not tickets.

##   
**The role**

We are hiring a Founding Engineer to take ownership of core platform architecture as we rebuild for a system roughly 50x the scale of what we had before. You'll design and scale distributed systems from scratch (this is deep systems-architecture work, not feature development on an existing system.) You will work directly with the Head of Development and a small team of engineers to ship production systems operating at global scale.

**Non-negotiable**

- 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with real, hands-on ownership of designing and scaling a production system from scratch. You can describe specific production incidents at scale (what broke, why, and what you changed) not just system-design-interview theory.
- Deep TypeScript/Node.js expertise. You should be able to design a NestJS microservice from scratch, not just work in one.
- Strong PostgreSQL skills. You can design schemas for complex, high-throughput production data, write migrations, and reason about transaction isolation and locking.
- Experience with event-driven architectures (Kafka, RabbitMQ, or similar). You understand the difference between request-reply and fire-and-forget patterns and when to use each.
- You ship. You can take a spec document and turn it into production code without waiting for someone to break it into small tasks.

**Nice to have, not required**: prior fintech/payments experience or blockchain/distributed-ledger exposure

## **AI-augmented engineering (required mindset)**

We expect every engineer at Share to use AI tools as a daily part of their workflow. This is how we operate. Our entire project planning, specification, and documentation process runs through AI-assisted sessions. Our codebase includes AI-readable context files. We use Claude for architecture decisions, code review, spec generation, and technical writing.

What this means for you:

- You already use AI coding assistants (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, or similar) daily and can articulate how they change your workflow.
- You are comfortable working with AI-generated specifications and can critically evaluate them, push back where they are wrong, and extend them where they are incomplete.
- You see AI as a force multiplier that lets a small team operate at the capacity of a much larger one. You are not threatened by it; you are faster because of it.
- You are willing to contribute to improving our AI-assisted workflows

## **Compensation & Details:**

- Competitive Salary & Equity package
- Additional Benefits
- Paid Business Travel when needed
- Ownership in a venture-backed early stage startup building the future of physical and digital infrastructure in Africa

title: Sr. Product Marketing Manager
description:
## **Who Are We?**

Thanx is a leading loyalty and guest engagement platform for regional and national restaurants. We help brands drive profitable growth by increasing guest frequency, growing digital sales, and reducing reliance on discounts. Most loyalty platforms work for guests who are already loyal. Thanx unifies loyalty, digital ordering, and marketing automation in one platform that turns first-time and casual guests into regulars, treating loyalty as a business outcome, not a program, and engaging across the entire guest base.

Thanx has raised more than $30M from elite investors including M33 Growth, Ribbit Capital, and Sequoia Capital. Our success is rooted in a culture that has attracted some of the best talent in the country, and we are proud of strong employee tenure, a track record of internal promotions, and the company-wide shift to working AI-native over the last 18 months. We credit our cultural “core behaviors” with these accomplishments: Think Boldly, Execute Reliably, Focus on What Matters, Say “Thanx” Genuinely, Encourage Diverse Perspectives, and Lead, Virtually.

## **Who Are You?**

You're a product marketer who owns outcomes, not output. You are naturally curious about customers and not-yet customers. You write well and fast, and you get real satisfaction out of turning a customer's results into something a salesperson, a CSM, or a prospect can immediately use.

You've spent enough time in growth-stage B2B SaaS to know how companies like ours work: how sales cycles move, what CS teams need, why launches succeed or stall. You have run launches where you set the strategy, not just the deliverables, and you have built positioning that sales adopted because it worked, not because you told them to.

You decide what matters and what doesn't. You hold a steady output of high-quality material, you figure things out when the path isn't obvious, and you notice a gap and fill it before anyone assigns it. You are equally comfortable briefing the exec team and sitting on a customer call taking notes.

Everyone at Thanx has equity and is expected to operate like an owner. That means real intensity, including evenings and weekends when the work calls for it. If that isn't what you're looking for right now, this isn't the right role. **We would rather you know that before you apply than after you start.**

## **Position Overview**

Thanx ships a lot. That effort only matters if the market, our prospects, and our own customers understand it and adopt it. The range is wide: big agentic AI launches like our most recent, RecoveryAI; technical ones like Square ordering, where the value exists in the minutia; and everything in between. Each has a different goal, and you work backward from that goal rather than running the same playbook every time.

That's this role. You own how the market understands what we build. You set launch strategy, own positioning and messaging for the surface areas you cover, and turn what our customers are doing into proof that makes the value obvious to prospects, customers, internal teams, and partners.

You report to the VP of Marketing and operate as a peer to sales, CS, product, and partnerships leadership. You will lead cross-functional launch teams without formal authority over them, brief the exec team on what is and isn't landing in market, and make the call on what we do and don't invest in.

## **How We Work With AI**

**What Thanx gives you**

AI capability at Thanx is infrastructure, not a perk. You will be given the tools, the budget, and the working culture to get good at this quickly:

- **Real token budgets.** You will not be rationed on the tool you use to do your work.
- **Keystone.** Our homegrown connective tissue that puts company data and tooling into a queryable, natural-language format.
- **The Grid.** An internal site to host AI-built applications, reports, and tools that can be shared company-wide.
- **A show-and-tell culture.** People here demo what they have built, and it becomes something the rest of the company uses. Getting up the learning curve is a shared project, not a solo one.
- **A growing library of tools we built ourselves.** Marketing runs its own marketing calendar app, marketing dashboard, competitive intelligence hub, case study asset builder, and sales demo platform. You will add to it: build the tools that take repeatable work off your plate, and hold the output to a higher standard.

**What we expect from you**

- **You treat AI as a working partner.** You know the output is only as good as the context you give it and the review you do afterward, and you invest time in both.
- **You build or improve things other people use**. When you solve a problem, you put in the extra effort to make the solution reusable, so nobody on your team has to solve it again. Then you do the harder part: make it good enough, and obvious enough, that using it beats going back to the old way.
- **You do not wait to be assigned the work.** You notice when a one-off request is really a recurring problem, and you decide it is worth solving before anyone asks you to.

At review time, the question is not how much you used AI. It is what you built, who else is using it, and how your team works differently because of it.

**What it looks like in this role**

- **You build the tool that makes the content.** Instead of just writing the case study, you also build what orchestrates the whole case study production process: one customer interview in, a dozen usable formats out, page drafts in Webflow, deck content, and social assets that don't wait on a designer. Sales and CS run it themselves rather than queuing behind you, and the test is whether what comes out is usable without review cycles.
- **You find the stories in the product.** You use our internal analytical AI tool, Sherlock, to investigate how customers actually run their business on Thanx, surfacing the learnings and outcomes that today only exist in our CSMs' heads. You turn those golden nuggets into externally facing content in days, not weeks. Gone are the days of long-form content that takes months to produce.
- **You get content seen.** You treat distribution as half the job. You keep trying formats until one breaks through: video, podcasts, live events, office hours, community forums, whatever gets the audience to show up, and you use AI to make the learning curve shorter and the output more fun.
- **You know the market and the competitive landscape cold.** You use AI to listen for and understand what competitors are shipping and what operators are actually dealing with - traffic softness, labor costs, delivery margins - and can explain how those connect to what we sell and how we are different.

## **Key Responsibilities**

- **Positioning and messaging.** Own product-level positioning and messaging for the platform areas you cover. Build the frameworks, get sales and CS to adopt them, and revise them as the market and the roadmap change. You are the person who decides how we talk about what we build, and the person who defends that choice when someone disagrees.
- **Launch strategy and delivery.** Own launches end to end: set the tier, define the goal, choose the tactics that fit that goal, run the cross-functional team, and report honestly on what worked. You decide what gets a full launch and what gets a release note, and you make that call based on business impact, not internal enthusiasm.
- **Customer stories and proof.** Own the proof library, not just the individual stories. Interview newly launched customers and the internal teams behind them, find the unique angle, and produce everything from short reference stories to full case studies with quotes, metrics, and narrative. Build the system that turns one interview into one-pagers, slides, use case documentation, and the proof that answers "show me someone doing this" and "when would I use this feature?" Know where the gaps in our proof are before sales tells you.
- **Enablement for sales, CS, and partners.** Own what those teams know and say about the platform. Build the training, the competitive positioning, and the objection handling, then measure whether it is being used and whether win rates moved. Work directly with sales and CS leadership on where the gaps are.
- **Market and competitive command.** Own our point of view on what competitors are shipping and what restaurant operators are actually dealing with. Bring that back into positioning, roadmap conversations, and exec discussions. Be the person the exec team asks when they want to know what is happening in market.
- **External and in-product content.** Keep a regular cadence of customer-win content for social and partner channels ("this brand launched this week, here's why it's interesting"), and apply a product marketing lens to the Help Center and in-dashboard content: embedded video, plus the context that explains why and when to use a feature, not just how it works.

## **How We Will Know It's Working**

At six months: you have run at least one Tier-1 launch end to end, sales is using messaging you wrote, and you have published proof for customers who launched on your watch.

At twelve months: positioning is largely owned by you, the exec team comes to you for market intel, and the systems you have built mean the next launch takes less of everyone's time than the last one.

## **What We’re Looking For**

We don't believe in rigid requirements, but success in this role typically involves:

- 8+ years in B2B SaaS, including 5-7 years in product marketing, customer marketing, or a closely adjacent role.
- Ownership of at least one major product launch end to end, including the strategy and the tradeoffs, not just the deliverables.
- Positioning or messaging work that sales and CS actually adopted, and a clear account of how you got them to.
- A portfolio of written work you can walk us through, including case studies, product content, and enablement materials, and a clear sense of what it accomplished.
- Experience conducting customer interviews and finding the story inside them.
- Strong instincts for learning core personas, and for adapting the same material across prospects, customers, internal teams, and partners.
- A track record of working productively with sales and customer success, and of creating enablement content those teams actually used.
- Experience influencing cross-functional teams you don't manage, and presenting to executives.
- Comfort with video and multimedia formats, not just written content.
- Restaurant or hospitality technology experience is a plus.
