title: Game Designer — UI & Illustration (Online Games)
description:
We're looking for a designer who already figured out that AI isn't a threat — it's leverage.

You'll design the interfaces and illustrations for online games that are simple, fast, and hard to put down.

And you won't be doing it alone. Here, AI is part of the process: style exploration, asset variations, a clickable prototype the same day as the idea. People who master these tools ship more, ship better, and grow their value in the market. That's exactly the kind of person we want.

About the role

We're building the product design team for our online games. These are simple games by nature — few screens, clear rules, short loop.

We're looking for a UI and illustration designer who treats AI as part of the craft, not as a suspicious shortcut. Here, using AI well doesn't make you "less of a designer." It makes you a designer who validates an idea with a working prototype in hours, and spends the time saved on curation, art direction, and detail. That compounding is what we want to hire.

What you'll do
Design and maintain the interfaces for our games and platforms: game screens, onboarding, wallet, promotions, missions, and campaigns.
Create original illustrations, icons, mascots, and assets that give our products personality — using generative AI as an engine for exploration, while keeping curation and finishing under human control.
Turn concepts into wireframes and interactive prototypes, fast.
Evolve and maintain our design system: tokens, components, states, documentation.
Work side by side with engineering, product, and marketing so that what was designed reaches the player's screen the way it was designed.
Create animations and microinteractions that bring the interface to life (Lottie, Rive, After Effects).
What we're looking for
A solid portfolio demonstrating UI, UX, and illustration.
Real use of AI in your workflow. "I've tried ChatGPT" isn't enough. We want someone who knows prompting, refinement, upscaling, style control — and above all, when to throw out what the AI produced. Tools like Midjourney, Nano Banana, Firefly, Sora, Claude, ChatGPT. What you use matters less than how you use it.
A genuine desire to learn how to build the UI, not just draw it: a working grasp of HTML/CSS, AI-assisted prototyping, an understanding of how design becomes code. If you already do this, great; if you want to learn, you'll learn it with us.
Interest (or experience) in online games, casual games, gamification, or digital entertainment products.
Excellent communication and a real ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams.
The autonomy to run several projects in parallel and hit tight deadlines without drama.
Solid command of design principles, usability, and accessibility.
Initiative, problem-solving, and an obsession with detail.
Nice to have
Strong motion design, animation, and microinteraction skills (Rive, Lottie).
Experience with responsive and mobile-first design.
Previous experience in iGaming, casual games, entertainment apps, or products with a heavy gamification layer.
Having automated part of your own design workflow — scripts, plugins, pipelines, agents. Counts for a lot.
What we offer
Work model: fully remote.
Budget and freedom to use whatever AI tools you want.
A team that ships fast, and a product with a real audience using it every day.

If you know how to turn technology into creativity, speed, and experiences that hold attention, we want you on our team. 🚀

title: SAP ABAP Specialist (FI/CO)
description:
**Come Make an Impact on Millions of Brazilians!**

At RecargaPay, we’re on a mission to deliver the best payment experience for Brazilian consumers and small businesses, by building a powerful digital ecosystem where the banked and unbanked connect, and where consumers and merchants have a one-stop shop for all their financial needs.

We serve over 10 million users and process more than USD 4 billion annually. We’ve been profitable since 2022 and operate our own credit business. We are an AI-first, 100% remote team, scaling in the rapidly changing Brazilian financial market.

Our goal? Deliver the best payment experience in Brazil for people and small businesses alike.

We value autonomy, ownership, and a bias for action. We’re looking for people who are curious, hands-on, and driven by impact, who want to solve real problems, work with strong teams, and rethink what’s possible.

**If you’re ready to do your best work, at scale, with purpose, this is your place.**

### Responsibilities

As **SAP ABAP Specialist (FI/CO)**, you will be the hands-on ABAP developer of RecargaPay’s SAP S/4HANA platform, with a strong background in Finance and Controlling and in Brazilian Localization. You own custom code end to end, from impact analysis and design to development, testing, and production support, and you bring enough FI/CO and fiscal process knowledge to understand what the business is asking for, read and implement SAP Notes for legal and tax changes with autonomy, and challenge a requirement when standard functionality already solves it.

This is a founding role in a small, senior squad. You will work directly with the SAP & Corporate Systems Tech Lead, who owns technical governance, integration architecture, and engineering standards, and with the squad’s Product Owner and functional partners, who own configuration and business stakeholder management. Your job is the code: keeping it small, clean, upgrade-ready, and aligned with how FI/CO and Brazilian fiscal processes actually run.

RecargaPay is a BACEN-regulated fintech running SAP S/4HANA with FI, CO, SD, and MM under Brazilian Localization. The immediate agenda is the S/4HANA release upgrade currently in progress with an implementation partner, followed by the adaptation of the platform to Reforma Tributária (CBS/IBS) via DRC. You will be hands-on in both, first on custom code remediation during the upgrade, then on the SAP Notes and developments that the fiscal and accounting changes require.

Basis and platform operations (SUM, kernel, HANA administration, backup and recovery) are delivered by a managed partner under the Tech Lead’s governance and are not part of this role. Functional configuration of FI/CO and localization is owned by functional specialists and partners; you are their technical counterpart, not their replacement.

You are expected to apply clean-core principles in daily development, favoring released APIs and extensibility options (in-app, developer, and side-by-side) over modifications, reducing the custom code footprint, and preparing the landscape for future upgrades and ABAP Cloud adoption where applicable.

### Key Responsibilities

- Design, build, test, and maintain custom developments end to end on S/4HANA, including reports and programs, enhancements (BAdIs, enhancement spots, implicit enhancements), user exits and substitutions/validations in FI/CO, CDS views, AMDP, RAP-based services, OData services for Fiori applications, forms (Adobe Forms / Smart Forms), background jobs, data migration and correction programs, and interfaces (IDoc, RFC/BAPI, OData, REST via ABAP HTTP client, proxies).
- Lead hands-on custom code activities for the S/4HANA release upgrade, including custom code impact analysis (ATC, Simplification Item checks, Custom Code Migration), SPDD/SPAU adjustments, remediation of obsolete or incompatible objects, cleanup of modifications and enhancements, technical regression support, cutover support, hypercare, and post-upgrade stabilization, in coordination with the Tech Lead, the implementation partner, and functional teams.
- Provide hands-on ABAP development for regulatory and fiscal changes impacting Brazil, including Reforma Tributária (CBS/IBS via DRC), SAP Notes analysis and implementation with manual steps and code adjustments, localization extensions (tax determination, NF-e, NFS-e, DRC / Document and Reporting Compliance, SPED and related obligations), custom code impact analysis, and technical support to functional changes led by FI/CO, Tax, Product, and external partners.
- Apply your FI/CO and localization background to translate business requirements into robust technical designs, assess technical feasibility, estimate effort, debug SAP standard code in finance and tax scenarios, and propose standard or extensibility-based alternatives to custom code where they exist.
- Assess the current custom code landscape, identifying unused or duplicated objects, modifications to SAP standard, undocumented developments, performance hotspots, security exposures, clean-core violations, integration dependencies, technical debt, partner dependencies, and opportunities for simplification, refactoring, or automation.
- Help define the SAP development operating model with the Tech Lead, including coding standards, naming conventions, code review practices, ATC baseline and check variants, ABAP Unit expectations, technical specification templates, definition of done, transport discipline, partner handoffs, and audit evidence practices for changes.
- Own custom code quality through ATC and Code Inspector, ABAP Unit tests, peer code review, and performance analysis (SQL Monitor, ST05, SAT, runtime analysis), ensuring HANA-optimized code (code pushdown, efficient data access) and durable, maintainable solutions.
- Follow the change management process through STMS and ChaRM / SAP Cloud ALM, ensuring traceability between requirements, technical specifications, transports, and test evidence, segregation of duties, emergency-change control, approval evidence, and safe promotion across DEV, QAS, and PRD.
- Apply secure coding practices in partnership with Security and GRC stakeholders, including proper authorization checks in custom objects, Code Vulnerability Analyzer findings remediation, protection against SQL injection and directory traversal, secure handling of personal and sensitive data, logging and audit trail requirements, and evidence generation aligned with LGPD, BACEN, and SOX where applicable.
- Develop and support the ABAP side of integrations between SAP and corporate systems, including SAP Integration Suite / CPI scenarios (proxies, OData and REST endpoints, IDoc and RFC interfaces), interface monitoring and error handling from the application perspective, and coordination with the Tech Lead, integration developers, or external partners for iflow changes.
- Lead troubleshooting and root-cause analysis of complex application-level incidents, including short dumps (ST22), failed background jobs, interface and runtime failures, performance degradation in custom code, authorization-related blockers in custom programs, posting and tax determination errors in custom logic, data inconsistencies, and upgrade defects, ensuring durable corrective actions and clear documentation.
- Act as the internal ABAP counterpart for implementation partners and AMS providers, reviewing and challenging technical designs, code quality, enhancement approach, SAP Notes strategy, transport sequencing, test evidence, security implications, documentation, and production-readiness criteria.
- Establish technical acceptance criteria for partner deliveries, including technical specifications, code review results, ATC compliance, unit and regression test evidence, rollback plans, performance validation, operational documentation, and handover quality.
- Create and maintain technical documentation, custom object inventories, technical specifications, developer guidelines, interface and job runbooks, known-error databases, and audit evidence repositories, ensuring readiness for internal, external, BACEN, LGPD, and SOX-related reviews.
- Use AI-assisted engineering tools responsibly for code generation, code review, test generation, ATC finding remediation, SAP Notes analysis, log and dump analysis, documentation, and knowledge base creation, ensuring all outputs are reviewed and validated before use in production or audit-relevant contexts.

**Requirements**

- Solid hands-on ABAP development experience on S/4HANA, including enhancements, CDS views, OData, and debugging of SAP standard code, with a clear understanding of clean-core principles and extensibility options.
- Several years developing for FI/CO and Brazilian Localization scenarios, with working knowledge of General Ledger, Accounts Payable and Receivable, Asset Accounting, cost objects, period-end closing, tax determination, NF-e / NFS-e, DRC or its predecessors (NF-e/GRC, TDF), and SPED, sufficient to read functional requirements and SAP Notes with autonomy.
- Experience implementing SAP Notes for fiscal and legal changes, including manual steps and code adjustments.
- Experience with S/4HANA release upgrades or conversions, including SPDD/SPAU and custom code remediation.
- Proficiency with ATC, Code Inspector, ABAP Unit, and performance analysis tools (SQL Monitor, ST05, SAT), and with HANA-optimized coding practices.
- Familiarity with transport management and change control in a regulated environment (STMS, ChaRM or Cloud ALM, segregation of duties, audit evidence).
- Ability to work directly with functional analysts, Accounting, Tax, and external partners, and to push back with standard-first or extensibility-first alternatives.
- Fluent Portuguese or Spanish; the squad works across Brazil and Spanish-speaking LATAM, so candidates from either market are welcome. Working English for documentation and vendor interaction.

**Nice to have:** RAP and ABAP Cloud, Fiori development, SAP Integration Suite / CPI from the application side, exposure to Reforma Tributária (CBS/IBS) preparation, experience in fintech or another BACEN-regulated company, and experience acting as the internal counterpart to an AMS or implementation partner.

**Benefits**

- Competitive and market-aligned salary.
- Remote work — wherever you are, you’re part of the team!
- Home office allowance through a monthly deposit in the RecargaPay app.
- Health and dental plans with no co-pay.
- Life insurance.
- Flexible meal allowance (via Flash).
- TotalPass membership to take care of your health.

**Diversity & Inclusion at RecargaPay**

At RecargaPay, you’ll have the freedom to be who you are because we believe that diverse perspectives and experiences make us more creative and stronger. Here, everyone is welcome to express themselves authentically. We value the richness of each journey and the multiple ways of seeing the world, without distinctions of gender, race, sexual orientation, age, religion, or any other characteristic that makes us unique.

**About the use of your Data**

By sharing your resume with us, you authorize the use of your data for analysis during the selection process and possibly for other opportunities within the RecargaPay group. You can request the update or deletion of your information at any time, in accordance with LGPD (General Data Protection Law).

title: Senior Scientist
description:
**Location:** Oxford or London (Hybrid)

**The Mission: Why We Exist**

Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer healthier lives, using the power of genomics.

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

**A Day in the Life**

As a Senior Scientist, you'll drive innovation and collaboration, acting as a strategic consultant on high-impact projects with diverse external pharma and biotech partners. You’ll communicate insights effectively, helping to shape team direction and leading transformative initiatives across the discovery and development spectrum.

You will navigate across the entirety of the drug development pipeline, from target discovery and validation through to patient stratification. Utilizing a strategic approach and advanced statistical techniques, you will work closely with external collaborators to prioritize therapeutic targets, optimize clinical insights, and unveil new treatment possibilities.

Success here demands a robust grasp of statistical human genetics applied inventively in a partner-facing environment. You'll excel in unraveling complex genomic data and possess a knack for translating raw findings into actionable consulting insights, whilst working collectively with both your highly skilled internal team and external partners.

**Who You Are**

- Experience in performing foundational genetic association analyses (e.g., GWAS; PRS)
- Strong competency in statistical programming (e.g., R, Python) sufficient to enable large-scale genomic data analysis

- Experience in data mining and/or management of large datasets.
- Confident in engaging with a variety of stakeholders, contributing and supporting in the delivery of presentations to customers.

**Your Package**

We are committed to providing a transparent, supportive, and rewarding work environment.

### **Compensation & Growth**

- **Vibrant Social Culture:** From regular Town Halls and team picnics to organised sports events, our social committee ensures frequent opportunities to connect and celebrate.
- **Green Commute:** Cycle-to-Work scheme and convenient office locations near major transport hubs.

**Ready to Build the Future?**

If this opportunity excites you, **apply now!**

We are dedicated to creating a diverse environment and are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

*Genomics politely requests no contact from recruitment agencies. We do not accept speculative CVs from recruitment agencies nor accept the fees associated with them.*

**The Mission: Why We Exist**

Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer, healthier lives, using the power of genomics.

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

**Role Purpose**

As our Associate Director/Director Business Development, you'll be a senior commercial force in the life sciences market - leading high-value, strategic new business for Mystra, our SaaS data and analytics platform, as well as our technology-enabled consultancy business . You'll engage at the most senior levels of pharma and biotech, building the kind of relationships and deals that define Genomics' trajectory.

This is a role for someone with deep commercial instincts, a genuine scientific grounding, and the confidence to operate as a trusted peer to R&D and data leaders at the world's leading pharmaceutical companies. You'll be a key senior individual contributor in a fast-moving Commercial team, and your success will directly shape the future of the business.

## **The Role**

We are looking for a strategic New Business Hunter to drive enterprise sales into the Research & Development (R&D) arms of global pharma and biotech companies.

This isn't a standard account management role; we need a closer who understands the life sciences landscape, speaks the language of R&D scientists, and knows how to navigate complex, high-value enterprise sales cycles from first contact to signed contract.

## **A Day in the Life**

- **Strategic New Business:** Own and drive the most significant new commercial opportunities across pharma and biotech. You will build multi-stakeholder relationships at the senior and executive levels, leading complex, high-value sales cycles from initial outreach to contract close.
- **Executive Client Relationships:** Invest deeply in understanding your clients’ long-term R&D and data strategies. You will position Genomics not just as a vendor, but as a critical scientific partner embedded in their workflow.
- **Market Leadership:** Bring a sophisticated view of the life sciences landscape, feeding strategic market intelligence back into our go-to-market approach and directly influencing how we evolve our platform.
- **Sales Operations & Discipline:** Maintain a high standard for pipeline hygiene, accurate forecasting, and strategic reporting to inform senior leadership and board-level decision-making.
- **Internal Influence:** Act as the internal "voice of the customer." You'll collaborate closely with our Product, Science, and Marketing teams to ensure our commercial strategy is always grounded in delivering genuine scientific value.

## **Who You Are**

- **Proven Hunter:** You have a substantial, proven track record of net-new enterprise SaaS, digital health, or technology sales into pharma and biotech, with demonstrable success closing complex, high-value deals.
- **Pharma R&D Domain Expert:** You have deep experience selling directly into Research, Discovery, and R&D departments inside major pharmaceutical companies. You navigate senior scientific and commercial stakeholders with ease.
- **Scientifically Credible:** You possess a strong working knowledge of genetics or genomics-enough to speak credibly, confidently, and compellingly about what advanced genetic analytics can unlock for drug discovery.
- **Commercial Strategist:** You think critically about markets, positioning, and competitive landscapes, bringing that strategic lens to every deal.
- **Autonomy:** You are a self-directed, senior operator who thrives in a fast-paced scale-up environment.
- **Education:** A degree in Life Sciences, Business, or a related field is required; an advanced degree (MSc/PhD) is a genuine asset.

**Your Package**

We are committed to providing a transparent, supportive, and rewarding work environment.

### **Compensation & Growth**

- **Competitive Salary**: Salaries are externally benchmarked annually to ensure top-of-market compensation.
- **Clear Career Path:** A straightforward, open progression framework means you'll always know the path to promotion and how to achieve your next career goal.
- **Continuous Learning:** Including external courses and a wide library of L&D materials, because your growth is our success.

**Wellbeing & Time Off**

- **PTO:** 25 days vacation, plus 8 federal holidays, plus an extra 3-day company-wide shutdown at year-end.
- **Full Coverage**: 401k, Comprehensive Health, Dental, and Vision plans, Health Savings Account (HSA), Life/AD&D, and Disability coverage.

### **Work Environment & Culture**

- **Flexible Working:** Hybrid Working.(e.g. From our RTP Office )
- **Truly Inclusive Time Off:** Our 'Bank Your Bank Holiday' program allows you to exchange public holidays for dates that hold personal or cultural significance to you.
- **Vibrant Social Culture:** From regular Town Halls and team picnics to organised sports events, our social committee ensures frequent opportunities to connect and celebrate.

**Ready to Build the Future?**

If this opportunity excites you, **apply now!**

We are dedicated to creating a diverse environment and are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

*Genomics politely requests no contact from recruitment agencies. We do not accept speculative CVs from recruitment agencies nor accept the fees associated with them.*

title: Business Development Representative
description:
Company: Corvane
Location: Remote
Compensation: 100% Commission
OTE: $30,000–$60,000+ per year (Uncapped)

THE SOLUTION

Corvane is building the next generation of consumer intelligence.

Our AI-powered research platform helps consumer brands make better decisions by giving them fast access to reliable consumer feedback. Brands use Corvane to validate ideas, test messaging, recruit verified research participants, track brand perception, test concepts, and understand what consumers actually think.

Corvane helps companies move from question to consumer insight faster, without the time and complexity of traditional research processes.

Our customers span beauty, fashion, wellness, food & beverage, consumer technology, and agencies serving consumer brands.

We are customer-driven at our core and are looking for a Business Development Representative who can help us put Corvane in front of more businesses and consistently generate qualified sales meetings.

THE ROLE

As a Business Development Representative at Corvane, your primary goal is simple:

Book qualified meetings for our Account Executive.

You will be responsible for identifying potential customers, reaching the right decision-makers, starting conversations, qualifying interest, and getting qualified prospects onto the AE's calendar.

This is a hands-on outbound role. A significant part of your day will involve cold calling, cold email, LinkedIn outreach, prospect research, and persistent follow-up.

You will build targeted prospect lists, identify decision-makers, run outbound sequences, make calls, send personalized emails, follow up across channels, qualify prospects, and schedule meetings.

Once a prospect is qualified and interested, your job is to make the handoff to the AE as seamless as possible.

You will work closely with the founder and Account Executive to refine our ICP, messaging, outreach strategy, qualification criteria, and meeting-generation process.

This is an early-stage role for someone who enjoys the hunt, is comfortable with rejection, and is motivated by measurable results.

YOUR PRIMARY GOAL

Your primary KPI is qualified meetings booked on the Account Executive's calendar.

You will be measured on:

Qualified meetings booked
Meetings that actually take place
Qualified opportunities generated
Outbound activity
Prospect-to-meeting conversion
Pipeline generated from your meetings

You are not expected to close the deals yourself.

Your job is to create conversations and turn those conversations into qualified meetings for the AE.

WHAT YOU'LL SELL

You will introduce prospects to Corvane's consumer intelligence and research solutions, including:

Consumer research engagements
AI-powered research platform subscriptions
Verified respondent recruitment
Brand tracking
Concept testing
Pricing research
Packaging and messaging validation
Enterprise research programs

Opportunities range from one-off research engagements to recurring enterprise contracts.

Enterprise contracts start at $21,000 annually, with larger opportunities available depending on customer needs, research scope, usage, and expansion potential.

Your role is not to sell the entire solution or negotiate the contract. Your role is to create enough interest to earn the meeting.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Prospecting & Lead Generation
Build targeted lists of companies that fit Corvane's ICP.
Research companies, decision-makers, and relevant business initiatives.
Identify founders, CEOs, CMOs, Heads of Marketing, Consumer Insights leaders, Brand leaders, Product leaders, and agency executives.
Find the right person to contact within each account.
Maintain organized prospect lists and outbound sequences.
Continuously identify new prospects and opportunities.
Cold Outreach
Make consistent daily cold calls.
Conduct personalized cold email outreach.
Prospect through LinkedIn and other relevant channels.
Follow up persistently across phone, email, and LinkedIn.
Test different messaging, subject lines, hooks, and CTAs.
Start conversations with prospects who have never interacted with Corvane.
Clearly communicate what Corvane does and why it may be relevant to the prospect.
Qualification & Meeting Booking
Engage prospects who respond to outbound outreach.
Ask thoughtful questions to determine whether there is a potential business need.
Identify whether the prospect is a good fit for Corvane.
Understand their current approach to consumer research and insights.
Identify relevant pain points, upcoming initiatives, or research needs.
Qualify prospects against agreed-upon criteria.
Book qualified meetings directly onto the Account Executive's calendar.
Provide the AE with useful context before each meeting.
Confirm meetings and reduce no-shows through appropriate follow-up.
Follow up with prospects who do not immediately book.
AE Handoff

Once a prospect agrees to meet, you will:

Schedule the meeting directly on the AE's calendar.
Capture relevant prospect information in the CRM.
Document the reason for the meeting.
Include key pain points, research needs, company information, and other relevant context.
Ensure the AE understands why the prospect agreed to meet.
Continue supporting the opportunity with follow-up when appropriate.
Sales Development Operations
Maintain accurate CRM records.
Track calls, emails, responses, meetings, and conversion rates.
Report weekly on outbound activity and meeting generation.
Test and improve prospecting strategies.
Share prospect feedback with the founder and AE.
Help refine our ICP, messaging, qualification criteria, and outbound process.
Contribute to building a repeatable outbound sales engine.
IDEAL CUSTOMERS

You'll primarily prospect:

Shopify and DTC brands
Beauty companies
Wellness brands
Fashion brands
Food & beverage companies
Consumer technology companies
Marketing and branding agencies
Consumer-facing businesses with ongoing research and consumer intelligence needs

You'll typically reach out to:

Founders and CEOs
CMOs
Heads of Marketing
Consumer Insights leaders
Brand leaders
Product leaders
Agency executives
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Previous experience in BDR, SDR, business development, sales development, or outbound sales.
Demonstrated ability to generate meetings through outbound prospecting.
Comfortable and confident making cold calls.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Experience with cold email and outbound prospecting.
Ability to research accounts and identify relevant decision-makers.
Strong follow-up discipline.
Ability to qualify prospects and identify genuine sales opportunities.
Highly organized and capable of managing a large prospect list.
Competitive, persistent, and comfortable with rejection.
Self-starter mentality and ability to thrive in an early-stage startup.
Highly motivated by measurable activity and results.
Comfortable working independently in a remote environment.
Excited by the opportunity to build something from an early stage.

Bonus: Experience selling or prospecting for SaaS, market research, consumer insights, analytics, advertising, marketing technology, or AI products.

COMMUNICATION REQUIREMENTS

Proficiency in written and verbal English is required.

You must be able to:

Communicate clearly and professionally with prospects over the phone.
Have confident cold calls with senior decision-makers.
Write clear, persuasive, and grammatically strong cold emails.
Communicate effectively with executives and business leaders.
Explain Corvane's product clearly and concisely.
Ask intelligent qualification questions.
Handle initial objections and create enough interest to earn a meeting.
COMPENSATION

This is a 100% commission role with uncapped earning potential.

You earn commission for qualified meetings that you successfully book and that take place with the Account Executive, with additional commission tied to revenue generated from opportunities sourced by you.

The exact commission structure will be discussed during the interview process.

There is no cap on earning potential.

The more qualified meetings you generate, the more opportunities you create, and the more you can earn.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
First 30 Days
Learn Corvane's product, ICP, and positioning.
Understand our qualification criteria.
Become comfortable with our outbound messaging.
Build targeted prospect lists.
Establish consistent daily calling and email activity.
Begin booking your first qualified meetings.
First 60 Days
Consistently generate qualified meetings.
Develop a repeatable daily prospecting process.
Improve call and email conversion rates.
Build relationships with decision-makers at target accounts.
Generate qualified opportunities for the AE.
First 90 Days
Consistently book qualified meetings onto the AE's calendar.
Establish a predictable outbound prospecting rhythm.
Generate a meaningful pipeline of qualified opportunities.
Develop repeatable strategies for reaching our ICP.
Contribute insights that improve our outbound messaging and sales process.
WHY JOIN CORVANE?

Sell a product solving a real business problem.
Consumer brands need faster, better ways to understand their customers and make informed decisions.

Work directly with the founder.
You'll have a direct line to the person building the company and shaping the product.

Unlimited earning potential.
Your earning potential scales with the opportunities and revenue you help generate.

Own your results.
You'll have significant autonomy over your prospecting strategy, outreach, and daily workflow.

Build something early.
You'll help establish Corvane's outbound sales engine from the ground up.

Opportunity to grow.
Strong performance in this role can lead to increased responsibility and progression into an AE or broader sales role as Corvane scales.

Fully remote and flexible.

WHO SHOULD APPLY?

This role is for a hunter.

You should enjoy finding companies from scratch, researching prospects, picking up the phone, sending cold emails, starting conversations with people who don't know you, handling rejection, following up, and turning cold prospects into real sales conversations.

You should be motivated by the number on the calendar.

If you get excited when a prospect finally responds to an email, picks up a cold call, or agrees to meet, you'll probably enjoy this role.

If you're looking for a traditional sales role where leads are handed to you, this isn't it.

If you're competitive, persistent, commercially minded, highly articulate in English, and excited by the opportunity to earn based on performance, we'd like to hear from you.

HOW TO APPLY

Email onanma@corvane.com with the subject line:

Corvane BDR - [Your Name]

Give me your best pitch on why I should hire you for this role and why Corvane.

Attach a resume if it strengthens your application.

Please include your primary location. This is a remote role.

Start your email with the word "Lily."

Keep it intentional and sharp.

title: Senior .NET Core Full Stack Developer
description:
Build the backend and frontend of enterprise SaaS products used by some of Microsoft's most demanding Teams and telephony customers, entirely from home, anywhere in Canada (excluding Quebec).

- **Stack:** C#, .NET 8 to .NET 10, Azure CosmosDB / MS SQL / PostgreSQL, Svelte / React
- **Experience:** 10 to 15 years of professional software development
- **Location:** 100% remote, must be based in and legally able to work in Canada (excluding Quebec)
- **Compensation:** $95,000 to $125,000 CAD per year, based on experience, plus profit sharing
- **Job Type:** Full-time, permanent, Monday to Friday

## Who We Are

Microsoft Teams Phone gets organizations most of the way. Entergrade handles the rest.

We are Microsoft Teams Phone administration at scale, call routing built for how enterprises actually operate, emergency notifications that hold up under pressure, and the analytics and compliance visibility that regulated organizations need to trust their own systems.

Enterprise grade is our standard. It's our name. It's the bar we hold our own work to, every day. We're a distributed team that includes Microsoft specialists, we are spread across three continents, SOC 2 Type II certified, with 14 Microsoft MVP awards among us. 

Empowerment is a real thing here! 
Things you will hear from our co-founders:  What if we try... Just pitching thoughts... I don't know the solution.... I'll let you figure out the best path forward... 

Nobody here shows up with every answer, we bring our best plan and we have each others backs during the hard parts. If this sounds the kind of place you want to do your work, we'd like to hear from you.

## What You'll Do

- Design and build full stack features across our .NET Core backend and Svelte frontend

- Work directly with customers to understand their Teams, telephony, and compliance challenges, and translate them into working software
- Collaborate with product, design, and engineering to scope and ship new features
- Prototype quickly, ship, and iterate based on real customer feedback
- Evaluate and adopt emerging technologies, including voice and text bots, where they genuinely improve the product

### Must-Have

- Deep, hands-on experience with C# and .NET 8 through .NET 10, including recent version migrations.
- Strong REST API design, JSON, and SQL
- Production experience with Azure CosmosDB, MS SQL, or PostgreSQL
- Solid HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, plus real production experience in either of Svelte or React
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience

### Bonus Points

- Experience with Microsoft Azure services, whether building on, operating, or managing them
- Experience with Microsoft 365 administration
- Experience with Microsoft Teams, SIP, or telephony systems
- Experience building text or voice bots

## Why Entergrade

- Remote, for real: work from anywhere in Canada (excluding Quebec) or USA, on a team that has been remote-first from day one
- Meaningful ownership: you'll work directly with customers and see your work ship, not sit behind five layers of process

- Profit sharing (Canada only) tied to the company's growth, not just your individual output

## How to Apply

Send us your resume along with a short note on the most interesting .net problem you've solved recently, what made it hard, and how you solved it.

Entergrade Solutions is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates.

title: Head of Growth & Marketing
description:
### **Company Description**
Arro is a fast-growing fintech on a mission to make fair credit accessible to everyone. More than 160 million Americans are overlooked by traditional financial institutions due to limited credit history, outdated underwriting models, or past financial setbacks. We're changing that.

Backed by the same people behind Chime, Square, Revolut, Step, and Brex, Arro combines credit access, financial education, behavioral science, and AI to help consumers build lasting financial health.

We believe that everyone deserves the opportunity to access fair credit and we're excited to bring on a Head of Growth to help make this a reality.

### **What You’ll Be Doing**
As a key marketing and growth leader, you'll own the entire growth engine, from strategy through execution. You'll work directly with the executive team to define how Arro acquires customers, engages members, builds trust, drives revenue, and becomes the leading brand in credit building and financial health.

This is a rare opportunity to build a category-defining fintech brand while having an outsized impact on millions of consumers who have historically been excluded from mainstream financial services.
Own Arro's growth strategy and be accountable for customer acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, and revenue growth.
* Develop and execute marketing initiatives across all channels, including affiliate marketing, partnerships, lifecycle marketing, social media, content, SEO, PR, referrals, and paid acquisition.
* Identify and scale low-cost, high-ROI growth opportunities through experimentation, partnerships, community building, and innovative distribution strategies.
* Define and evolve Arro's brand strategy, positioning, messaging, customer personas, and voice.
* Create and manage compelling content across web, email, social media, video, partner channels, and emerging platforms.
* Own Arro's social media presence and content strategy across LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Reddit, and other relevant channels.
* Build and manage affiliate, influencer, referral, and strategic partnership programs that drive measurable growth.
*  Develop and execute lifecycle marketing campaigns that improve onboarding, engagement, retention, and customer lifetime value.
*  Drive Arro's external visibility through media relations, thought leadership, speaking opportunities, awards submissions, and public relations initiatives.
*  Own marketing analytics, attribution, reporting, conversion optimization, and growth experimentation across the customer journey.
*  Support investor communications, fundraising materials, enterprise partnership initiatives, and other strategic company priorities as needed.


### What makes this role unique****
* Own all growth and marketing for a venture-backed fintech at a pivotal stage of scale.
* Work directly with the executive team and influence company strategy.
* Build a category-defining brand helping millions of Americans access fair credit.
* See a direct connection between your work and meaningful consumer outcomes.
* Competitive compensation, meaningful equity, and the chance to help shape the future of financial wellness.

### Qualifications****
* 6-10+ years in growth, marketing, product marketing, or customer acquisition, preferably in fintech, consumer technology, or high-growth startups.
* Proven track record scaling customer growth with limited budgets and strong ROI discipline.
* Equally comfortable discussing company strategy with executives and implementing a marketing campaign.
* Strong analytical mindset with deep experience using data to make decisions.
* Exceptional storyteller, communicator, and brand builder.

title: Software Engineer,  Frontend and Mobile
description:
## **About Bree**

Bree is a consumer finance platform that brings better, faster, and cheaper financial services to over half the Canadian population who live paycheque to paycheque. We operate in a huge, but overlooked market in a country with the least amount of financial technology innovation in the developed world. Our first act is to become the cheapest and best provider of short-term credit to the 20 million people in Canada who live paycheck to paycheck.

More than 800,000 Canadians have already signed up with Bree and we believe we are just scratching the surface. We are in an exciting place where we have product market fit, explosive growth, and a clear path to becoming one of the most important FinTechs in Canada.

We were part of [Y Combinator ](https://www.ycombinator.com/)in 2021 and raised a $2M seed round shortly after. Since then, we have built a small, high-ownership team focused on moving quickly and delivering meaningful customer impact.

## **About the Role**

We are looking for a Software Engineer with a strong mobile and frontend focus to help shape the primary way customers experience Bree.

You will own customer-facing features across our React Native application, from understanding the problem and collaborating on the experience through implementation, testing, release, and follow-up. You will work closely with Product, Design, CX, and other engineers to make complex financial journeys feel clear, trustworthy, and easy to use.

This is primarily a mobile and frontend role, but you will not be limited to a single layer. You should be comfortable working end to end across frontend code, API contracts, and backend dependencies so you can own the complete customer experience.

You will help us expand Bree across Canada, support new regulatory requirements, improve our mobile architecture, and make releases safer as the product and team continue to grow.

## **What You'll Do**

- Own mobile and frontend features from product discovery through public release.
- Work across a TypeScript/Node serverless stack (AWS Lambda, API Gateway, SQS) and React Native frontends.
- Collaborate closely with Product and Design to turn early ideas and mockups into thoughtful, usable experiences.
- Make pragmatic calls in ambiguous situations; unblock yourself and others without waiting on perfect specs.
- Instrument what you ship (logging, metrics, alerts) and add tests to keep releases stable.
- Improve existing surfaces: refactor opportunistically, pay down tech debt without slowing delivery.
- Own release readiness through staging, TestFlight, Google Play, release notes, smoke testing, and production monitoring.

## **What You'll Need**

- Experience shipping customer-facing mobile or web products in a startup or similarly fast-moving environment.
- Strong TypeScript and React Native experience, or deep React experience with the ability to move quickly into React Native.
- A strong understanding of component design, state management, networking, navigation, and frontend architecture.
- An AI-native development approach, using modern tools throughout implementation, debugging, testing, and review while carefully validating their output.
- Demonstrate product judgment: you can refine a rough idea into a scoped, high-leverage release.
- Communicate clearly, default to ownership, and stay even-keeled when wrestling with engineering tradeoffs.

## **Nice to Have**

- Experience with Expo, EAS, over-the-air updates, or similar React Native tooling.
- Observability chops (e.g., structured logging, tracing, performance profiling).
- Comfort with analytics/experimentation (event models, simple A/Bs) to validate features.
- Contributions to OSS or public write-ups about projects you’ve shipped.

⚕️Comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits plan

🖥 $1,500 annual learning & home-office stipend

🧘🏼 $1,000 annual wellness stipend

🍔 Monthly Lunch Stipend

🚗 Commuter Benefits

🏝20 annual PTO days + unlimited sick days

☕ In Office Amenities

title: Growth Engineer
description:
## The role

This is not a traditional marketing role, and it is not a pure engineering role either.

You will decide which accounts matter, build the systems that research them, write the content that reaches them, build the partnerships that amplify it, and turn all of that into qualified pipeline.

Two things have to be true about you at once.

You are technically sharp enough to build your own workflows, wire up your own APIs, and ship a working system without waiting on engineering or anyone else. Nothing you own should be blocked on a single person, including us.

And you are obsessed with distribution — content, syndication, social, and partnerships — because pipeline goes to whoever the buyer already trusts. That means newsletters, communities, podcasts, comparison pages, partner audiences, and the people who influence them.

## What you will own

### GTM strategy and experimentation

- Develop and continuously refine Oliv's ICP, market segments, buyer personas, and account-selection criteria.
- Translate company goals into specific growth hypotheses and campaign plans.
- Identify new audiences, buying signals, use cases, and distribution opportunities.
- Build a structured experimentation roadmap across content, social, syndication, partnerships, outbound, and ABM.
- Define success metrics before launching a program, then stop, modify, or scale it based on pipeline outcomes.

### Account research and intelligence

- Build systems that identify high-potential accounts and contacts, and the triggers that show an account is ready to engage.
- Develop enrichment workflows using firmographic, technographic, hiring, funding, leadership, and intent data.
- Create account-scoring and prioritisation models.
- Automate repetitive research while keeping data and output quality high, and turn raw account information into usable campaign insight.

### Content and syndication

- Own Oliv's content engine end to end: what gets made, who it is for, where it goes, and what it is supposed to produce. You will write it yourself.
- Build and work a distribution list of newsletters, communities, podcasts, and industry publications, and land Oliv in them.
- Get Oliv into the third-party listicles and comparison pages that both human buyers and AI answer engines cite.
- Build syndication and repurposing as a system, not a manual chore.
- Judge content on pipeline influenced, not on traffic or impressions.

### Social and community

- Run Oliv's social presence, brand and founder accounts alike, including ghostwriting for executives.
- Show up in the communities where our buyers actually talk — Reddit, Slack, and peer groups included — as a useful participant with your identity and employer disclosed, not as a spammer.
- Turn engagement into a workable audience: capture the people who interact, enrich them, and route them into the right motion.
- Treat social as a research channel as much as a broadcast one, and feed what you learn back into messaging and targeting.

### Partnerships and ecosystem

- Identify, pitch, and land the partners worth having: integration and tech partners, agencies, consultancies, communities, creators, and resellers.
- Build co-marketing programs — joint webinars, co-authored content, newsletter swaps, integration launches, marketplace and directory listings.
- Own a partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline number, and the plumbing that makes it measurable.
- Be someone a partner's senior team is glad to have on the call, and someone their team wants to work with again.

### Campaign strategy and execution

- Personally build and launch targeted campaigns across email, LinkedIn, ABM, content, and other relevant channels.
- Develop campaign concepts, offers, messaging, and audience logic, including account-specific experiences.
- Build nurture, reactivation, closed-lost, and expansion campaigns.
- Coordinate closely with sales on account selection, follow-up, and pipeline conversion.
- Run small, fast experiments before scaling, and own quality from targeting through measurement.

### GTM systems and automation

- Build and maintain workflows connecting CRM, enrichment providers, campaign and content tools, internal data, and AI systems.
- Work hands-on with tools like HubSpot, Clay, Apify, n8n, Make, and PostHog — and be able to replace any of them with something better.
- Work directly with APIs, webhooks, scripts, and LLMs to build intelligent workflows.
- Design human-review and quality-control steps for AI-generated output, and evaluate that output rigorously rather than trusting it.
- Monitor automation failures, data-quality issues, and campaign errors before they become pipeline problems.
- Create reusable systems and documentation, and raise the execution standard across the growth organisation.

### Analytics and revenue accountability

- Connect campaign, content, social, and partner activity to meetings, opportunities, pipeline, and revenue.
- Own attribution and the CRM data quality it depends on. Build the tracking you need rather than waiting for someone to build it for you.
- Diagnose why campaigns are succeeding or failing.
- Monitor funnel conversion, account engagement, cost per opportunity, and pipeline contribution.
- Present clear recommendations to founders and senior stakeholders rather than simply reporting numbers.

## What we are looking for

- 4+ years in growth, GTM engineering, revenue automation, growth operations, or marketing operations. We weight what you have personally shipped far above titles, tenure, or company names.
- A track record of building and executing B2B SaaS growth campaigns for North American or global audiences.
- Working command of SQL and Python or JavaScript, plus real comfort with APIs and webhooks — reading the documentation, debugging the failing call, building the integration yourself.
- Strong practical understanding of LLMs, prompting, agentic workflows, and how to evaluate AI output instead of assuming it is right.
- A body of published writing you can point to, and the ability to write copy a senior buyer would actually finish reading.
- Evidence of building a distribution channel from zero: a newsletter, a community presence, a content engine, a partner program, a following.
- Credibility with senior people. You can run a call with a VP, a CRO, or a partner executive without a manager in the room.
- Strong analytical judgment, comfort working with incomplete information, and evidence of personally shipping rather than managing agencies.

## Strong indicators of fit

- You break vague growth problems into testable hypotheses.
- You can go from a spreadsheet or a customer insight to a working campaign within days.
- When a tool cannot do what you need, your instinct is to build it, not to file a request.
- You have opinions about where your buyers spend their attention, and you have tested them.
- You care more about qualified pipeline than impressions, opens, or activity volume.
- You enjoy early-stage environments where the role is not fully defined.

## How to apply

Send a Loom covering two things:

1. **A GTM system you personally built** — the problem, what you implemented, the tools and code involved, and the measurable outcome.
2. **A distribution channel you personally grew** — what you published or built, how you got it in front of the right people, and what it produced.

Show us the actual artefacts: the workflow, the posts, the partner page, the dashboard.

title: GTM Specialist / Sales Lead
description:
Location: Remote

Markets: India & North America

Type: Full-time

About Vaiu AI

Vaiu AI is building the orchestration layer for enterprise AI agents.

We help organisations move beyond AI experiments and deploy agentic systems that can actually operate inside their businesses — reasoning across workflows, connecting with existing tools and systems, automating conversations and tasks, retaining context, and continuously improving from real-world usage.

Our platform brings together the core building blocks required to run enterprise AI agents: intelligence, memory, tools and integrations, skills, monitoring, governance, and continuous learning.

The goal is simple: help companies become AI-native without having to spend months stitching together models, infrastructure, integrations, workflows, and observability themselves.

We already have the technology and product foundation in place. Now we want to build a repeatable sales engine around it.

That is where you come in.

**The Role**

We are looking for our first dedicated sales hire.

This is not a role where you inherit a large inbound pipeline, an established sales team, or a mature playbook.

You will build that playbook.

You will work directly with the founders to identify the right customers, figure out which problems resonate most strongly, build our outbound motion, start conversations, run discovery and demos, convert opportunities, and close new customers.

In the beginning, this will be a very hands-on role.

You might spend one morning refining an ICP, the afternoon reaching out to 30 target accounts, and the next day running discovery calls with enterprise leaders.

Over time, the goal is to turn what works into a repeatable sales process that can be scaled into a larger revenue organisation.

If you enjoy building sales motions from zero rather than simply operating an existing one, this role is for you.

**What You Will Own**

Define and continuously refine Vaiu's ICP across India and North America.
Identify industries, companies, use cases, and buyers where agentic AI can create meaningful business value.
Build target account lists and develop personalised outbound strategies for different buyer segments.
Own outbound prospecting across email, LinkedIn, referrals, partnerships, events, founder networks, communities, and other channels.
Experiment with messaging, positioning, offers, and outreach campaigns to understand what generates qualified conversations.
Own the complete sales cycle — prospecting, discovery, demos, solution discussions, proposals, negotiations, follow-ups, and closing.
Work with prospects to identify workflows that can be transformed through AI agents, conversational automation, and agentic orchestration.
Translate complex AI capabilities into simple business outcomes that CEOs, operations leaders, technology teams, and business owners can understand.
Work closely with our founders, product team, and engineering team to design solutions around real customer problems.
Bring structured customer feedback into product and go-to-market decisions.
Set up and maintain our CRM, pipeline stages, reporting, sales collateral, outreach tooling, and sales operating rhythm.
Develop repeatable playbooks for prospecting, qualification, discovery, demos, proposals, follow-ups, and closing.
Build partnerships and referral channels that can create additional pipeline.
Eventually help us hire, onboard, and scale the sales team once we have found a repeatable motion.

**What Success Looks Like**


During your first few months, we expect you to develop a strong understanding of the product, identify our highest-potential customer segments, create our initial sales process, launch multiple outbound experiments, and build a qualified pipeline.

From there, success means turning that pipeline into customers.

You should be able to tell us:

Who should we sell to?
What problem should we lead with?
Who inside the organisation should we approach?
What message gets them interested?
What sales process helps us close them?
And how do we repeat that process at scale?

Your ultimate objective is straightforward: help Vaiu acquire more customers and build a predictable revenue engine.

**Who We Are Looking For**

We would love to speak with you if you have:

1+ years of experience in B2B SaaS, enterprise technology, AI, enterprise sales, or an equivalent high-growth environment.
Experience owning a full sales cycle rather than only lead generation or account management.
A strong outbound mindset. You are comfortable creating opportunities rather than waiting for inbound leads.
Experience selling to mid-market or enterprise customers.
Evidence that you can take prospects from a cold introduction to a commercial conversation and eventually a signed deal.
Experience working in an early-stage startup or building a sales/GTM motion from scratch.
Strong discovery skills and the ability to uncover the real business problem behind what a prospect initially asks for.
The ability to understand technical products and explain them simply to non-technical decision-makers.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
The ability to sell consultatively. Agentic AI projects often start with a business problem rather than a predefined software requirement.
Comfort working directly with founders and operating with high autonomy.
A bias toward execution. You would rather launch an outreach experiment this week and learn from it than spend a month creating the perfect sales strategy deck.
Strong Plus

Experience selling any of the following would be particularly valuable:

Enterprise AI or Generative AI
AI agents or agentic workflows
Voice AI or conversational AI
Workflow automation
Enterprise SaaS
AI transformation or digital transformation services
Healthcare, financial services, government, utilities, or other regulated industries
Solutions involving integrations, APIs, CRMs, contact centres, or enterprise workflows
Products or services sold to customers in both India and the US


**This Role May Not Be For You If**

You are looking to manage an established sales team from day one.

You prefer working only with warm inbound leads.

You have primarily worked on sales strategy but have not personally prospected, run demos, negotiated, and closed customers.

Or you need a mature sales process before you can start selling.

We need a builder and a seller.

Someone willing to get their hands dirty, learn quickly, talk to customers every day, test different approaches, close the first wave of customers, and then build the system that allows us to do it repeatedly.

**Why Join Vaiu AI**

Build the revenue function from zero.
You will have the opportunity to shape how Vaiu sells, who we sell to, and how the company grows.

Work directly with the founders.
You will have direct access to the people building the product and making company-level decisions.

Sell into one of the biggest technology shifts happening today.
Companies are actively trying to understand how AI agents can move from experiments to real operational workflows. That is exactly the problem we are working on.

Influence the product.
Because you will be close to customers, your insights will directly influence our product roadmap, positioning, and priorities.

High ownership.
There are very few layers between identifying an opportunity and acting on it.

Meaningful upside.
Competitive compensation with equity aligned to the impact you create.

If you have built pipeline from nothing, enjoy enterprise conversations, understand how to sell emerging technology, and want the opportunity to build the sales engine of an AI company from the ground up, we would like to hear from you.

title: Founding Lead Product Designer
description:
Healf is Europe's fastest-growing company.

Number one on the FT1000, number one on the Sifted 100. From £1m to over £100m in under three years, with a small, talent-dense team and an electric culture with day one founder intensity. Now we're aiming for £1bn in the next three.

We curate the world's best wellbeing brands across The Four Pillars™: EAT, MOVE, MIND, SLEEP. That's the first chapter.

The next chapter is harder and more interesting.

We are moving from one market to many, from e-commerce to a technology platform, and from curating wellbeing to defining it. We are a health company, so we think we should act like one.

At its fullest expression, Healf redefines what wellbeing means for tens of millions of people.

**Why this role is Healf**
Healf is building Wellbeing Intelligence. A product that learns what works, for whom, and why — from the behavioural data of over half a million customers. It will personalise wellbeing decisions, close the feedback loop between what people do and how they feel, and get smarter with every interaction.

The most important question right now is not how to build it. It is “what should it be?” How does it earn trust with something as personal as your health? How does it tell you something true about your own body without creating anxiety? How does it feel like a companion rather than a dashboard?

Those are design questions. The best answers will not come from competitive audits or component libraries. They will come from someone who understands people at the level of motivation and emotion, who can turn a fuzzy problem into a sharp product decision, and who can hold a vision together across months of building without losing the thread.

This is the role that answers those questions.

**What you'll own**
The product, from first principles. You will define what Wellbeing Intelligence looks and feels like as a lived experience. The mobile app. The core surfaces. The information architecture. The emotional register. Not by inheriting a brief, but by thinking from the user’s life inward. What does it feel like to be someone who wants to be well and doesn’t know where to start? Start there. Research it. Frame it. Design it. Defend it.

The design system, from scratch. Components, patterns, standards. You will build the foundation that every designer and engineer after you builds on. Decisions made in the first six months will hold at ten times the scale. Overbuild for a future that hasn’t arrived yet and you slow the company down. Underbuild and you create chaos. Get it right.

The language and culture of design at Healf. How does Healf feel as a digital experience? Clinical or warm? Minimal or rich? Expert or approachable? You will define the product language and defend it. You are building the design function. Every decision you make — the tools, the rituals, the relationship with engineering, how research happens, how feedback flows — becomes precedent. You are not joining a design culture. You are creating one.

A clear, opinionated product direction. You will have a view on what we build next. You will bring it to the table with evidence and argue for it. If you’ve only ever executed other people’s roadmaps, this is not the role for you.

**What you'll deliver in the first 12 months**

A design language for Wellbeing Intelligence that is distinctive, coherent, and earns trust with users
A working design system that engineers build with and future designers will build on
User research that has actually changed what we built, not just validated what we had already decided
Users who describe the product experience in emotional terms, not functional ones
A clear, opinionated point of view on what the product should become next, backed by evidence from real usage
A design function that other people want to join

**Why you’re Healf**
You define problems, not just solutions. When handed a brief, your first instinct is to question whether it’s the right brief. You have strong opinions about what the user actually needs and the conviction to say so before a pixel is drawn.

You have been the first. Maybe the first hire. Maybe a founder. Maybe the person at an early-stage company whose design decisions determined whether the product survived. You know what it feels like when there is no design system, no established patterns, no one to validate your decisions. You prefer it that way.

You think in systems but you obsess over moments. The system creates consistency. The moments create feeling. An empty state that turns confusion into curiosity. An onboarding flow that makes someone feel understood before they’ve said a word. A notification that lands at the right moment and feels helpful rather than intrusive. These are not afterthoughts. They are the product.

You have cross-functional depth. You have stayed through build. You have caught production drift. You have pushed back when the implementation missed the intent, and you have been in the room when engineering had to make a hard call. You understand the constraints without hiding behind them.

You have strong opinions and you defend them without being precious. You push back on engineering when implementation drifts. You push back on product when the brief is wrong. You push back on yourself when the first version isn’t good enough.

You are ambitious. Not about titles. About the work. You want to look back at this chapter and know that what you built changed how people think about their health.

**Show us**
A product you led end-to-end where you can show the thinking, not just the screens. The problem framing, the decisions, the tradeoffs, the result, and what you would do differently.

Evidence you have worked at the zero-to-one stage: no design system, no established patterns, everything to define. What did you build and what did you decide?

A moment where your design changed what the company built, not just how it looked. Where you named a problem no one else had named and drove the solution.

Something that shows how you work with engineers. Not just hand-off artefacts. Evidence of real collaboration: the back-and-forth, the decisions made in implementation, the things that only became clear in code.

A point of view on what great health product design looks like and where most of it falls short. We want to see taste and opinion, not just craft.

**The Deal**
We ask a great deal of the people who work here. We expect full ownership and a genuine commitment to give this chapter everything you have.

In return, we will give you the same: everything we have, invested in your growth, your wellbeing, and the defining skills of the next decade.

We have built the fastest-growing company in Europe with a team small enough that every person in it shapes the outcome. That is still true today. The next person we hire will change the trajectory of the company.

title: Senior Analyst
description:
**About StudentCrowd**
StudentCrowd is where higher education and student accommodation decisions get made. More than 14 million students have used us to choose where to study and live, and we power the investors, developers, operators, universities and property advisers shaping the sector, with 4.3 billion+ real-time data points spanning pricing, availability, incentives, planning activity and verified student sentiment across the UK, Ireland and seven European markets, with the rest of Europe and the US next.
Behind all of that is a small team of people who genuinely care: about students making one of the biggest decisions of their lives, about the sector we serve, and about each other. We are over 70 people located remotely, and we've built a place we actually like coming to work.
We run on a freedom and responsibility framework: manage your own time, work flexibly, and own your work. No micromanagement, just clear expectations, mutual respect, and room to do great work that matters.

**About the team**
The Central Intelligence Team is the intelligence function of the business. We find, build, organise and synthesise the evidence that StudentCrowd relies on to make decisions, from proving hypotheses from our data, to understanding what the market needs and why, to turning what we know into content and narratives that drive commercial growth.
The intelligence function is anchored in two repositories: internal data knowledge and market knowledge. The rest of the business draws on this intelligence daily. The analyst function acts as the interface between the internal data repository and everyone else: answering questions, building dashboards and self-serve tools, and increasingly owning the systems and automation that enable people to find what they need themselves.

**About the role**
StudentCrowd has an established analysis and intelligence function which has supported decision-making across the business for a number of years. The focus of this role is the continued development of that function, with particular emphasis on process improvement, automation, and the application of AI to reporting and analysis.
This is a senior, hands-on position. The successful candidate will take day-to-day ownership of the internal data reporting layer and lead the transition towards more automated and self-serve ways of working, supporting the business as it expands into further European markets and the United States.
The role reports to the Director of Analysis and Market Intelligence, who retains overall responsibility for the function and its direction. The successful candidate will be accountable for delivery.

**What you'll do**
* Lead the ongoing development of reporting and analysis processes and the querying of our internal data repository, with a focus on automation, self-service and the reduction of manual effort
* Provide quality assurance over automated and AI-assisted outputs, catching what the system misses before it reaches a stakeholder
* Take day-to-day ownership of internal dashboards and reporting, maintaining and improving existing standards
*  Write and review the SQL underpinning analysis, and structure source data to support reliable reporting
*  Work as a partner to teams across the business, contributing to the definition of requirements rather than responding to requests alone
*  Present findings and recommendations to senior stakeholders, linking analysis to commercial outcomes
*  Establish and maintain templates, data models and documented processes to support consistent delivery as the business scales into new markets
*  Where requested, source, clean, normalise and structure data so it's ready for analysis, dashboarding or narrative-building
*  Spot and report data quality issues in our internal data (missing values, duplicates, formatting anomalies) before they reach a stakeholder

You’ll have significant autonomy and independence in a role that includes stable, ongoing, full-time work.

* Selected applicants will be offered a one day paid trial.
* Successful participants will attend a video interview.
* Chosen candidates will be given paid training on our content and SEO processes and complete a full week’s trial in the role, before being offered an ongoing position.

title: Group Chief Technology Officer
description:
**Group Chief Technology Officer
Ideawise · Remote-first, Europe (CET)**

Own the technology of every company we build — including the ones that don't exist yet.

**About Ideawise**
Most companies build a product. We build companies.
Ideawise is a venture builder: we fund, build and govern ventures from one shared machine — the operating system, service layer and AI platform every new company inherits on day one instead of spending its first year rebuilding. We hold equity in what we build, and the machine already pays for itself: an eight-figure-revenue, profitable portfolio, years in production. ~150 people. Hubs in Berlin, Barcelona and Shanghai.
You would not work on any one of our companies. You would work on the machine that builds them.
And one claim worth testing before you read further, because everyone makes it and almost nobody can show it: our own leadership function runs on an AI-native operating layer in production — planning, delivery tracking and decisions run through agents, today. That layer is now being spun out as its own company. You would inherit the proof, not build the case for it.


**The role**
We are hiring our first Group CTO. Nobody has held this seat, and it was built to be held once.
A company built inside Ideawise is technical from the morning it exists. It doesn't choose a stack, stand up infrastructure, or spend a year earning its way to production — it inherits all of that on day one: a spine already running, already proven, with real revenue flowing across it. That spine is what you forge — the machine that turns an idea into a shipping company in months, then does it again, faster.
That is the next phase of this company: a factory. And a factory needs a single technical authority at group level — one seat that owns the platform every venture inherits, the architecture and standards they build on, and the technical organisation behind all of it.
The seat carries technical authority above every C-level technical leader in the group and its ventures. You report to the COO. Technical calls stop with you.
And it grows in the direction that matters. As the portfolio scales, each venture gets its own CTO — and you hire them, set their bar, and lead them. You are not inheriting the technical leadership layer of a venture portfolio. You are the one who gets to build it.
This is a technology mandate, not a product one. The venture teams build the products. Your surface is the spine — and, increasingly, the people running technology on top of it.


**What you'll own**
The shared platform — infrastructure, data, agentic tooling and guardrails: the thing a new venture inherits on day one instead of choosing its own stack, and the reason our fifth company launches faster than our third.
The technical organisation, and then its leaders — you design the org on purpose: named leads, a written hiring bar, the authority to shape it. Then the venture CTOs: your hires, your bar, your bench.
Architecture, standards and build-vs-buy across every venture and service — including where LLM and agentic features get bought, built, or refused.
The decisions. Architecture, technical standards, build-vs-buy, the platform roadmap, and who joins the technical org. You are constrained by group capital allocation and by the regulatory limits below — which are real and not negotiable. The COO backs you.


**What's true eighteen months in**

Production AI depth, not proximity to it — LLM or agentic systems in front of real users, real build-vs-buy calls, inference cost managed at scale, and at least one model-safety incident you owned.
