title: Technical Product Manager
description:
Function: Product Management
Reports To: Head of Product 
Experience: Total 5 years experience (2-3 years in Product + 2 years prior Software Engineering)
Domain: SaaS / B2B  •  Clinical Health-Tech a strong plus
Start: Immediate to 30 days

THE ROLE  
We need a Technical PM who has been in the trenches as a software engineer and knows what it really takes to ship production software. You will own end-to-end product delivery across one or more core product areas — from discovery and roadmap through to launch and iteration. You will work daily with engineering, design, data science, and clinical stakeholders to build a product that is loved by users and respected by regulators.

WHAT YOU WILL DO  
**Product Roadmap**
Own the product roadmap end-to-end — define the Epics, sequence features by impact vs. effort, and communicate trade-offs clearly to engineering, design, and business stakeholders.
Translate business goals and user problems into a prioritised backlog; use frameworks like RICE, opportunity scoring, or jobs-to-be-done to make sequencing decisions defensible, not just intuitive.
Drive quarterly planning cycles — align product bets with revenue goals, capacity constraints, and platform health; flag conflicts early.
**Technical Execution & Engineering Partnership**
Write technically precise PRDs that include API contracts, data models, state machines, edge cases, and explicit error-handling expectations — not just user stories.
Participate actively in architecture and system design discussions; understand and articulate trade-offs between monolith vs. microservices, sync vs. async patterns, and build vs. buy decisions.
Review technical specs and ERDs for completeness; spot scope creep, hidden dependencies, and under-specified integrations before sprint kick-off.
Own the technical debt roadmap alongside engineering — balance new feature velocity with platform health, scalability, and security hygiene.
Understand SaaS infrastructure fundamentals: multi-tenancy, role-based access control (RBAC), SSO/SAML, rate limiting, webhooks, and API versioning. Able to make product decisions that affect these layers intelligently.
Run sprint ceremonies (planning, grooming, retros) and maintain the engineering team's flow — unblock dependencies, resolve ambiguity, and shield the team from context-switching.
**Data, Metrics & Analytics**
Define success metrics for every feature before it ships — activation rates, feature adoption, time-to-value, retention impact. Run post-launch reviews against these benchmarks without being asked.
Instrument product analytics from the requirements phase — specify event schemas, funnel definitions, and cohort logic for the data/engineering team.
**Integrations, Platform & Ecosystem**
Own the product's integration strategy — third-party APIs, webhooks, SDK/embed scenarios
Collaborate with the security and compliance team on features that touch PHI/PII — define data residency requirements, consent flows, audit logging, and access control at the product spec level.
**Go-to-Market & Stakeholder Management**
Partner with sales and customer success on feature positioning, release notes, and customer-facing documentation; translate engineering outputs into clear business value.
Manage stakeholder expectations across product, engineering, sales, and clinical SMEs — escalate risks early, communicate scope changes in writing, and keep every stakeholder in the right information loop.
Contribute to pricing and packaging decisions for new features — understand SaaS monetisation levers (seat-based, usage-based, module tiers) and their product implications.

MUST-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS  

**Experience**
At least 5 years of experience with 
2-3 years of product management experience on a B2B SaaS product, owning roadmap and delivery end-to-end with full accountability for outcomes.
2 years of prior software engineering experience in a production environment (any stack — backend, frontend, or full-stack). You have shipped code, managed deployments, and debugged production incidents.
Demonstrated track record of launching SaaS features that drove measurable improvement in activation, retention, or revenue — with numbers to back it up.

**Technical Skills**
Comfortable reviewing REST API specs (OpenAPI/Swagger), understanding authentication patterns (OAuth 2.0, JWT, API keys), and writing acceptance criteria that include API behaviour.
Able to read a system architecture diagram, understand data flow between services, and ask the right questions about scalability, latency, and failure modes.
Working knowledge of SaaS infrastructure concepts: multi-tenancy, RBAC, SSO/SAML, CI/CD pipelines, feature flags, and deployment environments (staging vs. production).
Hands-on with product analytics tools — Mixpanel, Amplitude, Heap, or equivalent — including defining event taxonomies, not just reading dashboards.
**Product Skills**
Writes PRDs that include functional specs, non-functional requirements, data requirements, and explicit out-of-scope boundaries — no ambiguity handed off to engineering.
Practised in agile delivery: sprint planning, backlog grooming, sprint reviews, and retrospectives. Comfortable in Jira, Linear, or equivalent; knows how to write a ticket that doesn't require a meeting to explain.
Experience defining and tracking OKRs or product KPIs at the feature and product-area level; can connect daily work to business outcomes.
Can conduct user interviews, synthesise qualitative feedback, and convert it into prioritised problem statements — not just a feature wish list.
**Soft Skills & Mindset**
Excellent written communication — can distil a complex technical problem into a one-page brief that a non-technical exec can act on and an engineer can build from.
Strong cross-functional influencer — comfortable pushing back on engineering scope creep, design gold-plating, and sales feature requests with data and user evidence, not authority.
High ownership mindset — you treat the product like it is yours, escalate blockers fast, and don't wait to be told what to do next.

NICE-TO-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS  

Experience in health-tech, clinical AI, or regulated software environments (SaMD, HIPAA, HL7/FHIR).
Familiarity with AI/ML product development — understanding of model evaluation, data pipelines, or MLOps workflows.
Prior exposure to B2B enterprise sales cycles and hospital/clinic procurement dynamics.
Background in neuroscience, clinical psychology, or adjacent fields.
Experience with design tools (Figma) and ability to contribute to wireframe-level discussions.

BrainsightAI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive team.

title: GTM- Engineer
description:
We are an innovative technology company providing a cutting-edge, AI-powered cloud platform for the construction industry. Created by industry experts with deep estimating experience, our software dramatically streamlines the pre-construction process. Our solution uses advanced machine learning to automate traditionally time-consuming takeoff tasks, helping estimators work up to 80% faster while reducing costly errors.

Our collaborative platform enables real-time teamwork, instant drawing analysis, and features a revolutionary conversational AI interface that transforms how professionals interact with construction plans. Founded by construction industry veterans, our award-winning application automates the takeoff process, enabling estimators to analyze blueprints in seconds rather than hours or days.

# **The job in one line**

You own the systems that turn raw signal into pipeline. Prediction models, campaign infrastructure, the AI that generates personalized outreach at scale. You inherit live systems carrying real revenue, and what you build is how we sell.

# **What you'll own**

- **Predict the account before anyone touches it.** Models for estimator count, seats, and expected ARR, each with confidence bands so reps know when to trust the number. Conversion scoring on top, and you own it through retraining as the data and the market shift.
- **Run the campaigns that carry real pipeline.** Multiple segments, multiple channels: email, LinkedIn, voicemail. Every campaign is code you own. Routing, retries, dedup, deliverability. You're on the hook for uptime and output quality, not just the initial build.
- **Generate the personalization.** Per-rep landing pages and AI avatar video, tracked end to end so a booked demo attributes to a specific asset.
- **Ground the AI in real calls.** Call intelligence as a knowledge endpoint feeding prep docs, follow-up emails, avatar scripts, and page copy, so outbound cites objections we've genuinely heard, not generic messaging.
- **Turn signals into tasks.** Job changes, promotions, news, clicks. Scored and routed into prioritized rep actions, not another ignored notification.

# **What you'll bring**

- 5+ years in growth engineering, RevOps, or a technical marketing or sales ops role you can tie directly to pipeline or revenue moved.
- Strong fluency in a programming language. You write, debug, and validate production code, not just generate it.
- Applied ML experience. You've built, trained, and maintained a model in production, and you can tell a non-technical stakeholder exactly how much to trust it.
- Deep comfort with REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, and rate limits, plus real patience for the debugging that follows when vendor APIs fail in undocumented ways.
- Strong SQL and enough data sense to know when a model is telling you something real, and to say so out loud when it isn't.
- Hands-on with a modern GTM stack: HubSpot or Salesforce, plus tools like Clay, Apollo, Instantly, n8n.
- Practical LLM experience. Prompting, function calling, evaluating output, knowing when a model is the wrong tool.
- A working v1 this week beats a perfect spec next month, and the judgment to know which one a given problem actually needs.

# **Bonus**

Construction or AEC background. ML research background. Frontend or backend depth. Experience scaling a GTM engineering function as the team around it grows.

# **More about the role**

You're inheriting a function that already exists and already carries real pipeline. There's no greenfield here. The job is judgment under live conditions: knowing what to fix first, what to leave alone, and when a quick v1 beats a perfect spec.

The stack is wide, and you'll move between retraining a model and fixing a broken webhook in the same week. Vendor APIs fail in undocumented ways. Labels are imperfect and attribution is never fully clean, and you have to be comfortable deciding on noisy data while saying out loud how noisy it is.

title: Part-Time Social Media Lead & On-Camera Content Creator - Health App
description:
**About Bearable**

We have two positive impact apps.

Foxtale is a guided journaling app with a fox companion — one you name yourself. You journal, and your fox collects your emotions as glowing orbs to restore a forgotten world. Along the way you pick up the emotional skills most of us were never taught.

We're a small, fully remote, bootstrapped UK team. We also build Bearable, a symptom-tracking app used by hundreds of thousands of people managing chronic conditions. Foxtale launched recently, people love it (our reviews are close to perfect), and now we need more people to find out it exists.

**The role**

We want one person to own Foxtale and Bearable's TikTok and Instagram presence: making the videos, appearing in them, and living in the comments.

This isn't an ads job. We already run paid creative separately. This is about building a real audience around the fox and the world of Foxtale and Bearable — the kind of account people follow because they like it, not because they were targeted.

You'd be starting close to scratch, which is the fun part.

**What you'd do**

- Make and post short-form video daily-ish — ideation, filming, editing, publishing. We're after volume and consistency over polish.
- Run both accounts. Most video will work on TikTok and Reels with light reworking, but Instagram isn't a dumping ground for TikTok exports — Stories, carousels and how we show up in Reels comments all need their own thought.
- Appear on camera. Not always, but often — though not everything needs a face. Some of our best content will be the fox and the world itself, so you'll be making animated and motion posts too.
- Make things look good without a designer. You'll have our illustrations, app footage, palette and fonts to work from. We're not expecting studio animation — we're expecting someone who can put together a lovely-looking motion post on their own using CapCut, After Effects, Canva, AI video/image tools, or whatever gets there fastest.
- Comment as Foxtale and Bearable on other people's videos. Brands that are genuinely funny and warm in the comments of viral posts get more reach than most of their own content does. This is a real part of the job, not an afterthought.
- Reply to comments and DMs on both accounts, and make people feel like there's a person there.
- Watch what's working in cosy games, virtual pets, journaling and mental health corners of TikTok, and adapt fast.
- Feed back to us: what people ask for, what confuses them, what they love. You'll be closer to our users than anyone.

**What we're looking for**

- You're comfortable and expressive on camera.
- You already make short-form video, and you can show us things you've posted.
- You have an instinct for TikTok and Reels — you know when a trend is worth using and when it'd be embarrassing, and how the two platforms differ.
- You can work unsupervised and hit a posting rhythm without someone chasing you.
- You care about mental health, and can talk about it without being preachy or clinical.
- You have a good eye. You don't need to be a designer, but you should be able to work inside a brand's look and make something that feels considered rather than thrown together.
- You're fluent with AI tools for video, image and motion, and sensible about where they help and where they'd cheapen the brand.
- Bonus: you're already into cosy games, virtual pets, journaling, or you use apps like Finch and How We Feel.

You don't need marketing experience, a degree, or to know what ASO means. We'd rather have someone who understands the platform in their bones.

**Practical stuff**

- 10–15 hours a week to start, flexible when you do them.
- Fully remote. UK or US time zones work best, but we're open.
- Paid monthly, at a rate that reflects experience.
- 3-month initial contract, with a view to extending and growing the role if it works. You can keep other clients or jobs.
- You'd work directly with the founder and our marketing lead. Small team, no layers.

title: Product Manager (Growth & UX), part-time, remote
description:
## About MyArchitectAI

MyArchitectAI is an AI rendering platform used by architects, interior designers, and visualization professionals in over 150 countries. We turn CAD designs, sketches, and line drawings into photorealistic renders in seconds, with no installs, no hardware requirements, and no learning curve.

We're a team of 5, fully remote, spread across Europe.

## Why we're hiring

Our product works. Our retention and engagement has a lot of room for improvement. Too many people sign up, render a few images, and never come back, or cancel when their current project ends. We have the data (PostHog, Stripe, cancel surveys, live chat) and we have the engineers. What we don't have is one person whose job is to find the leaks and fix them.

That's you.

## What you'll own

**Activation and engagement**
Dig into user behavior in PostHog and Supabase. Figure out where people get stuck between signup and their first "wow" render, and why paying users stop rendering. Turn that into a prioritized list of experiments, run them, and report what moved.

**UX improvements**
Take existing flows and make them simpler and nicer to look at. Our users judge us on how good the app looks, because that's their job. You'll design in Claude Design on top of our existing design system (and improve it), so you do need taste and the ability to tell good from almost good.

**New features from scratch**
From problem to shipped. Talk to users, define the feature, design it, write a spec, QA it on staging, ship it, measure it.

## Who this is for

- You've been a PM, growth PM, or product designer at a SaaS company, ideally one selling to non-technical users. B2B or prosumer both fine.
- You're comfortable doing your own analysis. Funnels, cohorts, SQL, experiment design, knowing when a result is noise.
- You have visual taste and opinions about UI. You can look at a screen and clearly explain why it feels off.
- You write clearly. Most of your output will be specs, hypotheses, and short reports, and other people have to act on them.
- You're self-directed. Nobody will assign you tickets. You'll find the problems yourself.

## Who this is not for

- People who need a designer, an analyst, and an engineer to get anything done.
- People who want to write strategy docs or call all-hands. We need someone who ships fast.

## The deal

- Around 20 hours a week to start. Can grow to full-time if it works for both sides.
- We start with a paid, scoped project so we both see how it goes. If it's good, we move to a monthly retainer.
- You invoice us as a contractor. Location doesn't matter.

## How we work

- Fully remote and mostly async.
- Specs go into Linear. Design happens in Claude Design. Analysis happens in PostHog and SQL.
- We use AI tools heavily and expect you to as well. If you're skeptical of AI-assisted design and coding, this isn't the right place.
- Short feedback loops. You'll get a yes or no within hours, not a week.
- You'll talk to real users. Support is handled by the founders, and you'll have access to every conversation.

## How to apply

Skip the cover letter. Send us:

1. One thing you shipped that moved a metric, and what it moved.
2. Why you're a good fit.
3. Your rate assuming 20hrs/week.

Keep it short. We read everything.

title: Research Analyst / Sociological Researcher
description:
Social Research Center is looking for a Research Analyst / Sociological Researcher to join our international research and communications team focused on Global Conflicts and Post-Conflict Transformations.

The Center's primary focus is on conflict dynamics and on the role of new actors in both conflict and post-conflict settings. Special emphasis is placed on how these actors are perceived by states, expert communities, and the media.

The research team will cover the full lifecycle of conflicts: from the accumulation of tensions and escalation, through to the cessation of hostilities (or their future prospects), peaceful resolution, and post-conflict reconstruction. War is examined as a factor that shapes state institutions, economies, social structures, public opinion, and historical memory. In the regional context, this includes research on mercenarism, paramilitarism, insurgent and criminal network movements, and their associated branding.

The Center's methodology combines comparative analysis of contemporary conflicts, expert interviews and sociological surveys, the study of official documents and diplomatic positions, media and social media analysis, conflict narrative research, scenario forecasting, and political risk assessment.

About the Role

We are seeking a proactive and analytically strong Research Analyst / Sociological Researcher who will be responsible for conducting expert-based research on topics related to the conflict situations, public perceptions, socio-economic developments, and other areas relevant to the Center's research agenda.

This is not a purely academic research position. We are looking for someone who can manage the full research cycle: identify relevant experts and respondents, conduct expert interviews and surveys, analyze qualitative and quantitative information, and translate research findings into clear, compelling insights.

The Researcher will work as part of a small project team alongside a Project Manager and a PR / Media Relations Specialist. The Project Manager coordinates the overall research and communications process, while the PR Specialist uses research findings to develop media materials and secure coverage in relevant media outlets across target countries.

A key part of the role is therefore the ability to produce research that is both methodologically sound and relevant to current public, expert, and media discussions.

Key Responsibilities

Design and conduct expert interviews, surveys, and other qualitative and quantitative research.
Identify and recruit relevant experts, respondents, and stakeholders across target countries.
Build and maintain a database and network of experts, researchers, business representatives, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders.
Analyze interview materials, survey results, secondary data, academic publications, policy documents, and other relevant sources.
Produce research reports, analytical briefs, summaries, presentations, and concise research findings.
Ensure research projects are delivered on time and meet agreed methodological and quality standards.

**Why This Role**

title: AI Social Media & Growth Manager-Remote
location: Delhi; Pune; Mumbai; Noida; Bangalore City Municipal Corporation Layout; Gurugram
description:
**Job description:**

**How to Apply**

**Please don’t send us only a standard CV.**

Show us what you can do.

**Send us:**

* Examples of social accounts or content you have created or grown.
* The AI tools you currently use for content creation and automation.
* A short explanation of how you would build an AI-powered social media engine for Travmonde.
* Three B2C and three B2B content ideas you would publish during your first weeks.
* One example showing how you would turn a single idea into content for multiple channels.
* An example of an account you have grown, including the numbers and your contribution.

**About Travmonde**

Travmonde is building an intelligent travel platform connecting travelers and travel professionals with exceptional local tours, guides and destination services worldwide.

We have built significant global supply, industry relationships and technology — but our social media presence does not yet reflect the company we are building.

**We want to change that.**

We are looking for someone who can build an AI-powered content, social media and audience-growth engine, rather than simply manually creating and posting content.

**Our ambition is both B2B and B2C:**

* Build awareness, authority and demand among travel advisors, tour operators and other travel professionals.
* Build a consumer audience that discovers experiences through our content and ultimately books directly with Travmonde.

**The Role**

Your mission is to:

Turn Travmonde’s destinations, experiences, guides, industry knowledge and founder insights into an AI-powered media and audience engine — building both B2B and B2C demand and ultimately converting attention into bookings and revenue.

You will combine creativity and judgment with AI and automation to dramatically increase the speed, quality and volume of content production.

This is not a traditional social media manager role where most of your time is spent manually designing and scheduling posts.

**We expect you to think AI-first and growth-first.**

You should constantly ask:

How can AI do most of the repetitive work while I concentrate on ideas, storytelling, quality, experimentation and growth?

**What You Will Do**
1. Build our AI-powered content engine

Create a repeatable workflow:

Idea → Research → Content → Design/Video → Approval → Publishing → Distribution → Analysis → Improvement

Use AI and automation wherever appropriate.

The objective is to create a scalable content operation without building a large traditional social media team.

2. Create and repurpose content

Turn strong ideas, experiences and information into multiple formats, including:

LinkedIn posts
Instagram posts and carousels
Reels and short-form video
Stories
Founder content
Company content
Destination and experience content
B2C inspirational content
B2B industry content
For example, one great Travmonde experience could become an Instagram Reel, carousel, story, LinkedIn post and other pieces of content — without producing everything manually from scratch.

3. Develop Travmonde’s content pillars

Potential themes include:

Travel Inspiration & Experiences Remarkable tours, destinations, local guides, hidden places and experiences worth traveling for.

Bookable Experiences Content that doesn’t just inspire people but moves them toward discovering and booking Travmonde experiences.

Travel Industry Intelligence Useful insights for travel advisors, tour operators and other B2B travel professionals.

AI + Future of Travel How AI, agents and technology are changing travel discovery, distribution, operations and customer experience.

Building Travmonde Behind-the-scenes stories about building a global travel technology company.

Founder Perspective Turn founder ideas, observations, experiences and industry opinions into compelling social content.

4. Build both B2C and B2B audiences

We are interested in relevant audiences, not vanity metrics.

**B2C**

Build an audience of travelers interested in:

Unique local experiences
Private and guided tours
Authentic destination experiences
Things to do in destinations
Travel inspiration
The long-term funnel is:

Content → Inspiration → Travmonde → Experience → Direct Booking

**B2B**

Build an audience among:

Travel advisors
Tour operators
Cruise companies
Travel companies
Travel-tech professionals
Local guides and experience providers
Other relevant industry decision-makers
The funnel is:

Content → Authority & Trust → Travmonde → Lead/Registration → Booking

5. Use AI aggressively

You should already use — or be excited to master — tools such as:

ChatGPT
AI research tools
Canva AI
AI image and video tools
Content repurposing tools
Social scheduling and automation platforms
Social analytics tools
We don’t care which exact technology stack you prefer.

We care whether you can create a high-quality, scalable content operation with very little unnecessary manual work.

We also expect you to continuously experiment with new AI tools and workflows as the technology evolves.

6. Grow, experiment and learn

You will continuously test:

Content formats
Hooks
Topics
Destinations
Calls to action
Posting frequency
Channels
B2B versus B2C content
Organic growth strategies
AI-generated and human-created formats
You should understand why something performed — not simply report that it received 20,000 views.

7. Turn attention into business

Social media for Travmonde is not simply a branding exercise.

Ultimately, we want to understand:

Content → Audience → Traffic → Leads/Customers → Bookings → Revenue

You will work with us to identify which content and channels actually contribute to business growth.

What We Are Looking For

You don’t need 10 years of social media experience.

**You do need to be:**

Extremely comfortable with AI
Curious about emerging AI tools
A strong storyteller
Visually aware
Excellent at creating hooks and simplifying ideas
Able to understand what makes people stop, watch, click and share
Analytical about what works and what doesn’t
Comfortable experimenting quickly
Able to work independently
Commercially minded
Obsessed with growth and continuous improvement
Experience in travel is useful but not essential.

Experience building social accounts from zero — personally or professionally — is highly valuable.

**What We Don’t Want**

We are probably not the right company for you if your approach is:

“Give me a content calendar and I’ll manually make three Canva posts every week.”

We are looking for someone who thinks more like:

“Give me Travmonde’s raw material and I’ll build a system that turns it into high-quality content at scale, learns what audiences respond to, grows distribution and ultimately generates business.”

**Initial 90-Day Mission**

Your first objective will be to take Travmonde from an almost inactive social presence to a consistent, measurable and scalable content and growth operation.

**During the first 90 days, you will:**

* Establish our B2B and B2C social strategy
* Define our content pillars and positioning
* Build the AI-assisted production workflow
* Establish a consistent LinkedIn and Instagram presence
* Test short-form video and other relevant formats
* Build Travmonde’s company presence
* Develop the founder’s social presence alongside it
* Test B2C content designed to drive travelers toward Travmonde
* Test B2B content designed to attract travel professionals
* Identify which formats and subjects generate meaningful growth
* Establish reporting connecting social activity to traffic, leads and bookings
* Create a system capable of scaling without requiring a large content team

**Success Looks Like**

After 90 days, we should be able to say:

We know what content works, which audiences respond to it, how to produce it efficiently, and how social media can become a meaningful acquisition and distribution channel for Travmonde.

Longer term, the goal is bigger:

Build an audience Travmonde owns — and turn that audience into B2B and B2C demand, direct traffic and bookings.

Bonus: Choose a travel experience, destination or travel-industry trend and create one example Travmonde post or short-form video concept.

We care much more about your thinking, creativity, AI capabilities and demonstrated ability to grow an audience than your job title or formal qualifications.

title: Director of Support Engineering - Americas
description:
### **Hello!**

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring a Director of Support Engineering in AMER.

As Ashby grows, our customers’ workflows, integrations, and technical environments become more complex. Support Engineering is the bridge that helps frontline Support investigate those issues, helps Engineering focus on confirmed defects and roadmap work, and turns technical customer issues into improvements across the product and support experience.

We’re looking for a leader to shape that bridge at scale. You’ll lead through a Support Engineering Manager and their team, partner closely with Support, Product, and Engineering leadership, and define the systems and standards that help a growing organization resolve complex issues with clarity, speed, and sound judgment.

## **About the role**

Support Engineering investigates the issues that require deeper technical understanding than frontline Support can provide. The team uses customer context, application behavior, logs, databases, integrations, APIs, and code-level context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through configuration, data correction, documentation, enablement, or an in-app change—or whether it is a product defect that Engineering needs to fix. Your role is to make that path clear and scalable: establish shared expectations across teams, ensure escalations are well validated and actionable, and help the organization learn from recurring patterns rather than treating each issue as an isolated event.

You’ll lead the strategic evolution of the function through strong partnership with Support Engineering managers, frontline Support, Product, and Engineering. You’ll shape routing, triage, escalation, and feedback mechanisms; build reporting that makes technical friction visible; and guide investments in diagnostics, tooling, documentation, and enablement. You’ll also help leaders make better tradeoffs between immediate customer resolution and durable product or process improvements.

As Director, you’ll directly manage the Support Engineering Manager and hold them accountable for team performance, technical quality, people development, and progress against the function’s priorities. You’ll set the vision for how Support Engineering grows with Ashby’s product surface area and customer complexity, while building the leadership structure, career paths, and operating model needed to scale over time.

## **What you’ll own**

- Set the vision and operating model for Support Engineering, aligning the function’s priorities with Ashby’s broader Customer Success goals.
- Directly lead, coach, and develop the Support Engineering Manager through clear expectations, regular feedback, career support, and accountability for team health, technical quality, and customer outcomes.
- Build shared operating standards across frontline Support, Support Engineering, Product, and Engineering for triage, investigation, documentation, escalation quality, ownership, and handoffs, while clarifying how technical issues move from Support intake through investigation to Engineering or Product partnership.
- Partner with Engineering and Product leadership to synthesize recurring technical customer patterns, improve supportability and operability, and influence prioritization of product, platform, tooling, and process improvements.
- Establish the data and review mechanisms needed to understand escalation health, recurring friction, resolution speed, frontline self-sufficiency, customer effort, and the function’s influence on product priorities and supportability. Use these signals to guide improvements and develop the team over time.
- Evolve the organization’s structure, hiring plan, onboarding, career paths, and regional model as Support Engineering scales.
- Build trust across leadership by making tradeoffs visible, communicating technical and customer impact clearly, and helping teams move forward when ownership or priorities are ambiguous.

## **You should apply if**

- You have led a Support Engineering, Technical Support, Developer Support, Production Support, or similarly technical function in a B2B SaaS or complex software environment.
- You have led through managers or built a leadership layer, and know how to create clarity, accountability, and growth without becoming a bottleneck for decisions.
- You have enough technical depth to reason about APIs, integrations, logs, databases, application behavior, architecture, and debugging approaches—and to earn the trust of experienced engineers.
- You have shaped the boundary between frontline Support, Support Engineering, Product, and Engineering, including escalation criteria, triage practices, ownership, and feedback loops.
- You have used data and recurring patterns to drive improvements in supportability, product quality, tooling, process, or Engineering prioritization.
- You are energized by systems-level problems and can turn operational friction into a focused strategy, a useful first version, and measurable improvement.
- You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences, especially when explaining tradeoffs, uncertainty, customer impact, and recommended action to senior stakeholders. You communicate with concision and can compress a complex tradeoff into a few clear sentences for senior stakeholders.
- You are a hands-on, customer-centric leader who can move between strategy, organizational design, technical details, and the day-to-day realities of supporting customers.
- You think about scalable support systems through automation, self-serve, and AI-enhanced tooling applied with good judgment.

## **You should not apply if**

- You’re looking primarily for a people-management or queue-oversight role and do not want to shape technical workflows, escalation quality, or cross-functional operating models.
- Most of your experience is in internal IT, infrastructure, cloud operations, or systems administration without substantial experience with customer-impacting SaaS applications, technical support, or product supportability.

description:

title: Security Research Engineer - (Member of Security Staff)
description:
**Team:** Security / Detection & Intelligence 
**Location:** Remote (Pakistan) - Gulf/USA timezone overlap required
**Level:** Early-career / Associate (0–2 years)

**About Himaya**

Himaya is an AI-native email and SaaS security platform built for organizations in the Gulf region. We protect enterprises against phishing, BEC, malware, and data loss across email, SaaS applications, and cloud data stores -combining threat intelligence, LLM-based classification, sandbox detonation, and data security posture management (DSPM) in one platform.

**The Role
**

We're hiring an early-career Security Research Engineer to help build the detection brain of Himaya. You'll work on intelligence and detection logic across three pillars -SaaS security, email threat analysis, and DLP  -turning real-world attacker behavior into detections that ship to production. You'll also assist with our SOC 2 certification effort and ongoing audit upkeep. High ownership, direct mentorship, and your research becomes product.

**What You'll Do**


* Build and tune detection logic for email threats — phishing, BEC, credential harvesting, malware, lookalike domains, and impersonation.
* Develop SaaS security detections — OAuth app risk, posture/misconfiguration drift, anomalous admin actions, risky-user signals (M365/Google).
* Improve DLP detections — sensitive-data classification, exfiltration patterns, and policy logic that balances recall with low noise.
* Curate and operationalize threat intelligence — feeds, IOC packs, domain/IP reputation, and enrichment for the detection pipeline.
* Analyze real samples and sandbox output to close detection gaps and reduce false positives.
* Assist with SOC 2 readiness — control-evidence collection, remediation tracking, and security documentation.

**What We're Looking For**


* 0–2 years in security, detection engineering, threat research, or a related area — internships, CTFs, and self-taught projects count.
* Understanding of email security fundamentals (SPF/DKIM/DMARC, header analysis, phishing/BEC tradecraft).
* Some exposure to SaaS/cloud security and/or DLP concepts.
* Comfortable writing Python and working with data.
* Analytical, evidence-driven mindset; clear written communication.

**Nice to Have**

* Exposure to SOC 2 / ISO 27001, YARA, malware triage, or sandboxing.
* Familiarity with LLM-based classification.
* Arabic and Gulf-region threat-landscape awareness.

**Compensation & Equity
**

Salary: $200/month (≈ PKR 56,000/month).
Equity: 0.5%, vesting over 4 years.

**Why Himaya**

1. Ground-floor security hire -your research ships to production and protects real organizations.
2. Wide surface area across email, SaaS, DLP, and DSPM, with real ownership.

title: Founding CTO / Technical Co-Founder

description:
**WeDecide  ·  Early-stage / Pre-seed  ·  Part-time to full-time  ·  Remote**

We are building the infrastructure for responsive governance.

WeDecide quantifies neighbourhood health. Residents track local conditions and the impact of policies on their household. WeDecide translates that engagement into a structured feedback loop for governments. 

**The role**
We are looking for a technical co-founder. This person will own the technical architecture and delivery of a data-intensive civic application currently in MVP development, and will share responsibility for company strategy, fundraising, and partnership development alongside the founder.

The seat carries genuine technical authority and genuine commercial weight. You will make foundational architectural decisions, ship the platform from MVP to first public release, and represent the technology to investors, government partners, and prospective hires. This is a role for someone who wants to shape both the product and the company.

**What you will own — technical**
●        Define and own the technical architecture across the web application, backend, data pipelines, and internal systems.
●        Lead MVP delivery on the current stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL / Supabase, with a modular API layer.
●        Build a modular data integration layer connecting a large number of external public data sources across multiple jurisdictions.
●        Design the platform so core product modules operate as interoperable services rather than a tightly coupled prototype.
●        Establish engineering standards for reliability, observability, testing, deployment, and documentation from the outset.
●        Own security architecture: encrypted data handling, anti-bot and abuse resistance, identity-related controls, and privacy-by-design.
●        Prepare the platform for penetration testing, security review, and pilot readiness before any public deployment.
●        Build for compliance requirements including GDPR, anonymisation, accessibility, and multi-market deployment constraints.
●        Recruit and lead early engineering hires as the team expands.
What you will own — co-founder scope
●        Partner with the founder on company strategy, product direction, and prioritisation under real constraints.
●        Represent the technology to investors: contribute to the fundraising narrative, lead technical due diligence, and help close the round.
●        Support partnership development with government, institutional, and delivery partners, including technical scoping of pilots.
●        Bring your professional network to bear on hiring, fundraising, and business development.
●        Set the engineering culture and the standards the company becomes known for.

**Technical environment
Current stack**
Next.js, React, TypeScript  ·  PostgreSQL / Supabase  ·  Inngest for scheduled data refresh, scoring, and background workflows  ·  Mistral Voxtral for voice and audio processing of qualitative civic input  ·  progressive web app delivered through Serwist service workers with Web Push (VAPID).
The platform is architected for multi-jurisdiction data integration and a secure government-facing interface. The path beyond the progressive web app — including any move to native mobile — is a decision this role will own.

 
**Technical challenges**
●        Building a scalable integration layer across roughly 75 government and public data sources over time.
●        Designing a system that supports daily data refresh, scoring logic, and synchronisation across devices.
●        Handling anonymised qualitative and quantitative inputs in a way that preserves privacy while producing meaningful aggregate insight.
●        Establishing trust controls in a politically sensitive environment: tamper-evident data provenance, authenticated messaging, bot resistance, and security hardening.
●        Meeting accessibility requirements such as WCAG 2.2 AA alongside broader multi-market usability expectations.
What we are looking for
●        Significant experience building and shipping software products, ideally 8+ years, with strong hands-on technical depth.
●        Strong backend and systems architecture skills: APIs, external integrations, data models, and service design.
●        Experience with modern JavaScript / TypeScript stacks; direct experience with Next.js, React, and PostgreSQL strongly preferred.
●        Deep understanding of cloud infrastructure, security, and technical delivery across complex projects.
●        Experience designing for privacy, compliance, and secure data handling in products where trust is mission-critical.
●        The judgement to move between product thinking and technical execution and to make clear trade-offs under ambiguity.
●        Commercial instinct: comfort representing a company to investors and partners, and a network you are willing to bring to bear.
●        Experience leading cross-functional delivery and, ideally, hiring or managing small engineering teams.

**Nice to have**
●        Silicon Valley connections
●        Public sector, GovTech, civic systems, or other regulated data environments.
●        PostGIS, legislative or open-data APIs, and data pipeline architecture.
●        Accessibility, internationalisation, and multi-region deployment.
●        ML, scoring systems, or analytics-heavy products.
●        Prior founder or early-stage experience, including exposure to fundraising.

**Compensation and equity**
This is a co-founder-level appointment. Compensation is equity-weighted and reflects founding status, with cash compensation calibrated to the stage and confirmed on close of the pre-seed round. 

**Why this role**
This is a high-ownership seat with architectural and commercial leverage. The person here will shape core infrastructure, engineering culture, product velocity, and the technical moat from the earliest stage. It suits someone who wants genuine authority, is comfortable operating with incomplete information, and is motivated by hard systems problems and real civic impact rather than polished corporate environments.

**How to apply**
Send your CV and portfolio and Linkedin to wedecide@pm.me
Detailed product and architecture materials are shared under a mutual non-disclosure agreement at a later stage of the process.
 
Allegra Grunberg  —  Founder & CEO, WeDecide Now Ltd  —  wedecide@pm.me

title: Creative Director
description:
We are a fast-growing creator management agency scaling from 30 to 80+ creators over the next 12 months, moving from $300,000 to $1,000,000+ per month in gross sales. Creative quality and output is the binding constraint on revenue per creator. This role exists to remove that constraint — by owning the creative direction, coaching, and commercial outcome of every creator in your pod.

THE ROLE
Every creator in this agency needs one person who owns their creative direction, their coaching, and their revenue outcome. That is this role.

You will manage a pod of creators, build and deliver their content plans, analyse what is performing across YouTube and Instagram, and coach them to produce stronger content so they grow their subscriber base and earn more. You are also the day-to-day relationship holder for your pod — fielding queries, resolving issues, and keeping those relationships healthy.

This is not a management role. You do not manage creators. You coach them, brief them, and hold the commercial outcome. Persuasion and relationship strength are your tools.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN
*Creative coaching — review what each creator in your pod is producing, identify where performance is dropping, and work with them directly to lift the quality of their output shoot by shoot

*Content and branding briefs — produce the briefs that direct each creator's output so every creator has a clear plan for what they are making, why, and what it is meant to achieve

*Data reviews — run regular performance reviews across your pod, identify what is winning and what is failing, and feed those findings back into the next round of briefs

*Competitor content analysis — analyse top performing content across the niche on YouTube and Instagram, pull the patterns, and translate them into formats your creators can execute

*Revenue ownership — drive creators toward their revenue targets using creative and media as the lever, accountable for the commercial trajectory of your pod

*Client support and retention — handle creator queries, resolve issues quickly, and reduce churn through strong day-to-day relationship management

*Onboarding new creators — own the onboarding of new creators joining your pod, set the creative baseline, build the first plan, and get them producing to standard fast

*Reporting upward — report pod performance, risks, and creator issues to the Head of Client Success on the agreed cadence

Requirements & qualifications
NON-NEGOTIABLES
— Self-starter who runs their lane without micromanagement once trained
— Ownership mindset — you own the result of your pod, not just the activity
— Operates through influence and coaching, not authority
— Comfortable being commercially accountable for creative decisions

WHAT YOU WILL BE MEASURED ON
— Subscribers per creator — average subscriber count across your pod, tracked over time
— Creator churn — the rate at which creators in your pod leave
— Speed to revenue for onboarded creators — time taken for a new creator to reach a defined revenue threshold
— Targets and weightings set quarterly with the Head of Client Success.

WHAT YOU BRING
Experience (non-negotiable)
— 3+ years in content strategy, branding, or creative direction
— Direct experience working with on-camera talent or creators — briefing them and coaching their performance

Experience (preferred)
— Creator economy or influencer marketing background
— Has worked in an environment where content performance was tied to revenue and been measured on it
— Experience running content across multiple accounts or brands simultaneously

Skills (must-have)
— Short-form video fluency across Instagram and YouTube, with a clear point of view on why content performs
— Brief writing — translating analysis into plans that others can execute
— Coaching and delivering feedback that lifts performance without damaging the relationship
— Data literacy — reading performance dashboards and acting on what they show
— Client relationship management

Skills (preferred)
— Analytics and dashboard proficiency
— Conflict resolution
— Hands-on editing or production knowledge

Who you are (non-negotiable)
— A self starter who owns their lane and does not wait to be directed
— Bubbly and energetic — you bring energy into every interaction and lift the people around you
— Able to hype creators up and make them feel like they are winning
— People-centred — a natural coach who gets genuine satisfaction from other people's progress
— Ownership mindset — you own the outcome of your pod, not the activity

WHAT WE OFFER
— $2,000 to $3,000 per month OTE, dependent on experience
— Fully remote, full-time (Monday-Friday, 7AM-4PM SAST)

LOGISTICS
Location: Fully remote. South Africa preferred,
Hours: Full-time, 8 hours per day, 5 days per week
Language: Fluent, professional-level English required — written and verbal
Reports to: Head of Client Success

title: Enterprise Account Executive
description:
Enterprise Account Executive (Commission-Only)

Company: [Corvane](https://corvane.com/)
Location: Remote
Compensation: 100% Commission
OTE: $50,000–$100,000+ per year (Uncapped)

THE SOLUTION

[Corvane](https://corvane.com/) is building the next generation of consumer intelligence.

Our AI-powered research platform helps consumer brands make better decisions by giving them fast access to reliable consumer feedback. Brands use Corvane to validate ideas, test messaging, recruit verified research participants, track brand perception, test concepts, and understand what consumers actually think.

Corvane helps companies move from question to consumer insight faster, without the time and complexity of traditional research processes.

Our customers span beauty, fashion, wellness, food & beverage, consumer technology, and agencies serving consumer brands.

We are customer-driven at our core and are looking for a salesperson who can help us bring Corvane to more businesses.

THE ROLE

As a Sales Account Executive at Corvane, you will own the full sales cycle from cold prospecting through signed contract.

This is a hands-on outbound sales role. A significant part of your day will involve cold calling and cold email prospecting to identify potential customers, start conversations, book meetings, and create qualified pipeline.

You'll research prospects, identify decision-makers, build targeted outreach lists, make outbound calls, send personalized emails, follow up consistently, run discovery calls and product demos, handle objections, negotiate, and close.

You'll work directly with the founder to refine our sales process, identify market opportunities, improve messaging, and build a repeatable sales engine.

This is an early-stage role for someone who enjoys the hunt, takes ownership of their pipeline, and is motivated by performance.

WHAT YOU'LL SELL

You'll sell Corvane's consumer intelligence and research solutions, including:

• Consumer research engagements
• AI-powered research platform subscriptions
• Verified respondent recruitment
• Brand tracking
• Concept testing
• Pricing research
• Packaging and messaging validation
• Enterprise research programs

Opportunities range from one-off research engagements to recurring enterprise contracts.

Enterprise contracts start at $21,000 annually, with larger opportunities available depending on customer needs, research scope, usage, and expansion potential.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Prospecting & Pipeline Generation

• Generate your own qualified pipeline through outbound prospecting.
• Make cold calls to founders, executives, marketers, consumer insights leaders, and other decision-makers.
• Conduct consistent cold email outreach and personalized follow-up.
• Research target companies and identify the right decision-makers.
• Build targeted prospect lists and manage outbound sequences.
• Follow up persistently across phone, email, and LinkedIn.
• Turn cold prospects into qualified sales opportunities.

Sales & Closing

• Own opportunities from initial outreach through signed contract.
• Conduct discovery calls to understand customer needs, challenges, and research objectives.
• Run product demos and sales presentations.
• Clearly communicate Corvane's value proposition and ROI.
• Handle objections and navigate complex sales conversations.
• Build relationships with senior stakeholders and decision-makers.
• Negotiate commercial terms and close new business.
• Identify opportunities for recurring subscriptions, larger research programs, and account expansion.

Sales Operations & Feedback

• Maintain an accurate and organized CRM pipeline.
• Consistently work toward and exceed monthly and quarterly sales targets.
• Track outreach, meetings, opportunities, and conversion rates.
• Share customer and market feedback directly with the founder.
• Help improve sales messaging, positioning, prospecting strategies, and the overall sales process.
• Contribute to building Corvane's repeatable sales engine as the company scales.

IDEAL CUSTOMERS

You'll primarily sell to:

• Shopify and DTC brands
• Beauty companies
• Wellness brands
• Fashion brands
• Food & beverage companies
• Consumer technology companies
• Marketing and branding agencies
• Consumer-facing businesses with ongoing research and consumer intelligence needs

You'll typically engage with:

• Founders and CEOs
• CMOs
• Heads of Marketing
• Consumer Insights leaders
• Brand leaders
• Product leaders
• Agency executives

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

• Proven experience in B2B sales, business development, or an Account Executive role.
• Demonstrated ability to generate your own pipeline and close new business.
• Comfortable and confident with cold calling and phone-based prospecting.
• Strong experience with cold email prospecting and outbound sales.
• Strong discovery, objection-handling, negotiation, and closing skills.
• Ability to sell a complex SaaS, research, technology, or professional service offering.
• Strong relationship-building skills with executives and senior decision-makers.
• Highly organized and capable of managing a sales pipeline independently.
• Competitive, persistent, and comfortable with rejection.
• Self-starter mentality and ability to thrive in an early-stage startup.
• Highly motivated by measurable results and commission-based compensation.

COMMUNICATION REQUIREMENTS

Proficiency in written and verbal English is required.

You must be able to:

• Communicate clearly and professionally with prospects over the phone.
• Conduct sales calls and product demonstrations in fluent, professional English.
• Write clear, persuasive, and grammatically strong cold emails.
• Communicate effectively with senior executives and decision-makers.
• Clearly articulate complex products, ideas, and value propositions.
• Handle objections and negotiate confidently in English.

Bonus: Experience selling SaaS, market research, consumer insights, analytics, advertising, marketing technology, or AI products.

COMPENSATION

This is a 100% commission role with uncapped earning potential.

You earn 20% commission on every deal you close.

There is no cap on commissions.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Within your first 90 days, you will:

• Build a qualified outbound pipeline.
• Establish consistent daily cold calling and cold email activity.
• Book recurring sales meetings and product demos.
• Close your first customers.
• Develop repeatable outbound prospecting strategies.
• Build relationships with high-value consumer brands and agencies.
• Create a predictable pipeline of qualified opportunities.
• Help establish Corvane's early sales engine.

WHY JOIN CORVANE?

• Sell a product solving a real business problem. Consumer brands need faster, better ways to understand their customers and make informed decisions.
• Work directly with the founder. You'll have a direct line to the person building the company and shaping the product.
• Unlimited earning potential. Your earning potential scales directly with the business you close.
• Own your pipeline. You'll have significant autonomy over prospecting, outreach, and sales strategy.
• Sell into meaningful contract sizes. Enterprise contracts start at $21,000 annually.
• Fully remote and flexible.
• Build something early. You'll help shape Corvane's sales process and have the opportunity to grow into a larger sales leadership role as the company scales.

WHO SHOULD APPLY?

This role is for a hunter.

You should enjoy creating opportunities from scratch, picking up the phone, sending cold emails, starting conversations with people who don't know you, handling rejection, following up, and getting deals across the finish line.

You should be comfortable with the reality that your pipeline is your responsibility.

If you're looking for a traditional account management role where leads are handed to you, this isn't it.

If you're competitive, persistent, commercially minded, highly articulate in English, and excited by the opportunity to earn based on performance, we'd like to hear from you.

HOW TO APPLY

Email [onanma@corvane.com](mailto:onanma@corvane.com) with the subject line:

Corvane AE - [Your Name]

Give me your best pitch on why I should hire you for this role and why Corvane.

Attach a resume if it strengthens your application.

Please include your primary location. This is a remote role.

Start your email with the word "Lily."

Keep it intentional and sharp.

title: QA Tester @ Revize (Remote)
description:
That frustrating moment when you hit 'confirm order' and immediately spot a mistake? We're fixing that. At Revize, we're tackling this common friction point by redefining a crucial part of the online shopping journey: what happens after checkout. As a dedicated Shopify Partner, we empower customers to seamlessly edit their orders post-purchase.

We're building the definitive solution that transforms the post-purchase experience – streamlining complex operations for merchants and creating happier, more loyal customers through essential flexibility. This isn't just a feature; it's becoming fundamental to modern customer expectations.

Our technology, honed over 7 years of building scalable applications within the Shopify ecosystem, already powers experiences for millions globally. It's trusted by rapidly growing brands like Knya and AlaMode in India, and international names such as Nude Project and Shelly.

We are a lean, fully remote team of three, driven by the challenge of creating category-defining solutions that make commerce fundamentally smoother and more user-friendly for everyone involved.

**Why Join Us**

* Real Impact: You'll be the quality gatekeeper for stores doing $30M+ in annual revenue — catching bugs before millions of shoppers hit them.
* Full Ownership: Own the entire QA process, from manual testing to building out automation as we scale.
* Close Collaboration: Work directly with the founders and dev team in a no-fluff, async-first environment.
* Remote Lifestyle: Join us from anywhere — our team works from Goa, Himachal, and wherever feels best.

**What You'll Work On**

* Nothing ships without your sign-off. You're the last line of defense before code hits production.
* Big brands trust our product — and by extension, they're trusting you.
* Hunt down bugs across browsers, devices, and the weird edge cases no one thought of.
* Build out our QA playbook from scratch — processes, automation, whatever you think we need.
* Work across the full product: merchant dashboards, customer portals, Shopify integrations.
* Move fast with us — we ship weekly, and you'll be in the middle of it all.

**You Might Be a Fit If You**

* Actually enjoy breaking things and finding what others miss
* Write bug reports that devs thank you for (clear steps, expected vs actual, no guesswork)
* Take initiative and don't wait to be told what to test
* Care about the end-user experience, not just checking boxes
* Thrive in small teams where your work is visible

title: Partnership & Event Executive
description:
**Partnership & Event Executive**
Team: Growth / GTM
 Location: Fully remote - anywhere in the world, 
 Reports to: Founder / CEO
 Type: Full-time
 
**About QuickAds**
QuickAds builds performance creatives as a service creative intelligence, creative strategy, creative production, influencer marketing at scale, and campaign management. Most tools in this space do one link of that chain; we cover all of it. Our computer-vision models are trained on 32M+ ads, and we've managed $200M+ in ad spend for brands that live and die by paid social. We're 70+ people across Bangalore, Noida, Singapore, Canada and the USA, and VC-funded. AI handles form here; humans own substance.
The role
We ship 100+ creatives a month for clients on 5–7 day turnarounds. What we don't yet have is a systematic way to get in front of the agencies, platforms and brand teams who should know us. That's this job.

You'll own two connected motions: building the partner ecosystem that sends us qualified pipeline, and running the events calendar  ours and the ones we show up at  that makes QuickAds the obvious name when a brand's creative pipeline breaks. This is a builder role, not a maintainer one. There's an existing network to lean on and very little existing process.

We're open on location. What we're not open on is being reachable: our teams sit across countries, so you'll need to hold a few hours of overlap with at least two of those. Being near a major international airport matters more than being near an office

**What you'll own**
**Partnerships**
* Build and run the partner ecosystem: performance agencies, media buying shops, platform partners (Meta, TikTok, Google, Shopify ecosystem), and adjacent martech
* Design the commercial structure for each partner type referral, reseller, co-sell, white-label and get it signed
* Own partner-sourced pipeline as a number, with clear attribution and a quarterly target
* Run co-marketing with partners: joint webinars, case studies, content swaps, shared events
* Be the internal owner of partner health  onboarding, enablement, QBRs, and the honest call on which partnerships to kill
**Events**
* Build the annual events calendar across your priority markets, and defend the budget for it
* Run our own formats: founder dinners, CMO roundtables, creative teardown sessions, webinars
* Decide where we sponsor vs. attend vs. skip, and negotiate those deals
* Own the full loop  pre-event outreach, on-ground execution, and the follow-up sequence that turns conversations into meetings
* Report on cost per qualified conversation and pipeline created per event
Cross-functional
* Work with Sales on which partners and events actually convert, and drop the ones that don't
* Work with Marketing on collateral, messaging and post-event content
* Bring what you hear in the market back to the product and creative teams

**What we're looking for**
* 2–4 years in partnerships, alliances, BD or field marketing  ideally some of it in adtech, martech, SaaS or agency-side
* You've built a partner program from close to zero, not just inherited one
* You've run real events end to end, including the unglamorous parts: vendor chasing, badge scanning, and the follow-up nobody wants to do
* Comfortable being measured on pipeline, not on activity
* Strong commercial instincts you can structure a deal and know when to walk
* Excellent written and spoken English; you'll be pitching to CMOs and growth leads across regions
* A track record of doing this well remotely  writing things down, running without supervision, and closing loops across time zones
* Able to travel roughly 25–30% of the time, including internationally, with the documentation to do so

**Nice to have**
* Existing relationships with performance agencies or platform partner teams
* Understanding of how paid social creative actually works  hooks, iteration velocity, why creative is the biggest lever left
* Experience selling into or partnering with e-commerce and D2C brands
* Experience working across India, SEA and North America  the three markets that matter most to us

**Why this role**
* You'll own a function, not a slice of one direct line to the founders, and the budget to go with it
* Genuine white space: nobody else is covering the whole creative value chain, which makes the partner pitch easy to differentiate
* Work from wherever you're based, with real reasons to be in the room when it counts
* A product that does what it says: 100+ creatives a month, 5–7 day turnarounds, and case histories you can put in front of a partner without flinching

**How to apply**
Interested? Send your CV to hr@quickads.ai with a short note on one partnership or event you built from scratch  and what you'd do differently now. Tell us where you're based and what hours you'd realistically be available.

QuickAds hires on capability. We welcome applicants from any location or background, and we're happy to accommodate what you need in the process.

title: Head of Growth
description:
[Techne] | Full-time contractor | Remote, with monthly travel for in-person work from any of our current hubs (Boston-Providence, Denver-Boulder, New Orleans) | USD

*Please read this post in its entirety, including instructions on how to apply; applicants who do not follow these instructions will not be considered*

Focus: Get people onto the product and make sure they bring their friends. We're starting in Boulder to prove the model, then scaling nationally. You own user acquisition end-to-end: the field work, the creators, the paid tests, and the partnerships. You own the numbers that tell us what's actually working.

### The mission
We're building something that moves people off their phones and back into their neighborhoods. Our first version, Beacon, lets you tell the people you actually know, "I'm going to the farmers market, find me there." It only works if your friends are on it. We are starting with mothers in Boulder because they are the center of the local social graph. If it works there, we move to the next city.

We can build a great product and still fail if nobody's friends are using it. This role exists so that doesn't happen.

### What you will own
* We grow through circles. The product works when existing groups—a school grade, a team, a neighborhood—move onto it. You find the connectors, recruit them, and get their circles to join. Right now, this is ten ambassadors in Boulder. By February, it needs to be a playbook any city can run without us.
* The invite loop. We don't do follower counts or social proof. The only way we grow is through direct invites. You are responsible for how many people actually accept those invites. You'll work with the product lead on every screen that touches that flow.
* Creators and content. You'll manage local creators who make video about what's happening in town. You select them, brief them, and make sure they deliver.
* Paid acquisition. Meta and Instagram tests. This is a bridge, not the foundation. We run these tests against a strict cost ceiling with a "kill rule" if they don't perform.
* Partnerships. You'll find organizations with active audiences—schools, charities, local groups. You open the door, structure the deal, and measure if their people actually show up.
* The scorecard. We need to know where every user came from and what it cost to get them active. You publish these numbers weekly. This scorecard decides where next month's money goes.
* Key outcomes (what success looks like)
* You're inheriting a plan that's already in motion for September and October. Your job is to take it over and make it better.
* By December 15, 2026: 12 to 15 active circles in Boulder, Providence, Boston, or New Orleans with at least 40% of members accepting invites. The scorecard is live and being used for board evaluations.
* By January 31, 2027: A finished playbook for moving into a second city. We need to see at least one active circle in a new market where you weren't physically on the ground.
* By February 28, 2027: Two growth channels running consistently inside our cost limits with clear documentation. You've built a solid list of local ambassadors and partners for the full launch.
* Ongoing: No "mystery" users. If we can't say where a user came from, they don't count.

### Candidate profile
* We are looking for one of two backgrounds, and ideally someone who has done both.
* Organizer. You have run a distributed organizing program: relational organizing, volunteer-led canvass, chapter or neighborhood team structures. You have gotten thousands of people to do a physical thing in the same week and you had a system that told you whether they did. You know what a captain is, what a turf is, what a ladder of engagement is, and why the ask has to be small and the deadline has to be real. Political campaigns, labor, faith, mutual aid, community organizing at scale all count.
* Growth operator. You have grown a consumer product where the user brings the next user: a social, community, events or local product. You have owned an invite loop, a referral mechanic, or a city launch. You know the difference between a signup and an activated user and you have killed a channel because the numbers said to.
* In either case, you must have:
* Fluency in short vertical video as a distribution medium, either making it yourself or directing people who do. You know what makes a 20-second clip about a farmers market travel and what makes it look like an ad.
* Comfort being measured. You will be held to circle activation, K, and cost per occasion, published weekly. If you prefer to be judged on reach and impressions, this is the wrong job.
* A record of closing. Partnerships signed, ambassadors recruited, cohorts filled. Not "worked on" or "supported."
* Proximity to the audience or a demonstrated ability to earn it fast. For example, you do not need to be a mother in Boulder. You need to be someone a mother in Boulder would take a call from and then text her friends about.
* The ability to work alongside a product team and argue with them about screens. Growth in this product lives inside the invite flow, and you need to be in that conversation, not downstream of it.
* What else you own
* Beyond acquisition, this role holds the public face of the product.
* Brand. You own the brand system once the name clears trademark: identity, design direction, and how it shows up in the product, on the site, in creator content and in ads. You brief designers and agencies; you do not need to be one.
* Voice. You write the voice guide and you enforce it. Every invite text, push notification, landing page, creator brief and ad reads like the same person wrote it, and that person is not a startup. The product's own copy sets the tone (short, plain, no engagement bait); you extend it to everything outside the app.
* Comms. You own what we say publicly and when: the marketing site, launch communications, press when it comes, and the cadence of what goes out on our own channels. You decide what gets said about the product before launch and you hold the line on what does not (no product name in public ahead of clearance, no donation asks ahead of fiscal sponsor confirmation).
* Messaging. One story about why this exists, told the same way to a mother in Boulder, a partner organization, a creator, and a funder. Emma will use it with donors. You write it and you keep it current as the pilots tell us what is true.

### What this role is not
Not the field operator. Our current Field Operator recruits ambassadors and works circles on the ground in Boulder. You set his targets, give him the playbook, and read his numbers. You do not run his list.
Not the product lead. Our current Product lead owns what the product does and how the screens work. You own how people arrive and what they see before they get there, and you are in the room for every screen that touches the invite flow. Disagreements are settled with data from the scorecard, not by title.
Not a designer or a copywriter for hire. You direct brand and voice and you can write. You are not the person producing every asset.

### Structure and compensation
Full-time independent contractor agreement, USD
Base range: $140,000 to $170,000 USD annually, set on experience and location.
Performance bonus: up to 25 percent of base, milestone-based, agreed in writing before start. Milestones are activated circles and occasions of community time.
No equity, token or phantom-equity compensation. All compensation approved through governance in a single decision before the offer is extended.
Boulder travel and field expenses covered.

### How to apply
Send a note, not a cover letter, answering two things: the last time you got at least 20 people who did not work for you to show up somewhere physical in the same week, and how you knew they did. And a link to one piece of short vertical video you made or directed that you think worked, with the numbers. Applicants who do not follow these instructions will not be considered.

description:
About the Role:
This role is for an ongoing member of the team who will work with the Embedded team. Primary tasks
will be to develop the ICV (in-car video) software applications. Work will be allocated in the sprint. The
hardware platform to support development will be supplied and must be kept in a state that can support
ongoing work. This may include sourcing and expensing local SIM cards, and providing local wired LAN
or WiFi and power.
Profile:
This role is suited to an engineer who enjoys building device-side software on Linux-based edge devices
and deploying solutions that operate reliably in real-world, mission-critical environments.
You will be responsible for designing, developing, testing, and maintaining applications and services
written primarily in C and C++, supported by Python and shell scripting, on Linux and embedded Linux
platforms. You will integrate the product range with Linux networking stacks, video recording and
streaming solutions, Bluetooth services, third-party SDKs, security and AI libraries, and hardware
peripherals including TPMs, GNSS/GPS receivers, GPIO interfaces, and cellular connectivity modules
(4G/5G).
The systems you build will be deployed at scale and must meet the expectations of public-sector
customers, most notably law-enforcement organizations, where reliability, security, and data integrity are
paramount.
The role involves working across the full software development lifecycle, including requirements
definition, system design, implementation, testing, deployment, and operational support. You will
collaborate closely with backend, platform, and QA engineers for configuration, installation scripts,
logging, provisioning, customer support, diagnostics and evidence handling.
Prior experience in embedded Linux, AI or evidence-management domains is beneficial but not
required. More important is a strong foundation in Linux-based systems development, multithreading
expertise, an understanding of video solutions, secure and networked edge devices, and the ability to
deliver robust, maintainable solutions suitable for safety-critical and compliance-driven environments.

Essential Skills and Experience:
1. Strong proficiency in C, C++, Python
2. Experience using scripting languages such as Python or shell to support development, testing, or
deployment
3. Proficiency with Linux development environments, debugging, profiling, Git and build systems
4. Proficiency in designing and implementing multithreaded and concurrent systems
5. Solid understanding of networked systems, including TCP/IP, UDP, HTTP/S, TLS, and device-to-cloud
communication
6. Familiarity with developing video recording and streaming applications or multimedia streaming
protocols such as RTSP, RTP, HLS or WebRTC
7. Demonstrated experience building long-running device-side services, agents, or daemons
8. Experience working with secure systems, including encrypted communications, secure storage, and
system hardening
9. Comfortable working in an Agile development environment and collaborating across disciplines
10. Familiarity with virtualization technologies (Docker, VirtualBox or Hyper-V)

Desired Skills and Experience: (The following are an advantage)
1. Experience with web backend integration
2. Basic knowledge of HTTP servers, databases, and SQL queries
3. Experience deploying AI models for video, audio, or sensor processing on edge or embedded
platforms
4. Knowledge of embedded and device security, including secure boot, certificate management,
hardware-backed key storage (TPM), and encrypted communications
5. Experience working on large-scale connected device fleets
6. Familiarity with Linux networking internals and performance optimization
7. Familiarity with video compression standards and developing applications using multimedia platforms
such as GStreamer SDK and FFmpeg
8. Experience with IP-based physical security product integration standards such as ONVIF
9. Knowledge of common network architectures (routers, switches, proxies, etc.)
10. Excellent troubleshooting skills using network analysis tools
11. Demonstrable ability to plan and manage own timelines and deliver applications on time and in line
with business needs
12. Experience in configuring, optimizing, and developing media streaming servers
13. Excellent presentation, communication, and documentation skills, together with the relevant tertiary
qualifications

title: Business Development Executive Intern
