2.  Study and recreate video formats from publishers such as Financial Times, Financial Express, The New York Times, and LA Times.
3.  Work with AI-generated scenes, stock footage, graphics, captions, music, and other visual assets.
4.  Improve AI-generated videos for pacing, storytelling, visual quality, and watchability.
5.  Identify what feels unnatural or ineffective in AI-generated videos and suggest improvements.
6.  Work closely with our product and engineering teams to establish quality benchmarks and      editing guidelines.
7.  Document your editing decisions and workflows so that repetitive manual work can eventually be automated by Voomo Publisher.

### What We’re Looking For:
1. Strong video editing and storytelling skills.
2. A good instinct for pacing, visual storytelling, and viewer engagement.
3. Experience with tools such as Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, or similar.
4. Interest in AI-generated video and creative AI tools.
5. Strong attention to detail and willingness to experiment and iterate.
6. Ability to look at a video critically and explain why it works or doesn't work.

Bonus: Experience with news, editorial, explainer, or social media video content.

### Why Join Us?
This is more than a traditional video editing internship. Your work will directly contribute to building an AI-powered video production workflow. The manual editing you do will help us understand what makes a story video good—and eventually automate those decisions.
You’ll work closely with a startup product and engineering team and have the opportunity to shape a product from an early stage.

To Apply: Send us your resume and portfolio/reel. Personal or college projects are welcome too.

title: Cross Border Tax Accountant and Team Lead
description:
We are seeking a knowledgeable, organized, and client focused Cross Border Tax Accountant and Team Lead. The successful candidate will prepare Canadian and U.S. tax returns while managing the daily work of a remote tax preparation team.

This position requires a professional who can combine technical tax knowledge with leadership, accountability, effective communication, and strong organizational skills.

## Position Overview

The Cross Border Tax Accountant and Team Lead will be responsible for the accurate and timely completion of Canadian and U.S. tax engagements. The individual will assign work, monitor deadlines, review team output, coach junior staff, communicate with clients, and report engagement progress to the firm’s partners.

This is not simply a tax preparation or data entry position. The successful candidate must understand the information being reported, identify missing or inconsistent information, recognize potential compliance concerns, and escalate complex matters for senior review.

The Team Lead will set a professional example for the team and help create a culture of accuracy, accountability, collaboration, learning, and excellent client service.

## Tax Preparation Responsibilities

1. Prepare Canadian T1 personal income tax returns and related schedules.

2. Prepare and assist with Canadian departure tax returns, including residency considerations, deemed disposition calculations, and applicable information forms.

3. Prepare U.S. individual income tax returns, including Forms 1040 and 1040NR.

4. Prepare or assist with U.S. partnership and corporate tax returns, including Forms 1065 and 1120.

5. Prepare supporting schedules, reconciliations, elections, disclosures, and tax working papers.

6. Assist with foreign tax credit calculations and the reporting of Canadian, U.S., and foreign source income.

7. Support tax residency determinations under Canadian and U.S. domestic tax rules and applicable tax treaties.

8. Review client documents to identify missing information, inconsistencies, filing obligations, and potential tax concerns.

9. Conduct technical research on Canadian, U.S., and cross border tax matters when required.

10. Assist with CRA and IRS notices, reassessments, correspondence, and information requests.

11. Maintain complete and properly organized electronic working papers, client documents, and engagement records.

## Team Management and Leadership Responsibilities

1. Provide daily leadership and direction to tax preparers and other assigned team members.

2. Allocate tax files and administrative responsibilities based on team members’ skills, capacity, and experience.

3. Establish priorities and ensure the team clearly understands assignments, deadlines, and expected quality standards.

4. Monitor the progress of all assigned engagements and follow up before deadlines are at risk.

5. Conduct regular virtual team meetings to review priorities, workload, technical concerns, and outstanding client information.
6. Review team members’ working papers and tax returns for completeness, consistency, accuracy, and compliance with firm procedures.

7. Provide clear and constructive review notes and ensure corrections are completed properly.

8. Coach junior and intermediate staff on Canadian and U.S. tax preparation, documentation, research, and client communication.

9. Help team members understand the reason behind a tax treatment instead of focusing only on data entry.

10. Identify technical or performance gaps and recommend appropriate training or support.

11. Develop checklists, templates, workflows, and standard operating procedures to improve consistency and efficiency.

12. Encourage team members to raise questions promptly and escalate uncertain matters appropriately.

13. Promote respectful communication, professional conduct, teamwork, and accountability.

14. Support the onboarding and training of new employees.

15. Assist management with evaluating team performance, productivity, accuracy, responsiveness, and professional development.

16. Address routine workflow or performance concerns professionally and report material issues to senior management.

17. Provide regular status reports to the partners regarding completed files, outstanding information, approaching deadlines, team capacity, and identified risks.

18. Lead by example through reliability, ethical conduct, attention to detail, and commitment to client service.

## Client Management Responsibilities

1. Act as a primary contact for assigned clients and engagements.

2. Prepare clear and customized client information requests.

3. Communicate with clients through email, telephone, and virtual meetings.

4. Explain filing requirements, outstanding information, tax results, and payment obligations in understandable language.

5. Follow up professionally on missing documents, unanswered questions, approvals, and approaching deadlines.

6. Ensure client inquiries are acknowledged and addressed promptly.

7. Review outgoing client communications prepared by junior team members when necessary.

8. Handle routine client concerns professionally and escalate sensitive or complex matters to the partners.

9. Maintain accurate records of material client communications, decisions, and outstanding matters.

10. Protect the confidentiality of all personal, financial, and tax information.

## Workflow and Quality Control Responsibilities

1. Maintain an accurate workflow tracker for every assigned engagement.

2. Monitor Canadian and U.S. filing deadlines, extensions, tax instalments, balances payable, and outstanding client information.

3. Ensure every engagement follows the firm’s preparation, review, approval, and filing process.

4. Confirm that working papers clearly support the amounts reported on each tax return.

5. Ensure review notes are resolved before a file is presented for final approval.

6. Identify recurring errors and develop solutions to reduce them.

7. Ensure no tax return is filed without the required client authorization and internal approval.

8. Escalate complex tax positions, uncertainty, missed deadlines, potential penalties, or client disputes to the partners.
9. Support continuous improvement in turnaround time, accuracy, documentation, and client experience.

10. Maintain professional standards even during high volume tax filing periods.

## Required Qualifications

1. Bachelor’s or master’s degree in accounting, taxation, finance, commerce, or a related field.

2. At least 2 to 3 years of relevant tax preparation, accounting, or public practice experience.

3. Practical experience preparing Canadian T1 personal income tax returns.

4. Knowledge and practical exposure to Canadian departure tax matters.

5. Practical experience preparing U.S. Forms 1040 and 1040NR.

6. Experience preparing or substantially assisting with Forms 1065 and 1120.

7. Demonstrated ability to supervise, coordinate, train, or lead other team members.

8. Strong understanding of tax working papers, reconciliations, supporting schedules, and review procedures.

9. Ability to review the work of others and communicate corrections constructively.

10. Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.

11. Strong client communication and relationship management capabilities.

12. Ability to organize multiple engagements, team members, priorities, and deadlines.

13. Strong analytical, reconciliation, research, and problem solving abilities.

14. Sound professional judgment and the ability to recognize when a matter requires senior review.

15. Experience using professional Canadian or U.S. tax preparation software.

16. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, document management systems, and virtual communication tools.

17. Ability to work independently and manage a remote team effectively.

18. Access to reliable internet service, dependable power arrangements, and a secure private workspace.

19. Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and follow all information security requirements.

20. Availability to work an agreed schedule with sufficient overlap with Canadian business hours, particularly during tax season.

## ACCA Preference

Preference will be given to candidates who are:

1. ACCA members.

2. ACCA affiliates.

3. ACCA finalists.

4. Actively pursuing the ACCA qualification and have completed a substantial number of examinations.

Candidates should clearly state their current ACCA status in their application. However, practical Canadian and U.S. tax experience, leadership capability, and client communication skills remain essential.

An ACCA qualification without relevant tax experience will not replace the technical and leadership requirements of this position.

## Additional Experience Considered an Asset

1. Knowledge of the Canada U.S. Income Tax Treaty.

2. Experience working with Canadian residents, U.S. residents, dual residents, nonresidents, newcomers, and individuals departing Canada.

3. Familiarity with Canadian Forms T1135, T1161, T1243, T1244, and NR73.

4. Familiarity with U.S. Forms 1116, 2555, 8938, and 8840.

5. Knowledge of FBAR and other U.S. foreign financial reporting requirements.

6. Experience with U.S. extensions, elections, disclosures, and international information reporting.

7. Experience responding to CRA or IRS notices and info8. Experience using QuickBooks Online or similar bookkeeping platforms.

9. Previous experience managing accountants or tax preparers in a remote working environment.

10. Experience developing tax preparation checklists, review procedures, training materials, or standard operating procedures.

11. Experience working for a Canadian or U.S. accounting or tax firm.

## Leadership Qualities We Are Looking For

The successful candidate should:

1. Take ownership of results rather than simply completing assigned tasks.

2. Remain calm, organized, and professional during busy filing periods.

3. Communicate expectations clearly and follow up consistently.

4. Treat team members and clients with respect.

5. Provide constructive feedback and help others improve.

6. Identify problems early and recommend practical solutions.

7. Balance efficiency with accuracy and professional judgment.

8. Accept responsibility for mistakes and ensure appropriate corrections are made.

9. Maintain confidentiality and demonstrate high ethical standards.

10. Build trust through reliability, fairness, consistency, and professional conduct.

## What Success Looks Like

The successful candidate will ensure that:

1. Tax returns are accurate, complete, and supported by proper working papers.

2. The team understands its responsibilities and completes work within established deadlines.

3. Missing information and potential tax issues are identified early.

4. Review notes are clear, constructive, and resolved promptly.

5. Clients receive timely and professional communication.

6. Complex matters are escalated appropriately.

7. The partners receive accurate and timely updates about workflow, capacity, deadlines, and risks.

8. Junior team members improve their technical knowledge and professional skills.

9. Client confidentiality and information security requirements are consistently followed.

10. The team operates with professionalism, accountability, and a commitment to quality.

## Compensation and Opportunity

1. Monthly compensation of ₹60,000 to ₹80,000, based on relevant tax experience, leadership capability, ACCA status, and demonstrated technical proficiency.

2. A fully remote working arrangement.

3. Exposure to specialized Canadian and U.S. cross border tax engagements.

4. Opportunities to develop expertise in departure tax, nonresident taxation, international reporting, and cross border tax compliance.

5. Direct interaction with the firm’s partners and senior professionals.

6. Responsibility for managing and developing a remote tax preparation team.

7. Opportunities for professional development and increased responsibility based on performance.

## Selection Process

Shortlisted candidates may be invited to complete:

1. An initial interview focused on tax experience, leadership ability, communication skills, and remote work readiness.

2. A practical technical assessment covering Canadian and U.S. taxation.

3. A tax return review or case analysis exercise using fictional information.

4. A team management and client communication scenario.5. A final interview with the firm’s partners or senior management.

Candidates must not provide confidential tax returns, working papers, or client information belonging to any current or former employer.

## How to Apply

Please submit your résumé and a brief cover message addressing the following:

1. Your total Canadian and U.S. tax preparation experience.

2. Your current ACCA status, if applicable.

3. Your experience preparing Canadian T1 returns and departure tax returns.

4. The approximate number of Forms 1040 and 1040NR you have prepared.

5. Your experience preparing or reviewing Forms 1065 and 1120.

6. The Canadian and U.S. tax software you have used.

7. The number and type of employees you have supervised or trained.

8. An example of how you managed a team deadline or resolved a performance issue.

9. Your experience reviewing tax returns prepared by other team members.

10. Your experience communicating directly with clients.

11. Your current city and time zone.

12. Your availability to work hours that overlap with Canadian business hours.

13. Your current compensation, expected compensation, and earliest available start date.

*Application Email:* [Insert application email address]
*Email Subject:* Application for Cross Border Tax Accountant and Team Lead | [Candidate’s Full Name]

Only candidates with relevant Canadian and U.S. tax experience will be considered. Applicants must accurately describe the returns they have personally prepared, reviewed, or substantially assisted with.

title: Transaction Monitoring Specialist (crypto)

 - Understanding of blockchain technology and cryptocurrency transaction flows

 - Knowledge of South African AML/CFT legislation (FICA) and familiarity with FSCA requirements for Crypto Asset Service Providers (CASPs) is a plus

title: Independent Behavioral Health Business Development Partner (Commission Only)
description:
100% commission role - no base salary; the range shown is expected annual commission earnings.

## About the project

Behavioral Health Operations Project is an early-stage, founder-led business developing focused operational services for growing U.S. behavioral-health organizations. Our first service is a seven-business-day Clinician Activation Diagnostic examining the cross-functional path from an accepted clinician offer through payer readiness and a verified first clean paid claim.

We do not provide clinical care, handle protected health information (PHI), or make unsupported savings claims.

## About this opportunity

This is a remote, nonexclusive independent-contractor business-development opportunity. Applicants must be based in and legally able to contract in the United States. It is not a salaried or hourly employee position. There is no base salary, hourly pay, retainer, minimum number of hours, guaranteed income, employee benefits, or equity.

The contractor controls when, where, and how the work is performed, uses their own equipment and methods, may serve other clients, and is responsible for their own expenses and taxes. A written independent-contractor and referral agreement must be signed before work begins. Worker status depends on the actual relationship, not merely this description.

## Compensation

- 30% of diagnostic revenue actually collected from customers you originate. At the current $1,500 founding price, full collection equals a $450 commission.
- 10% of implementation or recurring-service revenue actually collected from that same customer during the first six months.
- Total commissions are capped at $7,500 per originated customer.
- Commissions are paid only after customer funds clear.
- Refunds and chargebacks offset unpaid or future commissions.
- No payment for names, lists, unqualified leads, or meetings that do not produce collected revenue.
- No payment for patient referrals, insurance reimbursements, or federally reimbursed healthcare business.

## What you would do

- Identify growing U.S. behavioral-health organizations with approximately 15–150 clinicians.
- Reach operations, finance, credentialing, revenue-cycle, HR, and executive decision-makers.
- Conduct structured, 15-minute sales-discovery conversations.
- Document evidence of activation delays, operational impact, current workarounds, decision authority, and next steps without seeking PHI or confidential patient information.
- Present the seven-business-day, $1,500 Clinician Activation Diagnostic only where there is a genuine fit.
- Follow up professionally through a purchasing decision.
- Never invent case studies, promise savings, offer unauthorized discounts, or bind the project to an agreement.

## Who may be a fit

- An independent sales professional, consultant, or small agency already serving healthcare or behavioral-health organizations.
- Prior experience selling B2B professional services into behavioral health, healthcare operations, credentialing, revenue cycle, workforce operations, healthcare technology, or provider services.
- Existing relationships or a credible plan for reaching decision-makers.
- Able to provide two verifiable professional references.
- Ethical, self-directed, and comfortable with a nonexclusive 30-day trial.

## Initial evidence goals

These are outcome goals, not required hours or a guaranteed quota:

- Within 14 days: three qualified buyer conversations.
- Within 30 days: five qualified conversations, two serious diagnostic discussions, and one paid diagnostic.

The project is in the validation stage. No sales results or earnings are guaranteed. This opportunity concerns only B2B operational consulting—not patient referrals, clinical services, or clinical decision-making.

## How to apply

Please answer these five questions in your application or introductory message. Do not include PHI, patient details, or confidential employer or client information.

1. What behavioral-health or healthcare service have you sold, and what result did you personally help produce?
2. Which buyer roles can you credibly reach, and through what ethical channels?
3. How would you obtain the first three qualified buyer conversations within 14 days without paid lists, spam, or misrepresenting the project?
4. Are you comfortable with no base pay or guaranteed income and with commissions being paid only after customer funds clear?
5. Can you provide two verifiable professional references if we advance? Please do not post their contact information in the initial application.

1. Encode the target market. Validate and sharpen our existing ICP and persona work. Map and prioritise TAM. Build the account scoring model that decides who gets worked and who does not.

2. Sending infrastructure. Secondary domains, mailbox provisioning, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, warmup schedules, inbox rotation, volume caps, bounce and spam monitoring. Our primary domain reputation is never at risk. Volume increases only when infrastructure is healthy.

3. Data and enrichment layer. A centralised, maintained target list. Waterfall enrichment, deduplication, verification. You are accountable for data quality and for cost per enriched record.

4. Signal layer. This is where the leverage is, and it is the part most people skip. You build the triggers that tell us when to reach out, not just who. Named signals we already know exist are listed below.

5. Multi-channel plays. Email, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and call tasks. Each play is tied to a specific signal and segment, with a stated success criterion before it launches.

6. CRM, routing, alerts. Everything pushes to HubSpot. Leads route to an owner. Replies get handled inside an SLA. Nothing sits unclaimed.

7. Dashboards and attribution. Sends, deliverability, reply rate, positive reply rate, meetings booked, pipeline sourced — split by play and by segment. If we cannot see which play produced a meeting, the play does not count.

8. Operate the loop. Daily reply triage, list refresh, message iteration, and honest kill-or-scale decisions based on the data rather than on how much work went into building the play.

**Experience we're looking for**

At least 3 years hands-on in outbound, growth or GTM engineering.
More important than the experience year number: you should have built at ONE outbound system from zero - domains, warmup, data layer and signals included, not inherited from a predecessor and not operated inside someone else's setup.
Years matter less to us than the number of systems you've stood up and the number of plays you've killed. 
If you're at the lower end of that range but have one genuine zero-to-one build behind you, apply.
If you're above it and still hands-on daily, also apply — just be clear you're not planning to subcontract this.

**What "AI-first" means here**
Everyone says AI-first. Here is the specific bar.

The system should continuously detect qualified triggers, enrich the account and the buyer, select the correct play, and create the next action — with human judgment kept in the loop for approvals and for actual conversations.

**Concretely, we expect fluency in:**

Enrichment and orchestration: Clay or equivalent, built as real tables with waterfalls and conditional logic
Sending: Instantly, Smartlead, or similar, plus HeyReach/Expandi of similar for LinkedIn (we own a seat)
Data waterfall: Apollo, FullEnrich, Findymail, LeadMagic, PredictLeads, BuiltWith, or your own preferred stack
Automation: n8n, Make, or equivalent — including webhook and API work
LLM tooling: prompt chaining, agentic workflows, Claude Code / MCP or similar. Using ChatGPT to write subject lines is not what we mean.
CRM: HubSpot

We care about what you have built, not which logos you have used.

**Non-negotiables**
Ownership. There is no team behind you and no one to escalate to. You scope it, you build it, you fix it.
Response speed. Replies from prospects get handled the same day. Outbound dies on latency.
Discipline over hours. Four focused hours daily, consistently, beats ten sporadic ones.
Positioning. Flowace is productivity, not surveillance. Any copy that reads like spying on employees is disqualifying, regardless of how well it converts.
Individual, not agency. If you plan to subcontract the work, this is not the right fit.

**What this role is not**
Not closing deals. Not running demos. Not managing SDRs. Not content marketing or paid ads. You build and run the machine that fills the calendar; the sales team works the calendar.

**Success metrics**
Bounce rate under 2%, spam complaint rate under 0.1%, sustained at ramped volume
Positive reply rate benchmarked and improving month over month
Qualified meetings booked per month (target to be agreed at kickoff)
Pipeline sourced and attributable by play

title: Platform/SRE Lead
description:
About NewVue.ai
NewVue.ai is a rapidly growing healthcare technology company focused on modernizing radiology workflow. Our platform helps imaging groups and hospitals streamline their operations by connecting disparate systems—like PACS, dictation tools, and EHRs—into a unified, efficient radiologist cockpit. We work closely with radiologists, IT teams, and clinical leaders to improve turnaround times, reduce errors, and deliver better patient outcomes. We’re a growing, nimble team that values autonomy, flexibility, creativity, and a collaborative spirit.

Job Overview
The Platform/SRE Lead owns NewVue’s cloud platform and delivery pipeline so product teams can ship fast and safely. You will design and run our AWS foundations (IaC, networking, security), standardize CI/CD (blue-green/canary, rollback), instrument observability, and embed security/compliance gates for HIPAA/SOC 2. You’ll turn our orchestration platform into a paved road for products, so features launch in weeks, not quarters.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Engineering & AWS
• Build and own AWS foundations: VPC design, subnets, routing, security groups, WAF, KMS, IAM, backups, and DR (RTO/RPO).
• Implement Infrastructure as Code (Terraform and/or CDK) with reusable modules, environment strategy, drift detection, and change control.
• Operate core services (e.g., ECS/EKS, EC2, RDS/Aurora, S3, SQS/SNS/EventBridge, API Gateway/ALB/NLB) supporting multi-tenant microservices and data flows (HL7, FHIR, S3/SFTP).
CI/CD & Release Engineering
• Standardize pipelines for all services (build, test, scan, deploy) with artifact/versioning, progressive delivery (blue-green/canary), and automated rollback.
• Implement test gates (unit/API/contract/smoke), schema and API compatibility checks, and zero-downtime migrations.

Observability & Reliability
• Establish logs/metrics/traces and golden dashboards; define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets per product.
• Lead on-call readiness: runbooks, incident response/postmortems, MTTR improvements, capacity/perf tuning, and cost optimization (tagging/FinOps, Savings Plans).
• Stand up monitoring/alerting with Datadog/Dynatrace (or similar) and manage vendor integrations.
Security & Compliance by Design
• Embed SAST/DAST, dependency and container scans, IaC policy-as-code, SBOMs, and secrets management in the pipeline.
• Partner with CTO on HIPAA/SOC 2/HITRUST controls; document and evidence controls within CI/CD and cloud.

Developer Experience (“Paved Paths”)
• Provide service templates, adapter scaffolds, local dev tooling, and reference repos that enforce best practices by default.
• Coach engineers on cloud/runtime patterns (resiliency, retries/fan-out/fan-in, idempotency, backpressure).

Cross‑Functional Delivery
• Work with Head of Engineering to align capacity and keep the bi-weekly release train on time.
• Partner with CTO/Lead Architect on platform guardrails and reusable “pipes” for product teams (Ingress/Egress APIs only).
• Support COO/TPM and Implementation on onboarding tiers and reusable adapters for customer go-lives.

Required Qualifications
• 7+ years in DevOps/SRE/Platform Engineering; 3+ years leading or acting as primary owner for cloud platforms.
• Deep AWS expertise (networking, IAM/KMS, containers/orchestration, RDS/Aurora, eventing), with IaC at scale (Terraform and/or CDK).
• Proven CI/CD design and operation (progressive delivery, automated rollback, artifacts, env promotion).
• Strong observability practice (logs/metrics/traces), SLO/SLI design, and incident management (on-call, postmortems).
• Security-minded: secrets mgmt, least privilege, image/dependency/IaC scanning; experience supporting HIPAA/SOC 2 or similar.
• Proficiency in a scripting language (Python, TypeScript, or Bash) and solid Git workflows.
• Excellent collaboration and communication skills across Product, Engineering, Implementation, and
Security/Compliance.
• Comfort working with mixed in-house/outsourced teams.

Nice to Have
• Healthcare/radiology data flows (HL7, FHIR), PHI handling patterns, and regulated-environment experience.
• Experience with contract testing, schema registries, and message replay/poison queue handling.
• Datadog or Dynatrace administration; FinOps practices.

What Success Looks Like (90 Days)
• Blue-green/canary live for at least one service.
• Baseline observability with golden dashboards; documented SLOs for Reporting and Cockpit services.
• Incident/runbook library started; MTTR trending down; first cost dashboard live.
• Migration from ECS to EKS and GitOps is well underway.

Growth Path
• Build a Platform/SRE function (SRE + QA automation partner).
• Evolve paved-path tooling, expand policy-as-code, and scale multi-tenant controls as customer volume grows.

Benefits
• Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance
• Unlimited PTO – with the expectation of responsible use and alignment with team needs
• Fully remote work environment – work from anywhere in the U.S.

title: Director of Client Experience
description:
**How to apply:** Applications for this role are reviewed through our careers site. Please apply at https://travefy.bamboohr.com/careers/33

Travefy is the connected system powering the travel industry.

More than 50,000 travel agencies and advisors run their businesses on Travefy: one platform to manage clients, design and sell stunning trips, market their brands, and run the back office. Everything connects around the trip, so advisors spend less time juggling software and more time wowing clients.

At Travefy, support is not a cost center. It is a feature, and it is one of the biggest reasons our users stay. This role owns it.

## About the Role

We are looking for a Director of Client Experience to own and elevate our CX Support and CX Trainer teams, and to lead the next chapter of how we deliver support: humans and AI working together.

Our CX Support team handles high volume assistance over chat, email, and phone escalation. Our CX Trainers run one on one and group sessions that turn new users into confident power users. Our stack runs on Intercom (including Fin), HubSpot, and a growing set of AI and analytics tools.

You will own the strategy, the systems, the metrics, and the people. You will have a team that executes, and your first job is to make them great. You will also be in the queue or the training when it matters, because that is how the best leaders here stay close to the work.

You also love learning new things and must learn our product cold. Our users are travel advisors running real businesses, and they can tell in one message whether the person helping them actually knows the platform. The best people in this seat become genuine product experts in their first 60 days and never stop.

## What You'll Own

### Team Leadership and Development

You'll build a team that people want to be on and customers want to reach.

- Hire, coach, and develop a high performing team of CX Support and CX Trainer professionals.
- Set clear goals, career paths, and performance metrics, and hold the bar through real feedback.
- Know your team as individuals: what they are great at, where they are stuck, and what they want next.
- Lead from the front during high volume or high stakes moments.

### AI and Support Automation

You'll own the AI layer of our client experience, not just supervise it.

- Own Intercom Fin end to end: tuning, content sources, guidance, handoff rules, and resolution quality.
- Grow AI resolution rate without letting satisfaction slip, and know exactly where the line is.
- Build the workflows, macros, routing, and automations that let a lean team punch far above its weight.
- Use AI to raise the quality of human responses, not just the speed of them.

### Customer Education and Enablement

You'll make sure every advisor knows how to get value from Travefy.

- Own our help documentation, training materials, and onboarding content, and keep them current with a fast moving product.
- Ensure the CX Trainer team delivers onboarding and ongoing education that drives adoption and confidence.
- Keep the whole CX team fluent in a product that ships constantly.

### Operational Excellence and Analytics

You'll run the function on data, not vibes.

- Own the metrics that matter: first response time, resolution time, CSAT, AI resolution rate, contact rate per account, and backlog health.
- Build and read the reporting yourself in Intercom, HubSpot, and our analytics tools. You should be able to answer a question with data the same day it is asked.
- Spot trends, risks, and product problems before they become churn.
- Create and iterate the playbooks and workflows that scale with the team and the product.
- You'll be a voice of the customer inside the company.

## Who You Are

### Must Haves

- 3+ years leading a support or client experience team at a SaaS company, with high volume, multi channel work.
- Hands on depth in Intercom including the Fin era. Not "my team used it," but you configured it, reported on it, and improved it.
- Direct experience deploying or running an AI support agent with real results you can describe in numbers.
- A demonstrated track record of moving support metrics through leadership and operational change.
- Comfortable with data: you build your own reports, you know your numbers cold, and you use them to decide.
- A genuine product learner. You go deep on the product you support, fast, and stay there.
- A people leader who coaches. Your former team members would take your call today.
- Ownership mindset. You identify what needs to happen and make it happen, whether that means directing your team or doing it yourself.

### Nice to Haves

- Experience in travel: travel agencies, host agencies, consortia, tour operators, OTAs, or travel tech.
- You have supported small business or solopreneur customers, where the software is their livelihood.
- Experience building a CX function from a lean base rather than inheriting a large one.

### This role is probably not for you if

- You are not willing to get your hands dirty. You will have a team that executes, but this is a lean company and the best leaders here jump into the queue, a training, or a messy escalation when it counts.
- You need a big team and a big budget before you can make progress.

## What We Offer

- **Competitive compensation:** $100,000 to $125,000 OTE including base and performance compensation.
- **Health, Dental & Vision insurance** for you and your family.
- **Life and Disability insurance.**
- **401(k)** with automatic company contribution.
- **Flexible Time Off + Annual Travel Stipend.**
- **Annual all team retreat** to connect the whole company in person.
- Technology stipend, learning budgets, and more.
- **Real ownership** of a function that our customers name as the reason they stay.

## Location & Eligibility

This is a full time role. We have a strong preference for our Lincoln, Nebraska headquarters or our Pennington, New Jersey office, and we are open to exceptional remote candidates in the U.S. Our team is distributed across Lincoln, Pennington, Omaha, and remote.

At this time, we're not considering applicants who need immigration sponsorship (additional work authorization or permanent work authorization), now or in the future, to work in the United States.

Travefy does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies.

## How to Apply

Please submit your application at https://travefy.bamboohr.com/careers/33

Location: Remote
Schedule: Flexible, no required weekly hours
Experience Level: Student / Entry Level

About CardChirp

CardChirp is a fintech web application designed to help users better understand and optimize their credit card rewards.

The platform uses a recommendation engine that analyzes user spending patterns and compares them against different credit card reward structures to help users identify cards that may better fit their spending habits. CardChirp also incorporates AI-generated explanations to make the recommendation results easier to understand.

The application is currently built using technologies including Flutter/Dart, Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL/Supabase, and AI APIs.

About the Role

We are looking for Beta Testers to help test CardChirp as the platform continues to grow and improve.

This is a volunteer, unpaid position intended primarily for students or early-career individuals looking to gain hands-on experience with software testing, QA, product feedback, or startup development.

There are no required weekly hours. You can contribute whenever you have availability, even if that is only a few minutes at a time.

Most communication and testing coordination will take place through our Discord community.

What You'll Do
Test new and existing CardChirp features
Identify bugs, unexpected behavior, and usability issues
Submit clear bug reports and reproduction steps
Provide feedback on UI/UX and product functionality
Test the recommendation engine using different spending scenarios
Suggest potential product improvements
Help evaluate new features before wider releases
Communicate feedback with the development team through Discord
What We're Looking For

No professional QA experience is required.

This role may be a good fit if you:

Are interested in software engineering, QA, fintech, or product development
Enjoy testing applications and finding bugs
Can clearly explain issues you encounter
Are willing to provide constructive feedback
Want experience contributing to a real software product

Students studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, or related fields are especially encouraged to apply.

What You'll Gain

This opportunity is intended to provide practical exposure to how software products are tested and improved in an early-stage startup environment.

Active contributors may gain experience with:

Software QA and beta testing
Bug reporting and reproduction
Product feedback
Startup development workflows
Fintech applications
Working with engineers on real product issues

Contributors are welcome to list their Beta Tester experience with CardChirp on LinkedIn and their resume based on the work they perform.

Commitment

This is intentionally flexible.

There are:

No required weekly hours
No fixed schedule
No minimum time commitment

If you have a few minutes to test a feature or submit feedback, that contribution is appreciated.

Important

This is an unpaid volunteer opportunity and is not a traditional employment or internship position.

The purpose of the program is to give contributors an opportunity to gain experience while helping CardChirp improve its product.

Learn more about CardChirp on LinkedIn:

https://www.linkedin.com/company/cardchirp

B2B consumer-electronics sales

Technology or computer-accessory sales

title: Long-Term Urdu Transcription Role
description:
Role: Freelance Urdu Audio Proofreader & Editor
Company: 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗺 𝗔𝗜 𝗟𝗮𝗯𝘀 𝗟𝗟𝗣

𝗔𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁:
We are looking for Urdu speakers for a very simple audio-checking task. You will listen to short recorded conversations between two people. The best part? You do not have to type anything from the beginning! The computer has already done most of the hard work for you.

𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗝𝗼𝗯 𝗶𝘀 𝗦𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 (𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗪𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗗𝗼):

  1. 𝗙𝗶𝘅 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗧𝗲𝘅𝘁: We will give you the audio and the typed Urdu text. You just have to listen to the audio and correct any wrong words.
  2. 𝗙𝗶𝘅 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗔𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗼 𝗖𝘂𝘁𝘀: The audio is already chopped into very small clips (3 to 15 seconds). You only need to slightly adjust the start or end time if a word accidentally gets cut in half.
  3. 𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗰𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿𝘀: The system already marks who is talking (like Speaker 1 or Speaker 2). You just have to correct it if the computer labeled the wrong person.

𝗣𝗮𝘆𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗗𝗲𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘀:

𝗥𝗮𝘁𝗲: $13 USD per Speech Hour.

(What is a Speech Hour? It simply means you are paid for the total time people are actually talking in the audio. Silent moments, pauses, and empty gaps are not counted in this time).
